sbc426bbbeb.title: Jensen Huang still thinks a succession plan creates unnecessary hierarchy
sbc426bbbeb.description: It's a remarkable stance for a company that spent the last two weeks finding out what happens without its founder.
sbc426bbbeb.summary: Jensen Huang reportedly still opposes a succession plan at Nvidia, arguing it would create unnecessary hierarchy, after the company's recent leadership disruption.

sd6a3974a1a.title: Yale’s Sonnenfeld: Nvidia is a ‘detriment’ to US industrial might — not a champion
sd6a3974a1a.description: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld warns that what the market cheered Monday, Jensen Huang's White House–backed return as Nvidia's CEO and board member, could prove a giant mistake, exposing the directors to "historic" personal liability from a growing pile of lawsuits and raising the question of whether the country is celebrating a company that has helped put advanced chips in its adversaries' hands.
sd6a3974a1a.summary: Yale's Jeffrey Sonnenfeld argues that Jensen Huang's White House-backed return as Nvidia CEO and board member could be a mistake, exposing directors to lawsuits.
sd6a3974a1a.why: It flags governance and legal risk for leadership and boards, and questions Nvidia's role in US chip policy and export concerns.

sdce071d658.title: Irreducible Governance Structure for Autonomous Agent Systems: Fair Allocation, Strategy-Proofness, and Multi-Scale Composition
sdce071d658.description: arXiv:2611.31284v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous agent governance is commonly framed as a problem of enforcing correct execution. However, in multi-agent systems, an equally fundamental question precedes execution: which agents are allowed to act. In this paper, we show that allocation is not an auxiliary concern but a structural component of governance. When multiple agents compete for execution under constrained resources, any allocation mechanism introduces unavoidable trade-offs between fairness, efficiency, and resistance to strategic manipulation. We formalize this through a set of impossibility results, including Sybil amplification and the incompatibility of desirable allocation properties. We then show that these allocation constraints cannot be resolved within a single
sdce071d658.summary: An arXiv paper argues that deciding which agents may act is a structural part of multi-agent governance, formalizing fairness, efficiency, and strategy-proofness trade-offs.
sdce071d658.why: Offers formal allocation trade-offs for designing resource-constrained multi-agent systems, though it is a theoretical preprint.

sb02e0bf3ed.title: MOZAIC: An Audio-Video Deepfake Benchmark for Telling What Is Fake
sb02e0bf3ed.description: arXiv:2611.31301v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Audio-video (AV) deepfakes can fake the face, the voice, or both. Most benchmarks only ask whether a clip is real or fake, so they cannot show whether a detector relies on the picture, the voice, or encoding traces. We present MOZAIC, a paired benchmark with a 4-way label in which every source clip is released in all four combinations of real or fake video and real or fake audio so each modality contribution can be measured directly. Fakes cover inner-face swapping, whole-frame video diffusion and voice conversion. MOZAIC has 137,745 clips from 15,014 source pairs and four tasks: T1 AV authenticity, T2 manipulation type, T3 identity verification and T4 explanation. We evaluate 12 AV multimodal LLMs (MLLMs), train four detectors and fine-tune
sb02e0bf3ed.summary: MOZAIC is a paired audio-video deepfake benchmark with 137,745 clips, labeling real or fake video and audio separately.
sb02e0bf3ed.why: Lets teams test whether deepfake detectors rely on video, audio, or encoding artifacts, improving evaluation beyond binary real-or-fake labels.

s9b5199cc4b.title: Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Sets for Incomplete Data
s9b5199cc4b.description: arXiv:2611.31329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Attribute reduction in incomplete information systems is difficult because missing values break the equivalence-class structure of rough set theory. We propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set (COFRS) model. Each object is described by its set of present attributes. The similarity of two objects is a weighted overlap on the attributes present in both, divided by the fixed number of attributes |A| instead of the size of their union, so missing values are penalised globally and are not matched as wildcards. From this similarity we define a soft dependency degree based on weighted granule consistency, and we search for reducts by greedy backward elimination in O(|U|^2 |A|^2) time. We show that the relation is symmetric and non-reflexive,
s9b5199cc4b.summary: Researchers propose the Conservative Overlap Fuzzy Rough Set model for attribute reduction in datasets with missing values.

sbc1d896f25.title: Beyond Static Charts: Benchmarking Interactive Chart-to-Code Generation for MLLMs
sbc1d896f25.description: arXiv:2611.31345v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In recent years, multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have achieved significant progress in chart-to-code generation. However, existing benchmarks mainly focus on static charts, overlooking interactive charts that enable richer and more expressive data exploration. Unlike static chart-to-code generation, which emphasizes visual consistency, interactive chart-to-code evaluation targets behavioral consistency, requiring chart states to evolve correctly under sequences of user interactions, thereby rendering traditional one-step evaluation paradigms ineffective. To address this gap, we introduce ChartInt, the first benchmark specifically designed for interactive chart-to-code generation. ChartInt consists of 2,779 carefully annotated example
sbc1d896f25.summary: Researchers introduce a benchmark for interactive chart-to-code generation by multimodal LLMs, evaluating behavior across user interaction sequences.
sbc1d896f25.why: Shows that static chart benchmarks miss interactive behavior, so teams evaluating chart-generating models need richer tests.

s9a43d7dd6f.title: What People Choose Not to Say: A Multimodal Benchmark for Fine-Grained Information Manipulation in Conversations
s9a43d7dd6f.description: arXiv:2611.31346v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in MLLMs have improved social understanding, enabling models to recognize emotions and distinguish truthful from deceptive behaviors. However, existing benchmarks largely focus on coarse-grained emotion recognition or binary truth-deception detection, overlooking the diverse ways people manipulate information in conversations, such as withholding, leakage, fabrication, evasion, and defensive counterclaim. Understanding these behaviors requires reasoning about underlying facts, participant knowledge, and conversational context, making them difficult to evaluate reliably. To address this gap, we introduce InfoCon, a multimodal benchmark for fine-grained information manipulation in conversations. InfoCon identifies six fine-grain
s9a43d7dd6f.summary: Researchers released a multimodal benchmark testing how MLLMs detect fine-grained information manipulation such as withholding, leakage, and evasion in conversations.
s9a43d7dd6f.why: Points to gaps in current models' ability to reason about deception beyond simple truth-or-lie detection.

s1e984615ee.title: Antares-Smaug: Adversarial Names, Tokens and Attack Rewrites: Sanitisers Miss Unseen Generalisations
s1e984615ee.description: arXiv:2611.31347v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Laya is an open decision model: given a text, a question and K named options with descriptions, it returns one probability per option in a single pass, and software may act on the answer unseen. We attack six Laya models with 81 programmatic edits of 566 synthetic items (injected sentences, label leaks, edited descriptions, decoy options, invisible and look-alike characters, floods) and report the share of correctly answered items hijacked or lost, with bootstrap intervals. Attack wordings that no defence was built from win the attacker's option on 59% of items for released Laya and 36% for fine-tune v1 (trained on 109 written injections). An injection works through the option name: a sentence naming an option steers the released model even w
s1e984615ee.summary: Researchers attacked six Laya decision models with 81 programmatic edits and found that sanitizers miss unseen attack generalizations.
s1e984615ee.why: Shows that defenses built on known attacks may fail against novel prompt-injection wording, a risk for automated decision pipelines.

s6d2a8f9c18.title: ContextLure: Exploiting Benign Conversation History for Indirect Prompt Injection
s6d2a8f9c18.description: arXiv:2611.31424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As LLMs become more capable, agents can perform more complex tasks with tools and maintain longer interactions with users. These benign conversations contain evidence on task results, user concerns, and operational constraints. The risk is that attackers who can observe benign conversations (evidence) may construct stronger indirect prompt injections without increasing the attackers' control over prior turns or the later injection. However, we still lack a clear study of how effectively attackers can select and use this evidence. To address this gap, we introduce ContextLure, a red-teaming framework in which an attacker silently observes an existing benign conversation, extracts evidence, and constructs an injection. The challenges are twofol
s6d2a8f9c18.summary: ContextLure is a study showing attackers can use observed benign conversation history to craft stronger indirect prompt injections against LLM agents.
s6d2a8f9c18.why: Agents that carry long conversation context may expose new injection paths even when attackers do not control earlier turns.

s842222505d.title: Learning What vs. Learning How: Decomposing Task and Interface Competence in Agentic Training
s842222505d.description: arXiv:2611.31427v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents operate through harnesses that define system prompts, action formats, feedback loops, and resource constraints. A model may possess the knowledge needed to solve a task yet fail to express that knowledge through a particular harness. This raises a basic question: when a policy fails under a given harness, is it missing task knowledge or the competence to operate the interface? We distinguish two components of agentic competence: task competence, the knowledge and reasoning needed to solve a task, and interface competence, the ability to act on that knowledge through a given harness. Across four reasoning and agentic benchmarks, we show that harness-conditioned training yields vastly different outcomes depending on how these interac
s842222505d.summary: A paper decomposes agent failures into missing task knowledge versus inability to operate the interface, distinguishing task competence from interface competence.
s842222505d.why: Helps teams diagnose whether agent failures stem from the model's knowledge or from harness design and action formats.

s9216299406.title: Taxi: Analyzing Agents at (Real) Scale
s9216299406.description: arXiv:2611.31457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this technical report, we present Taxi -- a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale. Taxi scales to millions of steps efficiently. This is made possible by a combination of scalable analysis methods. Taxi relies primarily on clustering to generate a taxonomy over steps for a structured overview of the data, and provides full SQL access for engineers and automated agents to ask complex questions. Clustering and querying are best used together in a hybrid pipeline guided by a coding agent. Taxi also includes an experimental integration of Jev-style decision models: models that map state and bounded questions directly to typed, probabilistic decisions. They add low-cost semantic routing and evaluation where embeddings
s9216299406.summary: Taxi is a technical report describing a system for debugging, clustering, and monitoring agents at scale, with SQL access for analysis over millions of steps.
s9216299406.why: Offers a practical approach for analyzing large volumes of agent execution traces, useful for teams running agents in production.

sd97bcf0fef.title: SpatialCraft: Evolving Procedural Intelligence from Experience and Skills for Spatial Reasoning Agents
sd97bcf0fef.description: arXiv:2611.31475v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spatial reasoning agents increasingly rely on external tools, such as 3D reconstruction, segmentation, and geometric computation, to answer questions that a multimodal large language model (MLLM) cannot resolve from pixels alone. Tool access, however, shifts the bottleneck to orchestration: the agent must decide which tools to call, in what order, and how to interpret their outputs, yet a stateless agent repeats the same mistakes across tasks. We ask whether a frozen tool-using agent can improve its orchestration from its own interaction history, without parameter updates. We present SpatialCraft, a self-evolving framework that maintains two forms of external knowledge: Experiences, condition-action tactics distilled by contrasting rollouts o
sd97bcf0fef.summary: Researchers propose a method letting a frozen tool-using spatial reasoning agent improve its tool orchestration from its own interaction history.
sd97bcf0fef.why: Shows how agents can learn better tool-call sequencing from past runs without retraining the underlying model.

sc810ea565a.title: Evaluating Frontier-Model Agent Skills with Open-Weight Models in a Science Gateway
sc810ea565a.description: arXiv:2611.31480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific analyses that span many jobs and computing sites depend on workflow management systems to run reliably, but writing a production workflow requires expertise in such a system, which many domain scientists do not have. Coding agents can supply this expertise when they are guided by skills and packaged procedures for recurring tasks. We wrote skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow management system with a frontier model, and the PegasusAI Studio science gateway offers them to scientists through a chat interface. New users without frontier-model credits need an open-weight model, served at no cost on research cyberinfrastructure, but skills written for a frontier model may not work with an open-weight solution. This pape
sc810ea565a.summary: Researchers describe skills and specialist agents for the Pegasus workflow system, offered to scientists via the PegasusAI Studio science gateway chat interface.
sc810ea565a.why: Illustrates packaging frontier-model coding agent skills for domain users, with evaluation using open-weight models.

s08f8a7fd6a.title: XRL4T1D: A Post-hoc Explainability Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Type 1 Diabetes Management
s08f8a7fd6a.description: arXiv:2611.31498v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Type 1 diabetes (T1D) requires lifelong insulin therapy, and reinforcement learning (RL) has shown promise for automated dosing in the UVA/Padova simulator. However, the decisions of RL controllers remain difficult to interpret. We present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework for evaluating pretrained insulin-dosing policies without retraining. Each policy uses 60 minutes of continuous glucose monitor (CGM) and administered-insulin history, sampled every 5 minutes, to recommend insulin. We use SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) to compare the importance of CGM and insulin-history inputs and summarize insulin-history attributions over three 20-minute windows motivated by insulin-on-board. We assess whether these attributions correspo
s08f8a7fd6a.summary: Researchers present XRL4T1D, a post-hoc explainability framework using SHAP to evaluate pretrained reinforcement learning insulin-dosing policies without retraining.
s08f8a7fd6a.why: Offers a way to interpret RL controller decisions in a safety-critical medical setting without changing the trained policy.

s1d8eb48ffe.title: PatientFlowSynth: Evaluating FHIR Agents with Matched Patient Charts
s1d8eb48ffe.description: arXiv:2611.31521v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents that search patient charts must classify claims from retrieved records, including cases with missing or conflicting evidence. In Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), status fields can change how those records should be interpreted. PatientFlowSynth provides 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients and 18 templates that hold the patient, question, and retrieval program fixed across chart variants representing four evidence states. Re-executing the program verifies each variant's reference answer, evidence sets, and search requirements. Strict success requires a completed response with correct labels and citations exactly matching an accepted evidence set retrieved during the episode. Where required, a tool response must al
s1d8eb48ffe.summary: PatientFlowSynth is a benchmark of 18,000 tasks from 225 synthetic patients for evaluating FHIR chart-search agents on claims with missing or conflicting evidence.
s1d8eb48ffe.why: Gives teams a controlled benchmark for testing healthcare records agents on evidence states that affect answer correctness.

sd0679e7d06.title: One Step, Four Clocks: How GUI Agents Fall Out of Step
sd0679e7d06.description: arXiv:2611.31522v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: GUI agents can choose correct actions yet fail as interfaces change during deliberation. Latency alone cannot explain these failures because actions may become invalid at different interaction stages. We model four events: environment change, observation availability, decision commitment, and action receipt (EODA). We introduce ChronotopeGym to study these failures under Paused, Replay, and Live execution. Across five tasks, agents can fail in Live despite succeeding when responses remain valid, even when actions meet deadlines. On Moving Balloon, updating a pending click raises success from 0% to 100% without changing response time. Our accelerator-resident GUI controller, Chronotope, maintains compact interaction history and selectively kee
sd0679e7d06.summary: Researchers model four timing events in GUI agent interactions and introduce ChronotopeGym, finding agents can fail in live execution despite succeeding under valid responses.
sd0679e7d06.why: Shows that latency and interface changes during deliberation can invalidate agent actions, a concern for deploying GUI automation.

s8642462bbe.title: Agent Evaluation Without Ground Truth: A Null Proportion Perspective
s8642462bbe.description: arXiv:2611.31539v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The correctness of actions taken by agents is typically evaluated against known, externally verified ground truth labels, such as whether a proof is correct or whether code compiles and passes unit tests. However, as coding and science agents are entrusted with more end-to-end autonomy -- proposing interventions, running experiments, and deciding what to deploy and investigate next -- whether an agent's actions genuinely improve an outcome must be inferred from noisy, often inconclusive experiments. To evaluate agents in this setting, we define agent quality as a weighted sum of correct decisions along its trajectory, using sequences of $e$-values as statistical evidence regarding correctness in place of ground-truth labels. Our framework acc
s8642462bbe.summary: Researchers propose a null-proportion framework for evaluating agents whose actions must be inferred from noisy, inconclusive experiments rather than ground-truth labels.
s8642462bbe.why: Addresses how to measure whether autonomous agents genuinely improve outcomes when no verified ground truth exists.

s45d0a75ba2.title: Agent Recovery Gone Wrong: Measuring Harm Beyond Duplicate Calls
s45d0a75ba2.description: arXiv:2611.31554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Code-executing LLM agents submit blocks of code that issue several API writes. If a block fails after some of its writes have taken effect, the agent rewrites the block and continues. It is unknown how often such a recovery harms the external state when the failure occurs naturally in the code written by the agent. In this paper, we measure it on recorded trajectories of AppWorld agents. In a stratified random sample of 200 candidate episodes across ten models, 145 are partial executions confirmed by the database state. In the sample, 30 of 143 confirmed partial executions with a determinable outcome are followed by a harmful recovery, and its violation remains at the end of the run, which gives a stratification-weighted estimate of 24.6%. Tw
s45d0a75ba2.summary: A study of AppWorld agent trajectories finds that recovering from partially executed code blocks can harm external state through repeated API writes.
s45d0a75ba2.why: Highlights that agent retry logic can cause unintended duplicate side effects in production API environments.

s4b55c71e9c.title: COGENT: A Modular Cognitive Architecture for Agentic User Simulation
s4b55c71e9c.description: arXiv:2611.31559v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM-based user simulation can support interface design, accessibility research, and interactive-agent evaluation, but standard computer-use agents are optimized for task completion rather than reproducing how people perceive, reason, and act. We introduce COGENT (COGnitive agENT), a modular cognitive architecture for simulating user interaction with desktop interfaces. COGENT draws on established cognitive theories, such as Norman's action cycle and ACT-R, to enable explainable, intervenable, and modular user simulation by decomposing the simulation process into cognitive modules with explicit representations of perception, memory, user state, intentions, and action selection. We begin by presenting six intervenability demonstrations, each tr
s4b55c71e9c.summary: Researchers introduce COGENT, a modular cognitive architecture that simulates user interaction with desktop interfaces based on cognitive theories.
s4b55c71e9c.why: Offers a more explainable approach to simulating users for interface design and accessibility testing, beyond task-completion agents.

s71e21bfe60.title: Off-the-Shelf Autonomous Agents for Game Playtesting
s71e21bfe60.description: arXiv:2611.31570v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In playtesting games, a human operator is typically required to test most gameplay elements. In this work we present Buddy, an autonomous game solving agent which can solve long time horizon objectives in an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems. Buddy will take actions, receive feedback on those actions, and pursue a goal across many turns. No written walkthrough or model training of any kind is required, and we show that this paradigm holds in a novel environment where the agent must discover solutions via exploration rather than recalling them from pretraining. We demonstrate three downstream capabilities: game solving with no provided walkthrough, logging bug tickets for encountered difficulties, and conve
s71e21bfe60.summary: Researchers present Buddy, an autonomous agent that plays an unseen 3D role-playing game using off-the-shelf language model systems without walkthroughs or training.
s71e21bfe60.why: Suggests general-purpose LLM systems can handle long-horizon exploration tasks like playtesting with no task-specific training.

se85d829d86.title: Safe Autoformalization: Sufficiency and Necessity with Entailment Graphs
se85d829d86.description: arXiv:2611.31571v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autoformalization translates a natural-language statement into a formula that captures its intent, which depends on the statement's context: the background that disambiguates it. LLMs make autoformalization practical, but their probabilistic output carries no formal guarantees. We propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy: a formula sufficient for the intent is safe to enforce, and a formula necessary for it is safe to rely on. We use LLMs to generate candidate formulas and order them by logical strength in an Entailment Graph (EG), an ordering a solver decides. Each edge carries a residual and a co-residual, the two adjoints of the entailment order, all fixed by the candidate pool alone. In a conte
se85d829d86.summary: Researchers propose techniques for safe autoformalization that certify one-sided logical adequacy using LLM-generated candidate formulas ordered by logical strength.
se85d829d86.why: Offers a route to attach partial formal guarantees to LLM-generated logical specifications, though the text gives limited deployment detail.

s1c3033b758.title: Provably Near-Optimal PQ in the Extended Zador Model
s1c3033b758.description: arXiv:2611.31579v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates Product Quantization (PQ) Optimization with Gaussian data. It offers three key contributions (i) a proof that SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for PQ; (ii) a new Extended Zador (EZ) estimator of the $k$-means quantization cost that is accurate in low bit rates and low dimensions; and (iii) a novel segmentation algorithm based on 1-d bin packing of global bit allocations. The result is a simple algorithm (EZPQ) with strong approximation guarantees. It matches OPQ's empirical accuracy while providing a per-instance distortion lower bound certificate under the Gaussian EZ cost model. On typical real embedding spectra, EZPQ with 2 bits per coordinate is often certifiably within 1% of the optimum in this model. I
s1c3033b758.summary: Researchers prove SVD is the optimal preconditioning rotation for product quantization on Gaussian data and introduce an EZPQ algorithm with approximation guarantees.
s1c3033b758.why: Provides theoretical grounding and a simple algorithm for tuning vector compression, relevant to embedding search infrastructure.

seef28d1c21.title: Frequency-Conditioned Privacy Auditing of Fine-Tuned Language Models
seef28d1c21.description: arXiv:2611.31581v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models are increasingly fine-tuned on sensitive data, where the same person's information may appear multiple times across records. This can cause models to memorize sensitive information, but memorization does not necessarily mean that the information can be recovered. A more serious privacy risk arises when the model begins to reproduce that information during generation. In this paper, we study how often sensitive information must appear in the fine-tuning data before it becomes recoverable. Across four language models, we vary the frequency of email addresses and phone numbers from $1\times$ to $50\times$ and compare standard fine-tuning, gradient clipping, and differentially private training. We find that the number of rep
seef28d1c21.summary: Researchers study how often sensitive information must appear in fine-tuning data before a language model can reproduce it during generation, across four models.
seef28d1c21.why: Informs privacy risk assessment for fine-tuning on records where the same person's data appears multiple times.

s4d3997d08c.title: Monitorable-by-design architectures for a post-Astra world: a compartmentalization-based approach
s4d3997d08c.description: arXiv:2611.31610v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier models like GPT-6 Astra are increasingly able to do substantial reasoning without a monitorable chain of thought, chains of thought are becoming less legible, and are often monitored asynchronously to reduce cost. With the future of chain of thought monitoring unclear, it may be necessary to design LLMs with monitorability in mind. We propose a modification to existing LLM architectures based on GRAM, SGTM, DEMix, BTS, and similar methods to compartmentalize dangerous capabilities so that their use, especially in combination with dangerous reasoning types that may indicate strategic adversarial use, can be monitored more cheaply than chain of thought in a way that might outlast monitorable chain of thought. We propose several variant
s4d3997d08c.summary: Researchers propose modifying LLM architectures to compartmentalize dangerous capabilities so their use is easier to monitor when chain-of-thought becomes less legible.
s4d3997d08c.why: Points to architecture-level design choices for maintaining oversight of frontier models as reasoning becomes harder to monitor.

se5fa006d6d.title: Multi-agent System for Automatic Discovery of Pareto-optimal Meta-solvers for PDEs
se5fa006d6d.description: arXiv:2611.31611v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Designing linear solvers for discretized partial differential equations requires problem-specific expertise. We present a multi-agent framework, in which language-model agents propose, critique, implement, and evaluate solver configurations assembled from Krylov methods, preconditioners, block factorizations, and neural operators. Inside the proposing agent, a non-dominated sorting genetic evolutionary algorithm evolves the population of meta-solvers toward the Pareto front of six measured quantities, so that one run returns a front of trade-offs rather than a single tuned solver. The system runs on small open-weight language models served on a single laptop, and we compare it with a single agent on four problems. For three-dimensional acoust
se5fa006d6d.summary: A multi-agent framework uses language-model agents and a genetic algorithm to evolve Pareto-optimal linear solver configurations for discretized PDEs.
se5fa006d6d.why: Shows agent-driven search can automate solver design across trade-off metrics, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sfb383e81ff.title: Self-Improving Long-Horizon Reasoning by Learning Summaries from Local Continuations
sfb383e81ff.description: arXiv:2611.31621v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reasoning models degrade as their context grows, so longer reasoning traces do not by themselves give longer effective horizons. One way to extend the horizon is to compress the reasoning history into a compact state from time to time and continue from the state. Existing methods train the state with the final-answer reward or distill it from a stronger model. Neither signal is tailored to measure the contribution of the state alone. We observe that a reasoning model that degrades over long trajectories still behaves reliably in short contexts. We aim to preserve this short-context behavior when compressing the reasoning history. Motivated by this, we train a separate summarizer with Delta-KL, a reward computed from the frozen reasoning model
sfb383e81ff.summary: Researchers propose training reasoning models to compress their reasoning history into summaries by measuring the state's contribution through local continuations.
sfb383e81ff.why: Targets degradation of reasoning models over long contexts, a practical limit for long-horizon agent tasks.

s60604a1190.title: Wavefront: Low-Rank Drafting with Parallel Causal Refinement for Speculative Decoding
s60604a1190.description: arXiv:2611.31638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by letting a cheap drafter propose tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Parallel block drafters such as DFlash and P-EAGLE propose a whole block in one forward pass, but they lose the dependence between tokens in the block; DSpark restores part of it with a lightweight correction head that runs sequentially. Measuring DSpark, we find that this head overrides the base prediction on most slots, so the expensive base readout through the target's full lm_head mostly provides a seed. We therefore propose Wavefront, which follows a simple principle: shrink the base and strengthen the correction head. Wavefront replaces the full lm_head with a learned low-rank base, conditions the correcti
s60604a1190.summary: Researchers propose Wavefront, a speculative decoding method that uses low-rank drafting with parallel causal refinement to speed LLM inference.
s60604a1190.why: Faster verified token drafting can cut LLM serving latency and compute costs for engineers running inference.

s600513770b.title: E2SIM: Long-Horizon Simulation of Everyday Human Behavior with Evolving States
s600513770b.description: arXiv:2611.31641v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents are increasingly expected to support users over long periods, across work, and daily life. This requires modeling not only who users are, but also how their goals, interests, activities, and interactions evolve over time. A challenge in longitudinal user simulation is maintaining consistency between these evolving states and the consequences of actions in a shared environment. We introduce E2SIM, a longitudinal user simulation framework that jointly models evolving actor states and a dynamic shared environment. E2SIM connects actor-state updates with shared-world changes through a feedback loop linking immediate actions, delayed outcomes, and actor-specific observations across work and life. This allows the consequences of earlier a
s600513770b.summary: Researchers introduce E2SIM, a framework that simulates long-horizon everyday human behavior by jointly modeling evolving user states and a shared environment.
s600513770b.why: Consistent longitudinal user simulation could help teams test agents that support users over long periods.

sf4ea7faa42.title: Constructing physical mechanisms with artificial intelligence
sf4ea7faa42.description: arXiv:2611.31653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mechanisms recur across the sciences: the equation for heat in a solid also describes molecular diffusion or a Brownian particle. A mechanism is rarely written in one equation; its operation, boundaries, parameters and closures are stated at different steps of a derivation, where methods that read text or fit formulas miss it. We built an equation-native system that reads the equations of all 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts, and show that mechanisms can be compiled from them and constructed by deterministic calculation. A constructor detaches, transfers, unfolds, composes and joins their parts across disciplines; where parts do not fit, the failure is an equation for the missing term. Constructions turn a threshold reactor into a memory that a
sf4ea7faa42.summary: Researchers describe an equation-native AI system that reads 2.5 million arXiv manuscripts and compiles physical mechanisms from their equations.

sbaaee125a7.title: Stranded Compute in AI Inference Workloads: Recovering Value Through Demand Aggregation
sbaaee125a7.description: arXiv:2611.31654v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI inference infrastructure is commonly analyzed as an energy business. Under full total cost accounting it is not: in the reference deployment modeled here, capital recovery is 87.3% of fully loaded cost per token and electricity 3.7%. Because capital accrues per unit time irrespective of use, accelerator value is destroyed by non-utilization rather than by consumption. Yet, SLO qualified goodput reaches only 59.6% of nameplate throughput, and the decomposition of the loss chain shows that 25.2 of the 40.4 lost percentage points arise from scheduling idleness and stranded burst reserve. Both are properties of a tenant's demand portfolio rather than of its silicon, and neither is diversifiable by a single tenant acting alone. Modelling reserv
sbaaee125a7.summary: A paper argues AI inference economics are dominated by capital recovery and idle accelerator time, and that demand aggregation could recover stranded compute value.
sbaaee125a7.why: Low utilization of accelerators drives inference cost per token, so scheduling and demand aggregation matter for infrastructure planning.

sf629944ee2.title: Look Before You Commit: Visual-Evidence-Guided Decoding for Multimodal Diffusion Language Models
sf629944ee2.description: arXiv:2611.31677v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diffusion multimodal large language models rely on confidence to decide when to commit candidate tokens during generation. In multimodal tasks, however, confidence cannot distinguish whether a candidate originates from image evidence or the language prior. We perform paired forward ablation and find that nearly nine out of ten high-confidence commits are insensitive to the image, while degenerate and hallucination samples exhibit significant increases in the entropy of deep-layer attention organization. Based on this diagnosis, we propose CD-APC, a training-free decoding method. CD-APC performs evidence-adjusted scoring within a base-supported pool and uses dual gating based on model acceptability and contrastive concentration to decide wheth
sf629944ee2.summary: Researchers propose CD-APC, a visual-evidence-guided decoding method for diffusion multimodal LLMs that reduces image-insensitive token commits and hallucinations.
sf629944ee2.why: Grounding decoding in image evidence targets hallucination in multimodal models that teams deploy on vision tasks.

sfa789566d2.title: LimoBench: How Street Smart Are Large Language Models?
sfa789566d2.description: arXiv:2611.31682v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have transformed how humans interact with information, enabling natural-language interfaces across various domains. They are increasingly deployed for geospatial applications including map-based question answering, location-based services, and natural-language interfaces to spatial databases. But are LLMs truly location-aware, able to reliably interpret and precisely answer location queries involving real-world coordinates, points of interest (POIs), and geospatial distances? To answer this concretely, we present LimoBench, a street-level benchmark of 82 natural-language location queries over seven canonical spatial operations: geocoding, reverse geocoding, routing, directionality, range search, $k$-nearest-neighb
sfa789566d2.summary: Researchers present LimoBench, a benchmark testing whether large language models reliably answer location queries involving coordinates, POIs and geospatial distances.
sfa789566d2.why: Shows gaps in LLM geospatial reliability, relevant to teams building map or location-based natural-language interfaces.

s88b4fee001.title: CROSS-Calib: Selective Channel Calibration for Ultrasound Reconstruction
s88b4fee001.description: arXiv:2611.31684v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultrasound imaging provides views of internal tissue in real time for medical diagnosis. However, ultrasound signals may be affected by interference, and correcting errors and removing transient interference while preserving valid echoes remains challenging. We propose CROSS-Calib, a channel recovery method that uses predictions from other channels as references for amplitude and phase calibration, while a gate using context selectively combines calibrated measurements with predicted echoes to retain usable samples and repair unreliable ones. On the in vivo test set, CROSS-Calib outperforms all baseline models under gain errors and transient interference, while phantom tests show that the model restores cyst contrast with echo widths of wire
s88b4fee001.summary: Researchers propose CROSS-Calib, a channel recovery method that calibrates ultrasound signals using predictions from other channels and a context-based gate.

s942a72dbf7.title: PRETZEL: A Benchmark for Cyclic Peptide Structure Prediction
s942a72dbf7.description: arXiv:2611.31708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Macrocyclic peptides are a growing therapeutic modality, and co-folding models are increasingly used to predict their structures. Yet published evaluations rely on small, loosely curated target sets that differ from paper to paper, so results are not comparable, and most report pose RMSD alone, without checking whether the predicted molecule is chemically correct. We introduce PRETZEL (Prediction of Ring-Enclosed Topology: Zero-shot Evaluation of cycLic peptides), a benchmark of 285 curated cyclic peptide-protein complexes spanning three cyclization chemistries, all post-dating the training cutoff of every model evaluated. PRETZEL has three components: PRETZEL-SET, an evaluation set annotated by cyclization chemistry and chemical novelty; PRE
s942a72dbf7.summary: Researchers introduce PRETZEL, a benchmark of 285 curated cyclic peptide-protein complexes for evaluating structure prediction, including chemical correctness checks.
s942a72dbf7.why: Standardized benchmarks make co-folding model results comparable and check chemical validity beyond pose RMSD.

s0ea9aa954b.title: Reproducing History Is Not Enough: Intervention-Level Assurance for LLM-Generated Simulators
s0ea9aa954b.description: arXiv:2611.31736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models can now write simulation programs of operational processes and workflows. These programs can be reused to answer what-if questions on new records and policies. However, a program that reproduces recorded history can still give wrong answers to what-if questions; requested changes may be applied wrongly, or they may be applied to records other than the ones the question is about, or the program may stop being valid once its policy is revised. Current checks return a pass-or-fail verdict for the whole program, which says little about whether any single answer can be trusted. We propose Vouch, a library that judges whether an answer from a generated simulator can be trusted for the change being asked about. Each what-if que
s0ea9aa954b.summary: Researchers argue that LLM-generated simulators passing historical reproduction checks can still fail what-if questions, and propose intervention-level assurance.
s0ea9aa954b.why: Whole-program pass/fail checks can miss wrong what-if behavior, a risk for teams using generated simulation code for policy decisions.

sb663e004c7.title: GreenDynaMix: Thermal-Aware Dynamic Mixed-Precision MoE LLM Inference Systems
sb663e004c7.description: arXiv:2611.31737v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sustained Large Language Model (LLM) inference generates significant heat that exacerbates silicon aging and reduces GPU reliability. Because GPU temperature fluctuates continuously with workload intensity and ambient conditions, keeping it in a safe range requires real-time frequency scaling, which inevitably comes at the cost of either throughput or accuracy. To address this tightly coupled challenge, we propose GreenDynaMix, the first runtime system to jointly integrate a DVFS-based thermal manager with a dynamic precision-tuning throughput compensator. A sensitivity-aware allocator leverages intrinsic importance signals from the Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router to assign higher precision to critical experts, preserving accuracy. Experiment
sb663e004c7.summary: Researchers present GreenDynaMix, a runtime system combining DVFS-based thermal management with dynamic mixed-precision tuning for MoE LLM inference.
sb663e004c7.why: Thermal-aware scaling addresses GPU reliability and throughput trade-offs during sustained inference workloads.

s160e3afedf.title: FN-Prune: Training-Free Expert Pruning with Finite RMSNorm Perturbations
s160e3afedf.description: arXiv:2611.31747v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Expert pruning reduces the memory footprint of mixture-of-experts language models, but retaining model quality depends on which experts are removed. Frequency- and magnitude-based scores measure the expert in isolation and overlook how normalization consumes its contribution: subtracting one expert changes both the direction of the residual stream and the scale applied to what remains. We propose FN-Prune, a training-free criterion that compares the next RMSNorm outputs before and after subtracting each router-weighted expert contribution, holding original routes and weights fixed. Squared differences are averaged over all calibration tokens in one pass; low-scoring experts are physically deleted at uniform per-layer ratios, and inference rer
s160e3afedf.summary: Researchers propose FN-Prune, a training-free expert pruning criterion for mixture-of-experts models that accounts for RMSNorm effects after removing an expert.
s160e3afedf.why: Training-free pruning could reduce MoE memory footprint while better preserving model quality for deployment.

s6eb51df2ae.title: TACT-Bench: Testing Adaptive Conversational Threats against Tool-Use Agents
s6eb51df2ae.description: arXiv:2611.31756v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing autonomy of AI agents in using external tools and making decisions has created an urgent need for comprehensive safety benchmarks. Existing benchmarks test compromised tool channels or adaptive multi-turn attacks, though they may not capture the unique capabilities of policy-governed tool-use agents, which must resist unauthorized requests without abandoning the legitimate work embedded in the same interaction. To fill this gap, we introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark built around scenario-specific stories, personas, manipulation tactics, and response-adaptive escalation. Each adversarial task targets an action explicitly prohibited by the policy provided to the assistant, while the policy remains hidden from the attacking u
s6eb51df2ae.summary: Researchers introduce TACT-Bench, a stateful benchmark testing whether policy-governed tool-use agents resist adaptive conversational threats while completing legitimate work.
s6eb51df2ae.why: Tool-using agents need tests for resisting unauthorized requests without abandoning legitimate tasks in the same interaction.

sfa3edd752f.title: Verified Proof Refactoring with Codex and Qwen
sfa3edd752f.description: arXiv:2611.31762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We refactor existing Lean 4 proofs to reduce source length and checking cost while preserving theorem statements and compatibility across Lean versions. A locally served Qwen model uses the open-source Codex CLI to inspect source, retrieve declarations, and test proof replacements. The host keeps a replacement only if it improves the objective and Lean accepts it on every required version. A deterministic CPU pass then refines the verified proofs. On the 60 problems in Lean Refactor Arena, model search achieves a local mean combined score of 82.07, and cleanup raises it to 82.18. The final proofs pass all 127 required proof--version checks. Our system placed first in the open-source LLM track of Lean Refactor Arena at VeriCodeGen.
sfa3edd752f.summary: A workflow uses a locally served Qwen model with the Codex CLI to refactor Lean 4 proofs, keeping changes only when Lean accepts them across versions.
sfa3edd752f.why: Shows verified, automated code refactoring with local models, useful for teams maintaining formal proof codebases.

s7806e40164.title: SciFig2Data: A Workflow for Recovering Structured Data from Scientific Figures
s7806e40164.description: arXiv:2611.31787v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Scientific measurements reported in scholarly articles are often embedded in compound figures rather than available as machine-readable data. Recovering these measurements at literature scale requires an integrated workflow for figure localization, panel decomposition, chart identification, numerical reconstruction, and experimental context association. We present \textit{SciFig2Data}, an automated, high-throughput workflow for harvesting structured experimental data from scientific PDF repositories. The system integrates multi-scale document element detection, adaptive compound figure decomposition, two-stage OCR-based semantic filtering, Swin-based chart classification, and instruction-guided multimodal large language model (MLLM) reconstru
s7806e40164.summary: Researchers present SciFig2Data, an automated workflow that recovers structured numerical data from charts in scientific PDF figures.
s7806e40164.why: Automated extraction of figure data could enable literature-scale datasets for research and data teams.

s8eb6158b71.title: AGL-SKILL: Coding Harnesses as Agentic Optimizers
s8eb6158b71.description: arXiv:2611.31794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used through harnesses as agents, with growing autonomy to do useful work. Agent performance can often be enhanced by the use of skills: reusable workflows, code, and prompts that provide task-related information or guide the behaviour of the model. Skills, being textual in nature, present themselves as another editable surface to be optimized; current methods have improved on handcrafting and one-shot generation by treating skill development as an iterative process, using score-driven search to tweak and improve performance. In this paper, we demonstrate the efficacy of the agents themselves as optimizers: across five benchmarks, a coding agent without guidance substantially improves every target and outperfo
s8eb6158b71.summary: Researchers present AGL-SKILL, which treats agent skills as editable text optimized iteratively with score-driven search inside coding harnesses.
s8eb6158b71.why: Optimizing agent skills as a search surface could improve agent performance without manual handcrafting.

s3ccf039f49.title: Constructive Causal Abstraction and a Case Study in Mechanistic Interpretability
s3ccf039f49.description: arXiv:2611.31795v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Existing frameworks in causal abstraction first propose a high-level causal model, and then verify whether its interventional effects agree with those of a given micro-level model - the two models are declared causally consistent when the discrepancy is zero. However, proposing a consistent macro causal model is difficult, because macro causal relations are almost never well-defined, since distinct micro-level interventions associated with the same apparent macro intervention can produce different effects. Our central insight is that causally consistent macro-level models can be obtained constructively: ill-defined macro interventions can be interpreted as missing variables on the macro level, and can be accounted for by introducing a complem
s3ccf039f49.summary: An arXiv paper proposes constructive causal abstraction, arguing macro causal models should be built to be consistent with micro-level models rather than verified after the fact, with an interpretability case study.
s3ccf039f49.why: Offers a method for building high-level causal explanations of neural networks, relevant to engineers doing mechanistic interpretability.

sf2d6acc853.title: A Generative AI Agent to Emulate Interactive Human-driven Vehicles for Automated Driving Testing in Urban Areas
sf2d6acc853.description: arXiv:2611.31797v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Realistic modeling of human-driven vehicle (HDV) interactions is essential for automated driving safety testing in urban areas. Existing methods struggle to reproduce realistic safety-critical interactions involving high collision risk for the following reasons: they often assume full observability, overlooking interactions arising from occlusion. Driving styles are mainly characterized by vehicle maneuvers, limiting the diversity of safety-critical interaction behaviors. Moreover, learning signals from safety-critical interactions can be diluted by non-critical driving behaviors. To address these issues, we propose a generative AI agent to emulate interactive HDVs. The agent incorporates field-of-view modeling to account for driver visibilit
sf2d6acc853.summary: Researchers present a generative AI agent that emulates interactive human-driven vehicles to generate safety-critical urban interactions for testing automated driving systems.
sf2d6acc853.why: Provides a way to produce realistic, occlusion-aware test scenarios for validating autonomous driving software in urban settings.

sabfcc175f2.title: Compressible Representations: Functional Spines in Deep Neural Networks
sabfcc175f2.description: arXiv:2611.31817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Deep networks embed inputs in high-dimensional representations, but how much of this capacity actually drives behavior? We introduce a framework for identifying, at each layer, the subspace of the representation that is functionally sensitive to the task. Using a matrix analogous to the Fisher information but defined over the hidden representation, we rank directions by their influence on downstream computation and project onto the most task-sensitive subspace. Across pretrained vision networks, representations are remarkably compressible: a small fraction of the task-sensitive subspace preserves most performance, often requiring far fewer dimensions than geometric alternatives. We find that this compressed representation is also more robust
sabfcc175f2.summary: A paper introduces a method using a Fisher-like matrix to find the task-sensitive subspace of each layer in deep networks, finding pretrained vision network representations are highly compressible.
sabfcc175f2.why: Suggests much of a network's representation capacity is unused by behavior, which could inform model compression and efficiency work.

s07b2aecd22.title: GaokaoMathGen: Chinese Gaokao Mathematics Finale Problem Generation Controlled by Latent Reasoning Structures
s07b2aecd22.description: arXiv:2611.31823v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generating Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problems requires controlling not only the included skills, but also the underlying mathematical kernel and solution path. Existing LLM-based methods mainly rely on surface-level specifications, while the realized difficulty of generated problems cannot be determined directly from prompted targets. Therefore, we propose GaokaoMathGen, a framework for Chinese Gaokao mathematics finale problem generation controlled by latent reasoning structures. It extracts standardized latent reasoning structures from seed problems and performs constrained synthesis using skills, methods, a core identity, and a pivot step as structural controls. We further estimate realized difficulty through logical-quality filter
s07b2aecd22.summary: GaokaoMathGen is a framework that generates Chinese Gaokao math finale problems by controlling latent reasoning structures rather than surface prompt specifications.

s1c8a2e400c.title: Not All Interpretation Methods Are Created Equal: Tiered Evaluation of AI Interpretability
s1c8a2e400c.description: arXiv:2611.31833v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As AI transitions to sociotechnical deployments, uninterpretable models pose serious threats to reliability, public trust and contestability. However, not all interpretation methods are created equal: for interpretability to enhance deployment safety and effectiveness, interpretation methods must be evaluated in a tiered system to differentiate evidence levels of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated interpretation instances. Our core vision is that elevating the evaluation of interpretation methods to a core AI assessment metric will drive robust knowledge discovery from data (KDD) and ensure safe, contestable sociotechnical deployments of AI. To this end, we propose TRUST, a tiered evaluation framework that builds upon the
s1c8a2e400c.summary: A position paper argues interpretation methods should be evaluated in a tiered system that grades evidence of trustworthiness, rather than validated through isolated instances.
s1c8a2e400c.why: Suggests teams should judge interpretability tools by graded evidence levels before relying on them for deployment safety decisions.

s87097a0602.title: Modeling Event-Conditioned Emotional Expression Response with LLM Agents in a Synthetic Social Simulation
s87097a0602.description: arXiv:2611.31851v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Emotions are central drivers of human behavior, yet most behavioral models fail to capture their role in shaping perception, decision-making, and collective action. Application areas such as emergency response and public health are especially constrained by the lack of emotion-aware modeling. While large language models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into agent-based models (ABMs), little work has examined how to endow LLM agents with emotional reasoning or validated their ability to reproduce empirically observed emotional patterns. This study addresses this gap by introducing a hierarchical prompting framework that conditions LLM agents with demographic, psychological, and contextual cues to generate event-conditioned emotional response
s87097a0602.summary: Researchers study LLM agents with emotional reasoning in an agent-based social simulation, testing whether they reproduce empirically observed emotional response patterns to events.
s87097a0602.why: Points to validated emotion-aware agent modeling for applications like emergency response and public health simulation.

sf1055fbcd0.title: Explainable Deep Learning for Malaria Parasite Detection and Species Differentiation in Thick Blood Smear Images: A Pilot Feasibility Study
sf1055fbcd0.description: arXiv:2611.31855v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Species-level differentiation of Plasmodium falciparum (PF) and P. vivax (PV) determines treatment, yet deep learning detectors rarely test whether their explanations are reliable. In this pilot feasibility study of TRACE-Mal, a research prototype combining YOLOv8n-seg detection and a six-model soft-voting ensemble, we examined whether agreement among three post-hoc explanation methods (Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP) is associated with the correctness of species calls. the study analysed 2,847 parasite crops from 250 thick smears within publicly available Lacuna Malaria Datasets. The model achieved an mAP50 score of 0.79 and the ensemble had a macro F1 of 0.84 (PF recall 0.86; PV recall 0.74). Unadjusted analyses of crops revealed that predictions
sf1055fbcd0.summary: A pilot study of TRACE-Mal examines whether agreement among Grad-CAM, LIME and SHAP explanations predicts correctness of malaria parasite species calls from blood smear images.
sf1055fbcd0.why: Shows explanation agreement may serve as a reliability signal for medical imaging classifiers, though it is a pilot feasibility study.

s31b484ba3b.title: No Fixed Configuration Is Best: Context- and Cost-Aware Tuning of LLM Pipelines, with an Application to Schema Matching and Mapping
s31b484ba3b.description: arXiv:2611.31864v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The numeric settings of a multi-stage LLM pipeline (a compound AI system) are the usual target of tuning. We tuned all of them for an LLM pipeline for schema matching and mapping, with accuracy and cost as joint objectives, and we show what this buys, what it cannot buy, and where the remaining accuracy is. First, tuning buys cost and a little accuracy. On 35 tasks, with whole groups of tasks held out from tuning, one tuned configuration gains 2.9 points of top-1 accuracy (HR@1) over the default at 18% more cost, and another keeps the accuracy of the default at 32% lower cost. Second, the accuracy depends on a choice that numeric tuning cannot reach. Restricting the search for each source column to one assigned target table changes HR@1 by +3
s31b484ba3b.summary: A paper shows that tuning all settings of a multi-stage LLM schema matching pipeline for accuracy and cost yields modest accuracy gains and cost trade-offs, with no single best configuration.
s31b484ba3b.why: Indicates tuning compound LLM pipelines per context and cost budget may matter more than one fixed default configuration.

s1d74e541b4.title: RepoEviAgent: Scalable Synthesis of Evidence-Grounded Repository-Level Question Answering Tasks
s1d74e541b4.description: arXiv:2611.31873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-world software engineering (SWE) tasks require agents to understand repository structures, cross-module dependencies, and runtime behaviors, posing significant challenges for constructing high-quality training and evaluation data. To address this, we propose RepoEviAgent, a scalable SWE data construction framework that integrates quality-aware data curation and role-specialized multi-agent task synthesis. Starting from 8,477 open-source repositories and approximately 2.48 million pull request records, we employ semantic alignment, complexity constraints, and multidimensional quality assessment to identify valuable SWE data. We further develop a sandbox-based multi-agent framework that integrates automated environment construction, execut
s1d74e541b4.summary: RepoEviAgent is a multi-agent framework that synthesizes evidence-grounded repository-level question-answering tasks from thousands of open-source repositories and pull requests.
s1d74e541b4.why: Offers a scalable way to build training and evaluation data for software engineering agents working across real codebases.

s70f945614d.title: HEAR, SEE, SPIKE ONCE: Highly Efficient NeuroAI Temporal Neural Networks for Low-Precision Multimodal Audio-Visual Classification and Online Learning
s70f945614d.description: arXiv:2611.31884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Spiking neural networks for multimodal audio-visual classification reach high accuracy by adopting deep-learning machinery: multi-stage convolutional or transformer encoders trained end-to-end with surrogate-gradient backpropagation through time. These prior works typically rely on full-precision (32-bit) parameters and do not treat hardware efficiency as a primary design objective. In this paper, we propose NeuTNN-AV, a much simpler hardware-amenable multimodal substrate built on the recently proposed NeuroAI Temporal Neural Network (NeuTNN) and demonstrate that it can match or outperform state-of-the-art SNN baselines with a fraction of their synapse counts. NeuTNN neurons carry multiple active dendritic segments. Each input line spikes at
s70f945614d.summary: NeuTNN-AV is a simpler, hardware-amenable spiking neural network for multimodal audio-visual classification and online learning, aiming for low-precision efficiency.
s70f945614d.why: Targets hardware efficiency as a primary design goal for multimodal neuromorphic classifiers, relevant to edge deployment.

see3246c16d.title: Cheap Memory Costs Future Compute: Co-Designing Persistent KV and GPU Execution for Efficient Streaming Video Diffusion
see3246c16d.description: arXiv:2611.31892v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Block-causal video diffusion generates long videos block by block, conditioned on a persistent key-value (KV) cache. After each block is denoised, an extra noise-free ($t=0$) forward pass writes its clean KV into the cache; once distillation and speculative early exit make denoising cheap, this clean KV update dominates the runtime. Reusing stale KV shortens the update, but stale memory corrupts the conditioning of later blocks and inflates their denoising steps, so the saved compute reappears downstream. We present SAMR (Step-Aware Memory Reconstruction), a training-free method for frozen causal video DiTs that refreshes only part of the cache and reconstructs the rest without DiT forwards. Our key observation is that, once rotary position p
see3246c16d.summary: SAMR is a method for streaming block-causal video diffusion that reconstructs stale persistent KV cache to reduce costly clean-KV update passes while preserving conditioning quality.
see3246c16d.why: Addresses a runtime bottleneck in long video generation, where cache updates dominate cost once denoising is accelerated.

s49727fe8f2.title: Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Unlearning
s49727fe8f2.description: arXiv:2611.31932v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model unlearning aims to remove the influence of designated training data while preserving unrelated model capabilities. Existing likelihood-based methods commonly optimize against fixed forget sequences, providing only negative supervision on what the model should not generate and overlooking the states visited by the evolving unlearned policy. We introduce Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation (CPSD), a new unlearning framework that constructs an explicit knowledge-reduced target distribution and distills it along the model's own trajectories. Given a student rollout, a frozen reference model evaluates each token under a plain context and a privileged context containing the forget information. CPSD treats the resulting dist
s49727fe8f2.summary: Researchers introduce Contrastive On-Policy Self-Distillation (CPSD), an LLM unlearning method that distills a knowledge-reduced target along the unlearned model's own rollouts.
s49727fe8f2.why: Offers an alternative to fixed-forget-set unlearning that may better remove training data influence while preserving other capabilities.

s950384a079.title: CAPE: Coordinating Calibration and Search for Tool-Use Policies
s950384a079.description: arXiv:2611.31938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A tool call can fail even when the operation behind it is correct, because the receiving tool parses delimiters, dates or record layouts under a configuration the agent cannot inspect. Compiling a tool-use policy for such a tool requires both calibration, which evaluates candidate calls on candidate configurations, and search over the evaluated calls. The two share one compilation budget: calibrating everything first postpones any improved policy until the end, while re-solving every partially known model delays the next useful query. A call becomes usable as soon as its effects are known on the configurations that reach it. We present CAPE, a training-free compiler built on this observation. It maintains an executable policy at all times, di
s950384a079.summary: CAPE is a method that coordinates calibration of tool-call configurations with search over tool-use policies under a shared compilation budget.
s950384a079.why: Addresses why agent tool calls fail due to unseen tool configurations, a practical reliability issue for agent builders.

s08809b3dfa.title: Perception Is Enough, at the Right Scale: Scale-Adaptive Token Pruning for Vision-Language-Action Models
s08809b3dfa.description: arXiv:2611.31954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models must process continuous streams of visual observations, and the resulting computational cost limits real-time robotic control. Token pruning reduces this cost, but a fixed semantic scale of perceptual representation can overlook information needed at different stages of manipulation. We show that perceptual semantics can guide effective token selection without relying on internal attention when the selection scale adapts to the scene's evolving semantic structure. Based on this observation, we introduce TauPrune-VLA, a training-free method that controls the scale of the retained perceptual representation through a single perception temperature $\tau$. To adapt this scale as manipulation proceeds, TauPrune-V
s08809b3dfa.summary: TauPrune is a scale-adaptive token pruning method for vision-language-action models that selects tokens based on perceptual semantics, reducing compute for robotic control.
s08809b3dfa.why: Could lower inference cost for real-time robot control models without relying on internal attention maps.

s259f8681bd.title: DexOPD: Dual-Extrapolation On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Models
s259f8681bd.description: arXiv:2611.31969v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Flow-based diffusion models have become a mainstream paradigm for text-to-image generation, where task-specific post-training produces specialist models with complementary strengths. Multi-teacher on-policy distillation (OPD) offers an efficient way to consolidate these specialists into a single unified student. Recent methods strengthen supervision through teacher extrapolation, constructing stronger proxy teachers that allow distilled students to surpass the original specialists. However, their extrapolation directions remain defined solely by frozen teacher and reference models, leaving the student's own training progress unexploited. To address this limitation, we introduce DexOPD, a dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation method for di
s259f8681bd.summary: DexOPD proposes dual-extrapolation on-policy distillation to consolidate multiple specialist flow-based text-to-image diffusion models into a single student model.
s259f8681bd.why: Offers a route to merge several specialist image models into one unified model that can surpass its teachers.

s5ef0c0aa6f.title: Coding4Games: Can Modern Coding Agents Play Modern Video Games?
s5ef0c0aa6f.description: arXiv:2611.31974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Games, especially modern AAA games, challenge language models to perceive complex scenes, control actions, and make decisions over long horizons. Existing game benchmarks primarily test language models as computer-use agents that query a language model throughout play, incurring repeated inference cost and, in real-time games, acting while the environment continues to evolve. We ask whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to develop standalone game-playing programs that run without language model inference. We thus introduce Coding4Games, a benchmark for evaluating whether coding agents can develop standalone programs that play modern games through visual observations and standard game inputs. Coding4Games has three defining fea
s5ef0c0aa6f.summary: Coding4Games introduces a benchmark testing whether coding agents can learn from game interaction to build standalone programs that play modern video games without LLM inference.
s5ef0c0aa6f.why: It offers a path to game-playing programs that avoid repeated model inference costs and latency issues in real-time environments.

s0499cded43.title: Discovering Bandwidth-Efficient Prefetchers to Shrink the Cache Hierarchy
s0499cded43.description: arXiv:2611.31983v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shared last-level caches (LLCs) increasingly dominate server processor die area, forcing architects to trade core counts for cache capacity. While intelligent data prefetching offers a pathway to reclaim this silicon, designing coordinated, multi-level prefetching policies for multi-core systems is bottlenecked by day-long, cycle-level simulations. This simulation wall limits even LLM-based microarchitecture discovery; the state-of-the-art ArchAgent system evolves one cache level at a time on single-core benchmarks, adds multi-core configurations only at the end, and trails the human champion under multi-core shared cache contention. We introduce DuoArchitect, an autonomous agentic framework for multi-fidelity, multi-core co-discovery of pref
s0499cded43.summary: Researchers use LLM-based discovery to design bandwidth-efficient multi-level prefetchers that could let server processors shrink cache hierarchies.
s0499cded43.why: Shows LLM-driven microarchitecture search could help reclaim cache die area, though the excerpt gives limited detail on results.

sa70b833b71.title: How Much Dependency Can a Marginal Rule See? Total Correlation in Diffusion LM Parallel Decoding
sa70b833b71.description: arXiv:2611.31990v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A masked diffusion language model is fast because it commits several tokens per step. Each token is sampled from its own marginal, so the dependency between the tokens is lost, and the size of that loss is the conditional total correlation C of the committed set. Most decoders choose the set from per-position marginals, which can bound C but cannot determine it. We ask how well they predict it. We estimate C for fixed candidate sets on four masked diffusion LMs from two families. On three of the four, the best marginal-only predictor is off by about one bit (0.74 to 1.17), 1.8 to 3.7 times less than a baseline that knows only the bound, and most of this accuracy comes from the bound itself. On a subset, our estimate ranks sets like the exact
sa70b833b71.summary: A study measures how well marginal-only decoding rules predict the total correlation lost when masked diffusion language models commit multiple tokens per step.
sa70b833b71.why: Clarifies when parallel decoding in diffusion LMs loses accuracy, relevant to choosing decoding strategies for speed-quality tradeoffs.

s520cd7260b.title: TableRouter: Query-Aware Evidence Construction for Long-Table Question Answering
s520cd7260b.description: arXiv:2611.32006v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLMs can reason over tables, but when tables outgrow the context budget, retrieving relevant rows is only part of the solution. A retrieved subset may omit information required for an exact aggregate; even complete evidence may remain difficult for an LLM to use. We introduce TableRouter, a training-free framework that analyzes each query, then chooses between two routes: a computation route, which derives question-conditioned statistics from the full table, and a coverage route, which retrieves relevant rows and column summaries. The chosen context is passed to a frozen LLM in one call. Across three LLMs and three large-table benchmarks, TableRouter outperforms the strongest of six single-call baselines in all nine settings by 1.2-18.3 accur
s520cd7260b.summary: TableRouter is a training-free framework that routes each long-table question to either a computation route or a coverage route to build evidence for LLMs.
s520cd7260b.why: Offers a practical method to improve LLM answers over tables too large for the context window without additional training.

sce006e48c5.title: Marketing-Bench: Evaluating Frontier Models and Agents on Real-World Marketing Capabilities
sce006e48c5.description: arXiv:2611.32012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As frontier AI models and agents are deployed more broadly in the real world, marketing is emerging as one of their largest applications. Marketing teams use AI models to produce brand assets like website copy and social media posts, while consumers' agents autonomously discover products, research purchases, and navigate websites. However, evaluating marketing capability is difficult because unlike areas like software development, customer support, or legal review where ground truth is more objectively defined, marketing is subjective, and output quality is judged based on taste and brand. We introduce Marketing-Bench, the first open-source marketing benchmark, which pairs discriminative tasks (detecting brand anomalies) with generative tasks
sce006e48c5.summary: Marketing-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating frontier models and agents on real-world marketing tasks, where ground truth is subjective.
sce006e48c5.why: Gives teams a way to assess model suitability for marketing workloads, an area where objective evaluation is hard.

sf88b32686a.title: From Rule-based to Agentic: LLM Agent based Real-time Control of Urban Drainage Systems for Flooding and Sewer Overflow Mitigation
sf88b32686a.description: arXiv:2611.32046v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time control (RTC) for urban drainage systems (UDS) remains hampered by sparse in-network sensing. While heterogeneous multi-modal meteorological early warnings often contain decision-critical information for UDS RTC, none of the existing approaches can exploit such externally-sourced information within the control workflow. Here we introduce AgenticAI-Control, an agentic artificial intelligence framework able to assimilate multi-source meteorological early warnings in RTC. Two coupled large language model agents are integrated to generate control strategies by retrieving meteorological early-warnings and fusing them with domain engineering expertise. Validated via simulation studies of a combined sewer catchment in eastern China across
sf88b32686a.summary: AgenticAI-Control uses two coupled LLM agents to incorporate multi-source meteorological warnings into real-time control of urban drainage systems.
sf88b32686a.why: Demonstrates applying LLM agents to critical infrastructure control, though the excerpt provides few performance details.

s329aefbfd3.title: EffectWAM: Learning Action-Grounded Effects for Robot Manipulation
s329aefbfd3.description: arXiv:2611.32053v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World-action models connect visual prediction with executable robot control. We present EffectWAM, which develops this connection through three complementary components: Effect, camera positional encoding (CaPE), and Action Grounding. Effect represents visual change as the difference between independently encoded future observations and a shared current-observation anchor. CaPE conditions endpoint pooling on relative camera pose when reliable extrinsics are available, while sharing the same learned parameters with pose-free pooling for uncalibrated trajectories. Action Grounding trains the visual representation to retain measured changes in end-effector pose and gripper state. An exponential moving average of the observation encoder supplies
s329aefbfd3.summary: EffectWAM is a world-action model for robot manipulation that represents visual change as effects and grounds them in executable actions using camera pose encoding.
s329aefbfd3.why: Provides a method linking visual prediction to robot control, relevant to teams building manipulation systems.

s2deefcdb3e.title: More Powerful, Less Verifiable? Mitigating Hard-to-Verify Hallucinations in MLLM's Reinforcement Learning
s2deefcdb3e.description: arXiv:2611.32055v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) strengthens model capabilities through feedback from humans and environments. However, emerging evidence suggests that reward optimization can produce outputs whose errors are harder for humans to detect. To address this issue, we construct ITHV (the Image-Text Hallucination Verifiability Dataset), comprising 2,728 visually grounded instances that distinguish between obvious hallucinations, which humans readily detect, and elusive hallucinations, which humans struggle to identify. We then propose DAPO-V, an extension of DAPO that maximizes correctness subject to a budget on verifiability-aware risk. Specifically, DAPO-V combines a verifiability-aware reward with adaptive dual control, where larger penalties are ass
s2deefcdb3e.summary: The authors build ITHV, a dataset distinguishing easy and hard-to-verify image-text hallucinations, and propose DAPO-V, an RL extension aimed at reducing the latter.
s2deefcdb3e.why: Highlights that reward optimization can yield errors humans struggle to detect, a verification risk for RL-tuned multimodal models.

s51fefaea28.title: ExpGuard: Guarding Long-Horizon LLM Agents against Corrupted Experience
s51fefaea28.description: arXiv:2611.32085v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-horizon large language model (LLM) agents distill past trajectories into reusable experiences. Misleading or adversarial guidance in source trajectories can corrupt these experiences, allowing harmful instructions to persist across tasks and influence future agent actions. Assessing the risks of potentially corrupted experiences poses three challenges: (1) modeling provenance and execution dependencies before experience reuse, (2) learning task-conditioned risk from trajectory outcomes, and (3) repairing risky experiences at online inference. To address these challenges, we present ExpGuard, a framework for retrieval-triggered experience risk assessment and online repair. Specifically, to tackle challenge (1), ExpGuard integrates experie
s51fefaea28.summary: ExpGuard is a framework that assesses and repairs corrupted experiences in long-horizon LLM agents so harmful instructions do not persist across tasks.
s51fefaea28.why: Addresses a real risk for agents that reuse past trajectories, where adversarial guidance can propagate into future actions.

s00fc3ee55d.title: From Memory Access to Evidence Sufficiency: Diagnosing and Addressing Demand--Evidence Misalignment
