s00fc3ee55d.description: arXiv:2611.32088v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-term memory retrieval often returns query-relevant records, but relevance does not guarantee sufficient evidence: answering requires a set of records that jointly satisfies a question's factual, relational, temporal, and state constraints. We study this demand--evidence misalignment through MemPath, an interventional framework that diagnoses failures in memory access, demand coverage, and evidence utilization. Guided by this diagnosis, we propose BiDE-Mem, which represents questions as typed demands and uses them to guide retrieval and evidence organization. We formalize demand--evidence support; in the evaluated compact path, it is conveyed through provenance-aware evidence organization and Reader guidance rather than a separate generat
s00fc3ee55d.summary: MemPath diagnoses memory retrieval failures, and BiDE-Mem uses typed demands to retrieve sets of records that jointly provide sufficient evidence for questions.
s00fc3ee55d.why: Shows relevance-based retrieval can miss needed evidence, a design concern for agent memory systems.

sa1535ee016.title: CoverMem: Coverage-Constrained Visual Memory for Budgeted Embodied Question Answering
sa1535ee016.description: arXiv:2611.32119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Episodic-memory embodied question answering enables agents to answer questions based on previously recorded visual observations of the surrounding scenes. However, growing observation histories, varying observation quality across viewpoints, and limited computational resources make it challenging to construct and maintain compact visual memories while retrieving sufficient evidence for question answering. To address these challenges, we introduce CoverMem, which incorporates three key components: (1) a coverage-constrained memory construction method that selects a compact set of informative full frames satisfying object-quality and representative-scene coverage requirements; (2) a coverage-preserving incremental maintenance strategy that loca
sa1535ee016.summary: CoverMem is a coverage-constrained visual memory method for embodied question answering under limited computational budgets.
sa1535ee016.why: Offers ideas for keeping compact visual memories for embodied agents when observation histories grow large.

s3951081dad.title: Breaking the Binary-Lifting Barrier for DNA Minimizer Density: Exact Optimization of a Native 4-ary Order at (w, k) = (12, 5)
s3951081dad.description: arXiv:2611.32159v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Minimizer schemes sample at least one $k$-mer from every window of $w$ consecutive $k$-mers via a total order $\pi$ on $\Sigma^k$. For DNA ($\sigma = 4$), state-of-the-art lookup schemes such as GreedyMini and OptMini optimize a binary order ($2^k$ ranks) and lift it to $\Sigma^k$ by ranking one bit-plane primarily and breaking $2^k$-way ties lexicographically on the other bit-plane. At $(w, k) = (12, 5)$, this projection locks sets of $32$ DNA $5$-mers into contiguous blocks and restricts the active universal hitting set (UHS) prefix to $448$ of $1024$ $5$-mers, giving exact expected DNA density $2246214544 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1307468945$ for OptMini (k5-w12-13.txt) and $2248978620 / 2^{34} \approx 0.1309077849$ for GreedyMini (w12_k5.gm). We
s3951081dad.summary: Researchers present an exact optimization of a native 4-ary order for DNA minimizer density at (w, k) = (12, 5), avoiding binary-lifting projection.
s3951081dad.why: Relevant mainly to bioinformatics sequencing tools; the excerpt offers little for general engineering teams.

sb4d1668269.title: XMind: Thinking Twice via Cross-Memory Reasoning for LLM-Based Autonomous Driving
sb4d1668269.description: arXiv:2611.32209v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory-augmented large language model (LLM) driving agents can reuse past experience, yet previously learned corrections often fail to transfer when traffic conditions change. A key limitation is that existing memories mainly record observed outcomes, providing little evidence about alternative actions. We introduce XMind, a training-free framework that enables LLM-based driving to "Think Twice" through cross-memory reasoning. XMind integrates working memory of recent traffic states with episodic memory of critical risk events. The agent first makes an initial decision from the current context and then cross-checks it against retrieved historical experience. If a conflict arises, it makes a second decision guided by the retrieved evidence. To
sb4d1668269.summary: XMind is a training-free framework that lets LLM driving agents reason across working and episodic memories to consider alternative actions.
sb4d1668269.why: Suggests memory designs that store alternative actions could help LLM agents transfer learned corrections as traffic changes.

s1d7b2e592a.title: PoseVLN: Learning Geometric State Evolution for Vision-Language Navigation
s1d7b2e592a.description: arXiv:2611.32218v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an embodied agent to relate past experience, current spatial state, and future motion while following natural-language instructions. Recent approaches improve these capabilities through long-horizon memory, state-aware reasoning, and future prediction, yet these components are often modeled separately, leaving navigation state evolution insufficiently connected across time. We argue that camera pose provides a natural geometric representation for bridging past, present, and future states. Based on this insight, we propose PoseVLN, a pose-aware VLN framework that jointly learns navigation decisions and geometric state evolution. PoseVLN organizes visual memory and the current observation in an episode-
s1d7b2e592a.summary: PoseVLN uses camera pose as a geometric representation to link past, present, and future navigation states for vision-language navigation agents.
s1d7b2e592a.why: Proposes connecting memory, state reasoning, and prediction through pose, which may inform embodied navigation system design.

s192199e400.title: Refining and Aligning Clinical Reasoning with Health Guidelines via Formal Constraints
s192199e400.description: arXiv:2611.32247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Clinical reasoning from incomplete or conflicting patient evidence must account for low-probability but high-risk concerns while remaining grounded in health guidelines. We introduce VerClin, an explainable framework that extracts guideline conditions, exclusions, recommendations, and priorities into executable knowledge and represents patient conversations as scoped cases. A deterministic four-valued reasoner produces traceable guideline matches while preserving uncertainty and enforcing exclusions. Multiple specialty agents then screen matched guidelines for case applicability, and a consultation model synthesizes accepted guidance through specialty recommendations and a sentence-preserving formal-constraint channel. We present accepted gui
s192199e400.summary: VerClin converts health guidelines into executable knowledge and uses a four-valued deterministic reasoner with specialty agents to screen clinical cases.
s192199e400.why: Shows how formal constraints can make LLM clinical reasoning traceable, though the excerpt gives no validation results.

s83ea2a4b47.title: VC-OPD: Learning to See What Matters via Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation
s83ea2a4b47.description: arXiv:2611.32292v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Visual On-Policy Distillation (OPD) commonly uses cropped or zoomed-in image regions as teacher-side privileged information to improve fine-grained perception in small Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs). However, local pixel-level cues are insufficient for complex visual reasoning that requires global structure, spatial relationships, and high-level semantics. We propose Visual Cue On-Policy Self-Distillation (VC-OPD), which extends teacher-side privileged information beyond local image regions to question-conditioned visual cues. Advanced MLLMs generate cues capturing key visual details, structural relationships, and semantic evidence needed to answer each question. A multi-stage quality filtering process selects reliable cues, which a
s83ea2a4b47.summary: Researchers propose VC-OPD, an on-policy self-distillation method that uses question-conditioned visual cues beyond local crops to improve small multimodal models' visual reasoning.
s83ea2a4b47.why: Offers a training technique for small vision-language models that goes beyond zoomed-in crops, relevant to teams deploying compact multimodal models.

sa612d2ebe4.title: Sparse Poison, Strong Hijack: Efficient Trajectory-Level Backdoors in Vision-Language-Action Models with Only 1\% Poisoning
sa612d2ebe4.description: arXiv:2611.32304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models advance robotic manipulation, but their reliance on demonstrations exposes them to backdoor threats. Among these threats, trajectory-level targeted backdoors are particularly challenging and may pose greater safety risks than behavior-disrupting attacks: rather than merely causing task failures or local action deviations, they must sustain closed-loop redirection to complete an attacker-specified multi-step task. To reliably induce such behaviors, existing methods typically rely on high poisoning rates to obtain sufficient target-trajectory supervision. However, high poisoning rates may compromise clean-task performance, whereas low rates leave target-trajectory supervision scarce and backdoor learning vuln
sa612d2ebe4.summary: A paper shows trajectory-level backdoors in vision-language-action robot models can be induced with only about 1% poisoned demonstrations, redirecting multi-step tasks.
sa612d2ebe4.why: Highlights a practical data-poisoning risk for robotic VLA models trained on demonstrations, so teams should audit training data.

sc1bfc65fe5.title: Alpha-Beta Pruning via Monadic Continuations
sc1bfc65fe5.description: arXiv:2611.32320v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Alpha-beta pruning is a fundamental technique in game-playing AI, enabling efficient minimax search by avoiding the exploration of branches that cannot affect the optimal decision. We present a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning based on the combination of the continuation monad and the reader monad. Unlike previous approaches that encode alpha-beta bounds into the types of available moves, our construction records these bounds within monadic outcomes, leaving the move types unchanged. We further show that the ordinary continuation monad suffices to compute not only optimal outcomes but also optimal plays, by extending the outcome type to include the corresponding sequences of moves. This provides an alternative to generalisations of t
sc1bfc65fe5.summary: A paper presents a monadic formulation of alpha-beta pruning combining the continuation and reader monads, keeping bounds in monadic outcomes rather than move types.

sbce2bb47d8.title: FigmaEval: A Benchmark for Evaluating AI Agents in Professional UI Design
sbce2bb47d8.description: arXiv:2611.32321v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in AI agents have enabled autonomous UI design using professional tools such as Figma, yet evaluating their design capabilities remains challenging due to the open-ended nature of design tasks and the absence of unique ground truths. We introduce FigmaEval, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design tasks, comprising 84 tasks and 783 screens derived from real-world Figma design files. FigmaEval adopts a constrained-specification, open-solution paradigm, standardizing task requirements and design resources while allowing agents to independently determine layouts, visual hierarchies, component composition, and visual presentation. To assess design quality beyond reference similarity, we develop 22 expert-grou
sbce2bb47d8.summary: FigmaEval introduces a benchmark of 84 tasks and 783 screens from real Figma files for evaluating AI agents on professional UI design work.
sbce2bb47d8.why: Gives teams a standardized way to assess whether design agents built on tools like Figma are actually useful.

s782fb494a2.title: The Control-Flow Tax: Specialized Decision Routing for LLM Agent Workflows
s782fb494a2.description: arXiv:2611.32365v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An agent can spend almost as much deciding what to do as doing it. In our documentation workflow, control-flow routing accounts for 42.5% of baseline reference cost on the initial task. Lower token prices alone do not solve this control-flow tax: inexpensive general-purpose routers can trigger additional calls to the expensive generator. We evaluate a heterogeneous architecture in which Jev, a specialized System 1 decision model, controls finite actions while Sol generates documents. Across four software tasks, 480 valid runs comprise 470 completions and ten request-limit endpoints. Jev full routing achieves the lowest mean cost and elapsed time on every task, completing all 40 specialist-controlled runs along the shortest trajectory. On the
s782fb494a2.summary: A paper reports that control-flow routing consumed 42.5% of baseline reference cost in a documentation agent workflow, and proposes a specialized routing model separate from the generator.
s782fb494a2.why: Shows agent orchestration overhead can rival task cost, suggesting specialized routers as a way to cut LLM agent spend.

s45d69c097a.title: Can AI Design a Better nnU-Net? A Hypothesis-Driven Architecture Discovery Loop from Failures to Design Rules
s45d69c097a.description: arXiv:2611.32384v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Neural architecture search and LLM-driven evolution often reduce evaluation to a scalar fitness score, discarding failures that could explain why designs succeed or fail. We present a hypothesis-driven architecture discovery loop in which LLM agents diagnose structured error patterns, formulate falsifiable hypotheses, test counterfactual controls under a frozen nnU-Net pipeline, and distill validated mechanisms into executable trigger-to-action rules. Across eight search waves, the loop identifies two principles for 3D medical image segmentation. First, reallocating computation from high-resolution decoders to the mid-encoder preserves thin-anatomy boundaries while reducing cost. Second, support-confined region contrast addresses errors betwe
s45d69c097a.summary: Researchers describe an LLM-agent loop that diagnoses failures, tests hypotheses, and distills rules to improve nnU-Net architectures for 3D medical image segmentation.
s45d69c097a.why: Demonstrates using structured failure analysis rather than scalar fitness scores to guide automated architecture search.

se3d8157833.title: VISE: Verifier-Independent Skill Self-Evolution with Feedback from Tool Implementations
se3d8157833.description: arXiv:2611.32480v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills provide reusable workflows that guide LLM agents in using tools. Refining these workflows requires feedback on missing or incorrect instructions, but task-specific verifiers are not always available. We propose VISE (Verifier-Independent Skill Evolution), a scripts-first approach that uses tool implementations to guide skill revision. It extracts tool capabilities, input requirements, usage conditions, and output formats from source code. Using the task request and execution trace, it compares this information with current workflow instructions to identify missing or conflicting steps. It then recommends specific edits to SKILL.md, linking each change to the relevant implementation and usage conditions. We evaluate VISE as an add
se3d8157833.summary: VISE proposes revising agent skills using tool implementation source code as feedback, without requiring task-specific verifiers.
se3d8157833.why: Offers a way to improve agent workflow instructions when no task verifier exists, reducing evaluation setup effort.

s16b10ad502.title: RecurSciBench: Benchmarking Recursive Self-Improvement in Data-Driven Scientific Research
s16b10ad502.description: arXiv:2611.32508v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents are advancing the automation of data-driven scientific research. Recent advances in recursive self-improvement (RSI) offer the potential for these agents to continuously improve through experience, but evaluating transfer across scientific tasks requires executable, scientifically verifiable tasks and independent assessment of self-improvement gains. We introduce RecurSciBench, a scalable benchmark for evaluating RSI in data-driven scientific research. Its RecurSciPipe framework automatically constructs scientific modeling and data analysis tasks from raw datasets, with execution-based verification and scientific validity checks. RecurSciBench spans four scientific domains, multiple data modalities, and
s16b10ad502.summary: RecurSciBench is a benchmark for evaluating recursive self-improvement of LLM agents on data-driven scientific research tasks.
s16b10ad502.why: Provides a framework to measure whether research agents actually improve across tasks over time.

s0765651ff1.title: A Text-to-SQL Benchmark for Official Statistics
s0765651ff1.description: arXiv:2611.32646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Official statistics are critical datasets for a wide variety of actors, including policymakers and businesses. For providers of official statistics, improving accessibility, governance, and disclosure of their data is of key importance. This can be improved by providing question-answering systems based on text-to-SQL approaches. However, existing text-to-SQL benchmarks do not resemble this setting. Official statistics are published as open-domain catalogs of thousands of wide tables whose columns and values are codes, and whose meaning is recorded in separate metadata rather than in a relational schema. To address this gap, we introduce LOCuST, a text-to-SQL benchmark that pairs over two thousand English and Dutch tables from Statistics Nethe
s0765651ff1.summary: A new text-to-SQL benchmark targets official statistics, where data is published as thousands of wide tables with coded columns and values.
s0765651ff1.why: Reveals that standard text-to-SQL benchmarks miss the coded-schema realities of government data, a gap for enterprise data QA.

s1f25f7f2d1.title: GeoSurge: Geometry-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning for Auditable Liver Resection Planning
s1f25f7f2d1.description: arXiv:2611.32657v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Surgical resection planning centers on generating executable resection surfaces from anatomical evidence and operative constraints. Medical multimodal foundation models enable anatomical understanding, and segmentation models predict resection regions, but neither translates these capabilities into explicitly constrained, executable resection surfaces. We present GeoSurge, an anatomy-grounded framework that combines mask-derived metrics with structure-aware point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable resection surfaces. To make resection geometry learnable and editable, GeoSurge maps actions to parametric geometry through a surface-action grammar. Using this grammar, anatomy-oriented and tumor-centered templates generate candidates, w
s1f25f7f2d1.summary: GeoSurge is a framework combining mask-derived metrics and point-cloud tokens to generate executable, editable liver resection surfaces for surgical planning.

sbcbc6e9ed7.title: Economic World Model
sbcbc6e9ed7.description: arXiv:2611.32663v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can artificial intelligence reproduce the economic dynamics that emerge as households, firms and governments interact and adapt through markets and institutions? To answer this question, we define an economic world model (EWM) as an agent's internal representation of how an economic system works, enabling counterfactual simulation and decision-making under resource constraints. We then propose a general framework for studying EWMs that links three tasks: simulating agent behaviour, learning economic transitions and systematically evaluating the dynamics. As an initial implementation, we learn household policies from microeconomic data and calibrate a structural economic transition model using macroeconomic data, linking individual decisions t
sbcbc6e9ed7.summary: The paper defines an economic world model as an agent's internal representation of economic dynamics and proposes a framework to simulate and evaluate it.

s875a747b9f.title: CAPTA: Identifying LLMs Behind AI Agents
s875a747b9f.description: arXiv:2611.32686v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-based agents access remote services through tools to complete user tasks, often via API calls. In this setting, a remote service may want to identify the backend LLM of an agent to launch model-specific attacks, including prompt injection or selective delivery of manipulated content. However, the service cannot directly query the backend model and must instead collect observable responses through its interactions with the agent, making identification challenging. In this paper, we present Completely Automated Preference Test to tell LLMs Apart (CAPTA), a model identification approach inspired by CAPTCHA (Completely Automated Public Turing test to tell Computers and Humans Apart), which distinguishes humans from auto
s875a747b9f.summary: CAPTA is a method for identifying which backend LLM powers an AI agent by observing its responses through tool-mediated interactions.
s875a747b9f.why: Shows remote services can fingerprint underlying models, relevant to security threat modeling for agent APIs.

sabdc42110e.title: EviCraft: Can Minecraft Agents Find What They Cannot See?
sabdc42110e.description: arXiv:2611.32765v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In Minecraft, a common testbed for embodied agents, semantic tools such as mineBlock pick targets from the simulator's loaded world state without a visibility test, so a buried ore the agent has never seen is one call away, and scores cannot show whether the agent searched. We formalize the missing requirement as evidence closure: every decision of an agent system, including those inside its tools, may depend on the world only through facts for which the agent holds evidence. EviCraft is a runtime and benchmark that enforces closure below the agent and makes the admission rule an experimental variable: a perception-grounded regime (G) admits only what is in line of sight or returned by the agent's own actions, and a loaded-state regime (L) re
sabdc42110e.summary: EviCraft is a Minecraft runtime and benchmark that enforces evidence closure, so agents and their tools can only use world facts the agent has observed.
sabdc42110e.why: Addresses a flaw where agent tools access hidden simulator state, making evaluations misleadingly high.

s590287cd9a.title: RubikSQL-HB: Agentic Text-to-SQL with Knowledge in the Loop
s590287cd9a.description: arXiv:2611.32772v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Database agents need more than schema structure: business meanings, stored values and reference queries supply knowledge that becomes relevant at different points in reasoning. We introduce RubikSQL-HB, which exposes these materials through queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces built on the HeavenBase platform. Its knowledge interface remains available as an agent constructs and investigates an answer. Candidate agents interleave knowledge access with SQL construction and execution; a downstream Judge can reuse the same interfaces to investigate disagreements. A two-stage example interface separates discovering a reference question from expanding its SQL. On a 500-question BIRD Mini-Dev evaluation, the full pipeline reaches 75.2%
s590287cd9a.summary: RubikSQL-HB gives text-to-SQL agents queryable, database-specific knowledge workspaces covering business meanings, stored values and reference queries throughout reasoning.
s590287cd9a.why: Shows how exposing business knowledge interactively during SQL generation may improve database agents over schema-only approaches.

sb97c8d6c37.title: Learning World Models through Contrastive Identification of Actions
sb97c8d6c37.description: arXiv:2611.32776v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Latent world models enable goal-directed planning from offline visual data, but prediction alone does not specify which action-related distinctions their representations should preserve. Inverse dynamics provides auxiliary supervision, yet squared-error action regression rewards additional information only through changes in the conditional action mean. We propose Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), which identifies the executed action among alternatives sampled from a history-conditioned behavior proposal. Comparing actions plausible in the same context targets information supplied by the next latent beyond history. Under exact behavior matching, we show that CIA can reward action information that leaves optimal inverse-regression e
sb97c8d6c37.summary: The paper proposes Contrastive Identification of Actions (CIA), a training objective for latent world models that identifies the executed action among alternatives.
sb97c8d6c37.why: Offers an alternative to squared-error inverse dynamics for learning action-relevant representations in offline visual planning.

s723d67b943.title: Accuracy of Noise Ceiling Estimators for Brain Scores
s723d67b943.description: arXiv:2611.32792v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The internal activations of modern machine learning models align surprisingly well with the activities recorded in real brains. In the last five years, the alignment between encoding models and brain activities, often called brain scores, has steadily increased. Because brain recordings are noisy, there exists an upper bound to the brain scores that any model can achieve. This bound, called the noise ceiling, is crucial for two reasons: it determines whether further improvements in model performance are possible, and it enables meaningful comparisons of brain scores across benchmarks. The field has developed multiple approaches to estimate noise ceilings, but the statistical properties of existing estimators remain poorly understood, leaving
s723d67b943.summary: Researchers examine how accurate noise ceiling estimators are for brain scores, which bound how well models can match neural recordings.
s723d67b943.why: Gives evaluators of brain-alignment benchmarks a clearer sense of whether reported model gains are meaningful or near the measurement limit.

s098e96e6d5.title: Interactive Neural Computers
s098e96e6d5.description: arXiv:2611.32811v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computers and their interfaces are usually treated as fixed, so a person, or increasingly an AI agent, must adapt to whatever the operating system presents. This is limiting when someone needs a different workflow, or an interface suited to hands-free use or a disability. We explore an overlooked alternative. Rather than training an agent to operate an existing computer, we train a generative model to be the computer, predicting each next screen from past screens and the user's mouse and keyboard actions. Treating a desktop as an interactive world model raises problems that natural-video world models largely avoid. Without a camera pose to index memory, the model must remember content that has left the screen without any geometric cues. Arith
s098e96e6d5.summary: Researchers propose training a generative model to act as the computer itself, predicting each next screen from past screens and user inputs.
s098e96e6d5.why: Suggests an alternative to agents operating fixed interfaces, which could enable customizable or accessibility-focused computing workflows.

sf8f4002206.title: Measurement Artifacts in Trustworthiness Evaluations of Quantized Small Language Models
sf8f4002206.description: arXiv:2611.32848v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Evaluations of quantized language models attribute the change in a benchmark score to quantization. We write the measured change as the true change plus a term contributed by the instrument. Instrument error that is the same at every precision can shrink a paired comparison but cannot create or reverse an effect. Error that interacts with quantization can do both, and it is reported as an effect of quantization. We estimate this interaction for four measurement choices in 8 instruction-tuned models below two billion parameters, at float16, LLM.int8() and NF4, on identical items. Measured against labels from two human annotators, the 4-bit rise in harmful compliance is about half to two-thirds of the rise in non-refusal that a corrected key wo
sf8f4002206.summary: A study finds instrument error can interact with quantization to create apparent effects on trustworthiness benchmarks of small quantized language models.
sf8f4002206.why: Teams comparing quantized models on trust or safety benchmarks may be misattributing score changes to quantization rather than to measurement artifacts.

s3d12a70e86.title: Lazy Agents Answer Against Their Own Beliefs: Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs Teaches Them to Act on What They Believe
s3d12a70e86.description: arXiv:2611.32884v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents working on long tasks often commit to an answer before they have enough evidence, a behavior called laziness. In our evaluations, they frequently commit even while their stated belief still names several possible answers. An outcome reward at the end of the episode scores only the final answer, so it cannot teach the agent when to commit, because a lucky guess receives the same reward as an answer backed by evidence. During training, however, the simulator can compute the exact posterior over the answer at every step and tell whether the evidence is already enough. We propose Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Beliefs (RLVB), which rewards the agent for taking further steps while this posterior still allows several answers and f
s3d12a70e86.summary: Researchers propose reinforcement learning with verifiable beliefs to teach AI agents to commit to answers only when evidence supports them.
s3d12a70e86.why: Addresses premature answer commitment in long-horizon agents, a reliability problem for engineers building agentic systems that must decide when to act.

s31f1d742e9.title: InstructReplay: Replaying Assistant Turns to Preserve General Behavior During Factual Fine-Tuning
s31f1d742e9.description: arXiv:2611.32918v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning an instruction-tuned language model on new facts often erodes its general abilities. We find that standard fine-tuning lowers instruction-following, reasoning and coding benchmarks by 35 points on average, and that these losses track a collapse in answer length: fine-tuned models at least halve their responses, and the further a response drifts from the initial model's length, the more often it fails. We propose InstructReplay: the initial model answers a set of general instructions once, and during fine-tuning the model is kept close to the initial model on these answers. Across three model families and two domains, InstructReplay reduces the average decline on five general benchmarks from 28.1 to 2.4 points and keeps answer leng
s31f1d742e9.summary: InstructReplay is proposed to keep instruction-tuned models' general behavior intact during factual fine-tuning by replaying assistant turns.
s31f1d742e9.why: Reports that standard fine-tuning cut instruction-following, reasoning and coding scores by about 35 points on average, a practical risk when updating models with new facts.

sbdc523c87e.title: Reading Decisions Before Spans: Efficient Generative Verification
sbdc523c87e.description: arXiv:2611.32931v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A developer checking an assistant's report may need only an alarm that a claim is unsupported. A generative verifier, however, can continue decoding to quote and classify the errors. We study how much of that output is needed to recover its decision. In a frozen 2B span verifier, the choice between an empty error list and its first object precedes all localization. Native8 stops generation at this branch. The preceding seven syntax tokens are fixed, so Prefill1 supplies them as input and generates only the unrestricted branch token, using the same native instruction. On 2,015 code-agent TEST responses, Prefill1 reduces eager resident service by 84.84% relative to full generation, with released-reference F1 of 83.43 versus 83.41. It saves 31.9
sbdc523c87e.summary: Researchers show a generative verifier's accept-or-error decision can be recovered from early output tokens, avoiding full decoding for claim checking.
sbdc523c87e.why: Could lower latency and compute for teams running generative verifiers that only need a pass or fail alarm on claims.

s63aad5f945.title: ShellBench: What Matters More for AI Agents, Models, or Harness for Everyday Tasks
s63aad5f945.description: arXiv:2611.32946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The use of AI agents among the general public has been increasing exponentially throughout 2026, though it is often hard for users to determine which configuration is most effective for their personal use. To help provide clarity here we introduce ShellBench, 100 day-to-day tasks based on more than 10 million user requests, each set in a realistic workspace with messy files and competing data sources, and graded for both correctness and safety. We evaluate 12 models across 5 agent harnesses at 3 reasoning levels for a total of 53,100 rollouts, 20% of which are on tasks designated for public release. We find that model choice impacts performance more than harness choice, but the three leading models differ by only 1.1 percentage points. GPT-6.
s63aad5f945.summary: ShellBench introduces 100 everyday tasks to compare how models and agent harnesses affect correctness and safety, evaluating 12 models across 5 harnesses.
s63aad5f945.why: Offers evidence on whether model choice or agent harness matters more for everyday agent tasks, informing configuration decisions.

s1cba622c8f.title: Beyond Expected Value: PPO with Distributional Critics for Systematic Conservation Planning
s1cba622c8f.description: arXiv:2611.32948v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Systematic conservation planning must allocate limited protection budgets sequentially under ecological and climatic uncertainty. Static tools cannot adapt as conditions change, and policies optimised only for expected outcomes can fail on the worst-case trajectories climate change makes increasingly likely. CAPTAIN was the first framework to cast this as sequential reinforcement learning, but its gradient-free Evolution Strategies (ES) optimiser lacks per-timestep credit assignment. We replace ES with Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) via a Plackett-Luce solution to CAPTAIN's non-differentiable action space, and replace its scalar critic with an Implicit Quantile Network (IQN) modelling the full return distribution. A matched-granularity co
s1cba622c8f.summary: Researchers replace evolution strategies with PPO and distributional critics in CAPTAIN, a sequential reinforcement learning framework for conservation planning.
s1cba622c8f.why: Shows how distributional critics can address worst-case outcomes in sequential planning under uncertainty, though the application is domain-specific.

s2bcf1650c0.title: LoomKV: Lossless KV Cache Compression from GPU Memory to SSD for LLM Serving
s2bcf1650c0.description: arXiv:2611.32954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) serving engines offload the key/value (KV) cache from GPU memory to host DRAM and SSD so multi-turn and agent requests can reuse prompt prefixes. Capacity then limits service at two levels: external tiers govern prefix reuse before eviction, while the GPU KV pool bounds concurrent long requests, and lossy compression alters KV values and outputs. LoomKV brings lossless KV compression to both external tiers (tier mode) and the GPU pool (pool mode) on an unmodified engine. Using a calibrated per-head two-level 3-bit code over BF16 high bytes (sign and upper seven exponent bits), LoomKV stores BF16 KV at 0.71 of its raw size across nine models and FP8 KV at 0.85-0.87. In tier mode, TileStream writes exact-length record
s2bcf1650c0.summary: LoomKV proposes lossless KV cache compression spanning GPU memory, host DRAM and SSD for LLM serving on unmodified engines.
s2bcf1650c0.why: Lossless KV offloading to SSD could raise concurrency and prefix reuse for long-context and agent serving without changing outputs.

scf518275b3.title: Can LLM Judges Catch Unsafe Clinical Actions? A Fault-Injection Study
scf518275b3.description: arXiv:2611.33012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: As clinical AI agents begin to interact with electronic health records (EHRs), large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to evaluate their actions. But how reliably can these judges recognize clinically dangerous mistakes, especially when an agent appears to have completed its task successfully? We investigate this question using MedAgentBench by introducing controlled clinical errors into verified agent trajectories. The experiments include 416 faulty trajectories, eight error categories, and six open-weight LLM judges. By comparing each faulty trajectory with its correct counterpart, we measure whether judges genuinely recognize errors rather than simply flagging more actions as unsafe. The findings show that access to clinical evi
scf518275b3.summary: A fault-injection study tests whether six open-weight LLM judges can detect unsafe clinical actions in MedAgentBench agent trajectories.
scf518275b3.why: Indicates LLM judges may miss dangerous clinical errors even when agents appear to finish tasks, a caution for evaluating healthcare agents.

s4135a1dd13.title: RecordRoute: Auditing Agent Failures with Localization-Guided Diagnosis
s4135a1dd13.description: arXiv:2611.33022v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Auditing failed agent executions requires identifying the responsible actor, the earliest decisive step, and the error mode. Representative supervised methods either focus on step localization or predict multiple attribution targets from shared trajectory representations. These methods do not use the localization result to select the text for mode diagnosis. To address this limitation, we propose RecordRoute, which couples comparative localization with local diagnosis. Specifically, it represents each record with word and character features and learns to rank records through comparisons within each trajectory. The selected record supplies the actor and step, while its text and metadata drive mode prediction. On controlled-injection Who&When P
s4135a1dd13.summary: RecordRoute proposes couples localization with diagnosis to audit failed agent executions, identifying the responsible actor, decisive step and error mode.
s4135a1dd13.why: Offers a method for post-hoc debugging of failed agent runs, which matters for teams operating multi-step agents in production.

s095a984fa4.title: Hybrid AI for AI-Native RAN Control: A Functional Perspective
s095a984fa4.description: arXiv:2611.33035v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI-native radio access network (RAN) control involves interdependent decisions across network entities, protocol layers, and timescales. Understanding how AI and conventional methods can jointly support these decisions requires a common basis for comparing their functional roles. This survey introduces a technique-agnostic taxonomy of RAN decision-making organized around four complementary capabilities: Representation and Reasoning, Prediction and Simulation, Adaptive Control, and Decision Synthesis. These capabilities are defined by their roles in the control process, independently of the techniques used to implement them. Through this perspective, we examine representative AI and model-based approaches, including foundation models, world mo
s095a984fa4.summary: A survey proposes a technique-agnostic taxonomy of AI-native radio access network control, covering representation, prediction, adaptive control and decision synthesis.
s095a984fa4.why: Provides a common framework for telecom engineers weighing how AI and conventional methods should divide RAN decision-making.

s990a11374d.title: Auditing the Judge: Human-Derived Bias Discovery, Quantification, and Mitigation in LLM Judges
s990a11374d.description: arXiv:2611.33065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as automated evaluators in evaluation and training pipelines, their judgements are often affected by systematic biases that conflict with human preferences. Although prior work has identified various biases and proposed methods for detecting and mitigating them, less attention has been paid to using human preferences to inform bias identification and mitigation. Moreover, these approaches rely heavily on pre-discovered bias lists, overlook bias strength, and depend on costly interventions. In this work, we propose HUB-J, an integrated framework based on human-derived bias factors that detects, quantifies, and mitigates biases in LLM-as-a-Judge systems. Our approach leverages human-L
s990a11374d.summary: Researchers propose using human preferences to discover, quantify and mitigate systematic biases in LLM judges used as automated evaluators.
s990a11374d.why: Teams relying on LLM-as-judge pipelines may get more reliable evaluations by auditing judge bias against human preferences.

sb3450c9677.title: Uncertainty-Aware Candidate Generation for Entity Linking in Cyber Threat Intelligence
sb3450c9677.description: arXiv:2611.33086v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Entity Resolution (ER) pipelines often collapse ambiguity into early hard decisions: upstream Named Entity Recognition (NER) selects a single span and type, and downstream Entity Linking (EL) treats that choice as ground truth. This discards valuable information about the ambiguity of the underlying data (e.g., span boundary disagreement and type confusion), leading to brittle systems that fail unpredictably when faced with uncertainty in inputs. Therefore, this work presents a proof-of-concept for uncertainty-aware ER that treats uncertainty as native data that should be preserved and exploited throughout ER pipelines. We (i) capture uncertainty signals in the NER stage and (ii) leverage these signals into the EL stage to improve candidate r
sb3450c9677.summary: A proof-of-concept keeps uncertainty in named entity recognition and passes candidate sets to entity linking instead of single hard decisions, for cyber threat intelligence.
sb3450c9677.why: Could make threat-intelligence entity pipelines more robust by avoiding brittle early commitments under ambiguous inputs.

s3aa248a7c2.title: Delegent: A Multi-Agent Harness That Reduces Cost without Sacrificing Performance
s3aa248a7c2.description: arXiv:2611.33098v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agents built on frontier language models are expensive. At every step, the frontier model re-reads its entire context and executes every subtask regardless of its difficulty. This paper explores the simple thesis that much of this cost can be removed by delegating easy subtasks to a small language model, or SLM, that runs on hardware one already owns. To test it, we build Delegent, a simple and effective agent harness built on Claude Code, in which the frontier model stays in charge of every task but hands focused subtasks, such as investigating code, running tests, and searching a corpus, to SLM subagents. Existing approaches such as cascades and model routers usually choose which model executes the entire task, whereas in Delegent, the fron
s3aa248a7c2.summary: Delegent is a multi-agent harness built on Claude Code that delegates easy subtasks to a small local language model while the frontier model stays in charge.
s3aa248a7c2.why: Suggests cutting frontier-model agent costs by offloading simple subtasks to owned hardware, though results depend on the paper's evaluation.

s69319dd648.title: Temporal Conditioning for Human Behavioral Cloning in Chess
s69319dd648.description: arXiv:2611.33106v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Behavioral cloning models in chess typically predict human moves from board states while ignoring temporal inputs such as the remaining clock. However, time pressure is a major determinant of human decision-making quality, and temporal state is a missing dimension of human behavioral modeling. This paper introduces a time-aware transformer that extends a Chessformer-style architecture with learned temporal conditioning tokens encoding player clock state, time control, and recent tempo, together with behavioral heads for thinking time and resignation. The model is trained on large-scale online chess data and evaluated against time-agnostic baselines and the state of the art. Results show that temporal conditioning yields modest overall accurac
s69319dd648.summary: Researchers introduced a time-aware transformer for chess behavioral cloning that conditions on clock state, time control, and tempo to predict human moves, thinking time, and resignation.
s69319dd648.why: Shows that temporal context such as time pressure can be modeled explicitly to better capture human decision-making quality.

scf1b67acee.title: MetaFORGE: A Meta-Learning Framework for Harness Optimization in Automated Code Generation for Parallel Computing
scf1b67acee.description: arXiv:2611.33119v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate parallel programs, but their correctness and performance depend strongly on the instructions that guide generation. We present \textsc{MetaFORGE}, an execution-grounded meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes persistent natural-language skill specifications for MPI C code generation. \textsc{MetaFORGE} combines correctness testing, compiler diagnostics, static-analysis findings, runtime measurements, and rank-level load-imbalance profiles into a scalar reward that drives textual-gradient refinement, while an external memory distills and retrieves reward-supported optimization knowledge across runs. Across six MPI tasks and three workload sizes, \textsc{MetaFORGE} improves static-analysis qu
scf1b67acee.summary: MetaFORGE is a meta-learning framework that iteratively optimizes natural-language skill specifications to improve LLM generation of MPI C parallel code, using test, compiler, and runtime feedback.
scf1b67acee.why: Offers a feedback-driven way to improve LLM-generated parallel code by tuning instructions against correctness and performance signals.

sd18c130d97.title: SoundWeaver: Compositional Warm-Starting for Text-to-Audio Diffusion Serving
sd18c130d97.description: arXiv:2603.07865v2 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-audio (T2A) diffusion models generate high-quality audio but require tens of neural function evaluations (NFEs), resulting in substantial inference latency. Existing acceleration methods primarily optimize each generation trajectory independently, even when reusable acoustic structure exists in prior examples. We introduce SoundWeaver, the first training-free framework for compositional cross example acoustic reuse. Rather than generating from pure noise, SoundWeaver constructs a prompt-conditioned acoustic prior from segments distributed across cached audios and warm-starts diffusion from an intermediate noise level. We introduce an Acoustic Composition Graph (ACG), which uses neural codec representations and segment-level identifi
sd18c130d97.summary: SoundWeaver is a training-free framework that speeds text-to-audio diffusion by building a prompt-conditioned acoustic prior from reusable segments of prior examples instead of starting from pure noise.
sd18c130d97.why: A training-free acceleration technique could cut inference latency and serving cost for text-to-audio diffusion systems.

s0ade816bf5.title: When Can a Rewiring Control Test LLM Weight Readers? C2 and an Eligibility Protocol
s0ade816bf5.description: arXiv:2611.29120v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can predict the outputs of small neural networks from raw weights, but success could reflect recognition of weight-space regularities (fingerprints) rather than computation, and function-preserving controls cannot tell these apart. We propose C2, a counterfactual that permutes the columns of a network's final linear readout: every other parameter, and the readout's singular values, norms and entry multiset, are unchanged, and the function can change in an exactly recomputable way; we verify that each evaluated permutation does. C2 separates fingerprinting from computation only under three conditions, which we state as an eligibility protocol: a strategy restricted to C2-invariant summaries must already predict the targ
s0ade816bf5.summary: The paper proposes C2, a counterfactual control that permutes a network's final linear readout to test whether LLMs predict network outputs from computation or from weight-space fingerprints.
s0ade816bf5.why: Clarifies how to validate claims that LLMs can read computation from raw model weights, avoiding confounds from weight regularities.

s701f15a963.title: InletScope: Multiscale pressure-based inlet unstart monitoring under changing sensor configurations
s701f15a963.description: arXiv:2611.31246v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Supersonic inlets capture and compress air for aeroengines, and unstart can disrupt the air supply and compromise propulsion-system stability. Pressure-based monitoring must accommodate flow responses that vary with operating condition and measurement location. InletScope combines shared multiscale pressure encoding, learned scale fusion and sensor-probability averaging, allowing measurement sets to change without retraining. Separate models evaluate unstart detection and new-onset prediction within a 0.5-s future interval. Seven Mach-2.9 runs, each with one annotated event, cover downstream throttling, throat regulation and splitter adjustment; three are held out with fixed weights and source-derived settings. Across three training seeds,
s701f15a963.summary: InletScope is a multiscale pressure-based monitoring model for supersonic aeroengine inlets that detects unstart and predicts onset within 0.5 seconds, handling changing sensor configurations without retraining.

sbb6775e834.title: Actionwave: A Systematic Benchmark for Waveform-Centric Clinical Prediction Across Care Scenarios
sbb6775e834.description: arXiv:2611.31249v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continuous bedside waveforms record rapid physiological changes that can inform clinical decisions. Existing benchmarks examine selected prediction conditions, but it remains unclear how model advantages depend on signal duration, warning time, and available inputs across care settings. We introduce Actionwave, a benchmark for waveform-centric clinical prediction across intensive-care, operating-room, and emergency-department settings. Actionwave uses a common decision-time prediction interface and groups clinically grounded tasks by what is inferred and when. It varies conditions relevant to clinical use, including the warning required before an intervention. We compare diverse architectures and pretrained biosignal encoders under specifie
sbb6775e834.summary: Actionwave is a benchmark for waveform-centric clinical prediction across intensive-care, operating-room, and emergency-department settings, testing how performance depends on signal duration, warning time, and inputs.
sbb6775e834.why: Provides a standardized benchmark for comparing clinical waveform models across care settings before deployment decisions.

sb68e21f361.title: Validation Bias in Large Language Model Responses to Cancer Treatment Queries: A Factorial Cross-Sectional Study
sb68e21f361.description: arXiv:2611.31251v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) chatbots are increasingly used by patients seeking cancer information, but their safety when users present evidence-misaligned beliefs about treatment remains uncharacterized. We hypothesized that LLMs exhibit validation bias, affirming rather than correcting such beliefs, and evaluated this with a 2x2x2 factorial design crossing conversation format (single-turn vs multi-turn), treatment type (evidence-based vs alternative), and query valence (positive vs negative). Framing was evidence-aligned (supporting evidence-based treatments or questioning alternative therapies) or evidence-misaligned (promoting alternative treatments or questioning evidence-based therapies). We analyzed 1,272 conversations (6,360 interacti
sb68e21f361.summary: A factorial study finds that LLM chatbots may validate patients' evidence-misaligned beliefs about cancer treatment rather than correcting them, based on tests across conversation format, treatment type, and query valence.
sb68e21f361.why: Highlights a safety risk for health-facing LLM products, where models may affirm misleading treatment beliefs instead of correcting them.

sc154e225fd.title: DAGGER: Deployment-Free Quality Estimation for Generative AI Workflows
sc154e225fd.description: arXiv:2611.31252v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Estimating the quality of generative AI workflows is challenging because these workflows comprise multiple stages, and errors can propagate across them, making end-to-end performance depend not only on the accuracy of individual models but also on how their outputs affect downstream stages. Each stage can use one of many candidate models. Estimating end-to-end workflow quality by deploying and evaluating every resulting model configuration is therefore prohibitively expensive. As a result, existing approaches face a tradeoff between estimation cost and accuracy: inexpensive methods often produce unreliable quality estimates, while accurate methods require deploying and evaluating many workflow configurations. In this paper, we introduce DAG
sc154e225fd.summary: DAGGER proposes a deployment-free method to estimate end-to-end quality of multi-stage generative AI workflows, avoiding the cost of deploying and evaluating every candidate model configuration.
sc154e225fd.why: Could reduce the cost of choosing model configurations across multi-stage AI pipelines without exhaustive deployment testing.

s8f935cc372.title: Instantiation of Human Values in Image Generation
s8f935cc372.description: arXiv:2611.31253v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-image (T2I) models are increasingly embedded in everyday visual culture, yet little is known about how they translate abstract human values into visual scenes. We address this gap by introducing a framework, grounded in Schwartz's theory of basic human values, for studying value instantiation: the process by which ideals such as success, care, or freedom are visually realized. Using person-centered prompts from 70 positive and negative value items, we generate 28,000 images across four state-of-the-art T2I models. We identify visual prototypes, recurring combinations of subjects, actions, and settings, and use them to quantify how narrowly models instantiate these values and how this breadth compares with human descriptions of the s
s8f935cc372.summary: Researchers generated 28,000 images from four text-to-image models using value-laden prompts grounded in Schwartz's human values theory to study how abstract values are visually depicted.

sdc789263b5.title: The Date You Didn't Set: The System-Prompt Date as a Hidden Variable in LLM Evaluation
sdc789263b5.description: arXiv:2611.31254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The system prompt of many instruction-tuned models carries a date, usually today's, filled in automatically for conversational and agentic requests alike, so an unchanged evaluation can send a different prompt each day. In this paper, we explore how much this hidden input changes evaluation outcomes. Across six instruction-tuned models and four benchmarks, with prompts, decoding, and configuration fixed, every model is affected: two plausible dates (2024--2026) switch a median $6.6\%$ of test items between correct and incorrect. Even rerunning the evaluation one day later flips about as many items as changing the batch size, although nothing in the setup was changed. In addition, using a grammar-constrained variant of Greedy Coordinate Grad
sdc789263b5.summary: The paper shows that the date automatically inserted into system prompts can change LLM evaluation results, flipping a median 6.6% of test items between correct and incorrect across six models.
sdc789263b5.why: Evaluation pipelines that auto-insert dates may produce unstable results, so teams should pin or record that hidden input.

s94c7821f54.title: INCLUDE-2.0: Disentangling Knowledge Gaps in Multilingual LLM Evaluation
s94c7821f54.description: arXiv:2611.31255v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current multilingual benchmarks cover only a fraction of the languages represented in modern pretraining corpora and often conflate language proficiency with the ability to answer questions grounded in specific regions and communities. We introduce INCLUDE-2.0, a large-scale benchmark for region-aware multilingual factual evaluation, which covers 91 languages from 86 countries (127 total language--country pairs), comprising over 220K curated samples drawn from native regional sources. Unlike existing benchmarks that often treat language as a proxy for region, IINCLUDE-2.0 distinguishes between questions whose answers are independent of context, vary by country, concern widely documented facts about a place, or depend on knowledge primarily
s94c7821f54.summary: INCLUDE-2.0 is a multilingual benchmark covering 91 languages from 86 countries with over 220K samples, designed to separate language proficiency from region-specific factual knowledge.
s94c7821f54.why: Gives teams a region-aware benchmark to distinguish language ability from local knowledge gaps in multilingual models.

s46d2690623.title: Directly Maximizing On-policy Expected Accepted Length for Speculative Decoding
s46d2690623.description: arXiv:2611.31256v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model inference by using a lightweight draft model to propose tokens for verification by a target model. Draft training commonly optimizes token-level distribution alignment, but this does not directly optimize the length of the accepted prefix: once a draft token is rejected, all subsequent draft tokens are discarded. We propose FreDraft, an on-policy training method that directly maximizes the expected accepted length of drafts sampled from the current draft model. This objective accounts for first-rejection truncation and induces prefix-aware credit assignment, weighting each token by its contribution to the acceptance of the current and subsequent tokens. To optimize the objective efficien
s46d2690623.summary: FreDraft is an on-policy training method for speculative decoding drafts that directly maximizes the expected accepted length rather than token-level distribution alignment.
s46d2690623.why: Targeting accepted length directly could yield faster LLM inference from speculative decoding without changing the target model.

se89644cc89.title: RECAP: Training Long-horizon LLM Agents with Context Compaction
se89644cc89.description: arXiv:2611.31258v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Context compaction enables large language model agents to tackle long-horizon tasks within limited context budgets by replacing interaction histories with compressed summaries. However, learning effective compaction jointly with the agent policy remains challenging, as summaries affect task success over many subsequent interactions. We introduce RECAP, a reinforcement learning (RL) framework based on the principle that a summary should preserve the behavior induced by the original interaction history. We formalize this principle with a behavior distortion objective that measures the divergence between the agent's subsequent behavior under compressed and original contexts. We show that the gradient of the distortion objective decomposes into
se89644cc89.summary: RECAP is a reinforcement learning framework that trains LLM agents to compress long interaction histories into summaries that preserve the behavior induced by the original history.
se89644cc89.why: Addresses how long-horizon agents can stay within context limits while keeping task performance through learned context compaction.

sdcc2dbedb3.title: RecipeADQA: A User-aware Question-Answering Dataset for Multi-Constraint Recipe Recommendation
sdcc2dbedb3.description: arXiv:2611.31259v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Question-answering recipe recommendation tasks lack datasets with ground-truth labels. Existing methods often generate datasets from simple combinations of ingredient or tag constraints, leading to unnatural expressions and unreasonable constraints that are hard to reflect users' real preferences. This paper proposes a construction method for a benchmark-style QA dataset for natural-language recipe recommendation. Driven by real user behavior, our method integrates external user query and review data to extract fine-grained preference signals by LLMs and maps them onto a knowledge-graph-based tag schema, thereby constructing QA data consisting of preference and ingredient constraints. Besides, a greedy strategy for constraint selection is a
sdcc2dbedb3.summary: RecipeADQA is a question-answering dataset for multi-constraint recipe recommendation, built from real user queries and reviews to capture natural preference signals.

sd8a13dd079.title: Capability and Interpretability of Transformers on Multi-task Recurrence
sd8a13dd079.description: arXiv:2611.31260v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Transformers are widely used in various language tasks, with limited understanding of their internal mechanisms. Motivated by the recurrent structure of many linguistic rules, we study the capability and interpretability of Transformers through a controlled family of linear recurrence tasks over finite cyclic groups. These tasks range from executing a single fixed rule to identifying a latent rule from context and switching between explicitly specified rules, with and without input masking. Through extensive experiments across different configurations, we find that switching specified rules is simpler than identifying latent rules for Transformers in general. We also identify how several key factors affect the generalization capability of T
sd8a13dd079.summary: The paper studies capability and interpretability of transformers on controlled linear recurrence tasks over cyclic groups, ranging from a single fixed rule to latent rule identification and rule switching.
sd8a13dd079.why: Provides controlled insight into how transformers internally represent recurrent rules, which may inform interpretability work.

s3fb9ed757d.title: Does Item Response Theory Generalize Across Languages? Evidence from Cross-Lingual LLM Benchmarks
s3fb9ed757d.description: arXiv:2611.31261v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The application of Item Response Theory (IRT) for data selection in benchmarks has mostly been limited to monolingual settings. In this work, we ask: how does IRT generalize when the same benchmark is translated across languages? We conduct experiments on Multilingual GSM and Global MMLU, covering over 100 language models and 11 languages. Fitting 1PL, 2PL, and 3PL IRT models per language, we assess cross-lingual consistency of parameters and whether IRT-filtered subsets preserve model rankings across languages: item difficulty emerges as the most stable parameter followed by guessing and then discrimination. A differential item analysis also shows that lack of stability can be tracked to specific items shifting under translation across lan
s3fb9ed757d.summary: Researchers test whether Item Response Theory data selection for benchmarks holds across languages, using translated Multilingual GSM and Global MMLU with 100+ models and 11 languages.
s3fb9ed757d.why: Suggests IRT-filtered benchmark subsets may not transfer cleanly across languages, which matters when building multilingual evaluation suites.

s1261a2962d.title: RegioZH: Unveiling Comprehension Disparities across Regional Chinese Varieties in LLMs
s1261a2962d.description: arXiv:2611.31262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Current evaluations often treat Chinese varieties as monolithic, obscuring failures for regional users. We introduce RegioZH, a 2,607-item multiple-choice benchmark for regional lexical reasoning across Mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Malaysia. Built by region-specific annotators and expert-validated, it targets localized idioms, slang, code-mixing, politeness conventions, and sociocultural expressions. Zero-shot results on eleven LLMs show large disparities, including a 29.4-point average accuracy gap between Taiwan and Singapore. Persona and structured chain-of-thought prompts for five models yield selective gains, suggesting that some errors stem from retrieval or framing rather than only missing knowledge. Representati
s1261a2962d.summary: RegioZH is a 2,607-item benchmark testing LLMs on regional Chinese varieties from five regions; eleven models show a 29.4-point average accuracy gap between Taiwan and Singapore.
s1261a2962d.why: Shows that treating Chinese as one language hides large performance gaps for regional users, relevant to localization and evaluation.

s0b5ba7eab0.title: Evaluating Large Language Models on Iranian Doctoral Entrance Exams in Electrical and Computer Engineering
s0b5ba7eab0.description: arXiv:2611.31263v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We evaluate four large language models (LLMs) on multiple-choice questions from the 2024 and 2025 Iranian national Ph.D. entrance examinations in Electrical Engineering (EE) and Computer Engineering (CE). Of the 440 questions in the four official booklets, 7 were excluded because the question statement or its figure was ambiguous, leaving 433 questions (186 EE, 247 CE), of which 171 (39.5\%) depend on a figure. Each question was presented in the original Persian and in an English translation, giving 3,464 scored responses. GPT-5, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Grok 4 were queried zero-shot, with reasoning enabled, through a single commercial web interface (Perplexity) in October 2025, using an automated script. Because every model an
s0b5ba7eab0.summary: Four LLMs were evaluated on 433 Iranian doctoral entrance exam questions in electrical and computer engineering, in both Persian and English, with figure-dependent items included.
s0b5ba7eab0.why: Gives a domain-specific reference point for LLM performance on technical engineering exams, though the text offers limited detail on results.

s2e6b4e2c7b.title: How Persona Conditioning Changes Open-Ended Task Execution: A Paired Evaluation of Behavioral Gains and Reliability Costs
s2e6b4e2c7b.description: arXiv:2611.31264v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are often prompted with role- or persona-based instructions, yet persona conditioning has mainly been evaluated through character fidelity or aggregate benchmark accuracy. We study persona conditioning as a task-execution steering signal that changes how models interpret, structure, and sustain responses. Using paired instances derived from real user role-play logs and expanded into simulated multi-turn continuations, we compare with-persona and no-persona conditions while fixing task content, constraints, user simulation, and evaluation criteria. Across eight models, persona conditioning improves expert content depth and procedural fidelity, and these gains survive length control. At the same time, it lowers st
s2e6b4e2c7b.summary: A paired study finds persona prompts change how LLMs execute open-ended tasks in multi-turn role-play, measuring behavioral gains alongside reliability costs.
s2e6b4e2c7b.why: Indicates persona prompting can alter task behavior and reliability beyond character fidelity, which affects prompt design decisions.

sa185f31062.title: SD-Cache: Learnable Memory Consolidation with State-Guided Dynamic Caching
sa185f31062.description: arXiv:2611.31265v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as persistent services that must reason over large volumes of external knowledge. Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) grounds model responses in relevant documents, but the retrieved content must still be encoded and stored in the key-value (KV) cache. As this content accumulates, the cache grows linearly, increasing memory consumption and inference cost. Existing memory-compression methods address this problem either by retaining a subset of cached states or by learning context compressors that map documents to compact latent representations. Despite these advances, consolidating information under tight memory budgets while preserving its usefulness for future queries remains challeng
sa185f31062.summary: SD-Cache proposes learnable memory consolidation with state-guided dynamic caching to limit KV cache growth from retrieved content in RAG systems.
sa185f31062.why: Addresses linear KV cache growth in persistent RAG services, a direct cost and memory concern for inference infrastructure.

sffe765e3a7.title: AhaPro: A Process-level Rebus benchmark for probing Aha moments in LLM reasoning
sffe765e3a7.description: arXiv:2611.31268v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing research on Aha moments in large language models has largely focused on reflective expressions or final revision outcomes, leaving their role in the visible reasoning process insufficiently characterized. Rebus puzzles encode answers through character forms, spatial arrangements, and homophony. Reinterpreting key details may trigger Aha moments and shifts in the reasoning process and candidate answers. We introduce AhaPro, a process-level benchmark that uses rebus puzzles to examine how models reorganize evidence and revise answers through Aha moments. The framework represents CoT as sequences of candidate answers, evidence, and verification states, using hierarchical metrics to assess conflict detection, state improvement, and sub
sffe765e3a7.summary: AhaPro is a process-level benchmark using rebus puzzles to study how LLMs reorganize evidence and revise answers during visible reasoning, the so-called Aha moments.
sffe765e3a7.why: Offers a way to probe reasoning-trace behavior beyond final answers, useful for evaluating reasoning models.

sb5d3fc5fd8.title: Reliability of Language-Model Judges for Quantitative Scientific Question Answering: Evidence from Perovskite Photovoltaics
sb5d3fc5fd8.description: arXiv:2611.31269v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Evaluating retrieval-augmented language models increasingly relies on automated model judges, yet their reliability on quantitative scientific synthesis remains largely unmeasured. Here, we evaluate automated grading on a quantitative benchmark for perovskite photovoltaics, where all 755 ground-truth answers are deterministically computed from 45,441 experimental device records. We evaluate a frontier judge (Claude Opus 5.5) alongside two local open-weight judges (Qwen3-14B and Qwen3-8B) across 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures under three regimes: reference-augmented (with the computed key), evidence-augmented (with retrieved passages and query logs), and unassisted (question and answer alone). Equipped with the refe
sb5d3fc5fd8.summary: Evaluation of LLM judges on 755 perovskite photovoltaic questions, with 4,530 free-text answers from six retrieval architectures, finds reliability on quantitative science synthesis is largely unmeasured.
sb5d3fc5fd8.why: Highlights that LLM-as-judge grading may be unreliable for quantitative answers, a caution for teams relying on automated evaluation.

s3f14709ebd.title: Agentic Optimization: LLM Agents Select and Configure Algorithms for Engineering Design
s3f14709ebd.description: arXiv:2611.31275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Engineers solving new multi-objective design problems commonly commit to a multi-objective evolutionary algorithm (MOEA) before seeing a result. The best MOEA differs from benchmark to benchmark. We propose agentic optimization, placing an LLM agent outside the optimization loop, where it reads a natural-language problem description to configure and launch algorithms, drawing on parametric knowledge rather than on a performance history that a novel problem lacks. We compare five LLMs in a fixed harness on four engineering benchmarks and a real-world SARS-CoV-2 molecular docking task, using hypervolume (HV) and IGD+ with multiple comparison-corrected tests. Three models (GPT, DeepSeek, Qwen) dominate every baseline on combined HV and IGD+, a
s3f14709ebd.summary: The paper proposes agentic optimization, where an LLM agent reads a problem description to select and configure multi-objective evolutionary algorithms, comparing five LLMs on engineering benchmarks.
s3f14709ebd.why: Points to LLM agents as a way to pick optimization algorithms for new design problems without performance history.

s916764a505.title: LLM Genetic Feature Engineering
s916764a505.description: arXiv:2611.31277v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Feature Engineering is the (traditionally manual) process of constructing derived variables from an existing dataset by combining, transforming, or otherwise manipulating the original data fields to reduce statistical noise and extract meaningful, domain-specific quantities of interest from the raw dataset. Recent work demonstrates promising progress toward the au tomation of this process through the integration of large language models (LLMs) and various metaheuristics to guide the search for useful features. We build on this approach by introducing a novel genetic algorithm that implements selection, crossover, and mutation at the individual feature level, rather than at the level of the entire engineered feature set. In doing so, we enab
s916764a505.summary: The paper builds on LLM-guided metaheuristic feature engineering, introducing a genetic approach to automate constructing derived variables from datasets.

scb02079583.title: The Industrialization of Noise: Why Automated Proof-Solving is the Same Old Dead End
scb02079583.description: arXiv:2611.31286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nearly fifty years ago, DeMillo, Lipton, and Perlis argued that mathematical proofs are not static, isolated structures of formal logic, but the products of a vibrant, evolving social process of human critique, internalization, and shared intuition. In October 2026, OpenAI challenged this thesis by releasing a massive repository of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts, claiming full or partial solutions to 372 longstanding open problems. This paper examines the immediate crisis through the lens of the original DLP framework. We argue that the sudden, automated overproduction of dense, unreadable proofs represents an industrial pollution of the mathematical ecosystem. By examining the three fatal structural pillars of this automated approa
scb02079583.summary: A paper argues that OpenAI's release of 722 automated mathematical manuscripts claiming solutions to 372 open problems repeats a failed approach to proof, drawing on the DeMillo-Lipton-Perlis framework.
scb02079583.why: Frames debate over the value of automated proof generation, which is relevant to how engineers assess AI-generated research claims.

s18c627a04a.title: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL: Polarization-Keyed Examination Papers and Mandatory Issued Eyewear that Displace AI Glasses and Extend Universal Design
s18c627a04a.description: arXiv:2611.31299v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-equipped AI glasses turn an examination page into a query for a remote vision-language model. Device detection targets possession, and our companion work SEOYUN targets the model. PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL instead changes who owns the eyewear. Every candidate wears authority-issued glasses for the whole session, and the question paper is printed so that it can be read only through them. As in cinema stereoscopy, a patterned laminate encodes the text in the handedness of circular polarization rather than in brightness. The page looks uniformly grey to the naked eye and to unfiltered cameras, and the issued circular analyzer reveals the text. Compulsory issued eyewear turns the smart-glasses form factor against itself. The face position is o
s18c627a04a.summary: PEACE-TEST-PROTOCOL proposes polarization-encoded exam papers readable only through authority-issued glasses to prevent AI glasses from reading test questions.

s68ed86a3ed.title: Differential evolution with perturbation for continuous function optimization
s68ed86a3ed.description: arXiv:2611.31305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper presents differential evolution with perturbation (DEP) for continuous function optimization. Differential evolution is a simple and efficient algorithm. Perturbation is the phenomenon that the motion by the contribution of the main force is disturbed by the influence subsidiary power. In order to show the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm, we compare it to existing algorithms by CEC2017 datasets.
s68ed86a3ed.summary: The paper presents differential evolution with perturbation (DEP) for continuous function optimization and compares it to existing algorithms on CEC2017 datasets.

s73b1249ea6.title: Set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem
s73b1249ea6.description: arXiv:2611.31306v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper describes a novel algorithm of set-based comprehensive learning and particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problem. Our algorithm is an approach of searching for the best position in a set by referring to the current position when updating the solution. In order to show the validity of our algorithm, we examine numerical experiments compared to existing algorithms.
s73b1249ea6.summary: The paper introduces a set-based comprehensive learning particle swarm optimization with memory for discrete optimization problems, validated through numerical experiments.

sea3e031478.title: When Successful Collaboration Becomes an Attack Surface: Insider Memory Poisoning in Multi-Agent Systems
sea3e031478.description: arXiv:2611.31307v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent Multi-Agent Systems (MAS) increasingly use shared memory to store and reuse successful collaboration records, enabling teams to improve across tasks. However, this memory introduces a new attack surface for malicious insiders. Unlike existing insider attacks that inject misleading information directly into the current collaboration, misinformation stored in shared memory can later appear as successful team experience and gain greater credibility and influence. We propose MIMPA (Multi-Agent Insider Memory Poisoning Attack), which exploits this vulnerability using only normal participation privileges, without direct memory access. During an earlier task, the malicious agent embeds a target-specific payload while helping the team answer
sea3e031478.summary: MIMPA is proposed as an attack in which malicious insiders poison shared memory of successful collaboration records in multi-agent systems, so false information appears as trusted team experience.
sea3e031478.why: Identifies shared agent memory as a new attack surface that engineers building multi-agent systems need to defend against.

s6477f479ad.title: Evolutionary AI Control: Population-Level Safety Under Reproduction, Heredity, and Selection
