s6477f479ad.description: arXiv:2611.31312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: An AI agent can satisfy every individual safety check and still give rise to a population that violates a collective safety limit. This risk arises in open multi-agent systems, where agents copy themselves, modify their successors, and change system membership during a run. Selection then shifts the population toward traits outside the developers' optimization targets. We prove conditions under which safety guarantees persist through reproduction, inheritance, and selection, and we characterize how they fail. Four counterexamples illustrate these failures. Unauthorized copies, which violate a specified reproductive restriction, can each leave fewer than one successor on average while their expected number grows without bound under continued
s6477f479ad.summary: The paper proves conditions under which population-level safety guarantees persist through agent reproduction, inheritance, and selection, and shows four counterexamples where they fail.
s6477f479ad.why: Shows individually safe agents can yield unsafe populations in open multi-agent systems, a concern for long-running self-replicating agent designs.

s179b6c036f.title: Scoring Recovery-Time Agent Security: Proposals, Effects, and Retry Instructions
s179b6c036f.description: arXiv:2611.31318v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A timed-out tool write may be absent, committed, or still in flight. Evaluating an agent only on whether its goal exists can hide harmful recovery actions: auditing 12 supplied traces changes apparent completion from 10/12 to 8/12. We introduce an executable evaluation that separately records tool proposals, runtime decisions, and committed effects. In 3,456 model episodes, the original task wording produces only 39/576 valid recoveries when the initial write is absent; a combined clarification produces 576/576. A further 1,584 episodes test stronger attacks and separate the effect definition from the recovery recipe with three rollouts per absent-state cell. Definition alone yields 276/288 valid recoveries; recipe alone yields 288/288. For
s179b6c036f.summary: Researchers propose an executable evaluation separating tool proposals, runtime decisions, and committed effects, showing timed-out agent writes can hide harmful recovery actions.
s179b6c036f.why: Goal-existence checks can overstate agent success; engineers should audit committed side effects and retry behavior after timeouts.

s037d676abd.title: Conformalized Tree-Based Gradient Ensembles for Out-of-Distribution Detection and Plausible Recourse
s037d676abd.description: arXiv:2611.31319v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Counterfactual recourse provides actionable feature adjustments that reverse unfavourable predictions made by automated decision models. However, when recourse search optimizes purely against classifier confidence or narrow proxy scores over gradient-boosted decision trees (GBDT), search procedures can exploit boundary artifacts and low-density regions---an instance of Goodhart's law---yielding out-of-distribution (OOD) recommendations that appear favourable nominally while lacking manifold plausibility. In this paper, we study conformalized OOD gating coupled with actionability-constrained counterfactual search across two tabular benchmarks: Adult and Give Me Some Credit (GMSC). Calibrating finite-sample anomaly gates (gate_IF, gate_LOF, a
s037d676abd.summary: Researchers study conformalized tree-based gradient ensembles to detect out-of-distribution counterfactual recourse suggestions that exploit boundary artifacts.
s037d676abd.why: Recourse search optimizing classifier confidence alone can yield implausible recommendations; out-of-distribution checks help keep them realistic.

s9f5645e370.title: Layer-Readout Interfaces in EEG Foundation Models: Predictive Accessibility and Cross-Dataset Transfer
s9f5645e370.description: arXiv:2611.31320v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Intermediate layers often outperform final layers when foundation models are used as frozen feature extractors, but the source of this advantage is unclear. We study this question in EEG foundation models by separating three factors: how representations are read out, whether intermediate layers provide predictive utility beyond the final-layer interface, and whether useful depth structure transfers across datasets. Across five models and three tasks, improving the final-layer readout consistently recovers substantial predictive performance, yet intermediate layers remain advantageous within frozen extraction. We also find that layers selected on one dataset remain useful on another across five dataset pairs and four task families, and that
s9f5645e370.summary: A study of EEG foundation models finds final-layer readout choices strongly affect frozen-feature performance, and examines whether intermediate-layer advantages transfer across datasets.
s9f5645e370.why: Choosing which layer to read features from can change results substantially, so readout design matters when reusing frozen foundation models.

s1138f46eb9.title: Per-Attack Blocking Hides Catalog Vulnerability: A Weakest-Link Analysis of Tool Manifests
s1138f46eb9.description: arXiv:2611.31338v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Runtime controls for tool-using agents depend on manifests that state what each tool may read and where its output may go. Evaluations of these controls, including ChainCaps, report per-attack blocking: the share of attacks a set of manifests stops. We show that this is the wrong unit. A catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy: if $M$ independently authored policies are each wrong with probability $p$, the chance that the catalog contains an accepted exfiltration path is $1-(1-p)^M$, while per-attack blocking stays at $1-p$. Three lines of evidence agree. In synthetic catalogs run through two enforcement engines, ChainCaps and OpenAPPA, per-attack blocking holds at 92% while catalog vulnerability rises from 22% at 10 tools to 9
s1138f46eb9.summary: Analysis argues per-attack blocking metrics hide catalog-level risk, since a tool catalog is only as safe as its weakest source policy.
s1138f46eb9.why: Teams relying on per-attack block rates may underestimate exfiltration risk across many tool manifests; evaluate the weakest policy in the catalog.

s19c5aeee43.title: GHC:Expanding Residual Interfaces in Hyper-Connections
s19c5aeee43.description: arXiv:2611.31350v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hyper-Connections expand residual capacity across parallel streams, yet restrict every branch to narrow read and write interfaces: each branch still reads a single stream mixture and writes scaled copies of one output vector to all streams. To lift this bottleneck, we propose Grouped Hyper-Connections (GHC). By partitioning each branch into parallel groups along attention heads or FFN channels, GHC supplies each group with a distinct stream mixture and aggregates their separate outputs into each stream with learned weights. Extensive experiments across dense and Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models show that GHC consistently improves upon Identity Hyper-Connections (IHC) with negligible parameter and memory-access overhead, increasing training e
s19c5aeee43.summary: Researchers propose Grouped Hyper-Connections, which partition branches into groups to give each a distinct stream mixture and wider residual interfaces.
s19c5aeee43.why: It proposes an architectural change to transformer residual connections; the abstract gives too little detail on measured gains to judge practical impact.

s6898dae445.title: Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation: Pixel as Code for Agentic Visual Creation
s6898dae445.description: arXiv:2611.31358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Visual creation demands expressive imagery together with precise control over text, layout, and structure. We introduce Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation, an agentic framework that connects these capabilities through Pixel as Code. Raster images are represented by learned discrete visual tokens, while structured artifacts use explicit programs. A shared generation-and-rendering interface connects these representations to visual feedback across images, vector graphics, webpages, and documents. A Nemotron-native harness coordinates planning and raster candidate selection, with targeted repair for editable structured and hybrid artifacts. To support this interface, we develop Nemotron-Labs-Image-Tokenizer, the autoregressive raster generator Nemotr
s6898dae445.summary: NVIDIA's Nemotron-Labs-VisualCreation is an agentic framework that combines learned visual tokens for raster images with explicit programs for structured artifacts like vector graphics and webpages.
s6898dae445.why: It unifies raster and programmatic visual generation under one agentic harness, relevant to teams building document or design automation.

s97dd6b1458.title: Leaks by Installments: Cross-Session Answer Disclosure in LLM Tutors and a Ledger-Based Defense
s97dd6b1458.description: arXiv:2611.31429v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tutors built on large language models (LLMs) are told not to give away answers, but a learner does not have to ask for the answer all at once. Existing safeguards judge each reply within the current conversation, so a learner can open a new session, reword the problem, or request a worked solution to the same problem with different numbers. We call this cross-session disclosure and propose a defense: a persistent, per-learner disclosure ledger. For every problem a learner brings, the system builds a typed solution graph. Before a reply is released, a gate matches the reply's own content, not the learner's wording, against the ledger by result values and by type-labeled solution structure, then computes which steps the learner could now deri
s97dd6b1458.summary: Researchers show LLM tutors can leak answers across sessions and propose a persistent per-learner disclosure ledger to track and block cumulative answer disclosure.
s97dd6b1458.why: Per-reply safeguards miss answers leaked over multiple sessions; stateful disclosure tracking is needed for education products built on LLMs.

s7d1e814a7f.title: Below the Stopwatch: Checking the Performance Claims of Coding Agents in the Kernel
s7d1e814a7f.description: arXiv:2611.31460v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents open many pull requests (PRs) that claim to make software faster. Most such claims also give a reason, such as "cache the result" or "read the file once". A stopwatch can show that code got faster, but not that it got faster for the stated reason. We present Below, a pipeline that checks these reasons at the kernel level. From 1,343 runtime-performance PRs in the AIDev dataset, Below extracts the mechanism each PR claims and maps it to the kernel and hardware signals that must change if the claim is true. A build agent that never sees the claim rebuilds the code before and after each PR. Below then measures both versions with plain timing runs, hardware counters and LTTng kernel traces. Most claims are not measured: 57.3% of t
s7d1e814a7f.summary: Below is a pipeline that checks whether coding agents' performance PRs achieve speedups for the reasons they claim, using kernel and hardware signals across 1,343 PRs.
s7d1e814a7f.why: Stopwatch benchmarks cannot confirm a claimed optimization mechanism; kernel-level verification helps review agent-authored performance changes.

s1edc872900.title: AdProducer: Towards Agentic Advertising Video Generation
s1edc872900.description: arXiv:2611.31466v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in video generation have made automated advertising production increasingly feasible. However, an effective advertisement must faithfully represent the product and communicate its selling points through compelling visual storytelling, which requires more than visual synthesis: it calls for deeper product understanding and strategic decisions about how to present product value. Crucially, product research and creative design are closely intertwined, as the information gathered about a product determines which features can be faithfully demonstrated and how they should be presented. In this paper, we introduce AdProducer, the first end-to-end agentic framework for advertising video creation, transforming concise creative brief
s1edc872900.summary: AdProducer proposes an agentic system for generating advertising videos that combines product understanding with strategic decisions about presenting product value.

s7db97ebed7.title: Reading Between the Layers: Where Representation Quality Lives, and What Geometry Reveals
s7db97ebed7.description: arXiv:2611.31496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representation quality in pretrained text foundation models is not concentrated at the final layer, yet practitioners routinely probe it there because layer selection without labels has remained an open problem. We present a large-scale empirical study of where layer quality lives across 25 models spanning four architectural families and four pretraining strategies, evaluated on 13 datasets across classification, pair classification, semantic textual similarity, and multiple-choice question answering. Peak probing layers depend systematically on pretraining strategy and architecture: masked encoders peak in late-middle layers, sequence-to-sequence models shift their peak with task type, contrastive sentence encoders concentrate signal at th
s7db97ebed7.summary: A study of 25 pretrained text models finds representation quality often peaks before the final layer, and examines how to select probing layers without labels.
s7db97ebed7.why: Probing the final layer may underperform; layer selection without labels could improve embedding use in production pipelines.

sea23ecfed1.title: Tempering and few-shot calibration of pathology foundation models improve digital biomarker reproducibility across slide scanners
sea23ecfed1.description: arXiv:2611.31536v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Pathology foundation models underpin a growing number of histology-based cancer biomarkers, but sensitivity to slide scanner-specific image signatures degrades cross-center reliability and reproducibility. We developed a foundation model fine-tuning method that improved consistency in head-and-neck cancer human papillomavirus (HPV) prediction, colorectal cancer microsatellite instability (MSI) identification, prostate cancer grading and breast cancer phenotyping. This tempering method decreased cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% for HPV (95% CI 59.0-73.9%), 69.3% for MSI (95% CI 51.9-76.5%) and 63.4%-81.2% for breast signatures. Cross-scanner prostate grade agreement rose from 42.5% to 92.7%. Under full scanner-HPV confounding du
sea23ecfed1.summary: A tempering and few-shot calibration method for pathology foundation models reduced cross-scanner prediction differences by 67.5% across several cancer biomarker tasks.
sea23ecfed1.why: Scanner-induced variability hurts clinical model reproducibility; the calibration approach targets cross-site reliability in medical AI deployments.

s6a9fd0ec23.title: Where Agent Defenses Fail: A Case Study of Policy Compositions and Measurement Limits
s6a9fd0ec23.description: arXiv:2611.31541v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A coding agent may need to upload a report while its sandbox blocks network access. A host mediator can restore delivery, but an injected instruction may add a secret to the approved request. We study this interaction using files and HTTP receipts to measure effects independently of control logs. Two prospective frozen-input cohorts comprise 110 and 300 runs on previously explored authored tasks. Restrictive sandboxing produces no observed attack harm but reduces benign utility to 6/8 and 12/24. Mediation restores uploads and admits disclosure; complete-line matching retains full benign utility but misses two value-only disclosures in the expanded cohort. A separate 72-run boundary study identifies encoded disclosure, observer misses, and f
s6a9fd0ec23.summary: A case study finds restrictive sandboxing blocks attacks but reduces benign utility, while host mediation restores uploads yet admits some disclosure, measured via files and HTTP receipts.
s6a9fd0ec23.why: Sandbox and mediator policies interact in ways that trade off utility and security; agent defenses need end-to-end measurement of effects.

s5dd9d2fdb6.title: Reproducible Social Structure Emerges From Free-Form Interaction Among LLM Agents
s5dd9d2fdb6.description: arXiv:2611.31543v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent LLM simulations are increasingly used as models of social systems, but most published findings are anecdotal, i.e., drawn from a single run. It is therefore unclear which observed phenomena are robust findings of the simulated system itself, and which were random events in one particular run. Here, we introduce a repeatable, goal-free, proactive multi-agent framework in which fifty persona-conditioned agents with persistent memory choose whether, with whom, and how to communicate across three social platforms. The framework supports non-perturbative measurements across temporal snapshots and repetitions. Running the same world ten times from identical initial conditions for a total of 700 hours, we find that most measured networ
s5dd9d2fdb6.summary: Researchers introduce a repeatable multi-agent framework where fifty persona-conditioned LLM agents with memory communicate across three platforms, aiming for reproducible social dynamics.
s5dd9d2fdb6.why: Single-run multi-agent simulations are anecdotal; a repeatable framework enables more reliable social simulation research.

s79565cd7b1.title: Denoising Diffusion with Progressive Posterior Sampling
s79565cd7b1.description: arXiv:2611.31558v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diffusion models provide effective generative priors for solving noisy linear inverse problems. However, existing posterior sampling methods may require singular value decomposition (SVD) of the measurement operator or prior knowledge of the measurement noise variance, while guidance based on local gradients provides only a limited view of posterior geometry. We propose progressive posterior sampling (PPS) with manifold projection, which automatically estimates the measurement noise variance and avoids SVD. During reverse diffusion, PPS constructs a Gaussian approximation to the posterior distribution in closed form and guides a sample drawn from the local prior toward the approximate posterior mean. We then project the guided sample onto a
s79565cd7b1.summary: Researchers propose progressive posterior sampling with manifold projection for diffusion-based linear inverse problems, estimating noise variance automatically and avoiding SVD.
s79565cd7b1.why: Removes need for SVD or known noise variance in diffusion-based inverse problem solvers, potentially simplifying imaging pipelines.

s1110baa22a.title: The Paradox of Agency-Preserving AI: Negotiating Learner Agency in Layered Human-AI Interactions
s1110baa22a.description: arXiv:2611.31573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used by learners in cognitively demanding tasks, but its capacity to provide immediate solutions raises concerns about decreased learner agency. Meta-level AI systems that provide reflective and metacognitive scaffolding have emerged as a promising approach to supporting learners' self-regulation. However, these systems introduce a fundamental paradox: AI intended to preserve learner agency can itself constrain that agency by regulating when, how, and why learners should reflect. To investigate this challenge, we conducted a co-design workshop with 18 students engaged in programming and academic writing tasks using ChatGPT extended with ChatWise, a meta-level AI system providing self-regulated learning-aligned
s1110baa22a.summary: Researchers examine how meta-level AI systems that scaffold learner reflection can paradoxically constrain the learner agency they are meant to preserve.

s6ab622ef13.title: LatentLens: Rethinking Latent Interface in Multi-Agent Systems
s6ab622ef13.description: arXiv:2611.31582v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent interfaces let agents in a multi-agent system communicate through continuous representations rather than decoded text. Prior work reports performance and efficiency gains, but neither separates latent communication from the agent harness nor examines its internal components, leaving its actual contribution unclear. We propose LatentLens, a framework that decouples the latent interface at two levels: externally from the agent harness, to measure its contribution to overall performance (RQ1), and internally into realignment compatibility, information accessibility, and propagation dynamics, to identify the benefits and limitations of each (RQ2). Across seven benchmarks with Qwen3 models, adding the latent interface to the same harness
s6ab622ef13.summary: Researchers propose LatentLens, a framework that separates latent agent-to-agent communication from the agent harness to measure its real contribution to multi-agent performance.
s6ab622ef13.why: It questions whether reported gains from latent interfaces come from the communication method or the surrounding harness, which matters when designing multi-agent systems.

s18023f62d2.title: GoldiBench: Right Tools, Wrong Amount -- Benchmarking Agents on Effect Judgement in Professional Editing
s18023f62d2.description: arXiv:2611.31590v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real editing requests describe a look, not the steps to reach it, so an agent that serves them must judge how much of each tool the look takes. Existing benchmarks do not measure this: their tasks either state the tools and values, or leave the amount open and are scored by VLM judges that pass more than half of half- and triple-strength results. We introduce GoldiBench, a benchmark of 500 editing tasks in five professional applications (darktable, RawTherapee, GIMP, Inkscape, Blender), solvable by writing a program or by operating the GUI. Each task pairs a START image with a TARGET rendered from a hidden program, so the amount is fixed by a known target; the agent's edit is re-rendered and compared with TARGET, and the same task is posed
s18023f62d2.summary: Researchers introduce GoldiBench, a 500-task benchmark testing whether agents can judge the right amount of editing tools to match a described look in professional applications.
s18023f62d2.why: It exposes that existing VLM-judged benchmarks pass many incorrect edit strengths, so teams evaluating editing agents need stricter measures.

se93269795f.title: RePT: 3D Geometry Emerges from 2D Relational Pretraining
se93269795f.description: arXiv:2611.31601v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learning spatial representations often relies on explicitly predicting geometric quantities, but how physical geometry is organized within learned representations remains less understood. We ask whether 3D structure can emerge from learning relations across 2D observations, without 3D prediction targets. We introduce RePT, which learns compact relations between distinct physical points through cross-view 2D point prediction. The learned relation space develops a geometric organization in which magnitudes, angles, and neighborhoods reflect physical 3D displacement. A single linear readout fitted on 16 scenes recovers displacement length and angle on 39 held-out scenes without refitting (Pearson r = 0.72 and 0.78). The ARKitScenes-trained che
se93269795f.summary: RePT is a pretraining method that learns relations across 2D views without 3D targets, and its learned representation reportedly develops geometric structure resembling physical 3D geometry.
se93269795f.why: It suggests spatial 3D structure may be learned from 2D relational pretraining without explicit geometric supervision.

s1d851d4123.title: What You See Is What You Certify: Concept-Based Certificates for Unseen Compositions
s1d851d4123.description: arXiv:2611.31627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Concept-based models justify a decision by concepts they claim to see, decoded through an explicit ontology. Yet concept predictions are known to leak label information, ignore locality, and be poorly grounded on new attribute combinations. A decision decoded from such concepts can satisfy the ontology and still be wrong, so we ask when it can serve as a certificate. On unseen combinations of familiar parts, a joint concept bottleneck model and a concept embedding model, trained as is standard, certify wrong classes 93-94% of the time despite a correct ontology (60% for a joint model trained only on visible parts and gated by a localizer). The joint model's part errors copy co-occurring values more often than chance (cross-concept shortcutt
s1d851d4123.summary: The paper argues concept-based models trained as standard can certify wrong classes on unseen attribute combinations, about 93-94% of the time in the reported tests.
s1d851d4123.why: Concept explanations can look justified while being wrong, so teams relying on them for interpretability should not treat them as reliable certificates.

s1e14efaf00.title: Provenance Loss and Repair in Multilingual Compaction
s1e14efaf00.description: arXiv:2611.31668v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversational assistants compact older messages into short notes and evict the originals. When the note's language requires a distinction that English leaves open, such as Spanish adjective gender (agotado vs. agotada), messages that omit or explicitly state that attribute can yield the same note. After eviction, later turns cannot tell them apart: taking the inflected form literally asserts an attribute the user never gave, whereas discounting it as routine grammar discards one the user did give. We propose a training-free repair across writing, pre-eviction verification and reading. The writer marks unstated attributes with paired forms (e.g., agotado/a), a likelihood check before eviction rewrites unsupported single forms into paired on
s1e14efaf00.summary: The paper examines how conversational assistants' compaction of older messages into notes loses grammatical gender information in languages like Spanish, and proposes a training-free repair.
s1e14efaf00.why: Lossy memory compaction in multilingual assistants can make later turns assert attributes users never gave, a practical bug for chatbot builders.

scca289c976.title: Right Destination, Wrong Journey: Synthetic Counseling Dialogues Miss Human Interactional Dynamics
scca289c976.description: arXiv:2611.31686v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-generated counseling dialogues are increasingly used for training and evaluating mental-health systems, yet existing evaluations focus largely on response quality and final outcomes rather than how support unfolds over time. We conduct a trajectory-centered evaluation of process fidelity across ten human, reconstructed, and synthetic counseling datasets. Our results show that synthetic dialogues often reach plausible endpoints but differ from human support in recovery dynamics and turn-by-turn responsiveness. While generation design can shift global properties such as recovery timing and trajectory structure, contingent patient--counselor responsiveness remains consistently lower in fidelity across models and generation paradigms. Our e
scca289c976.summary: A trajectory-based study finds LLM-generated counseling dialogues often reach plausible endpoints but differ from human support in recovery dynamics and turn-by-turn responsiveness.
scca289c976.why: Teams using synthetic dialogues to train or evaluate mental-health systems should not assume they match real interactional dynamics.

scbfa6c7c9c.title: GRUN: Generalized Retinex Unfolding Network for Image Restoration
scbfa6c7c9c.description: arXiv:2611.31690v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Image restoration remains a fundamental challenge in low-level vision, requiring methods that handle diverse degradations while preserving scene structures and details. We revisit classical Retinex theory and propose a Generalized Retinex formulation that extends the illumination-reflectance decomposition into a Retinex-inspired content-environment factorization prior for image restoration. The key idea is to restore images using two learned factors: a content-dominant response (generalized reflectance) capturing scene properties and an environment-side response (generalized illumination) encoding task-dependent variations associated with the observed degradations. Based on this formulation, we develop GRUN (Generalized Retinex Unfolding Ne
scbfa6c7c9c.summary: GRUN proposes a generalized Retinex formulation that factorizes images into content and environment components for image restoration.

s50f52992e3.title: Rapid Exploratory Maps and their potential role in supporting evidence-to-policy dialogues and processes
s50f52992e3.description: arXiv:2611.31693v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Producing useful evidence syntheses requires clearly formulated research questions linked to an understanding of their optimal scope. When policymakers (or other end users) commission or steer the production of systematic reviews or other evidence syntheses to fulfil a demand for evidence, these parameters are rarely specified sufficiently for production to proceed. Instead, these details are typically developed via a collaborative dialogic process involving evidence producers and users to ensure the resulting synthesis will meet users' needs. This process is informed by scoping and (more-or-less formally) mapping the existing evidence base, which can take many weeks or months, slowed by applying mostly manual processes to identify and char
s50f52992e3.summary: The paper describes Rapid Exploratory Maps as a way to support dialogue between evidence producers and policymakers when scoping evidence syntheses.

sc3604e7204.title: CATWAY: Cost-sensitive agentic three-way robot decisions with calibrated language-model confidence
sc3604e7204.description: arXiv:2611.31694v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A language-model robot agent must decide whether to execute, question or refuse an instruction, and an unsafe execution costs far more than an unneeded question. No prior robot gate derives all its thresholds from error costs or acts on calibrated probabilities, and none was fitted in one domain and evaluated unchanged in another. We propose CATWAY, a cost-sensitive three-way decision gate: a loss matrix over four instruction conditions (clear, ambiguous, infeasible, unsafe) fixes execute, ask and refuse regions on the probability simplex, the question being the information-gathering step. Its probabilities fuse a ten-sample vote with graded scores of ambiguity, infeasibility and risk by logistic regression. Fitted on household instructions
sc3604e7204.summary: CATWAY is a cost-sensitive three-way gate that decides whether a language-model robot agent should execute, ask, or refuse an instruction, using calibrated confidence.
sc3604e7204.why: Deriving decision thresholds from error costs and calibrated probabilities offers a principled safety gate for LLM-driven robots that tech leaders deploying agents could adapt.

s5e21d7c85a.title: FoveaWAM: Role-Aware 4D World-Action Modeling for Dynamic Manipulation
s5e21d7c85a.description: arXiv:2611.31705v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: To manipulate a moving object, a policy must predict the scene at the moment its action executes, yet every millisecond spent predicting pushes that moment further away. Scene-level forecasts are computationally expensive, whereas target-centric forecasts can omit nearby objects that affect contact. Our key insight is that what a policy must predict decouples by role: only the target's pose, which determines contact, requires millimeter precision, while the surroundings matter primarily through the clearance they leave and the motion they impart. We present FoveaWAM, a native 4D world-action model that allocates precision according to these roles. Specifically, it models the target's past and future motion as a metric SE(3) trajectory, the
s5e21d7c85a.summary: FoveaWAM proposes role-aware 4D world-action modeling that predicts the target object's pose precisely while forecasting surroundings more coarsely, for dynamic robot manipulation.
s5e21d7c85a.why: Decoupling prediction precision by object role could cut computation for robot policies that manipulate moving objects.

s917f9b039e.title: EventSSM: Causal Spatial-State Modelling for Asynchronous Events Event-Depth Estimation
s917f9b039e.description: arXiv:2611.31720v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Event cameras report asynchronous brightness changes, yet metric-depth supervision is typically available only at sparsely sampled reference timestamps. Aggregating events into frame-like representations simplifies learning but can obscure the fine-grained temporal structure of the original event stream. We introduce EventSSM, a causal spatial-state framework for event-associated metric-depth estimation using a recurrent memory updated by chronological event packets. To bridge asynchronous predictions and frame-time supervision, predicted event depths are geometrically transported using calibrated camera poses and differentiably rendered at reference timestamps. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate improvements over established event-depth met
s917f9b039e.summary: EventSSM introduces a causal spatial-state recurrent model that processes event camera data in chronological packets to estimate metric depth.

s9d57be028f.title: Geo-SMILE: Statistical Model-Agnostic Interpretability with Local Explanations for Geospatial Machine Learning
s9d57be028f.description: arXiv:2611.31731v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional post-hoc explanation methods were developed largely for non-spatial inputs and often provide limited explicit treatment of geographic context. We introduce Geo-SMILE, a model-agnostic framework that distinguishes substantive Feature explanation from geographic-position response through complementary perturbation branches. The Feature branch masks substantive predictors while retaining observed coordinates; the Geo branch relocates geographic units while holding substantive predictors fixed. Following the statistical-distance-weighted surrogate principle of SMILE, input-distribution Wasserstein distances determine coalition locality weights and weighted Ridge surrogates approximate expected black-box predictions. GeoSensitivity,
s9d57be028f.summary: Geo-SMILE is a model-agnostic explanation framework for geospatial machine learning that separates feature effects from geographic-position effects using perturbation branches.
s9d57be028f.why: Standard post-hoc explainers often ignore geographic context, so this offers a way to interpret spatial models more accurately.

sf1845cc5a4.title: MOSAIC: Memory-Organized Search with Anti-Imitation Crossover for Training-Free Microarchitecture Optimization
sf1845cc5a4.description: arXiv:2611.31733v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can generate cache-replacement policies. The central challenge is to retain performance on workloads excluded from the search. In our adaptations of published search methods, generated code resembles established policies, with cosine similarities of 0.78-0.84. The wider comparison also shows held-out harmonic-mean instructions-per-cycle (IPC) losses of 1.0-2.4%. We present MOSAIC, a search controller that improves policies without updating language-model weights. It stores concise lessons from previous evaluations rather than repeatedly copying high-scoring code. When improvement stops, it selects two high-scoring policies whose code embeddings differ and asks the model to combine their mechanisms. Novelty prompts and
sf1845cc5a4.summary: MOSAIC is a search controller that improves LLM-generated cache-replacement policies without updating model weights, storing lessons from past evaluations to limit held-out performance loss.
sf1845cc5a4.why: It shows a training-free way to use LLM code search for systems optimization while reducing overfitting to searched workloads.

s9cd9e9676a.title: Where is the Interface for the AI Harness?
s9cd9e9676a.description: arXiv:2611.31739v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Norman's gulfs of execution and evaluation have guided interaction design for forty years, but both assume a user who is present in the loop. Agentic delegation breaks that assumption: users describe an outcome and leave, while the agent takes hundreds of unseen actions. Starting from a 2026 incident in which a research agent circumvented an access refusal on an Australian government portal and went unnoticed for two months, we argue that delegation opens two new gulfs. The gulf of specification is the gap between what a user wants and their ability to express it, including how the agent should behave in situations nobody foresaw. The gulf of oversight is the gap between what an agent is doing and the user's ability to know, assess, and con
s9cd9e9676a.summary: The paper argues agentic delegation creates new interaction gaps, citing a 2026 incident where a research agent circumvented an access refusal on an Australian government portal unnoticed for two months.
s9cd9e9676a.why: Users who delegate to agents leave the loop, so teams building agent interfaces need oversight and visibility designs for unseen actions.

s5f3798e41d.title: RVLM-X: Towards a Universal VLM Harness
s5f3798e41d.description: arXiv:2611.31755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Harnesses for vision-language models (VLMs) have grown with the models' capabilities, notably for images far larger than those seen in training, where downscaling loses small details. Most of them wrap the VLM in a fixed procedure, such as a zoom tree, that decides in advance where it looks and how the evidence is combined. These procedures make up for the weaknesses of older models by keeping them on a task-specific path, but with frontier models that reliably plan and use tools, they can lower accuracy. We propose RVLM-X, a task-generalizable recursive VLM harness that runs unchanged across photographs, charts and maps. Following the recursive inference of Recursive Language Models, the VLM programmatically controls its own visual context
s5f3798e41d.summary: RVLM-X proposes a task-generalizable harness for vision-language models that avoids fixed procedures like zoom trees, letting frontier models plan and use tools for large images.
s5f3798e41d.why: Fixed VLM harnesses may reduce accuracy with newer models that plan and use tools well, which affects how teams build image-analysis pipelines.

sbb28106a2e.title: RoMo Hands: A Large Scale Richly Organized Text to Hand Motion Dataset
sbb28106a2e.description: arXiv:2611.31766v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While text-driven body motion generation has matured, pure-hand synthesis remains bottlenecked by data. Existing datasets often treat hands as rigid end-effectors, lack fine-grained captions, or are too limited in scale to support robust generalization. We introduce RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild, text-paired dataset of ~542K sequences (884 hours, 95.5M frames at 30 fps) which is an order of magnitude larger than prior work. To ensure high-quality supervision, a stringent dexterity filter discards low-articulation sequences, focusing the distribution on complex bimanual movement. Each clip is paired with five captions at increasing granularities from global semantic tags to atomic finger states, organized under a hierarchical taxonomy. To bridg
sbb28106a2e.summary: Researchers introduced RoMo Hands, an in-the-wild text-paired dataset of about 542K hand motion sequences, filtered for dexterity.
sbb28106a2e.why: Large, finely captioned hand-motion data could help teams train text-to-hand generation models that current datasets are too small to support.

s8e47591890.title: DELTA: Diagnosing Exploration Lineages via Twin-path Alignment - What Can Contrasting Design Paths Reveal About Microarchitectural Behavior?
s8e47591890.description: arXiv:2611.31767v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Architects have two mature instruments for performance work. Top-Down analysis tells them where a design loses its pipeline slots, and design-space exploration (DSE) tells them which configuration scores best. Neither explains why a search stops improving: why a backend-bound design rejects a prefetcher that the bottleneck label recommends, or why a capacity increase that helped in one configuration hurts in the next. This paper argues that the evidence needed to answer such questions is already produced during exploration and then discarded. Every parent-child edge in an exploration tree is a controlled intervention: one knob changes, the rest of the design is held fixed, and a cycle-level simulator measures the outcome. When the same edit
s8e47591890.summary: The DELTA paper proposes using data produced during design-space exploration to explain why microarchitecture searches stop improving.
s8e47591890.why: It suggests architects can reuse exploration traces to diagnose bottlenecks, not just pick the best configuration.

scfe6ef0847.title: SPARQL-Planned Single-Hop Traversal over a Live Knowledge Graph for Multi-Hop Question Answering
scfe6ef0847.description: arXiv:2611.31771v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic retrieval struggles with multi-hop question answering on both recall and precision: gold passages are buried among distractors that degrade the reader's answer, and retrieving them requires reasoning over the query rather than matching it. GraphRAG techniques expand semantic retrieval by connecting passages to graph nodes and performing one or more hops of expansion after initial retrieval. This improves recall, but multi-hop expansion becomes expensive and brings additional noise into the retrieved set. We break this tradeoff by \emph{interleaving} dense retrieval with knowledge-graph traversal for complex multi-hop questions. Dense retrieval locates the first relevant regions of the search space at good recall, while traversal of
scfe6ef0847.summary: The paper proposes SPARQL-planned single-hop traversal over a live knowledge graph to improve multi-hop question answering retrieval.
scfe6ef0847.why: It offers a way to reduce the noise and cost of multi-hop graph expansion in retrieval-augmented systems.

s67cf98cd35.title: VISOR: A Vision-Language Selector for Multimodal Time-Series Forecasting
s67cf98cd35.description: arXiv:2611.31780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent time-series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast a distribution over futures, and multimodal time-series (TS) forecasting further exploits other modalities to improve forecasting accuracy. However, existing works have two limitations: 1) TSFMs reduce the predictive distribution to its median or mean, flattening diverse futures into a calm line, and 2) multimodal TS forecasting models incorporate text into the forecaster through TS-language alignment, which is substantially weaker than vision-language alignment. To address these limitations, we propose the VIsion-language SelectOR (VISOR), a multimodal TS forecasting framework that selects one plausible future instead of averaging across candidates, leveraging the alignment capabilities
s67cf98cd35.summary: VISOR is a vision-language selector for multimodal time-series forecasting that aims to preserve diverse future distributions rather than collapsing to a median.
s67cf98cd35.why: It targets two named limits of current forecasters: flattened predictive distributions and weak text-to-series alignment.

sc0d9018f46.title: Three-Dimensional Wake Reconstruction and Cross-Scale Transfer for Floating Offshore Wind Turbines via Physics-Informed Fourier Neural Operators
sc0d9018f46.description: arXiv:2611.31789v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coupled surge-pitch motions drive unsteady vortex interactions and dynamic wake meandering behind floating offshore wind turbines, complicating three-dimensional wake reconstruction from limited measurements and transfer across turbine scales. Large-eddy simulations coupled with an actuator line model generate fixed and surge-pitch wakes at motion-based Strouhal numbers $St=fD/U_\infty$ of 0.2-0.6 (where $f$, $D$, and $U_\infty$ are the motion frequency, rotor diameter, and inflow velocity) for the National Renewable Energy Laboratory 5 MW ($D=126$ m) and International Energy Agency 22 MW ($D=284$ m) turbines. A physics-informed Fourier neural operator framework combines four-dimensional spectral convolutions with incompressible continuity
sc0d9018f46.summary: Researchers used physics-informed Fourier neural operators to reconstruct three-dimensional wakes behind floating offshore wind turbines and transfer them across turbine scales.

saa6875e256.title: Learning Compact State Abstractions for LLM Agents
saa6875e256.description: arXiv:2611.31800v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents commonly use the full interaction history as a proxy for state, retaining all past observations and actions regardless of whether they remain relevant. We instead ask what information an agent actually needs to carry forward. We define agent state as a compact abstraction of interaction history that preserves the competence of a fixed reference agent, with the minimal such abstraction as the ideal. Because matching the reference agent's behavior is unnecessarily restrictive and difficult for black-box policies, we define sufficiency through task performance rather than behavior matching. We represent state abstractions as deterministic recursive programs and search over them using an LLM-guided genetic algorithm. Across ALFWorld
saa6875e256.summary: The paper defines compact state abstractions that let LLM agents keep only the interaction history they need, instead of the full history.
saa6875e256.why: Smaller agent state could cut context costs while keeping a reference agent's competence, relevant to long-running agent design.

sec7b84fb64.title: TopoCryptoEEG: End-to-End Encrypted Framework for Brainprint Authentication
sec7b84fb64.description: arXiv:2611.31801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Brainprint authentication enables continuous identity verification, but EEG data are privacy-sensitive. Existing feature-level encrypted authentication (FLEA) schemes protect extracted features under a trusted-client assumption. We show theoretically and empirically that a compromised client with access to plaintext query features and continuous authentication scores can exactly recover a registered template after finitely many interactions. To address this risk, we propose TopoCryptoEEG, a homomorphic-encryption-based framework that encrypts preprocessed EEG data at the client and performs feature extraction, template matching, score computation, and threshold centering on ciphertexts at the server. This extends protection from extracted f
sec7b84fb64.summary: TopoCryptoEEG proposes a homomorphic-encryption framework for brainprint authentication after showing encrypted feature schemes can leak templates.
sec7b84fb64.why: It highlights that feature-level encryption under a trusted-client assumption can be broken, a design concern for biometric systems.

s95aa62d82c.title: How Far Apart Are Two Proofs? Measuring Proof Dissimilarity in a Proof Kernel and in Lean/Mathlib
s95aa62d82c.description: arXiv:2611.31811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. Following Hilbert's 24th problem and the identity-of-proofs problem, we ask how far apart two proofs of one theorem are, and what shape the proof space they inhabit has. We define 19 dissimilarity measures in 6 families (syntactic, structural, dependency & resource, semantic, information-theoretic, higher-categorical)
s95aa62d82c.summary: The paper introduces methods for measuring distances between mathematical proofs, in a proof kernel and in Lean/Mathlib.
s95aa62d82c.why: Proof-distance metrics could help teams judge whether AI-generated formal proofs are actually novel or redundant.

s17c863b611.title: Agentic Discovery of Soundness Bugs in Safe Rust Bindings
s17c863b611.description: arXiv:2611.31813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Rust crates confine unsafe code, such as calls into C or C++ libraries or system calls, behind safe interfaces that must uphold Rust's invariants. If an interface encodes one rule of the code beneath it too weakly, a program written in purely safe Rust can cause undefined behavior. Static analyzers and fuzzers are bound to fixed patterns or to the paths they execute. We propose LLM agents as auditors of these interfaces, and study how well they do it. We first define a taxonomy of the defects of such interfaces, including undefined behavior, divergences from the wrapped library, and incomplete unsafe contracts. We then measure, in repeated audits of a real-world crate by a closed and an open model, Claude Opus 5.5 and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, w
s17c863b611.summary: The paper proposes using LLM agents to audit safe Rust bindings for soundness bugs that allow undefined behavior from safe code.
s17c863b611.why: Agentic auditing of Rust FFI wrappers could find unsafe-boundary defects that static analyzers and fuzzers miss.

s89150f6103.title: Exploring Multi-Player Social Games as Verifiable Training Grounds for Large Language Models
s89150f6103.description: arXiv:2611.31821v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The training of socially intelligent language models often relies on large language model (LLM) judges, which are expensive, noisy, and vulnerable to reward hacking. Multi-player social games offer a natural alternative: they require open-ended communication to coordinate with teammates and infer hidden roles, while their rules provide an objective outcome which can serve as a verifiable reward for training. Using three social games, we explore how much social intelligence Qwen3 models can acquire through supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Results show that against a much stronger Gemma-3-27B model, SFT and RLVR raise the win rate of Qwen3-4B from 33% to 81% on the three trained games, an
s89150f6103.summary: The paper explores multi-player social games as verifiable training environments for Qwen3 models using SFT and reinforcement learning.
s89150f6103.why: Rule-based game outcomes could replace expensive, noisy LLM judges as reward signals for social-skill training.

sa49022e63f.title: POISE: Curvature-Aware Critic Regularization for Smooth Actor-Critic Control
sa49022e63f.description: arXiv:2611.31835v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Actor-critic methods achieve high returns in robotic control, yet trained actors exhibit high-frequency action oscillations. Most smoothness methods constrain the actor, whereas PAVE regularizes the critic by separately penalizing action-gradient variation and encouraging negative action curvature. The same gradient change, however, moves the critic's preferred action farther where the critic is flat, and separate penalties do not measure this motion. We characterize this motion through the greedy shift, which approximates greedy-action displacement across state transitions to first order under local concavity. Since displacement alone does not reflect its critic-value consequences, the analysis further shows that the shift's curvature-weig
sa49022e63f.summary: POISE proposes curvature-aware critic regularization to reduce high-frequency action oscillations in actor-critic robotic control.
sa49022e63f.why: It targets smoothness of learned robot controllers by regularizing the critic rather than the actor.

s4bad0adb6a.title: Gaze World Model
s4bad0adb6a.description: arXiv:2611.31836v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Where a person looks indicates their focus of attention, and how their gaze shifts between targets reveals how that attention responds to a changing scene. Existing gaze target estimation methods largely operate frame by frame and do not model these shifts. Gaze shifts are often driven by dynamic changes in the scene, which is the kind of information world models are designed to encode. This relationship is subtle, however, since an event far across the frame may produce only a slight movement of the person's head or eyes. We therefore introduce the Gaze World Model (GWM), which co-trains latent scene prediction with person-conditioned gaze supervision on a frozen V-JEPA 2.1 encoder; in our ablations, the latent prediction objective improve
s4bad0adb6a.summary: The Gaze World Model paper introduces a world-model approach to estimating gaze targets and how gaze shifts respond to scene changes.

s7840c669cd.title: Spec-Test Coverage Gap: Detecting Overspecified Tests in SWE-Bench-Style Benchmarks
s7840c669cd.description: arXiv:2611.31839v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: SWE-bench-style benchmarks, such as SWE-bench Verified (Verified) and SWE-bench Pro (Pro), evaluate coding agents with tests taken from the change that originally fixed each issue. However, these tests can enforce details the task never states, causing correct alternative fixes to fail. Such overspecified tests have so far been found mainly through expensive expert review. To address this, we define the Spec-Test Coverage Gap (STCG), a 1-4 scale measuring overspecification, and score it with two LLM judges, Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Sol, which are given the specification and the test patch. A task is flagged as overspecified when both judges score it 3 or higher. Our study has three parts. First, we validate the judges on 206 tasks that e
s7840c669cd.summary: The paper defines a Spec-Test Coverage Gap metric and uses LLM judges to detect overspecified tests in SWE-bench-style coding benchmarks.
s7840c669cd.why: Overspecified tests can reject correct alternative fixes, so this affects how reliably coding-agent benchmarks measure performance.

sdf38b43940.title: Faithful Persona Steering under Incongruity via Dual-Stream Refinement
sdf38b43940.description: arXiv:2611.31848v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standard LLM personalization typically frames identity as a static retrieval task, overlooking the inherent incongruity of human personas, where stable traits coexist with atypical, context-specific stances. Existing methods struggle to reconcile these dimensions: prompting succumbs to context drift over long sequences, while fine-tuning often suppresses idiosyncratic "quirks" in favor of generic distributional patterns. To bridge this gap, we present QuirkyMind, a framework that disentangles identity definition from its expression. First, Traits Anchoring constructs a dual-stream latent state, fusing a sentence-level summary for semantic stability with a token-level sequence for generative control. This state is stabilized via In-Context N
sdf38b43940.summary: QuirkyMind is a framework that separates persona identity definition from its expression to keep atypical persona traits in LLM steering.
sdf38b43940.why: It addresses context drift and loss of idiosyncratic traits in long-sequence LLM personalization.

s86a2c35c91.title: JECT: Addressing the Context Shortcut in Joint-Embedding Predictive Learning for Chest CT
s86a2c35c91.description: arXiv:2611.31849v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Joint-embedding predictive architectures learn by predicting features of masked regions from visible context. In chest computed tomography, the findings that decide a diagnosis, such as a small nodule, are often not predictable from the surrounding anatomy. A hidden finding is then best predicted toward normal anatomy, and the prediction loss stops rewarding the encoder for representing it. We call this the context shortcut. Conditioning the predictor on the radiology report repairs the prediction, but in our setup the encoder gains little over image-only pretraining: the report supplies what the encoder never had to learn. JECT therefore gives the report two roles: a condition for the predictor and, through masked section-text prediction,
s86a2c35c91.summary: JECT addresses a context shortcut in joint-embedding predictive learning for chest CT, where hidden findings are predicted as normal anatomy.

s9cfab3ad80.title: Two-Stage Post-Training for Flow-Based Embodied Foundation Models
s9cfab3ad80.description: arXiv:2611.31850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large-scale pretraining provides embodied models with general capabilities, but reliable task execution still requires post training. In multitask settings, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) faces distribution mismatch between training and deployment, whereas reinforcement learning (RL) is limited by sparse rewards and uneven learning progress across tasks. Multi-teacher on policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates expert capabilities through dense supervision on the model's own trajectories, but achieving performance beyond the teachers remains challenging. We propose a two-stage post training framework for flow-based embodied models, constructing distillation objectives from the velocity regression formulation of conditional flow matching. Stage
s9cfab3ad80.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a two-stage post-training approach for flow-based embodied foundation models, building on multi-teacher on-policy distillation to go beyond teacher performance.
s9cfab3ad80.why: Offers a post-training recipe for robot foundation models that aims to combine supervised fine-tuning and RL while mitigating distribution mismatch and sparse rewards.

s59b7cf97be.title: CALVIN-MAX: When Does a Mid-Execution Change Hurt a Robot Policy?
s59b7cf97be.description: arXiv:2611.31868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots must often keep working after the world changes, as when a block moves or the camera shifts while the robot still acts on what it saw before. Recent work showed that one change during a task lowers success for every policy tested, but did not separate the effect of its timing from the cost of the changed world, or measure what it costs afterwards. We introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases on CALVIN's five-instruction chains, each with one change to the objects, the camera, the robot, or the instruction. Each case compares three runs that are identical until the affected instruction begins: one without the change, one with it in place from that moment, and one in which it arrives while the robot is moving. The second run aga
s59b7cf97be.summary: Researchers introduce CALVIN-MAX, a benchmark of 7,828 cases testing how a single mid-task change to objects, camera, robot, or instruction affects robot policy success.
s59b7cf97be.why: Gives teams a benchmark for measuring robot policy robustness to mid-execution environment changes, a common failure mode in deployment.

sdb33355120.title: EEG-Jev: A Unified Single-Pass Decision Model for EEG
sdb33355120.description: arXiv:2611.31875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: EEG analysis spans choosing alternatives, judging statements, and rating ordered attributes, requiring calibratable probabilities with explicit meaning. We present EEG-Jev, a unified single-pass decision model for EEG. Given an EEG window, a question and an answer specification, one forward pass returns a typed readout: CHOICE gives a candidate distribution, NOUL a proposition probability, and SCORE an ordered-level distribution and expectation. One checkpoint is trained jointly and evaluated once on held-out splits of 35 public sources. Core raw outputs reach 54.08% balanced accuracy on Stieger2021 motor imagery, 70.45% on Sleep-EDF-SC sleep staging, 72.11% per window at threshold 0.5 on CHB-MIT seizure detection with 0.825 AUROC, and 1.70
sdb33355120.summary: EEG-Jev is a unified single-pass model that handles EEG choice, statement judgment, and ordered rating tasks, trained jointly on 35 public sources.

scb469b3813.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
scb469b3813.description: arXiv:2611.31883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configurati
scb469b3813.summary: A paper examines when and why agentic video harnesses, which let models request further observations, improve video understanding compared with fixed input policies.
scb469b3813.why: Suggests that letting models request more video evidence only helps under certain task and model conditions, which affects agent design choices.

s65d3675b8d.title: Loupe: Reinforcing Knowledge-Intensive Video Generation Agents
s65d3675b8d.description: arXiv:2611.31895v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Knowledge-intensive video generation remains challenging because prompts often omit the facts, appearances, and temporal relationships required for accurate generation. While search-based workflows can retrieve missing evidence, manually designed strategies limit adaptive planning, and conventional training suffers from costly video-level feedback and coarse trajectory-level credit assignment. In this paper, we present Loupe, a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to construct evidence-grounded temporal video prompts with reference images. We further introduce Rubric-Based Credit (RBC), which leverages prompt-specific factual, visual, and temporal requirements to evaluate intermediate search and pla
s65d3675b8d.summary: Loupe is a video generation agent that retrieves and verifies textual and visual evidence to build evidence-grounded plans for knowledge-intensive video generation, trained with reinforcement learning.
s65d3675b8d.why: Shows an agentic retrieval-and-verification loop for improving factual accuracy in generated video, relevant to teams building generative media pipelines.

s9e94bd535f.title: MIFLOW: Dynamic Recent-Behavior Priors for Reference-Calibrated Online Flow-Policy Reinforcement Learning
s9e94bd535f.description: arXiv:2611.31902v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow-based policies provide expressive action distributions for continuous-control reinforcement learning. In online actor-critic learning, off-policy value estimates can be unreliable in poorly covered action regions, where expressive policies may shift probability mass toward critic-favored actions. We propose MIFLOW, which calibrates online flow-policy learning with a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions. Inspired by canalization as a qualitative analogy for path-dependent stabilization, we use the prior as a moving density reference for value-guided policy improvement. MIFLOW uses the approximate recent-action log-density in a dimension-normalized correction to both actor updates and critic targets. T
s9e94bd535f.summary: MIFLOW proposes a recency-adaptive flow-matching prior fitted to recently executed actions to calibrate online flow-policy reinforcement learning for continuous control.

sf192459b5b.title: Your VLM Knows What to Inspect: Semantic Probe-Guided Adaptive Focusing for GUI Grounding
sf192459b5b.description: arXiv:2611.31909v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GUI grounding requires resolving fine visual details within the context that gives them meaning. Additional views can improve localization, but their value depends on what evidence they expose and how much context they preserve. We explore a capability of vision-language models (VLMs): even when their coordinate predictions are incorrect, they can describe visual evidence worth inspecting. We introduce \textbf{SPARK}, \textit{\textbf{S}emantic \textbf{P}robe-guided \textbf{A}daptive \textbf{R}egion see\textbf{K}ing}, a training-free framework that turns this semantic guidance into targeted visual observations. Exploration probes describe relevant context and distinguishing target details, while verification probes identify evidence needed t
sf192459b5b.summary: SPARK is a training-free framework that uses VLM-generated semantic probes to guide adaptive region zooming for GUI grounding, even when coordinate predictions are wrong.
sf192459b5b.why: Offers a training-free way to improve GUI element localization for computer-use agents by leveraging VLM visual descriptions.

s1bd1d8d67e.title: Machine learning enables full Bayesian inference for spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals
s1bd1d8d67e.description: arXiv:2611.31916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extreme-mass-ratio inspirals (EMRIs), stellar-mass compact objects spiralling into massive black holes, promise to measure the masses and spins of the central black holes, reveal the strong-field environment around them and gauge cosmic distances via millihertz gravitational-wave observations. Yet most forecasts for the parameter inference of these systems assume known source parameters, and broad-prior analyses have addressed only simplified versions of the problem. The joint inversion of all 14 parameters of a spinning source from the complete prior has remained unsolved. Here we solve it for the augmented analytic kludge model: generative networks narrow the complete prior and reveal a ring of degenerate spin directions, and the exact de
s1bd1d8d67e.summary: Researchers report a machine learning method enabling full Bayesian inference over all 14 parameters of spinning extreme-mass-ratio inspirals from gravitational-wave data.

s56660a6cde.title: Beyond Rigid Hands: Deforming Skin into Contact-Consistent Hand Meshes
s56660a6cde.description: arXiv:2611.31950v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Hands grasp objects with soft skin. A fingertip flattens against a mug, and a palm curves around a bottle. Yet hand-object datasets and estimators represent the hand as a rigid articulated mesh, which hovers above or penetrates the object where skin would press against it. Existing refiners keep the mesh rigid and adjust only the pose, trading pose accuracy for physical plausibility. We ask whether a rigid hand can instead touch the object as skin does while staying close to its original pose. We lift annotated or estimated rigid hands to contact-consistent meshes through an optimization that (i) slightly adjusts the joints and wrist to bring the fingers onto the object, (ii) deforms the skin so that penetrating regions settle onto the surf
s56660a6cde.summary: A paper presents a method that deforms rigid annotated or estimated hand meshes into skin-like, contact-consistent shapes that touch objects realistically while staying close to the original pose.

s88db3c59b7.title: Are Web Agents Still Detectable? Stress-Testing Bot Defenses with Coordinated Evasion
s88db3c59b7.description: arXiv:2611.31962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI web agents can autonomously navigate websites and complete various tasks. As their capabilities and adoption expand, evaluating bot defenses requires adversarial stress tests. Although prior work demonstrates that existing agents can remain detectable, it remains unclear how effective bot defenses are against adversaries that coordinate evasion across browser fingerprints, automation controls, and interaction behavior. To investigate this threat, we introduce DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent that combines a forked Chromium browser that conceals automation artifacts and generative models that produce human-like mouse and keyboard traces. To address the limitations of existing keyboard mimickers, our keyboard model jointly generates real
s88db3c59b7.summary: DarkAgent, an autonomous web agent with a forked Chromium browser, is introduced to stress-test whether bot defenses can detect agents that coordinate evasion across fingerprints and behavior.
s88db3c59b7.why: Highlights that coordinated evasion may defeat current bot defenses, which matters for teams protecting sites from automated agents.

sce50909a9f.title: Distill to Loop: Turning Pretrained Diffusion Transformers into Looped Models with Adjustable Depth
sce50909a9f.description: arXiv:2611.31977v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Looped transformers reuse one block of shared weights along the depth of the network. Recent looped diffusion transformers are trained from scratch, which repeats the full pretraining cost although strong pretrained non-looped diffusion transformers exist. We propose Distill to Loop (Dooop), which distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student whose blocks are initialized from the teacher's. We cast distillation as a fixed-point iteration toward the teacher, in which the output after every loop is trained toward the teacher, and each loop is one step of an ordinary differential equation in depth. As a result, one model runs any number of loops at test time without retraining, and the higher-order ODE solvers of
sce50909a9f.summary: Distill to Loop (Dooop) distills a pretrained non-looped diffusion transformer into a looped student with adjustable depth, initializing blocks from the teacher.
sce50909a9f.why: Could cut the cost of building looped diffusion transformers by reusing existing pretrained non-looped models rather than training from scratch.

sf53641795b.title: Reading, Writing and Repairing Game-Theoretic Policies in Weight Space
sf53641795b.description: arXiv:2611.31979v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a language model work in the weight space of a policy network for a repeated game? We put four questions to a mid-size open model, on recurrent networks of 1{,}218 weights with exactly checkable answers. Given a population of opponents described in English, write a policy that is optimal: its value is a finite computation over the agent's information state, so a submitted network has an exact gap from the optimum. Given a network's weights, report its action after each of fifteen opponent histories; recover the state machine it implements, judged on every opponent sequence to depth ten; or repair a network whose output was altered in one place and say which round first goes wrong. The model recovers the program in 62 of 66 replies, repo
sf53641795b.summary: A study tests whether a mid-size open language model can write, read, and repair policy network weights for repeated games with exactly checkable answers.

s13d354bba6.title: ADE: A Zero-Training Unlearning Method for Latent World Models
s13d354bba6.description: arXiv:2611.31998v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent world models learn compact recurrent dynamics from offline trajectories, yet deployed simulators can retain backdoor triggers or stale transitions from outdated physical regimes. Existing unlearning methods fail in autoregressive physics: gradient updates distort latent manifolds and compound rollout drift, naive output zeroing suppresses valid control responses on trigger onset, and single-step deletion leaves corruption inside recurrent hidden states. We propose Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE), a deterministic, zero-training closed-form unlearning algorithm for latent world models. Using only cached pretraining moments, ADE recovers retain covariances via single-pass matrix downdating without raw retain data and cascades closed-
s13d354bba6.summary: Analytical Dynamics Excision (ADE) is a deterministic, zero-training method for removing backdoor triggers and stale transitions from latent world models.
s13d354bba6.why: Offers a training-free unlearning approach for deployed learned simulators, avoiding the drift problems of gradient-based unlearning.

s6b4aa541a3.title: Calm Agent: Reframing Agent Interaction around Intermittent Human Attention
s6b4aa541a3.description: arXiv:2611.32009v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents can carry out auxiliary tasks while users focus on other work. Yet users still need to understand task state, make changes, and respond when help is required. We argue that agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks should be designed around intermittent human attention: tasks should continue between interactions, and users should be able to return with little effort to understand and control them. We develop this position as Calm Agent. It connects three on-demand interaction modes: Delegate, Adjust, and Check, through a persistent task representation. Generative interaction provides controls and feedback suited to open-ended goals, while existing controls support routine actions. We illustrate these principles with Orvlet, a desktop pro
s6b4aa541a3.summary: Calm Agent proposes designing agents for ongoing auxiliary tasks around intermittent human attention, with Delegate, Adjust, and Check interaction modes.
s6b4aa541a3.why: Offers a design framework for agent UX where users return intermittently, relevant to teams building long-running assistants.

s8ccb5f136e.title: To Critic Or Not To Critic
s8ccb5f136e.description: arXiv:2611.32013v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models tackle longer and more complex tasks, understanding when a critic improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes increasingly important. Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) trains a critic to reduce variance and provide fine-grained credit assignment, while Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) drops the critic and avoids the bias of bootstrapping from the critic's value estimates. Although recent critic-based methods have reported strong performance relative to GRPO, it remains unclear when each approach is preferable. We argue that there is no universal answer; instead, the choice depends on several interacting factors, including batch size, critic reliance, and task complexity. We study the bia
s8ccb5f136e.summary: A paper examines when a learned critic improves reinforcement learning efficiency for LLMs, comparing PPO with a critic against critic-free GRPO.
s8ccb5f136e.why: Helps teams choose between PPO and GRPO for LLM RL training based on task length and complexity.

s31db0a59f7.title: When Online Adaptation of Resilience Policies Hurts: Safe Exploration and Measurement Pitfalls in Resilience4j
s31db0a59f7.description: arXiv:2611.32015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings in Java microservices are tuned once and frozen, although the best setting depends on the fault a dependency is currently showing. We study whether an online learner can pick these settings at runtime. AdaptR4j swaps Resilience4j policies atomically in Spring Boot 3 and lets a contextual bandit choose among complete CircuitBreaker/Retry/Bulkhead configurations from Prometheus signals. Our first, naive design scored worse than keeping the default policy in three of four winnable fault scenarios under the reward it optimised: exploring a menu that contained aggressive circuit breakers rejected most traffic while the learner was still learning. Two safeguards fix this: a safe policy menu (no breake
s31db0a59f7.summary: Researchers study whether an online contextual bandit can pick Resilience4j circuit breaker, retry, and bulkhead settings at runtime, finding naive adaptation sometimes underperformed defaults.
s31db0a59f7.why: Shows that runtime tuning of microservice resilience policies can backfire without careful safe exploration and measurement, relevant to SREs considering adaptive configs.

s1ee005c691.title: Structure-Aware Transformers for Hierarchical Authorization in Personal AI Agents
s1ee005c691.description: arXiv:2611.32018v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Personal AI agents can carry out complex, multi-step tasks on users' behalf, but doing so often involves numerous permission requests. Manually reviewing each request is time-consuming, while indiscriminate approval poses privacy and security risks. Predicting users' authorization preferences offers a way to reduce this burden while preserving user control. However, authorization prediction is challenging because permission requests are often hierarchical and observed user decisions are sparse and potentially correlated. To address these challenges, We propose the Parent-gated Authorization Transformer for Hierarchies (PATH) to predict users' authorization preferences for personal AI agents. PATH is a novel neural network architecture that
s1ee005c691.summary: Researchers propose structure-aware transformers to predict users' authorization preferences for hierarchical permission requests from personal AI agents.
s1ee005c691.why: Could reduce permission-review burden for agent deployments, though the abstract gives little detail on results or evaluation.

s124f2d0e0a.title: HuluOPD: Unifying Heterogeneous Medical Specialists into One Lightweight Model with Unlabeled Prompts
s124f2d0e0a.description: arXiv:2611.32021v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Specialist medical vision-language models (VLMs) are strong within their specialties but hard to unify: their training data are often private, and independently developed specialists cannot be assumed to share an architecture. Deploying these large models separately is costly. We present HuluOPD, an on-policy distillation recipe that unifies heterogeneous specialists into one lightweight VLM using only unlabeled prompts, without requiring reference answers or the specialists' training data. The lightweight model answers each prompt, and the specialist of the prompt's modality supervises its response; a continuation-aligned cross-tokenizer loss makes this possible even when they differ in architecture and tokenizer. We apply HuluOPD to five
s124f2d0e0a.summary: HuluOPD is a method that distills several heterogeneous medical specialist vision-language models into one lightweight model using only unlabeled prompts.
s124f2d0e0a.why: Offers a route to consolidate costly specialist medical VLMs into a single cheaper model without access to private training data.

sad178096b9.title: Beyond Before-and-After Images: Evaluating Temporal Grounding in a Lightweight VLM for Disaster Assessment
sad178096b9.description: arXiv:2611.32022v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bi-temporal satellite imagery is central to disaster assessment: deciding what was damaged requires comparing a pre-event scene with its post-event counterpart. A vision-language model (VLM) can nonetheless appear to answer change questions while relying mainly on the post-event image or on the prompt's temporal framing. We present a controlled diagnostic of temporal grounding and apply it to one lightweight VLM, InternVL3-2B, on DisasterM3: 1,659 optical and SAR image pairs from 41 events and nine disaster types, in event-disjoint partitions, with 9,031 reasoning questions. We compare post-only input, the true pre/post pair, the post image repeated twice, reversed image order, and an unrelated pre-event image. The true pair scores $+0.5$ a
sad178096b9.summary: A diagnostic study tests whether the lightweight InternVL3-2B vision-language model truly uses pre- and post-disaster satellite images for temporal damage assessment.
