sad178096b9.why: Highlights that VLMs may answer change questions by relying on one image or prompt framing, a reliability concern for high-stakes remote sensing use.

s15737b9eaa.title: Do Occupancy World Models Really Follow Actions?
s15737b9eaa.description: arXiv:2611.32029v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Occupancy world models predict future 3D scenes conditioned on ego actions, yet their predictions may not faithfully follow the specified trajectory under counterfactual actions. Because driving datasets provide sparse coverage of alternative trajectories for each scene, existing models learn the spatial effect of ego motion implicitly from observed scene--trajectory combinations, which may entangle action effects with scene--trajectory correlations. We propose ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer that grounds future prediction in action-induced geometric correspondence across ego-centric frames. ReCast decouples historical encoding from future decoding and aligns deformable interactions using relative ego transformations, while ret
s15737b9eaa.summary: ReCast, an ego-trajectory-guided transformer, is proposed to make occupancy world models follow specified actions under counterfactual driving trajectories.
s15737b9eaa.why: Addresses whether driving world models actually respond to action inputs, which matters for their use in planning and simulation.

s75bc0154ef.title: Unifying Partner and Environment Diversity to Improve Human-AI Coordination
s75bc0154ef.description: arXiv:2611.32031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-world applications of modern AI systems require generalization to both unseen environments and novel human users. The field of zero-shot coordination (ZSC) has focused primarily on deploying AI to cooperate with novel partners in otherwise familiar environments. Popular population-based methods achieve this by partnering the agent with a diversity of simulated human users during training in a fixed environment, but does not consider the more realistic scenario where both the users and the environment are unseen during training. Recently, training across environments has been explored in training a single self-play agent, which shows better generalization on both novel human users and unseen environments. In this work, we ask whether jo
s75bc0154ef.summary: Researchers propose a method combining partner and environment diversity to improve zero-shot human-AI coordination when both users and environments are unseen.
s75bc0154ef.why: Targets generalization to new users and settings, a practical requirement for deployed cooperative AI, though the abstract is brief on results.

sba37971e15.title: Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums: Execution-Bound Evidence Certification and Plausible-World Safety Gating in Agentic Control Planes
sba37971e15.description: arXiv:2611.32032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agreement among large language models is not physical evidence for mutating production infrastructure. Because generative models share pretraining priors and conform to peer rationales during deliberation, voting ensembles correlate errors instead of providing independent fault tolerance; yet attaching rigid deterministic checks to unconstrained agent outputs paralyzes incident remediation. We present Provenance-Isolated Epistemic Quorums (PIEQ), an execution-bound certification layer that keeps every language model strictly outside the trusted computing base. PIEQ unifies assumption-based truth maintenance, physical provenance isolation, control-theoretic plausible-world safety shielding, and linearizable concurrency governance around thre
sba37971e15.summary: PIEQ, a certification layer, is presented that keeps language models outside the trusted path and gates mutating production infrastructure actions on execution-bound evidence.
sba37971e15.why: Argues LLM agreement is not evidence for production changes, a design concern for teams letting agents perform incident remediation.

s06aa91feda.title: Spec-CoFrGeNet: Reparametrizing Continued Fraction Networks for Stable and Accurate Training
s06aa91feda.description: arXiv:2611.32041v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Continued fractions have been shown to be a function class capable of constructing expressive yet parameter-efficient neural networks. These neural networks are not only effective for supervised learning, but also for training LLMs. However, the rational form of this function class introduces poles when the denominator approaches zero, which prior work has avoided by enforcing a small positive (non-smooth) lower bound. We show that performance and training stability can be highly sensitive to the choice of this lower bound. In this work, we introduce a novel transformation of the partial denominators, inspired by its connection to the Green's function in physics, that mitigates the above issue elegantly by constraining the spectra of the co
s06aa91feda.summary: Spec-CoFrGeNet reparametrizes continued fraction networks to improve training stability and accuracy, including for LLM training, by addressing denominator pole issues.
s06aa91feda.why: Shows training stability can be highly sensitive to a lower-bound choice, a practical tuning detail for this architecture class.

s88446f2a86.title: Integral DeltaNet: Improved Linear Attention with Adaptive Memory Integration
s88446f2a86.description: arXiv:2611.32063v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear attention replaces softmax attention with a linear formulation, enabling linear-time computation with a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a growing key-value cache. These computational and memory advantages have attracted growing interest in linear attention for long-context language modeling. However, compressing past information into a fixed-size state causes memory collisions that hinder long-context understanding. Although DeltaNet mitigates memory collisions through delta-rule updates and Gated DeltaNet extends this approach with gating, these mechanisms may also discard information relevant to future predictions. To address this limitation, we introduce Integral DeltaNet, which maintains two complementary recurrent states:
s88446f2a86.summary: Integral DeltaNet is proposed as an improved linear attention method using adaptive memory integration to reduce memory collisions in long-context modeling.
s88446f2a86.why: Targets a known weakness of fixed-size linear attention states for long-context language models, relevant to efficiency-focused architecture choices.

s201608d0a6.title: The algorithmic behavioral sink: Modeling the transition to irreversible demographic collapse
s201608d0a6.description: arXiv:2611.32084v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In 2025, the vast majority of major global economies reported a Total Fertility Rate below the replacement level of 2.1. This synchronized collapse has persisted despite extensive pro-natalist financial interventions, revealing a structural limitation in conventional linear demographic models. This paper proposes that the ubiquity of mobile internet and Artificial Intelligence acts as a synthetic mating disruptor, precipitating a non-linear phase transition in human pair-bonding dynamics. Treating the marriage market as a complex system governed by thermodynamic constraints, we present a Fermi-Dirac selection model, using national income distributions as the input spectrum and fitted with Japanese longitudinal data to illustrate how digital
s201608d0a6.summary: A paper models mobile internet and AI as a synthetic mating disruptor, proposing a non-linear phase transition toward irreversible demographic collapse.

s6ee3f4f03f.title: MARGIN: A Risk-Aware Agent for Robot Program Refinement
s6ee3f4f03f.description: arXiv:2611.32093v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot-programming agents improve executable control policies through repeated testing and repair, yet binary success saturates while execution risk persists across unseen scenes. We introduce MARGIN, a risk-aware agent that converts successful robot rollouts into actionable evidence for program refinement. Its near-miss margin measures the fraction of the execution budget remaining in the slowest successful development rollout. The agent uses this signal to prioritize fragile programs, guide targeted repairs, and select revisions that preserve development success while increasing execution headroom. An exact safe-racing rule accelerates success-based candidate evaluation. We evaluate MARGIN across LIBERO-Pro, LIBERO-90, and Robosuite. In ou
s6ee3f4f03f.summary: MARGIN is a risk-aware robot-programming agent that uses a near-miss margin signal to prioritize fragile programs and guide targeted repairs.
s6ee3f4f03f.why: Shows using execution-risk signals beyond binary success to refine robot control programs, relevant to robotics teams testing across unseen scenes.

s08d3b54c51.title: Clinical3D-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Spatial Intelligence of Multimodal LLMs in Hospital Environments
s08d3b54c51.description: arXiv:2611.32094v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Spatial reasoning in hospitals requires tracking look-alike equipment, interpreting patient-relative directions, and judging passage widths, yet existing benchmarks provide limited coverage of these abilities. We introduce Clinical3D-Bench, a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions of eight types on egocentric walkthroughs of 373 hospital-room layouts. Layouts follow hospital design guidelines, answers are computed from the 3D scenes, and paired scene states test whether models change their answers when relevant evidence changes. Videos are photorealistic, and ten physicians screened the layouts. Among 35 multimodal large language models (MLLMs), the best open and proprietary models reach 45.7% and 53.6% macro accuracy, against 40.8% for a
s08d3b54c51.summary: Clinical3D-Bench is a simulated benchmark with 3,368 questions on hospital-room walkthroughs to evaluate spatial intelligence of multimodal LLMs.
s08d3b54c51.why: Provides a targeted benchmark for spatial reasoning in clinical environments, useful for teams assessing embodied or assistive models in hospitals.

s34f825354a.title: PreferenceScene: Personalized Indoor Scene Synthesis from Feedback
s34f825354a.description: arXiv:2611.32099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-scene methods turn a short instruction into a furnished 3D room, but the room that a particular person wants rarely comes across fully in words: many preferences surface only when the person sees a concrete room and can point to what they like and dislike in it. We therefore study personalized indoor scene synthesis under hidden user preferences: over several turns, a system shows a 3D scene, and the user, who sees only rendered images of the scene, replies with brief free-form feedback and a satisfaction score. The system must therefore bring the whole room toward the user's preferences from feedback that comments on only part of it at a time. It must also be able to change every part of the room, because a preference concerns not
s34f825354a.summary: PreferenceScene proposes personalized indoor scene synthesis that learns hidden user preferences from multi-turn free-form feedback and satisfaction scores on rendered 3D rooms.
s34f825354a.why: Demonstrates interactive preference elicitation for generative 3D content, though the abstract gives little on results.

s786666eee3.title: Duo: Towards Spatiotemporal Action Coordination in Bimanual Policies
s786666eee3.description: arXiv:2611.32108v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bimanual manipulation requires each arm to perform distinct motions while coordinating with the other. Common flow-based robotic policies combine both arms' actions into one token per future timestep, giving attention distinct positions across time but not across arms. We introduce Duo, a simple but effective design that models spatial and temporal dependencies within one shared action head. Specifically, Duo separates both arms into two action tokens per timestep, allowing each arm's motion to interact via cross-arm attention during flow matching. On RoboTwin 2.0, Duo improves the overall success of all four base policies, from 0.45B to 3.62B parameters, with gains of 12.55 and 9.02 percentage points for FLOWER (0.89B) and $\pi_{0.5}$ (3.6
s786666eee3.summary: Duo is a bimanual robot policy design that splits each arm into its own action token per timestep, enabling cross-arm attention within a shared action head.
s786666eee3.why: Offers an architectural change for coordinated two-arm manipulation policies, relevant to robotics teams building flow-based policies.

s4987f1f082.title: An Automated Framework Integrating Deep Learning and Anatomical Reasoning for Cardiac Phenotyping From CCTA
s4987f1f082.description: arXiv:2611.32114v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA) depicts coronary anatomy and cardiac fat, but segmentation alone does not ensure anatomically consistent measurements. We propose an automated framework that combines deep learning with anatomical reasoning for quantitative cardiac phenotyping. Its anatomical measurement module uses graph geometry, branch identity, and surrounding structures to define vessel-specific pericoronary adipose tissue (PCAT) sampling and a surrogate epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) compartment. The latter also generates training targets without requiring expert pericardium contours. A companion module quantifies coronary calcium on non-contrast CT. Component-wise benchmarking was conducted on five public datasets: Ima
s4987f1f082.summary: Researchers present an automated framework combining deep learning with anatomical reasoning to quantify pericoronary and epicardial fat from cardiac CCTA scans.
s4987f1f082.why: Shows how adding anatomical constraints can yield more consistent clinical measurements than segmentation alone, relevant to medical imaging pipelines.

sced2e4a964.title: VIDE : Training-Free Video Anomaly Detection via Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation
sced2e4a964.description: arXiv:2611.32138v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In embedding-based video anomaly detection (VAD), normal clips can have high similarity to anomalous descriptions, an anomaly bias that leads to false positives. Methods such as PRISM mitigate this bias by measuring deviations from a normality reference along anomaly directions. Both the normality reference and the anomaly directions are derived from text and shared across videos, although normal activity and the appearance of anomalies vary across scenes. The resulting scores are also sensitive to prompt selection. To address these limitations, we propose Visual Intrinsic Distribution Estimation (VIDE), a training-free framework that adapts text-derived scoring to each test video using frozen clip embeddings. VIDE estimates normal scene co
sced2e4a964.summary: VIDE proposes a training-free video anomaly detection method that estimates visual intrinsic distributions to reduce the false positives caused by anomaly bias in embedding-based approaches.
sced2e4a964.why: Training-free anomaly detection that adapts to each scene's normal activity could reduce false alarms without costly retraining for video surveillance systems.

sbca174bc1c.title: Calibrated Reading of Latent Reasoning and Communication
sbca174bc1c.description: arXiv:2611.32143v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent reasoning and key-value communication store intermediate information in continuous representations, limiting direct inspection of model behavior. Existing activation readers trade the low cost of task-specific probes against the flexibility of language-model decoders. We propose the Calibrated Latent Reader, CLR, a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content through task-conditioned interactions between states and candidate answers. Source adapters support transfer across models, while conformal calibration provides coverage and false-alarm guarantees under exchangeability. On two CODI models, CLR improves accuracy over MLP and attention probes by 4-18 percentage points for final-answer prediction and ref
sbca174bc1c.summary: Researchers introduce the Calibrated Latent Reader (CLR), a compact transformer that predicts reasoning outcomes and message content from latent model states, with conformal calibration.
sbca174bc1c.why: Offers a cheaper, more flexible way to inspect latent reasoning and key-value communication in models, aiding debugging and transparency.

seb4090b99e.title: RetraQ: Manifold-Constrained Critic Guidance for Flow Policies in RL
seb4090b99e.description: arXiv:2611.32148v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A learned critic can improve a pretrained flow-matching policy by steering sampled actions toward higher predicted value. However, even a critic that fits the behavior data well can provide misleading action gradients. Gradient components pointing away from the data-supported region are weakly constrained by behavior data and can lead guidance to exploit critic extrapolation errors. We introduce RetraQ (Retraction-based Q-guidance), which uses geometry encoded by the pretrained flow to constrain both the direction and the destination of critic guidance. A single velocity evaluation of the frozen flow defines a denoising map. RetraQ filters the critic gradient with the map's Jacobian and applies the map itself to correct the updated action.
seb4090b99e.summary: RetraQ is a method that uses pretrained flow geometry to constrain critic-guided action gradients, aiming to keep flow-matching RL policies within data-supported regions.
seb4090b99e.why: Addresses critic extrapolation errors when steering flow-matching policies, which matters for teams applying offline RL to robotics or control.

s34631157b3.title: Making Evaluation Explicit Is Not Enough: Supervising the Evaluation Process in Generative Reward Models
s34631157b3.description: arXiv:2611.32161v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative reward models (GRMs) make language-model evaluation more explicit by generating critiques, rubrics, or intermediate analyses before predicting a final preference. However, explicit evaluation does not necessarily imply a reliable evaluation process: under outcome-only supervision, a model may reach the correct final preference while producing weak or unsupported intermediate judgments, turning the evaluation into a post-hoc rationalization. We introduce STEP-GRM, a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation process of rubric-based GRMs. In addition to conventional preference supervision, STEP-GRM provides structural guidance for rubric construction and local supervision for criterion-level judgments, encouragi
s34631157b3.summary: STEP-GRM is a framework that directly supervises the intermediate evaluation steps of generative reward models, rather than only final preference outcomes.
s34631157b3.why: Suggests outcome-only training can yield unsupported intermediate judgments, a concern for teams relying on LLM-as-judge evaluation pipelines.

s9d4c2eb4dd.title: RightDiff: Learning Generative Reward Models to Judge by the Right Differences
s9d4c2eb4dd.description: arXiv:2611.32166v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative reward models typically rely on generic query-level rubrics or unconstrained rationales, overlooking the fact that pairwise preference is driven by response-specific differences. Moreover, optimizing solely for outcome correctness encourages models to exploit superficial shortcuts such as verbosity and formatting, triggering rationale drift. To address this, we propose RightDiff, which structures pairwise evaluation into an evidence-grounded evaluation trajectory executed in a single autoregressive generation. RightDiff explicitly discovers contrastive differences between candidates, categorizes them into material or immaterial factors, and induces pair-specific rubrics before final adjudication. To train this process without pos
s9d4c2eb4dd.summary: RightDiff is a generative reward model that structures pairwise evaluation around response-specific differences in a single autoregressive pass to reduce shortcut exploitation.
s9d4c2eb4dd.why: Targets verbosity and formatting shortcuts in LLM judges, relevant for teams building reliable automated preference evaluation.

s42ff764dde.title: Benchmarking Protein Structure Tokenizers as Generation Targets for Language Models
s42ff764dde.description: arXiv:2611.32168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Discrete structure tokenizers are the standard way to give a language model access to protein three-dimensional structure, yet they are selected on how accurately they can be read, their reconstruction fidelity, while the property that governs generation is how well a model can write them. We measure this property, writability, directly: holding the base model, data, recipe and compute fixed, we swap only the tokenizer and train the same 9B model to emit structure tokens residue by residue, over eight tokenizers, four compute budgets and three evaluation sets (96 cells). At 2B tokens final writability runs from TM 0.662 down to 0.378 under identical conditions, with five of the eight arms clearing the TM 0.5 mark at which a fold is usually
s42ff764dde.summary: The paper benchmarks eight protein structure tokenizers by training the same 9B model to generate structure tokens, measuring how well each tokenizer can be written by a language model.
s42ff764dde.why: Shows reconstruction fidelity is not the property that governs generation, which matters for teams choosing tokenizers for protein language models.

s8772181721.title: Mind the Band: The Hidden Frequency Variable in Geometric RoPE
s8772181721.description: arXiv:2611.32171v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Geometric rotary position encodings (RoPE) incorporate 3D camera geometry into multi-view attention by rotating token features according to viewing rays, depths, and reprojected image coordinates. Each coordinate is rotated across a progression of frequencies--its frequency band--yet existing implementations leave this band to inherited defaults, either retaining standard 2D RoPE's top frequency or letting the frequency span grow exponentially with the attention head dimension. We show that this unstandardized setting can reverse benchmark rankings. In novel view synthesis on RealEstate10K, RayRoPE matches the strongest baseline in the 47M model (144-channel heads), yet trails by 1.2 dB in the 25M model (48-channel heads), and exhibits the
s8772181721.summary: The paper shows that unstandardized frequency bands in geometric RoPE for multi-view attention can reverse benchmark rankings, and examines this hidden variable.
s8772181721.why: Implementation defaults for positional encodings can silently change benchmark results, so teams comparing multi-view models should standardize them.

sf38fc13b4c.title: DocPristine: Content-Aware Document Appearance Enhancement under Real-World Mixed Degradations
sf38fc13b4c.description: arXiv:2611.32176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Camera-captured documents often exhibit mixed degradations, such as highlights, shadows, and blur, that distort backgrounds and obscure text details. Document appearance enhancement (DAE) aims to mitigate these degradations and improve readability. Existing document appearance enhancement methods rely either on input-derived visual cues that can become unreliable under severe degradation or on LLM-based degradation diagnosis that lacks spatial guidance. Notably, we find that pretrained document visual encoders continue to attend to text regions in degraded documents, providing content-aware guidance. Based on this insight, we propose DocPristine, which adaptively fuses multi-layer features from a frozen document visual encoder and injects t
sf38fc13b4c.summary: DocPristine is a content-aware document appearance enhancement method that targets mixed real-world degradations such as highlights, shadows, and blur in camera-captured documents.
sf38fc13b4c.why: Addresses document image cleanup under combined degradations, relevant for teams building OCR or document ingestion pipelines.

sb0ac2249d7.title: ThinkMorph-SSL: Scaling Interleaved Multimodal Reasoning with Pretext Tasks
sb0ac2249d7.description: arXiv:2611.32183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: People reason with pictures as well as words. Interleaved multimodal reasoning gives models a similar way to solve problems by creating intermediate images and using them to guide further reasoning. Training models with this ability usually relies on task-specific demonstrations, which are difficult to collect. We introduce ThinkMorph-SSL, a two-stage training recipe that uses images themselves as a source of supervision. The first stage, pretext reasoning, converts visual pretext tasks, such as image colorization and denoising, into instruction-free interleaved traces. Models describe a corrupted or transformed image, generate a restored or canonical image, and interpret the result. The second stage uses automatically constructed demonstra
sb0ac2249d7.summary: ThinkMorph-SSL is a two-stage training recipe that uses image pretext tasks like colorization and denoising to supervise interleaved multimodal reasoning without task-specific demonstrations.
sb0ac2249d7.why: Reduces reliance on hard-to-collect demonstrations for training models that reason through intermediate images.

s2637157992.title: Blaming the Machine, Billing the Victim? How Mock Jurors Reassign Fault from Generative AI Systems and Respond to Liability Cliffs in Tort
s2637157992.description: arXiv:2611.32188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI complicates tort liability attribution when people blame a generative AI system that cannot itself bear legally relevant fault. We investigate where this blame goes when fault must be allocated among legal persons, and whether American discontinuous apportionment doctrines influence mock jurors' factual findings of fault. Such doctrines include Contributory negligence, Joint and several liability, and their 50% or 51% variations, all of which have a fault-percentage threshold or a "cliff" where the victim-entitled compensation (or a defendant's liability) jumps to zero (or to all compensatory damages). Our pre-registered human subjects experiment (N=199 Prolific participants) shows that as many U.S. mock jurors (36%) blame the
s2637157992.summary: A study of mock jurors examines how they reassign fault from generative AI systems to legal persons and how contributory negligence and joint liability thresholds affect findings.
s2637157992.why: Shows how liability doctrines may shape blame allocation involving AI systems, relevant for legal and risk planning for AI deployers.

s6a94137cb0.title: SolarFilNet-V4: Multi-Scale Transformer Vision with Physics-Informed Adaptive Post-Processing for Solar Filament Segmentation
s6a94137cb0.description: arXiv:2611.32193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solar filaments are cool, dense chromospheric plasma structures held by magnetic field lines above polarity inversion lines. Their destabilization triggers coronal mass ejections and severe space weather hazards. Segmenting individual filaments from ground-based GONG H-alpha observations (2048 x 2048 pixels) is challenging due to low contrast, turbulent fibrils, delicate barb structures, and annotator boundary variance. In this technical report, we describe SolarFilNet-V4, a targeted segmentation framework developed for the MAGFiLO 1.0 benchmark (Solar Filament Segmentation Challenge 2026). Our method couples a lightweight Pyramid Vision Transformer (PVT-v2-B1) backbone with anisotropic curvilinear strip convolutions (k=15) and dual-frequen
s6a94137cb0.summary: SolarFilNet-V4 is a multi-scale transformer segmentation framework with physics-informed post-processing for segmenting solar filaments in GONG H-alpha observations.

s86c63cf108.title: LLM Agent Authorization Across Context Compaction
s86c63cf108.description: arXiv:2611.32194v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Request-derived authorizers such as Progent protect LLM agents from prompt injection by deriving what an agent may do from the user's request. Their guarantee rests on attribution: the request is taken to be what the user said. Compaction breaks it. At every automatic compaction we observed, Claude Code and Codex placed a model-written summary of earlier turns as a user message, so the compactor's quotation of the user, documents and injected text reads as the user speaking. Because a policy frozen at the first request lets the agent finish few later tasks, we let Progent derive its policy for each request, and find that what it grants then follows what the compactor wrote. Even a payee the user stated is not safe: when an attacker's notice
s86c63cf108.summary: The paper shows that request-derived authorization for LLM agents breaks during automatic context compaction, because summaries of earlier turns are placed as user messages in Claude Code and Codex.
s86c63cf108.why: Reveals a prompt-injection gap in agent authorization, so teams running coding agents with compaction should not assume request-based policies remain enforced.

sa940e2c5f4.title: When Answering Is Administering: Permission Replies That Rewrite Coding-Agent Policy
sa940e2c5f4.description: arXiv:2611.32195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents let plugins and remote services answer permission prompts, and Claude Code documents that such an answer cannot override the operator's deny rules. However, we show that this guarantee, checked one decision at a time, fails over a whole run, because an answer to one permission prompt can rewrite the policy that every later answer is checked against. For example, a remote service with no access to the operator's files approves an unrelated command and attaches an update that deletes the deny rule protecting the project's secrets. The agent then reads the secrets in that session and the next, even inside the vendor's strict sandbox. The root cause is that Claude Code checks only updates that add or replace allow rules. Relays th
sa940e2c5f4.summary: The paper shows that permission replies to coding agents can rewrite the policy checked on later decisions, letting a remote service delete deny rules across a run.
sa940e2c5f4.why: Demonstrates that per-decision permission checks can fail over a whole run, a concrete risk for teams granting plugins or remote services approval rights.

sad7f78b9d9.title: Steerable by Design: Conditional Pretraining for Robust Control of Language Models
sad7f78b9d9.description: arXiv:2611.32199v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Our goal is to build language models that are steerable by design. Today's language models are pretrained with next-token prediction, which relegates alignment and control to the final 1% of training tokens or inference-time interventions. These models repurpose a single input channel for both instructions and data, leading to common failure modes where the model mistakenly treats data as instructions such as intentional jailbreaks and unintentional in-context alignment drift. To correct this, we propose a pretraining method and architecture that separates the two from the very start, producing Mancelle-3B. An encoder processes high-level semantic features of upcoming text with cross-attention that prevents the token stream from writing bac
sad7f78b9d9.summary: The paper proposes a conditional pretraining method and architecture that separates instructions from data so language models are steerable by design rather than only aligned at the end.
sad7f78b9d9.why: Aims to reduce jailbreaks and in-context alignment drift by separating instruction and data channels during pretraining.

s98e5f4cc75.title: Who gets the information? An $\alpha$-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection
s98e5f4cc75.description: arXiv:2611.32200v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent information-theoretic filters for multi-label feature selection disagree on how to distribute relevance over labels: some amplify features that inform a few labels, others balance what every label receives. We show these choices are implicit social welfare functions. Treating labels as agents whose utility is the information they receive, we propose FLIC, which greedily maximises the $\alpha$-fair welfare of per-label information coverage. A single parameter $\alpha$ moves from utilitarian ($\alpha=0$) through proportionally fair ($\alpha=1$) to max-min selection ($\alpha\to\infty$), and a dozen published relevance terms lie on this axis, most as special cases, first-order approximations or limits. The objective is monotone submodula
s98e5f4cc75.summary: FLIC is an alpha-fair label-coverage framework for multi-label feature selection that treats labels as agents whose information utility is balanced via a welfare function.
s98e5f4cc75.why: Offers a tunable fairness parameter for feature selection across labels, though its practical impact for engineering teams is limited.

s1c2cab2037.title: OmniEVIE: Evidence-Vector-Informed Embedding for Multi-modal Retrieval
s1c2cab2037.description: arXiv:2611.32203v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal retrieval must match dense pages, fine-grained entities, ordered video, and agent tools and memory. Single-vector embeddings lose local evidence, cross-encoders reread every recalled item online, and uncompressed late interaction is too large to serve. We present OmniEVIE, a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools with one compressed index and a three-stage retriever. Each record stores at most 128 int8 vectors of dimension 64 (9,472 bytes, or 8.82 GiB per million records), providing a mean vector, 1-bit signs, and int8 multi-vectors for coarse, middle, and final search while localizing each hit to a page region or video interval. Training, merging, indexing, and retrieval are c
s1c2cab2037.summary: OmniEVIE is a 4.5B multi-vector embedding model covering text, images, visual documents, video, and tools, using one compressed index and a three-stage retriever.
s1c2cab2037.why: It offers a compressed multi-vector approach to multimodal retrieval, aiming to keep local evidence while remaining cheap enough to serve at scale.

s3b65fc2005.title: Joint Classification and Generation on Tabular Data: an Empirical Study
s3b65fc2005.description: arXiv:2611.32225v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many applications of machine learning on tabular data need both a classifier and a generator of realistic records. The default is to train two separate models, whereas a single joint model promises both from one set of weights. Several families of tabular deep learning models can be turned into such a joint model, which raises the question of which joint model is preferable at which computational budget. In this empirical study, we introduce and compare joint models based on four state-of-the-art tabular data modeling families (energy-based models, probabilistic circuits, tabular foundation models and tabular diffusion models) against measured FLOPs and wall-clock time, on 29 classification datasets. Methods are evaluated based on two defin
s3b65fc2005.summary: Researchers present an empirical study comparing joint models that both classify and generate realistic tabular records, built from four tabular deep learning families.
s3b65fc2005.why: It informs whether one shared model can replace two separate classifier and generator models at a given compute budget.

sf53e2cf979.title: Roboclock: A Unified Benchmark for Time-Aware Robotic Intelligence
sf53e2cf979.description: arXiv:2611.32233v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Time is a fundamental dimension of robotic intelligence: a robot may fail despite physically correct actions if it acts outside a valid time window, responds too slowly to an event, or fails to meet required throughput. Yet existing robotic benchmarks primarily emphasize spatial correctness and logical task completion, largely overlooking the temporal constraints of real-world applications. We present RoboClock, a unified benchmark for time-aware robotic manipulation featuring 60 tasks across five application domains. Mirroring these failure modes, RoboClock structures tasks around three types of temporal constraints: Temporal Window, Event-Reactive, and Throughput. Furthermore, RoboClock incorporates a Latency-Aligned evaluation protocol t
sf53e2cf979.summary: Researchers introduced RoboClock, a benchmark with 60 tasks across five domains that tests time-aware robotic manipulation, including temporal constraints.
sf53e2cf979.why: Current robotics benchmarks overlook timing constraints, so this gives teams a way to test throughput and response-time failures.

sa8b12218dc.title: Boundary-Aware Policy Learning for Agent-Orchestrated Robot Manipulation
sa8b12218dc.description: arXiv:2611.32238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent-orchestrated robot systems combine the general reasoning capability of multimodal agents with the precise physical control of learned visuomotor policies. Yet such systems often fail at the moment of handoff: a policy is reliable only from a limited set of start states, while the agent may invoke it outside this region. We call this region the policy's handoff boundary. Existing whole-task policies typically have handoff boundaries that are narrow and difficult for an agent to characterize, making reliable coordination challenging. We propose Boundary-Aware Policy Learning, which explicitly shapes and then expands the handoff boundary of a visuomotor policy. First, Boundary-Explicit Training fine-tunes the policy on contact segments w
sa8b12218dc.summary: Researchers propose boundary-aware policy learning to address handoff failures when an agent invokes a robot manipulation policy outside its reliable start states.
sa8b12218dc.why: Handoff failures between agents and learned visuomotor policies are a practical reliability problem for agent-orchestrated robot systems.

s536e8407fd.title: CoMNO: Commutator Memory Neural Operators for Long-Horizon PDE Prediction
s536e8407fd.description: arXiv:2611.32274v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Solving nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs) over long time horizons is computationally expensive using traditional numerical methods. While neural operators provide an efficient alternative, they suffer from the accumulation of approximation errors along the predicted trajectory, typically caused by the failure to capture fine-scale details. In this work, we design a Commutator Memory Neural Operator that identifies fine-scale dynamical details by commuting two operations and leverages these details to enhance the neural operator's capability in capturing fine-scale features over long time horizons. Specifically, we identify a performance gap between two operations: downsampling the high-resolution field before rollout predictio
s536e8407fd.summary: Researchers present CoMNO, a Commutator Memory Neural Operator designed to reduce error accumulation in long-horizon nonlinear PDE predictions.
s536e8407fd.why: Neural operators that stay accurate over long horizons could make PDE simulation cheaper than traditional numerical methods.

s99502c3ca2.title: Reproducing the Speech Labels of Qwen3-Omni's Talker: Mimi in bf16, and a Last-Frame Pitfall
s99502c3ca2.description: arXiv:2611.32286v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Qwen3-Omni speaks through a Talker predicting 16 codebooks of a 12.5 Hz audio codec, but the encoder that made its training labels was not released, so new voices cannot be trained on matching labels. We identify this encoder from the released model's behavior. White-box regression shows that the codebook embeddings of the Talker, its multi-token predictor and the Code2Wav decoder match the first 16 codebooks of kyutai's Mimi layer by layer. A decoder-based test looks convincing but fails calibration: decoders trained on known labels cannot tell them apart. Teacher-forced Talker likelihoods, calibrated with 13 code language models trained on known labels, do tell implementations apart: the Talker prefers labels from kyutai's moshi package w
s99502c3ca2.summary: Researchers reverse-engineered the speech codec labels behind Qwen3-Omni's Talker, finding they match kyutai's Mimi codec in bf16 and documenting a calibration pitfall.
s99502c3ca2.why: Recovering the unreleased encoder lets teams train new voices on matching labels, though the paper flags pitfalls in verification.

s2fa93f2178.title: DAiSy: Online Data Selection by Adaptive Utility Estimation for LLM Pretraining
s2fa93f2178.description: arXiv:2611.32294v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Model-aware online data selection prioritizes the training documents that contribute the most given the model's current state. Existing online selectors rank candidates upon gradient-based data utility scores, which requires the full forward-backward pass of the main model on every candidate document. Scoring each document therefore pays as much as training on it, yet only a small fraction is used for the real model update. We introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that learns to predict data utility scores from frozen document embeddings, which eliminates the computation overhead and infrastructure burdens. The linear estimator is updated alongside the main language model, fitting to the exact gradient-based utility scores o
s2fa93f2178.summary: Researchers introduce DAiSy, a lightweight linear auxiliary model that predicts data utility scores from frozen document embeddings for online LLM pretraining data selection.
s2fa93f2178.why: It avoids a full forward-backward pass per candidate document, which could cut the cost of online data selection during pretraining.

sd0f7225165.title: Query-Guided Visual Minimization for Selective Disclosure to Cloud VLMs
sd0f7225165.description: arXiv:2611.32302v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cloud-hosted vision-language models (VLMs) require sending images beyond the user's local trust boundary, potentially exposing sensitive information the query does not need. We study query-guided visual minimization: a trusted local transformation preserves query-relevant visual content and reduces unnecessary disclosure before transmission. Unlike query-agnostic anonymization, it preserves the same sensitive content when the query requires it and suppresses it otherwise. We introduce QGVM, a framework that combines query grounding with an independent sensitive-item inventory, determines disclosure necessity at the type, instance, and text-content levels, and renders a minimized image for a black-box downstream VLM. We evaluate QGVM on comp
sd0f7225165.summary: Researchers propose QGVM, a framework that locally minimizes images to disclose only query-relevant visual content before sending them to cloud vision-language models.
sd0f7225165.why: Teams sending images to cloud VLMs can reduce exposure of sensitive content the query does not need.

s4f8a4b9b16.title: ASTERISM: Do Multimodal LLMs Actually Look at All the Images?
s4f8a4b9b16.description: arXiv:2611.32316v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-image benchmarks aim to test whether a multimodal large language model (MLLM) combines evidence across images, but many of their items can be answered from a single image. Across about 33k items from 19 public benchmarks, our audit and a two-stage single-image filter find that one image or the question alone settles 24.2% of them. On these items, MLLMs recover from one image a median 78% of the accuracy that all images add over the text alone, so these items reward answering from one image, which we call the single-image shortcut. MLLMs take this shortcut even on items where one image is not enough. On such items, most of their wrong answers repeat an answer they give from one image, at a rate well above chance. We build ASTERISM, to
s4f8a4b9b16.summary: An audit of about 33k items from 19 multi-image benchmarks finds that 24.2% can be answered from a single image or the question alone, a shortcut MLLMs exploit.
s4f8a4b9b16.why: Benchmark scores may overstate multi-image reasoning, so teams should check whether evaluations actually require combining images.

s1996ce42d6.title: SPRUNN: Structural Proximity for Pruning in Deep Neural Networks
s1996ce42d6.description: arXiv:2611.32317v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) have demonstrated significant accuracy across various machine learning tasks. However, these networks suffer from a huge number of parameters and computations, which leads to time-consuming processes. Consequently, parameter pruning approaches have been proposed to compress DNNs and efficiently implement them. The main challenge in pruning is selecting the appropriate parameters for pruning without significantly damaging the accuracy. In this paper, we propose SPRUNN, an algorithmic pruning approach based on the structural proximity criterion for filter pruning in convolutional layers of deep neural networks. Structural Proximity (SP) calculates filter similarity by considering all filters and comparing each one
s1996ce42d6.summary: Researchers propose SPRUNN, a structural-proximity-based pruning approach for deep neural networks that aims to reduce parameters without large accuracy loss.
s1996ce42d6.why: Pruning that preserves accuracy could make deploying compressed DNNs faster and cheaper.

s69886e8810.title: When Exact Token Importance Is Not Enough: Limits of Top-K Selection in LLM Attention
s69886e8810.description: arXiv:2611.32324v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long-context language models often retain only a limited set of past token positions for an attention query. A common strategy scores positions individually and keeps the highest-ranked K. Yet attention weights are renormalized over the chosen set: two individually important positions need not form the best pair. We ask whether independent ranking suffices even when each importance score measures the exact downstream change in next-token predictions caused by deleting that position alone. It does not. A four-position construction makes the ranked pair incur 133.2 times the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence of the optimal pair, and a parametric family proves that this multiplicative gap is unbounded. An exact exchange identity and preference
s69886e8810.summary: A paper shows that ranking token positions independently by exact importance and keeping the top K can fail in LLM attention, because attention weights renormalize over the chosen set.
s69886e8810.why: Top-K KV cache selection heuristics may pick suboptimal token sets, which matters for long-context inference design.

s3e21e7f1c7.title: A recursive self-improvement framework for electron microscopy analysis
s3e21e7f1c7.description: arXiv:2611.32325v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Resolving local atomic structures such as defects and interfaces from electron microscopy contrast relies heavily on researcher judgement, leading to low efficiency and subjective standards. Here we present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided and expert-informed recursive self-improvement framework that turns one-off human corrections into reusable, verifiable capabilities by updating executable operators, parameters and routing rules with versioned inheritance. Given researcher-defined tasks, the system selects analysis paths from image features without expert labels, while testing and inheriting code updates under fixed budgets. Combining physical priors with expert feedback improves atomic point-defect detection over larger models and raise
s3e21e7f1c7.summary: Researchers present PhyEvo-Mic-RSI, a physics-guided recursive self-improvement framework that turns expert corrections into reusable, versioned analysis operators for electron microscopy.
s3e21e7f1c7.why: It shows a method for capturing one-off expert corrections as reusable, verifiable pipeline components in scientific analysis.

s92e4c99e9f.title: Part-Set Prototypes for Explainable Mountain Gazelles Sex Classification
s92e4c99e9f.description: arXiv:2611.32343v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-explainable visual models for fine-grained recognition are often hindered by rigid geometric constraints that cannot capture diverse semantic shapes in unconstrained "in-the-wild" imagery. Real-world camera-trap data introduces challenges, including non-optimal poses, lighting variations, occlusions, animal camouflage, and environmental shortcuts. To address this, we introduce set prototypes, a general architecture where both part cardinality and unconstrained spatial layouts are mined directly from data. Our joint-matching formulation places parts simultaneously on a frozen DINOv3 token grid via truncated Sinkhorn competition, allowing unsupported parts to abstain without spatial collapse. We evaluate our approach on Mountain Gazelle
s92e4c99e9f.summary: Researchers introduce set prototypes for self-explainable visual classification of mountain gazelle sex from camera-trap images.
s92e4c99e9f.why: The text gives little on broader engineering implications beyond this specific wildlife classification application.

s1bdfcb7f36.title: DiCT: Teaching X-ray Vision-Language Models to Reason via Imagining CT
s1bdfcb7f36.description: arXiv:2611.32344v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Diagnosing with X-rays often requires reasoning about the 3D locations of abnormalities and their spatial relationships to surrounding anatomical structures, yet such reasoning remains challenging due to the loss of spatial information in 2D projections. To address this challenge, we propose Dreaming in CT (DiCT), a three-stage progressive CT-to-X-ray reasoning transfer framework that leverages a CT vision-language model (VLM) to guide an X-ray VLM. Through this CT-guided transfer, the student acquires CT-informed 3D reasoning capabilities, enabling it to reason directly from 2D X-rays without explicit CT reconstruction at inference time. The framework begins with instruct the dreamer, which equips the X-ray student with initial CT-oriented
s1bdfcb7f36.summary: Researchers propose DiCT, a three-stage framework where a CT vision-language model guides an X-ray VLM to acquire CT-informed 3D reasoning for diagnosis.

s56549f038d.title: Validating Multi-Model AI-Generated Acceptance Criteria in Requirements Engineering
s56549f038d.description: arXiv:2611.32374v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in software engineering to generate artifacts such as requirements, user stories, acceptance criteria, documentation, and code. Their use in requirements engineering raises important questions about correctness, traceability, and hallucination, especially because flawed specifications can affect later design, implementation, and verification activities. While much recent work on AI-assisted software engineering has focused on code generation and code-level validation, the validation of AI-generated specifications has received less attention. This paper addresses this gap by presenting a validation-oriented approach for AI-generated acceptance criteria. The approach combines retrieval-augmen
s56549f038d.summary: A paper studies validating AI-generated acceptance criteria in requirements engineering, focusing on correctness, traceability, and hallucination in LLM-generated specifications.
s56549f038d.why: Flawed AI-generated requirements can propagate into design, implementation, and verification, so validation of these artifacts matters.

s428263e91c.title: Does Research-Paper Context Improve LLM-Generated Quadruped Navigation? An Exploratory Simulation Study
s428263e91c.description: arXiv:2611.32381v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models can write competent robot navigation code, but not only does the research on the topic advance, a model may also, due to the volume of findings, fail to recall relevant findings and apply them to the task at hand. In this work, we test whether providing particular research papers as context improves the LLM-written navigation code for the Go2 quadruped, with the LLM (Claude Opus 5) and locomotion policy frozen. Specifically, we compare the navigation controllers the LLM writes when provided with and without particular papers across three settings: behavior trees, navigators edited from a shared base, and controllers written from scratch. When a maze's shortest route is blocked mid-episode, 2 of 8 controllers written wi
s428263e91c.summary: Researchers test whether giving an LLM relevant research papers as context improves the navigation code it writes for a Go2 quadruped robot in simulation.
s428263e91c.why: It suggests retrieving domain research may improve LLM-generated robot control code, though the abstract alone gives limited evidence of the results.

sfdbf0586a2.title: Evolve to Learn: Gradient-aligned experience evolution for model self-improvement
sfdbf0586a2.description: arXiv:2611.32390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving language models can continuously acquire useful experience through test-time interaction, reflection, and prompt optimization, yet turning such experience into model itself to ensure self improvement remains challenging. On-policy self-distillation (OPSD) provides a natural mechanism for internalizing test-time information into model parameters, yet it largely assumes that the gener- ated experience is worth learning. We show that this assumption does not always hold: experiences that improve test-time performance may provide limited or even harmful training signals. To better characterize which experience should be inter- nalized, we systematically analyze diverse mutated experiences across multiple tasks and reflection model
sfdbf0586a2.summary: Researchers propose gradient-aligned experience evolution, arguing that on-policy self-distillation should only internalize experiences that are actually worth learning for model self-improvement.
sfdbf0586a2.why: Experiences that improve test-time performance may not be worth training into weights, so teams building self-improving models need filtering.

sa97a49c04e.title: Not All Pairs Align: Caption-Guided Audio-Visual Contrastive Learning
sa97a49c04e.description: arXiv:2611.32399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We address the problem of learning audio-visual representations from co-occurring modalities. Multimodal contrastive learning typically assumes that paired observations provide shared views of the same underlying information. While this may be true for datasets collected in constrained environments, it does not always hold. For instance, co-occurring audio and visual signals can differ substantially in their content due to off-screen sounds. Nevertheless, standard contrastive objectives treat all paired samples as equally aligned. In this work, we propose Caption Guided Alignment Aware Loss (CGAAL), a model-agnostic objective that leverages modality-specific captions to estimate semantic agreement between audio and video. CGAAL uses these a
sa97a49c04e.summary: Researchers propose caption-guided audio-visual contrastive learning, arguing standard objectives wrongly treat all audio-visual pairs as equally aligned despite off-screen sounds.
sa97a49c04e.why: Standard multimodal contrastive training may learn from misaligned pairs, so pair-quality handling could matter for multimodal representation training.

sbd84689e4b.title: Verify then Steer: Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery for Continuous Vision-and-Language Navigation
sbd84689e4b.description: arXiv:2611.32400v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) requires an agent to follow language instructions to reach a target in an unseen 3D environment. However, existing methods still struggle to recover from route deviations at test time. We investigate this limitation through the lens of instruction progress, and trace it to a phenomenon we term progress hallucination: agents misinterpret off-route observations as evidence of task progress, causing their internal instruction progress to advance beyond the actual task stage and hindering recovery based on earlier sub-instructions. To address this failure mode, we propose PHAR (Progress Hallucination-Aware Recovery), a test-time recovery framework following a verify-then-steer paradigm. The verifier examines
sbd84689e4b.summary: Researchers identify progress hallucination in vision-and-language navigation, where agents mistake off-route observations for task progress, and propose a verify-then-steer recovery method.
sbd84689e4b.why: Agents that misjudge task progress after route deviations can fail to recover, a reliability issue for embodied AI deployments.

s3152e3ca49.title: CPU-Eval: Evaluating Large Language Models for CPU Hardware Code Generation
s3152e3ca49.description: arXiv:2611.32405v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Benchmarks such as VerilogEval have supported rapid advances in hardware description language (HDL) generation by large language models (LLMs). However, recent HDL-generation systems achieve pass rates above 90% on VerilogEval, leaving limited headroom for revealing further advances. To provide a challenging target for further progress on a practically important hardware-development task, we introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 HDL-generation problems constructed from six CPUs. Drawn from practical CPU designs, including families fabricated in silicon, the problems span CPUs from small embedded cores to Linux-capable out-of-order cores and cover diverse CPU functions written in SystemVerilog, Chisel, and SpinalHDL. In each problem, an LLM
s3152e3ca49.summary: Researchers introduce CPU-Eval, a benchmark of 339 hardware description language generation problems drawn from six CPU designs, to test LLMs beyond saturated VerilogEval.
s3152e3ca49.why: Hardware code generation teams get a harder benchmark, since leading systems already exceed 90% pass rates on VerilogEval.

s6687635029.title: BEACON: Learning Observation-Conditioned Starting Points for Guided Conditional Flow Matching in Microscopy
s6687635029.description: arXiv:2611.32406v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fluorescence microscopy drives much of modern life science, but accessible imaging setups often yield images degraded by out-of-focus light, limited resolution, and strong signal-dependent noise. Computational restoration can recover high-quality images from such data, enabling cheaper and faster imaging at lower light dose, provided biologically meaningful structures are preserved. Guided conditional flow matching has recently shown strong results for microscopy dehazing and computational super-resolution by learning distributions of plausible restorations. However, it pairs each clean target with an independent standard Gaussian sample, so the starting point of every training path does not leverage the degraded observation. This arbitrary
s6687635029.summary: Researchers present BEACON, which learns observation-conditioned starting points for guided conditional flow matching to restore degraded fluorescence microscopy images.
s6687635029.why: It offers a method for computational microscopy restoration that aims to preserve biologically meaningful structures while enabling lower light dose imaging.

s857c0ca850.title: Within-task hazards of AI agents: unidentified by time-horizon curves, identified by repeated runs
s857c0ca850.description: arXiv:2611.32415v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The time horizon of an AI agent is read off a curve: the probability that the agent completes a task, plotted against the time a human needs for it. Several recent analyses fit survival models to this curve and conclude that agents' hazard of failure declines as a task goes on. The curve cannot support that conclusion. Every log-logistic horizon curve with slope $\beta\le1$ is a mixture of constant-hazard curves, and in a proportional-hazards frailty model the same curve is produced by every within-task Weibull shape $k\ge\beta$. If runs of a task are conditionally independent, repeated runs restore identification within this model: the probability that two runs both succeed is the single-run curve shifted by $1/k$ on the $\log_2$ time axis
s857c0ca850.summary: A paper argues that AI agent time-horizon curves cannot show whether failure hazard declines within a task, and that repeated runs are needed to identify within-task hazards.
s857c0ca850.why: Teams relying on time-horizon curves to judge agent reliability may draw wrong conclusions about failure patterns; repeated-run data is needed.

s46a7e8b4bd.title: NRG-Twins: Pixel-Level Ground Truth for Rigidity Violations in Generated Videos
s46a7e8b4bd.description: arXiv:2611.32431v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generators now produce realistic clips of scenes and objects, which makes generated video an attractive source of 3D content. Yet generated video is not 3D consistent: static content slowly deforms or slides, 3D reconstruction degrades, and the errors are too subtle to label by hand. To make generators 3D consistent, or to build rewards and guidance that push them there, we need data that say where and by how much a generated video breaks rigidity, and these data must come from generated video itself. We obtain per-pixel ground-truth labels from real-generated twins: a real clip paired with its re-creation by a keyframe-conditioned video generator. After inserting real keyframes so that the twin camera roughly follows the real one, we
s46a7e8b4bd.summary: Researchers present NRG-Twins, a method providing pixel-level ground-truth labels for rigidity violations in generated videos, to help make video generators more 3D consistent.
s46a7e8b4bd.why: Generated video often deforms static content, and per-pixel labels could support training rewards or guidance for more 3D-consistent generators.

s30ca383440.title: See the Answer, Learn to Embed: Learning Universal Multimodal Embeddings from Hindsight
s30ca383440.description: arXiv:2611.32439v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Universal Multimodal Embedding (UME) models map heterogeneous multimodal inputs into a shared embedding space, where pairwise similarity supports diverse downstream tasks. Recent reasoning-driven UME approaches use intermediate reasoning to generate additional context for embedding, but often incur extra computation at inference. In this paper, we explore the matched candidate (i.e., the paired target) as an alternative source of context, asking whether a model can "see the answer" during training and "learn to embed" without it at inference. However, direct conditioning on this privileged context can introduce candidate-specific information unavailable from the query alone or cause the candidate-conditioned query representation to collapse
s30ca383440.summary: Researchers propose learning universal multimodal embeddings by letting models see the matched candidate during training, avoiding extra inference-time reasoning computation.
s30ca383440.why: Training with hindsight context could yield embedding models that avoid the added inference cost of reasoning-driven approaches.

sb7492e3653.title: Describe, Don't Ask: Caption-Driven On-Policy Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Perception
sb7492e3653.description: arXiv:2611.32463v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) often recognize fine-grained details more accurately in a relevant crop than in the full image. Multimodal on-policy distillation (OPD) methods exploit this by transferring the advantage of a crop-view teacher to a full-image student. However, their supervision relies on region-specific questions curated through an elaborate synthesis pipeline, which brings three weaknesses: (1) every region needs a question--answer pair written exclusively for it, locking training into costly QA curation that is hard to scale to unlabeled images; (2) all rollouts of a region answer the same question, so the teacher supervises only the details it asks about, leaving other visual elements in the region unsupervised; and (3) ever
sb7492e3653.summary: Researchers propose caption-driven on-policy distillation to improve vision-language models' fine-grained perception, reducing reliance on costly region-specific question-answer curation.
sb7492e3653.why: Replacing per-region QA curation with captions could make fine-grained visual distillation easier to scale for multimodal training pipelines.

s845fbc3039.title: Gamification in the age of AI: surveying player perceptions of motivation, manipulation, and data protection
s845fbc3039.description: arXiv:2611.32464v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern games and applications increasingly employ artificial intelligence (AI), user modeling, and gamification to influence user behavior, sustain engagement, and monetize attention. Although these mechanisms can enhance motivation and enjoyment, they also raise concerns about manipulation, personal data usage, and transparency. To examine how players perceive these dynamics, we conducted a survey with 28 adult participants. Respondents expressed strong concerns about the collection and exploitation of personal information in games and gamified applications, while also reporting low awareness and a limited sense of control over how their data is used. They evaluated progression features such as leveling systems and leaderboards as motivati
s845fbc3039.summary: A survey of 28 adults finds players are concerned about manipulation, personal data collection, and transparency in AI-driven gamification.
s845fbc3039.why: Small survey of player attitudes; relevant mainly to teams designing engagement features that use user modeling and personal data.

s6a9f9450ad.title: Progressive Reliable Supervision for Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation
s6a9f9450ad.description: arXiv:2611.32474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Black-Box Universal Domain Adaptation (B$^2$-UniDA) aims to adapt a target model to an unlabeled target domain under arbitrary label-space relationships, while neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible during adaptation. Under such restrictive information access, reliable target supervision is unavailable, while predictions from the black-box source model can be unreliable due to source bias and domain shifts. To address this challenge, we propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS), which progressively establishes and refines reliable target supervision by coordinating complementary knowledge from the black-box source model, foundation models, and the evolving target model. PReS first identifies reliable known samp
s6a9f9450ad.summary: Researchers propose Progressive Reliable Supervision (PReS) for black-box universal domain adaptation, where neither source data nor source-model parameters are accessible.
s6a9f9450ad.why: Adapting models without source data or parameters addresses a restrictive deployment setting, though the abstract offers limited detail on results.

s18394dd955.title: CodeWAM: A Code World Action Model for End-to-End Autonomous Driving
s18394dd955.description: arXiv:2611.32483v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Driving world models anticipate action consequences through representations of how the world evolves. For autonomous driving, these representations must capture both the surrounding scene and the ego vehicle's motion under a candidate plan. We propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that incorporates executable code as part of its world representation. Code represents ego dynamics by expressing how the vehicle state evolves under plan execution, while a learned visual model captures scene-dependent consequences. Executing the code produces a candidate-conditioned motion sequence, which is evaluated relative to the prior plan and recorded motion history. The resulting execution consequences and learned scene outcomes jointly represent the can
s18394dd955.summary: Researchers propose CodeWAM, a driving world model that represents ego vehicle dynamics as executable code alongside a learned visual model for end-to-end autonomous driving.
s18394dd955.why: Combining executable code with learned visual models for driving planning is an architectural idea engineers in autonomy may evaluate.

s32df646f51.title: Assessing Robustness to Catastrophic Forgetting in Continual Deep Reinforcement Learning for Cyber-Physical Systems
s32df646f51.description: arXiv:2611.32496v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As the use of reinforcement learning (RL) becomes more widespread in cyber-physical systems, it becomes increasingly important to design RL agents that are able to adapt to changes in their environments in order to maintain safety and reliability. This paper addresses the question of whether different classes of RL algorithm are more robust against forgetting previously learned behaviours, a critical issue in continual learning, in non-stationary environments. We evaluate the robustness of representative examples of three important classes of RL algorithm in a non-stationary autonomous parking environment. These are Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO), which is a model-free on-policy algorithm, Soft-Actor-Critic (SAC), which is a model-free
s32df646f51.summary: Researchers evaluate how robust three classes of reinforcement learning algorithms are to catastrophic forgetting in continual learning for cyber-physical systems.
s32df646f51.why: Forgetting previously learned behaviours threatens safety in deployed RL controllers that must adapt to changing environments.

s382df81fd4.title: Branch and Consolidate: A Unified Recipe for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
s382df81fd4.description: arXiv:2611.32515v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Specialists post-trained from a shared checkpoint acquire complementary capabilities, and multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) can consolidate them into a single model. However, we find that existing consolidation methods, from weight merging to MOPD, fall short when specialists diverge substantially from the shared checkpoint, whereas prior studies mostly examine specialists that remain close to it. We present a unified recipe for multimodal MOPD that consolidates such specialists back into the single student they branched from. The recipe specifies initialization, data selection, balanced supervision across teachers, and preservation of existing capabilities for consolidation, together with a targeted refinement stage for capabilit
s382df81fd4.summary: Researchers present a unified multimodal multi-teacher on-policy distillation recipe that consolidates specialists which diverge substantially from a shared checkpoint back into one student.
s382df81fd4.why: Existing merging and distillation methods reportedly struggle when specialists drift far from the base checkpoint, relevant to multi-model consolidation work.

s7ea002af9a.title: Wi-Fi Enabled Edge Intelligence Framework for Smart City Traffic Monitoring using Low-Power IoT Cameras
s7ea002af9a.description: arXiv:2611.32517v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time traffic monitoring in smart cities demands ultra-low latency processing to support time-critical decisions such as incident detection and congestion management. While cloud-based solutions offer robust computation, their inherent latency limits their applicability for such tasks. This work proposes a localized edge AI framework that connects low-power IoT camera sensors to a client, or applies offloading of inference to an NVIDIA Jetson Nano (GPU). Networking is achieved via Wi-Fi, enabling image classification without relying on wide-area infrastructure such as 5G, or wired networks. We evaluate two processing strategies: local inference on camera nodes and GPU-accelerated offloading to the Jetson Nano.We show that local processi
s7ea002af9a.summary: Researchers propose a localized edge AI framework connecting low-power IoT cameras to a client or NVIDIA Jetson Nano over Wi-Fi for smart city traffic monitoring.
s7ea002af9a.why: Shows a low-latency edge inference design that avoids cloud round trips for time-critical tasks like incident detection and congestion management.

s67af7e4552.title: ContinualDrive: A Deployment-Anchored, Multi-Axis Benchmark for Continual Updates of Learned Driving Planners
s67af7e4552.description: arXiv:2611.32529v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Learned driving planners keep being updated after deployment as new logs arrive, yet continual learning evaluations rarely ask whether an update improves on the deployed model, and their verdicts rest on unstated evaluation choices. We present ContinualDrive, a deployment-anchored benchmark for post-deployment continual learning of driving planners. It updates a deployed planner on real-world nuPlan logs one scenario-type group at a time, evaluates the same checkpoints in open and closed loop, makes four measurement axes explicit (evaluation loop, reference checkpoint, temporal aggregation and stream protocol), and anchors a three-valued release verdict to the deployed checkpoint. We study two planners (PlanTF and Diffusion Planner) under f
s67af7e4552.summary: ContinualDrive is a benchmark for post-deployment continual updates of learned driving planners, using real nuPlan logs and open and closed loop evaluation.
s67af7e4552.why: Gives teams a way to test whether updating a deployed driving planner actually improves on the current model.

s0e5470d060.title: Next-Manip: On-Demand Agent-Policy Collaboration for Robotic Manipulation
s0e5470d060.description: arXiv:2611.32533v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: General-purpose robotic manipulation requires task reasoning, failure recovery, and precise control, yet limited manipulation data make these abilities difficult to obtain from a single policy. Recent multimodal agents show promise in task reasoning and recovery but lack reliable fine-grained control and incur high inference cost, whereas learned policies provide efficient fine-grained execution but struggle beyond their learned skills. Although their complementary strengths suggest combining the two, doing so requires repeatedly deciding which executor should act as task demands change. Instead of relying on the agent for each decision, we present Next-Manip, an on-demand agent--policy collaboration framework that decouples executor alloca
s0e5470d060.summary: Next-Manip proposes on-demand collaboration between multimodal agents and learned policies for robotic manipulation, switching between them as needed.
s0e5470d060.why: Suggests a hybrid design where expensive reasoning agents are called only when a fast control policy fails.

s52a5367532.title: MXI-MemICL: Towards In-Context Robot Manipulation through Self-Retrieved Interaction Memory
s52a5367532.description: arXiv:2611.32564v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) offers robots a way to acquire new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates. However, existing robotic ICL methods either rely on large-scale pretraining constrained by scarce, costly robot interaction data or require additional annotations yet struggle to generalize across tasks. To bridge this gap, we propose MXI-MemICL, a framework for memory-guided ICL in vision-language-action (VLA) models. By treating demonstrations as retrievable memory, MXI-MemICL enables in-context manipulation without additional large-scale pretraining or specialized annotations. Specifically, a visual-action causal encoder turns actions and their observed effects in demonstrations and completed interactions into reusa
s52a5367532.summary: MXI-MemICL introduces memory-guided in-context learning for vision-language-action models, treating robot demonstrations as retrievable memory to learn new manipulation skills.
s52a5367532.why: Offers a way to teach robots new skills from a single demonstration without parameter updates or extra annotations.

s6630e3e4b7.title: Boiling Down Uncertainty: Deep Generative Scenario Search with Decision-Guided Evolution Strategies for Two-Stage Stochastic Optimization
s6630e3e4b7.description: arXiv:2611.32573v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: One of the most common models for handling uncertainty is two-stage stochastic programming. Choosing the right number of scenarios is a trade-off between the uncertainty that can be represented and computational cost. A recent method, Deep Generative Scenario Search, generates synthetic scenarios and improves them by learning from the decisions they induce. The original approach used a black-box gradient estimate, since decisions are piecewise constant across scenarios. This paper provides the missing analytical foundation by deriving the gradient in closed form from recourse duality and an adjoint solve of the regularized reduced problem. The decision-focused direction, with a heuristic direction as a backup when duals are unavailable, def
s6630e3e4b7.summary: Researchers derive analytical gradients for Deep Generative Scenario Search, a method that generates and refines scenarios for two-stage stochastic optimization.
s6630e3e4b7.why: Provides a theoretical foundation for a scenario generation method, which may improve decision quality under uncertainty.

s2812221254.title: Gated Concept Adapters: Layer-Wise Concept Bottlenecks for Auditable Text Understanding
s2812221254.description: arXiv:2611.32600v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Human-facing text understanding systems are used to infer affect, moderate harmful content, and support socially sensitive decisions. However, Transformer predictions are difficult to audit because they are produced from high-dimensional hidden states that do not provide a compact, inspectable interface for human analysis or intervention. We introduce Gated Concept Adapters (GCA), a layer-wise concept bottleneck framework that attaches gated, low-dimensional concept-producing readout adapters to selected outputs of pretrained Transformers. Token representations are mapped into concept activations, filtered by learned gates, pooled into layer-level summaries, and exposed to the prediction head as a concept-mediated interface. The dimensions
s2812221254.summary: Gated Concept Adapters add layer-wise, low-dimensional concept bottlenecks to pretrained Transformers to make text understanding predictions more inspectable and auditable.
s2812221254.why: Offers a route to auditable intervention points in models used for moderation and other sensitive text decisions.

s2d41d08eac.title: RoboRecast: Intent-Preserving Demonstration Augmentation via Diagnosis-Driven Optimization
s2d41d08eac.description: arXiv:2611.32622v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Collecting diverse real-world manipulation demonstrations is costly, motivating the use of simulation to augment existing demonstrations for robot policy learning. When objects, layouts, or robots change, transferring motions from a source demonstration can produce behavior that is semantically implausible or physically infeasible in the new setting. We introduce RoboRecast, an agentic optimization framework that preserves the interactions required by the source task while jointly optimizing the simulated scene and robot motion to make those interactions executable in the target setting. When an interaction fails, the agent uses simulation feedback to diagnose the cause, revise the relevant scene or motion parameters, and test whether the r
s2d41d08eac.summary: RoboRecast is an agentic optimization framework that augments robot demonstrations in simulation by jointly adjusting scene and robot motion while preserving task interactions.
s2d41d08eac.why: Could reduce the cost of collecting real-world manipulation demonstrations for robot policy learning.
