s4de2b71113.title: REBEAL: Human References Are No Longer the Best Translation, and Metrics Do Not Notice
s4de2b71113.description: arXiv:2611.32623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reference-based MT evaluation assumes the human reference is correct and better than the systems it scores. Both assumptions now fail, since the human reference ranks first in none of the 2024 WMT MQM campaigns and carries annotated errors in 19% to 87% of its segments. What a metric does with a flawed reference is a question about the metric, and it would have been worth asking before reference quality came into doubt. We introduce REBEAL (Reference Bias EvALuation), a benchmark that probes how MT metrics respond to seven types of controlled reference contamination, drawn from the error categories those campaigns record. Across eight widely used metrics and three language pairs, recent learned metrics (xCOMET, MetricX) prove more robust th
s4de2b71113.summary: REBEAL is a benchmark testing how machine translation metrics respond to controlled flaws in human reference translations, noting references contain annotated errors.
s4de2b71113.why: Shows reference-based MT metrics may be unreliable when references are flawed, affecting how teams evaluate translation systems.

s1b397e8a3a.title: MargEmbed-Akan: Bridging Twi Questions and English Knowledge through Cross-Lingual Score Distillation
s1b397e8a3a.description: arXiv:2611.32630v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Most information sought online by Twi (Akan) speakers is written in English, making cross-lingual retrieval essential. We evaluate eight systems: BM25, five open embedding models, and two proprietary models (gemini-embedding-001 and OpenAI text-embedding-3-large) on two Twi-English tasks. AfriQA contains 1,221 natively written Asante Twi questions that must retrieve their answering English Wikipedia passages. Bible translation retrieval requires a Twi passage to retrieve its English translation from 6,195 candidates. We introduce MargEmbed-Akan, a 560M-parameter open query encoder trained from AfriE5-Large-instruct using cross-lingual score distillation. The frozen base model scores each English training question against its answer passage
s1b397e8a3a.summary: The MargEmbed-Akan paper evaluates eight retrieval systems on Twi-English cross-lingual tasks and introduces a distilled embedding model for Twi questions.
s1b397e8a3a.why: Highlights gaps in embedding retrieval for low-resource languages like Twi, relevant to multilingual search builders.

s0270c849bb.title: ReFocus: Progress-Guided Adaptive Practice for Long-Horizon Robotic Manipulation Reinforcement Learning
s0270c849bb.description: arXiv:2611.32639v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online reinforcement learning (RL) enables vision-language-action policies to improve through environmental interaction. However, in long-horizon manipulation, sparse success/failure feedback provides little information about where policies encounter bottlenecks. Moreover, repeated full-task rollouts also leave these bottlenecks weakly analyzed and insufficiently practiced. To this end, we introduce ReFocus, a progress-guided multi-round RL framework that alternates between Global and Local RL to identify task-specific bottlenecks and allocate additional practice to them. Specifically, during Global RL, we decompose each task into a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) of subtasks. Then a DAG-based Progress Reward is leveraged for both policy train
s0270c849bb.summary: ReFocus is a progress-guided multi-round reinforcement learning framework that alternates global and local RL to find and practice bottlenecks in long-horizon robotic manipulation.
s0270c849bb.why: Addresses sparse feedback in long-horizon robot RL by targeting specific bottleneck stages for practice.

s96a046e864.title: BARE: Body-Aware Reflexive Evasion for Humanoid Robots
s96a046e864.description: arXiv:2611.32642v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic obstacle avoidance is essential for safely deploying humanoid robots in real-world environments, where rapidly approaching objects require immediate evasive responses. Recent advances in reflexive evasion have focused primarily on quadrupeds, which typically rely on large-scale whole-body maneuvers. In contrast, humanoids can exploit their rich body articulation to evade through small, localized body adjustments. By moving threatened body regions without repositioning the entire body, these responses may require less execution time and less surrounding free space. However, local adjustments can alter mass distribution or support conditions, making it challenging to achieve rapid evasion while maintaining whole-body stability. To thi
s96a046e864.summary: BARE proposes body-aware reflexive evasion for humanoid robots, using small localized body adjustments to dodge rapidly approaching obstacles.

s7a419e1772.title: TeamFlowRL: Online Policy Optimization of Decentralized Flow Policies for Multi-Agent Coordination
s7a419e1772.description: arXiv:2611.32645v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Complex cooperative tasks require coordinated multi-agent behavior. Offline generative policies learn expressive cooperative behaviors from trajectories but remain limited by fixed datasets. Online reinforcement learning can improve them through environment interaction. However, fine-tuning flow policies is difficult because action likelihoods are hard to compute. We propose TeamFlowRL, a two-stage framework that pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online. We formulate team policy optimization over the complete denoising trajectories of decentralized flow policies, avoiding intractable action likelihoods. The resulting objective weights each agent's trajectory ratio with a shared team advantage and clips each rat
s7a419e1772.summary: TeamFlowRL pretrains multi-agent flow policies offline and fine-tunes them online with reinforcement learning for cooperative multi-agent coordination.
s7a419e1772.why: Offers a method for improving generative multi-agent policies beyond fixed datasets through online interaction.

s8fd5f0be76.title: ICLWorld: Benchmarking In-Context Learning of Agents from Digital to Physical Worlds
s8fd5f0be76.description: arXiv:2611.32649v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In-context learning (ICL) lets agents acquire new rules from context and adapt to user-specific requirements at inference time. The same frontier agents now operate both computers and robots, yet their ICL remains insufficiently assessed: existing benchmarks are largely offline, rely on text or static images, and risk training-data contamination, while robot evaluations are limited to method-level ablations. We present ICLWorld, an online benchmark that evaluates the ICL of agents from digital to physical worlds, covering computer use and robot use, together with UIverse, a unified harness that turns every environment into a user interface. We build 30 environments, record 630 demonstration videos (10+ hours), and design 160 tasks with cust
s8fd5f0be76.summary: ICLWorld is an online benchmark that evaluates in-context learning of agents across computer use and robot control in digital and physical settings.
s8fd5f0be76.why: Provides a contamination-resistant way to assess whether agents adapt to new rules at inference time across computers and robots.

s8169ffe3f4.title: DexWAC: A Unified World-Actor-Critic Model for Dexterous Robot Manipulation
s8169ffe3f4.description: arXiv:2611.32654v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot demonstrations provide more than actions to imitate: they reveal how actions change the world and how those changes contribute to task success. Recent world-action models (WAMs) extend vision-language-action (VLA) models with the first signal by jointly predicting actions and future observations, yet this predictive ability serves only as an auxiliary loss for policy learning. Meanwhile, most policy improvement methods learn dynamics and values in separate models, increasing training overhead and limiting representation sharing between these complementary objectives. We introduce DexWAC, a unified world-actor-critic model that jointly learns an actor, an action-conditioned world model, and a bootstrapped critic in a single robot pretr
s8169ffe3f4.summary: DexWAC is a unified world-actor-critic model for dexterous robot manipulation that combines action prediction, dynamics, and value learning in one model.
s8169ffe3f4.why: Suggests sharing representations across world modeling and policy learning could reduce training overhead for robot policies.

s02cb518410.title: Bathys: Advancing Deep Search Agents
s02cb518410.description: arXiv:2611.32660v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep search is a critical capability for agents tackling complex, open-ended tasks, where solving a problem requires iterative information gathering, query reformulation, and evidence-based verification rather than a single retrieval step. To address these requirements, we present Bathys 9B and 27B deep search agents built around a training framework that spans verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online reinforcement learning (RL) under context compression. Our high-quality data construction ensures both search depth and reliability: each clue is reformulated as an indirect reference requiring independent retrieval, and retained evidence chains enable verification that the clues jointly determine a unique answer. Curated traje
s02cb518410.summary: Bathys 9B and 27B are deep search agents trained with verifiable question synthesis, post-training, and online RL under context compression.
s02cb518410.why: Describes a training pipeline for multi-step search agents that gather evidence iteratively and verify answers.

sb53d7a1b07.title: Are We Rewarding the Wrong Module? Module-Specific Policy Optimization for Multimodal Reinforcement Learning
sb53d7a1b07.description: arXiv:2611.32687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) based on Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) has been widely adopted to enhance the multimodal reasoning of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). However, existing methods share a common limitation of Module-Level Credit Entanglement, in which the vision encoder, projector, and LLM modules are jointly optimized using the same advantage signals even when perceptual correctness and final-answer correctness differ. To address this limitation, we propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization (MSPO), a framework that separates perceptual and outcome-based learning signals across model modules. Specifically, MSPO uses responses to perception checklists comprising auxiliary questions ab
sb53d7a1b07.summary: Researchers propose Module-Specific Policy Optimization to stop RLVR/GRPO from applying one advantage signal to all modules of multimodal LLMs, including the vision encoder, projector, and LLM.
sb53d7a1b07.why: It targets credit-assignment flaws in RL fine-tuning of multimodal models, which could affect how teams train vision-language reasoning systems.

s63f1bdf262.title: FourStat: A Dual AutoEncoder Leveraging Frequency and Stationarity for Time Series Anomaly Detection
s63f1bdf262.description: arXiv:2611.32714v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: While numerous studies have focused on multivariate time series anomaly detection, many existing methods perform poorly or are not directly applicable to univariate settings. We introduce FourStat, a dual-model framework for univariate time series anomaly detection that combines two complementary approaches. The Fourier Autoencoder (FAE) captures global patterns like seasonality through frequency-domain analysis, while the Stationary Autoencoder (SAE) focuses on local structures by enforcing statistical stationarity. We also propose a new evaluation metric called Perfect Point that assesses whether perfect F1-scores can be achieved directly from anomaly scores, eliminating thresholding subjectivity. Results demonstrate that FourStat outperf
s63f1bdf262.summary: FourStat is a dual autoencoder for univariate time series anomaly detection, combining a Fourier autoencoder for global patterns with a stationary autoencoder for local structure.
s63f1bdf262.why: Univariate anomaly detection is a common monitoring need, and the approach claims to address settings where many existing methods perform poorly.

sb20bdd4ba7.title: ASCENT: A Benchmark for Evaluating and Advancing Stepwise Diagnostic Reasoning in Large Language Models on Common Clinical Scenarios
sb20bdd4ba7.description: arXiv:2611.32734v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) excel at medical question answering yet are rarely evaluated on the stepwise diagnostic reasoning that defines real clinical workflows, where impressions are revised as information accumulates. We build Annotated Stepwise Clinical rEasoning for NaturalisTic Diagnosis (ASCENT), a clinician-annotated benchmark and training resource of 3,078 stepwise problems derived from MedQA-USMLE that decomposes each vignette into EMR-aligned steps (Findings, Impression, supporting Rationale), enabling evaluation of intermediate reasoning under incomplete information. Experiments and training with ASCENT revealed insights into how current LLMs handle stepwise diagnostic reasoning. Even strong reasoning models that perform well
sb20bdd4ba7.summary: ASCENT is a clinician-annotated benchmark of 3,078 stepwise diagnostic problems derived from MedQA-USMLE, designed to evaluate how LLMs revise impressions as clinical information accumulates.
sb20bdd4ba7.why: It offers a way to test LLMs on multi-step clinical reasoning rather than only final answers, relevant to healthcare AI evaluation.

s87f93a554c.title: ReQOR: Operator-Discrepancy Subspace Repair for Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors in Large Language Models
s87f93a554c.description: arXiv:2611.32755v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Quantization-Conditioned Backdoors (QCBs) cause large language models (LLMs) to exhibit malicious behavior after quantization while remaining benign at high precision. Existing defenses often rely on security-guided configuration selection or iterative optimization, but do not identify which quantization-induced changes should be repaired. We isolate module-local quantization effects from upstream drift by evaluating the high-precision and quantized versions of each module on identical states from the quantized inference trajectory, and formulate QCB defense as repairing the resulting same-state operator discrepancies. We propose ReQOR, a training-free defense that identifies the dominant directions of these discrepancies on benign calibrat
s87f93a554c.summary: ReQOR proposes a method to repair quantization-conditioned backdoors in LLMs, which behave maliciously only after quantization while appearing benign at high precision.
s87f93a554c.why: Teams that quantize models for deployment may need to verify quantized versions, since backdoors can appear only after compression.

s7a49aba546.title: SGD with Large Learning Rates: General Analysis & Improved Rates
s7a49aba546.description: arXiv:2611.32762v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stochastic Gradient Descent lies at the core of modern machine learning. However its classical analysis typically restricts the stepsize to be below a curvature-dependent stability threshold. Recent developments in deterministic optimization have challenged this paradigm, showing that suitably chosen large stepsizes can not only preserve convergence, but also accelerate Gradient Descent (GD). Whether this phenomenon persists in the presence of stochastic gradient noise has remained an open question (Wu et al., 2024). In this work, we answer this question affirmatively for the cross-entropy loss with linear predictors and two-layer neural networks, establishing an accelerated $\mathcal{O}(T^{-2})$ convergence rate. At the core of our analysi
s7a49aba546.summary: Researchers analyze stochastic gradient descent with large learning rates and report improved convergence rates, answering an open question about whether large-stepsize benefits persist under gradient noise.
s7a49aba546.why: Results on stepsize choice under noise could inform optimizer tuning, though the text gives limited practical detail.

s263fdd8600.title: C3H: Compression-to-Consensus Criteria Hijacking in Multimodal LLM Recommender Systems
s263fdd8600.description: arXiv:2611.32780v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are transforming recommender systems into content-aware decision systems. In these systems, multimodal compression and cross-modal fusion are often viewed as robustness-enhancing mechanisms against content manipulation, as compression can filter noisy signals and cross-modal consensus can suppress inconsistent anomalies. We challenge this assumption by showing that the same process can expose a compression-to-consensus (C2C) bias in ranking decisions. Signals that remain salient after compression and receive consistent support across modalities can gain disproportionate influence in candidate comparison, offering an exploitable direction for content manipulation. In this paper, we introduce C3H, a no
s263fdd8600.summary: The C3H paper shows that compression and cross-modal fusion in multimodal LLM recommenders can expose a compression-to-consensus bias that attackers can exploit to hijack ranking decisions.
s263fdd8600.why: Recommender systems built on multimodal LLMs may be vulnerable to content manipulation that exploits the same mechanisms meant to add robustness.

s76681900aa.title: Scaling Laws of Ensemble Uncertainty in Language Models
s76681900aa.description: arXiv:2611.32801v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many use cases for large language models (LLMs)---from AI safety to exploration and human interaction---can benefit from epistemic uncertainty estimates. We argue that existing Bayesian Deep Learning solutions, which are often restricted to a fixed model family, fail to capture the full epistemic uncertainty at practical LLM scales. This is because the error due to the bounded capacity of the model family remains invisible to disagreement among models supported by the prior. We relate this error to the well-known power-law scaling of LLM loss with model size. We then show that a second power law quantifies the shrinking disagreement within ensembles as model size increases. Its slower decay relative to the capacity law above suggests that e
s76681900aa.summary: Researchers argue that existing Bayesian deep learning methods miss much of LLM epistemic uncertainty and study how ensemble uncertainty scales with model size.
s76681900aa.why: Reliable uncertainty estimates matter for safety and exploration use cases, and the scaling analysis may inform how teams estimate model confidence.

se87731b4e1.title: Sample-Efficient In-Context Adaptation via Sleep
se87731b4e1.description: arXiv:2611.32802v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The ability to learn and generalize from limited experience, or sample efficiency, is a cornerstone of intelligence. How can we build language models that turn a few user interactions, a few snippets of unfamiliar code, or a handful of experimental results provided in context into knowledge that generalizes? Prior work has found that sleep, a process where the model performs $N$ recurrent forward passes to refine its representations of a chunk of context, can improve long-context reasoning (specifically, within SSM-attention hybrid models). We study whether this method also improves in-context adaptation on general, non-synthetic tasks for transformer language models. To this end, we pre-train language models up to 1.2B-parameters on up to
se87731b4e1.summary: Researchers propose a sleep-like process in which a model runs recurrent forward passes over context to turn a few in-context examples into generalizable knowledge, improving sample efficiency.
se87731b4e1.why: If effective, a sleep-style refinement step could help models learn from limited user interactions or unfamiliar code without retraining.

sd91b53edb3.title: MRBench: Benchmarking Physical Necessity Reasoning in Heterogeneous Multi-Robot Manipulation
sd91b53edb3.description: arXiv:2611.32803v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in multi-robot manipulation have shown how robots can collaborate to accomplish complex tasks. However, successful coordination does not reveal which robots are actually needed. The same task may require different teams as robot capabilities change, resources become unavailable, or objects replace robotic support. We argue that reliable multi-robot manipulation requires physical necessity reasoning: understanding what a task demands, which resources can fulfill those demands, and which are truly necessary. We introduce MRBench, a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation. It comprises eight tasks with distinct concurrency and reach constraints, each evaluated under five configuratio
sd91b53edb3.summary: MRBench is a benchmark for physical necessity reasoning in heterogeneous multi-robot manipulation, testing which robots are truly needed for a task as capabilities and resources change.
sd91b53edb3.why: It highlights that successful robot coordination does not show which team members are required, a gap for planning in multi-robot systems.

s60513cd9f6.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
s60513cd9f6.description: arXiv:2611.32820v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Sp
s60513cd9f6.summary: Researchers identify context inertia in streaming video generation, where models keep following the previous prompt after a switch, and propose residual guidance to address it.
s60513cd9f6.why: Interactive video tools that let users change prompts mid-generation face this lag, which affects responsiveness in real-time products.

sd136968641.title: Reliable and grounded reporting of any computed tomography scan with FORA
sd136968641.description: arXiv:2611.32823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Artificial intelligence systems for computed tomography (CT) remain largely restricted to specific anatomical regions, examination types or predefined abnormalities, limiting their ability to provide comprehensive and spatially grounded interpretations. Here we present FORA, a general-purpose CT model that recognizes and spatially localizes 1,028 hierarchically organized radiological concepts and generates reports across the 28 CT protocols represented in our cohort. Trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations supervised by their accompanying reports, FORA learns to localize abnormalities without manually annotated lesions. Its architecture combines multiple-instance learning with an interpretable concept bottleneck that connects spatial evi
sd136968641.summary: FORA is a general-purpose CT model that localizes 1,028 radiological concepts and generates reports across 28 CT protocols, trained on 304,962 routine CT examinations.
sd136968641.why: It suggests a broader, spatially grounded approach to radiology AI than models limited to specific organs or predefined abnormalities.

s330fad6fc0.title: Field Life: Particle Life as Interacting Chemical Fields
s330fad6fc0.description: arXiv:2611.32844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by the interaction dynamics of Particle Life. In Particle Life, each particle has a colour, and an interaction matrix sets how strongly each colour attracts or repels each other colour. In Field Life, each colour is a channel of the automaton, and each cell holds a concentration of every colour. One step of the rule has three parts. Each colour is convolved with a ring-shaped kernel, which measures how much of that colour surrounds a cell. The interaction matrix combines these measurements into an attraction for each colour. The mass of each colour then moves toward higher attraction, in a way that conserves mass. A random matrix and a random initial state are usually enough to produce moving stru
s330fad6fc0.summary: Field Life is a cellular automaton inspired by Particle Life, where each colour is a channel holding concentrations per cell and interactions follow a ring-kernel convolution and interaction matrix.
s330fad6fc0.why: It is a research artifact on emergent dynamics with limited direct relevance to engineering or business decisions.

s9186b1c57f.title: Path-probability gradients for optimizing force fields against dynamical observables
s9186b1c57f.description: arXiv:2611.32851v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine learning force fields inherit the errors of the electronic-structure methods used to generate their training data, and refining them against experimental measurements provides a direct route beyond this limit. However, such refinement remains difficult for dynamical observables because differentiating chaotic molecular trajectories yields unstable gradients. Here, we introduce PathGrad, which differentiates Langevin path probabilities instead of the trajectories themselves. The resulting gradient estimator is accumulated on the fly from thermal noise and force derivatives, and its variance remains stable as the trajectory length increases. We validated the gradient estimator against finite-difference calculations and used it to fine
s9186b1c57f.summary: PathGrad introduces path-probability gradients for refining machine learning force fields against dynamical observables by differentiating Langevin path probabilities instead of chaotic trajectories.
s9186b1c57f.why: It offers a route to fit simulation models to experimental dynamics, relevant mainly to computational chemistry and materials teams.

s3c2460218e.title: MXFP4 for LLM Inference: Complementary Post-Training Quantization Techniques and Their Interactions
s3c2460218e.description: arXiv:2611.32873v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in low-precision representation have introduced several microscaling numerical formats for LLM quantization. By sharing a scale factor across groups of 16 or 32 elements, these formats enable aggressive low-precision quantization with minimal accuracy degradation, particularly when combined with modern PTQ algorithms. Their accuracy depends on how the numerical format interacts with rotation, PTQ, and scale selection. We study the composability of PTQ configurations across six LLMs and three microscaling formats: MXFP6, MXFP4, and NVFP4, systematically varying Hadamard rotation granularity, PTQ algorithm, and scale-selection strategy. Our central finding is that effective quantization recipes are format dependent: both MXFP4
s3c2460218e.summary: A study of six LLMs and three microscaling formats (including MXFP6 and MXFP4) examines how post-training quantization techniques compose and interact.
s3c2460218e.why: Practical guidance on combining MXFP4 with rotation and scale selection can inform low-precision LLM inference deployments.

s5b48e9db15.title: Adaptive Electromagnetic Transient-level Digital Twins for Data Centers via In-Context Learning with LLMs
s5b48e9db15.description: arXiv:2611.32882v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence (AI) workloads has significantly increased data center (DC) power demand. Frequent operational and configurational changes, such as load surges caused by dynamic workload allocation, can induce electromagnetic transients (EMTs) whose accurate prediction is critical for reliable DC operation and maintenance. Although high-fidelity EMT solvers are widely adopted for transient analysis, their computational cost limits large-scale and multi-scenario studies. Digital twins address this computational bottleneck by emulating the behavior of a physical system and enabling fast prediction in place of expensive high-fidelity simulation. However,data-driven digital twins are non-adaptive and fail to generali
s5b48e9db15.summary: Researchers propose adaptive electromagnetic transient-level digital twins for data centers using in-context learning with LLMs to speed up transient prediction versus high-fidelity solvers.
s5b48e9db15.why: Faster transient simulation could help data center operators plan for AI-driven power demand swings, though the text gives limited detail on results.

sdeeb599393.title: Joint Detection of Constructive Speech, Hate Speech and Agreement in Online Conversations
sdeeb599393.description: arXiv:2611.32889v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online hate speech is an ever-growing issue with negative impacts on both groups and individuals, potentially causing users to withdraw from online conversations and debate. With some prominent social media platforms reducing their moderation efforts, constructive speech has emerged as an alternative strategy for countering hate. Automated detection of constructive and hateful speech can aid monitoring and improve understanding of their prevalence and online dynamics. In this work, we collect and annotate a large dataset of English and Danish social media comments for hateful tone, constructive tone, and agreement with parent comments. We fine-tune several multilingual LLMs to classify along these three dimensions and compare context-enrich
sdeeb599393.summary: Researchers collected and annotated a large English and Danish dataset for jointly detecting constructive speech, hate speech, and agreement in online conversations.
sdeeb599393.why: Offers training data and methods for automated moderation that promotes constructive counter-speech, useful for trust and safety teams building classifiers.

s937a69c546.title: Motion Conditioned World Modeling for Embodied Visual Tracking
s937a69c546.description: arXiv:2611.32900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models support embodied decision-making by predicting future environment states. In embodied visual tracking, uncertain target motion and robot-induced viewpoint changes jointly affect visual observations, making future-state prediction challenging. We propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which incorporates predicted target-motion distributions and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions. A Geometry--Progress module jointly models geometric paths and single-step travel distances through shared motion modes and path-conditioned progress distributions. This formulation captures uncertainty in route selection and motion progress while preserving their dependence. Action-induced coordinate transformations express predicted pa
s937a69c546.summary: Researchers propose Motion-Conditioned World Modeling, which feeds predicted target motion and robot ego-motion into latent state transitions for embodied visual tracking.
s937a69c546.why: Shows how modeling target motion and viewpoint changes in world models can improve prediction for robots that track moving objects.

s599971afc9.title: Efficient Video Retrieval Augmented Generation via Token Allocation
s599971afc9.description: arXiv:2611.32938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Efficient long-video understanding requires identifying relevant evidence while minimizing the tokens processed by vision-language models (VLMs). Existing video retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) methods rely on frame selection and token compression, but overlook how much each additional token is worth. We introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that formulates video RAG as a token allocation problem over frames and subtitles under a shared budget. Our key insight is that the value of a token diminishes within each item and decreases further as similar evidence receives more tokens. Lembas captures both effects in a single objective and solves it with an efficient iterative water-filling algorithm that has a provable convergence guara
s599971afc9.summary: Researchers introduce Lembas, a plug-and-play framework that treats video retrieval-augmented generation as a token allocation problem across frames and subtitles under a shared budget.
s599971afc9.why: Could reduce VLM token costs for long-video understanding by allocating a fixed token budget more efficiently across retrieved content.

sd2f85934f0.title: Do Vision-Language Models Know Their Own Visual Weaknesses? Probing Capability-Level Metacognition
sd2f85934f0.description: arXiv:2611.32940v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Metacognition includes knowing one's own strengths and weaknesses across kinds of tasks, not only judging whether a single answer is correct. We test whether vision-language models (VLMs) know in advance which kinds of visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across a wide range of open and proprietary models. Because some tasks are hard for every model, we separate what a model knows about this shared difficulty from what it knows about itself. We find that VLMs know little in advance about their visual weaknesses. They misjudge their overall accuracy and do not even know which kinds of tasks are hard for every model, and most misjudge how degraded images affect them. We further train VLMs to predict their own accuracy, which t
sd2f85934f0.summary: A study finds vision-language models poorly predict in advance which visual tasks and image conditions are hard for them, across open and proprietary models.
sd2f85934f0.why: Suggests teams cannot rely on VLMs to self-report their weak spots, so external capability testing remains necessary before deployment.

s25718390b6.title: "I Do Intend to Deliver": Will LLMs Run a Marketplace Advance-Fee Scam?
s25718390b6.description: arXiv:2611.32957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online fraud is traditionally limited by the cost of the human labor needed to talk to potential victims. We ask whether hosted large language models will now supply that labor. We prompted ten off-the-shelf models to play the seller in the "free item, just pay delivery" advance-fee scam common on buy-and-sell sites, using a plain system prompt with no jailbreak. Each model played 30 conversations against each of four buyer personas, from credulous to guarded, with the same model playing the buyer (1,200 conversations). We label each conversation by what happened to the buyer's money, and validate the labels against two human coders. 737 conversations (61%) ended with the buyer paying in advance. Eight of the ten models played in almost eve
s25718390b6.summary: Researchers prompted ten off-the-shelf LLMs to play sellers in a marketplace advance-fee scam across 1,200 simulated buyer conversations, without jailbreaks.
s25718390b6.why: Highlights that hosted LLMs may be usable for scalable fraud with simple prompts, a concern for platform abuse and safety controls.

sdf139b75e2.title: Attestation is All You Need: Toward a Zero-Trust Architecture for HPC AI Agents
sdf139b75e2.description: arXiv:2611.32958v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI agents are beginning to automate data analysis, orchestration, and simulation steering in HPC environments, but they introduce a security problem that existing cluster defenses do not address: the hijacked authorized agent. An adversary can subvert an agent through prompt injection, poisoned shared data, compromised tools, or multi-agent coordination, then exfiltrate sensitive data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic. We propose behavioral attestation as a runtime defense for this setting. Our system, AEGIS, compiles task-derived behavioral constraints, monitors agent actions with ebpf-based syscall interception, verifies evidence against constraint profiles, correlates behavior across agents, and triggers slurm-level containmen
sdf139b75e2.summary: Researchers propose AEGIS, a runtime behavioral attestation system to defend HPC AI agents against hijacking via prompt injection, poisoned data, or compromised tools.
sdf139b75e2.why: Addresses a security gap where authorized agents can exfiltrate data through legitimate encrypted LLM API traffic that existing cluster defenses miss.

sc849f8b5d1.title: Benchmarking Evidence Sufficiency in Vision-Language Models for Autonomous Driving
sc849f8b5d1.description: arXiv:2611.32964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable driving VLMs must do more than answer correctly or localize relevant scene actors: they must determine whether the available visual evidence is sufficient to support an answer. Existing evaluations largely treat grounding and answerability as separate measurements, making it difficult to distinguish well-supported predictions from those localized to relevant but insufficient evidence. We introduce DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions across seven reasoning families, that operationalizes this distinction using matched strong- and weak-evidence configurations. Each pair preserves the underlying scene fact and semantic answer while changing whether the observations support answering, making abstention the appropriate response
sc849f8b5d1.summary: Researchers released DriveAnswer, a benchmark of 20,151 questions testing whether driving vision-language models judge if visual evidence is sufficient to answer.
sc849f8b5d1.why: Separates grounding from answerability, helping teams tell well-supported autonomous driving predictions from ones based on insufficient evidence.

s8c3e347472.title: CAPER: PartGround and PlanRefine for Reliable Manual-Guided Robotic Assembly Planning
s8c3e347472.description: arXiv:2611.32986v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-Language-Models (VLMs) used in robot task planning to derive assembly procedures from existing manuals may correctly interpret individual assembly actions yet confuse exact part identities, predict unsupported Part IDs, or produce inconsistent parts across assembly steps. Thus, we propose CAPER (Capacity-Aware Part-grounding and Evidence Refinement), a manual-guided robotic assembly framework that enables VLMs to generate assembly procedures with two modules--PartGround and PlanRefine. PartGround aligns step-level manual evidence with product-specific inventory and part-reference information to identify exact Part IDs and quantities, transforming free-form hardware prediction into evidence-guided assignments represented in a shared A
s8c3e347472.summary: Researchers propose CAPER, a framework with PartGround and PlanRefine modules to help VLMs generate robotic assembly procedures from manuals with accurate part identities.
s8c3e347472.why: Targets reliability issues like unsupported part IDs in VLM-based robot planning, relevant to teams automating assembly workflows.

s5c6f25d5a7.title: On Potentiality and Actuality Of Foundation Models
s5c6f25d5a7.description: arXiv:2611.32991v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Foundation models are built through large-scale pretraining, often followed by post-training, and are then adapted to specific tasks and behaviors. But, does the adaptation add truly new capabilities, or the base model already holds it? We decompose the update induced by different adaptations into a component shared across all inputs and a residual that varies with the input. We find that the shared component suffices for most of the adaptation gain and can be learned directly: a shift adapter that learns a constant vector per layer, identical for every input, reproduces the behavior of LoRA and full fine-tuning. sf1873fb0e8.title: One, No One and One Hundred Thousand CTs: Testing Anatomical Control in Text-to-CT Generation
sf1873fb0e8.description: arXiv:2611.33003v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent advances in deep learning and the public availability of computed tomography (CT) datasets with paired reports have enabled many Text-to-CT generators. However, their evaluations almost always differ in preprocessing and metrics, which hinders comparison. Moreover, their protocols almost never test how editing the report changes the CT, not even at the same seed, so the report is often assumed to control the anatomy without evidence of how much and how consistently it does. We therefore propose CtrlCT, a toolkit that tests two properties of a generator, Credibility and Control. sf1873fb0e8.summary: Researchers introduce CtrlCT, a toolkit that standardizes evaluation of text-to-CT generators and tests whether report edits consistently change the generated anatomy.
sf1873fb0e8.why: Provides a common evaluation protocol for medical text-to-CT generators, though the source text gives limited detail on results.

s6c7e3e2421.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
s6c7e3e2421.description: arXiv:2611.33004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates large language model (LLM) generation using a lightweight draft. Existing methods evaluate complete recipes under different training configurations, leaving component effects, interactions, and composition benefits unclear. Therefore, we present LEGOSpec, a composable framework for speculative draft design and training. LEGOSpec decomposes draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components that share a unified training infrastructure. s6c7e3e2421.summary: Researchers present LEGOSpec, a composable framework that decomposes speculative decoding draft models into Context, Backbone, Proposal, and Objective components for systematic study.
s6c7e3e2421.why: Helps engineers understand how individual draft-model design choices affect speculative decoding speed, though specific results are not in the provided text.

se274ec7e3c.title: Embodied AI Fails the Mirror Test: How a Simple Mirror Breaks Robot Policies
se274ec7e3c.description: arXiv:2611.33010v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a simple mirror expose the limitations of today's robotic manipulation policies? Inspired by the mirror self-recognition test in animal cognition, we investigate whether robot policies can reliably manipulate physical objects in scenes containing their reflections. We introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark built on RoboDojo that preserves task objectives, success criteria, and policy checkpoints while comparing a mirror-free baseline with single-mirror, dual-mirror, and mirrored-tabletop conditions. se274ec7e3c.summary: Researchers introduce RoboDojo-Mirror, a benchmark showing that adding mirrors to scenes causes five robot manipulation policies to perform worse.
se274ec7e3c.why: Reveals that common robot policies are brittle to reflections, a failure mode teams should test before deploying manipulation systems.

s2164a3d31d.title: Can a Frontier LLM Repair a Quantized Network by Tool-Free Weight-Space Programming?
s2164a3d31d.description: arXiv:2611.33031v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give four large language models (LLMs) of the Claude family the complete weights of a 20k-parameter CIFAR-10 CNN as text and ask them to produce a 4-bit network without tools, data or the ability to run inference. Standard round-to-nearest (RTN) quantization to 4 bit lowers the test accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%. We design four evaluation protocols that differ in the input and task description given to the LLMs and analyze their responses. In the first two protocols the LLMs are given the float and the 4-bit RTN network and are told that the accuracy has dropped significantly. s2164a3d31d.summary: Researchers tested whether four Claude-family LLMs could convert a CIFAR-10 CNN's weights to a 4-bit network without tools, where round-to-nearest quantization drops accuracy from 81.4% to 60.4%.

s5aa9e3310d.title: Context Scaling: A New Frontier of AI Scaling
s5aa9e3310d.description: arXiv:2611.33160v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many failures of deployed AI arise not from weak inference but from a mismatch between the state a task depends on and the context available when the system acts. Relevant user state, repository revisions, tool traces, sensor readings, or environment changes may be unavailable, distorted, or poorly selected. We call the effort to reduce this bottleneck context scaling. We frame a model as $P_\theta(d\mid c)$ within a system governed by three budgets: training $B_\theta$, decision-time $B_d$, and context-infrastructure $B_c$. s5aa9e3310d.summary: An arXiv paper proposes "context scaling," framing deployed AI failures as mismatches between task-relevant state and the context available at decision time.
s5aa9e3310d.why: It suggests context infrastructure, not just training or inference compute, may limit deployed AI systems and deserves budgeting alongside them.

s3965806fbc.title: Constraint-Aware Test-Time Scoring for LLM and VLM Candidate Selection
s3965806fbc.description: arXiv:2611.33161v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When an LLM or VLM produces several candidate answers, picking the best one usually relies on the model's own confidence, a learned judge model, or a domain check. s3965806fbc.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a test-time scoring framework that selects LLM and VLM candidate answers using hard checks plus blended softer checks.
s3965806fbc.why: Engineers choosing among model outputs could use explicit constraint checks rather than relying only on model confidence or a judge model.

sbe1cc5587b.title: AutoformBench: A Lean Formalization Benchmark for Advanced Mathematics
sbe1cc5587b.description: arXiv:2611.33165v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems are increasingly capable of producing machine-checked Lean proofs of advanced mathematical results. Real mathematical formalization, however, is not isolated theorem proving: it requires building the definitions and intermediate lemmas that connect a result to a formal library. sbe1cc5587b.summary: An arXiv paper introduces AutoformBench, a benchmark of 341 Lean 4 tasks testing whether models can build supporting definitions and lemmas for advanced mathematics.
sbe1cc5587b.why: It tests formalization beyond isolated theorem proving, which is closer to how real formal math libraries are built.

sc8682f0486.title: General-Purpose Decision Models for AI Configuration Tuning
sc8682f0486.description: arXiv:2611.33190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI configuration tuning searches for settings that improve the performance of AI systems under a limited budget. Existing tuners use different sampling and search policies, making the choice of decision strategy central to both tuning quality and cost. We investigate whether general-purpose decision models can guide tuning, using Jev as a deployed representative that returns structured choices and numeric scores across diverse tasks. sc8682f0486.summary: An arXiv paper investigates whether a general-purpose decision model, Jev, can guide AI configuration tuning as an optimizer, performance predictor, or region guider.
sc8682f0486.why: If general decision models can match specialized tuners, teams may cut the cost of tuning AI system settings under limited budgets.

sef0eeffeb9.title: What, Who, and When: Structured Harm Assessment for Mental Health Safety via Short Reasoning
sef0eeffeb9.description: arXiv:2611.33263v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The growing use of large language models (LLMs) for mental health support raises important safety concerns. Existing guard models primarily identify categories of harmful content, often overlooking the context needed to determine an appropriate response. We introduce a clinically grounded taxonomy that characterizes harm along three dimensions: what the harm is, who is involved, and when it occurs. It further separates harm characterization from intervention decisions, thus enabling safety policies to be specified outside the model weights through explicit, clinician-curated instructions that can be updated and audited. sef0eeffeb9.summary: An arXiv paper introduces a clinically grounded taxonomy for assessing LLM mental health harms along what, who, and when dimensions, separate from intervention decisions.
sef0eeffeb9.why: Separating harm characterization from intervention policy lets teams specify safety rules outside model weights for mental health applications.

s63908ad4c4.title: Certify What You Plant: Shortcut-Free Proof Depth in Logical Reasoning Data
s63908ad4c4.description: arXiv:2611.33303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Procedurally generated logic problems are used to both evaluate and train reasoning in language models. Their difficulty is usually set by planting a proof, that is, by sampling a proof of the desired depth and stating its premises as the problem. However, a planted proof is only one possible proof. A problem can also have shorter proofs, or several unrelated ones, and its stated depth then overstates what solving it requires. We measure what a problem actually requires, relative to a stated set of inference rules. s63908ad4c4.summary: An arXiv paper shows that planted proofs can overstate the true depth of procedurally generated logic problems, and proposes measuring the actual required proof depth.
s63908ad4c4.why: Benchmarks and training data labeled by stated depth may misrepresent reasoning difficulty, affecting how models are evaluated and trained.

s2e47ed7ddb.title: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis in Jacobian-Space: Language and Vision Models Agree Approximately Up to a Rotation
s2e47ed7ddb.description: arXiv:2611.33304v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) posits that AI models converge toward a shared representation of the world, even when trained on different data modalities. Previous work has found evidence for the PRH in the activations of vision and language models. In this work, we ask whether vision and language models also converge in how they act on these representations: precisely, in how these internal representations affect the models' output. At a chosen layer of a transformer, the Jacobian lens gives every word in the vocabulary (or class in an image classifier) a vector in the hidden state: the vector that most increases the model's tendency to generate that word, at that position or later, or to predict that class. s2e47ed7ddb.summary: An arXiv paper tests whether vision and language models converge in how their internal representations affect outputs, using Jacobian-space analysis.

sefa382521a.title: Brand Recall and Category Accuracy in Language Models: An Audit of 1,000 B2B SaaS Brands
sefa382521a.description: arXiv:2611.33322v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A language model can name a brand without classifying it correctly. This study measures these outcomes separately for 1,000 B2B SaaS brands across 333 product categories. On Gemma 4 12B, with no external retrieval, category prompts elicit 510 brands (51.0%). A separate five-candidate category probe ranks the reference label first for 787 brands, a distractor first for 194, and yields little separation for 19. Among the 981 separated rankings, the error rate is 19.8%. It falls to 3.5% for the 547 brands with a winner-to-runner-up log-probability margin above 0.6. These are within-cohort measurements, not calibrated confidence estimates. Exploratory regressions associate technical coverage with recall and an owned-properties composite with cate
sefa382521a.summary: An arXiv study finds Gemma 4 12B names many B2B SaaS brands without classifying them correctly, with separate measures of brand recall and category accuracy across 1,000 brands.
sefa382521a.why: Teams relying on LLMs for brand or market information should measure recall and classification errors separately, since a model can name a brand yet misclassify it.

saa03895220.title: Confidence scores for gated automation of large language models
saa03895220.description: arXiv:2611.33394v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents built on large language models (LLMs) demonstrate strong capabilities in automated decision-making. However, LLMs may produce incorrect answers with high confidence, limiting their applicability in decisions that affect individuals and organizations. Reliable confidence scores are necessary to gate such decisions, and existing estimates are frequently unavailable or too coarse to support effective gating. This work uses supervised learning to train models to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, enabling automated confident responses and routing uncertain ones for human review. saa03895220.summary: An arXiv paper uses supervised learning to predict the correctness of LLM-generated answers, producing confidence scores to gate automated decisions.
saa03895220.why: Reliable per-answer confidence scores could let teams automate low-risk LLM decisions while routing uncertain ones to humans.

s6109b6ac57.title: Partial Routing: Trace-Tuned Delegation for Resource-Efficient Agentic Workflows
s6109b6ac57.description: arXiv:2611.33402v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI models vary enormously in capability and price. Model routing exploits this by sending easier tasks to cheaper models. However, a single agentic task often combines easy and difficult subtasks, making one model choice for the entire task inefficient. s6109b6ac57.summary: An arXiv paper introduces partial routing, where a frontier model delegates suitable subtasks in agentic workflows to a cheaper worker model using trace-derived guidance.
s6109b6ac57.why: Delegating subtasks rather than whole tasks may reduce agent costs while keeping quality, which matters for production agent budgets.

s4cf7f9ebfa.title: Collaborative Language Models for Semantic IoT Data Processing: Validation through Zero-Shot Human Activity Recognition
s4cf7f9ebfa.description: arXiv:2611.33411v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) systems generate low-level sensor observations that are not directly suitable for process analysis and must first be transformed into semantically meaningful events. This paper investigates collaborative language models as a zero-shot semantic abstraction layer for converting such observations into higher-level event and activity labels. s4cf7f9ebfa.summary: An arXiv paper proposes a five-stage workflow using collaborative language models to turn raw IoT sensor data into semantic activity labels with zero-shot human activity recognition.
s4cf7f9ebfa.why: It offers a way to convert noisy sensor streams into event labels without task-specific training data.

s4dddd10969.title: Dynamic Reasoning in Next-Gen Detection and Response: An Empirical Study of LLM Triage, Reinforcement Tuning, and Adversarial Evasion
s4dddd10969.description: arXiv:2611.33470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present an end-to-end empirical study of dynamic reasoning in next-generation detection and response pipelines, evaluating how static classifiers, graph-based signal fusion, and large language model (LLM) triage agents perform under strict human-analyst attention budgets (Recall at B alerts/day). s4dddd10969.summary: An arXiv empirical study evaluates static classifiers, graph-based fusion, and LLM triage agents for security detection under analyst alert budgets across 56 experiments.

s80f404d8b5.title: CA-RAG: Constraint-Aligned Retrieval for Structurally Faithful Long-Form Generation
s80f404d8b5.description: arXiv:2611.33497v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) typically optimises evidence selection for semantic relevance, whereas compliance-sensitive long-form generation also requires evidence supporting explicit structural obligations. s80f404d8b5.summary: An arXiv paper proposes CA-RAG, a retrieval method that adds ontology-derived structural constraints to queries so long-form generation includes evidence for mandatory clauses.
s80f404d8b5.why: Compliance-sensitive document generation may omit required clauses when retrieval optimizes only for semantic relevance, and this targets that gap.

s7e922b4c2c.title: Learning to Reason in Real-Time
s7e922b4c2c.description: arXiv:2611.33513v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents that operate in the real world must reason correctly and on-time, yet they currently do not account for how time should alter their reasoning. Modern agents learn to do tasks in environments that are entirely synchronous: where the world waits for the agent to act before changing. A real-time environment, by contrast, changes independent of the agent. Existing approaches try to bridge this gap by imposing a ratio of thinking to acting. However, for an agent to succeed in real-time it must learn to act quickly when delay is costly and to reason longer when the benefit outweighs the missed opportunities. s7e922b4c2c.summary: An arXiv paper argues AI agents in real-time environments must learn to balance reasoning and action speed, since the world changes independently of the agent.
s7e922b4c2c.why: Agents acting in live environments face costs from delay that synchronous training setups do not capture, so timing-aware reasoning matters for deployment.

sbdb12eac8f.title: PeerReveal: Learning to Generalize in AI Peer Review Detection
sbdb12eac8f.description: arXiv:2611.33555v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Can we distinguish fully AI-generated reviews from those using AI only to rewrite human judgement? We evaluate PeerReveal on PeerShift, a new, challenging test set of 5,430 reviews spanning multiple domains, including machine learning, life sciences, and social sciences, combining variation in disciplinary review conventions with diverse AI review-production mechanisms. With
sbdb12eac8f.summary: Researchers introduce PeerReveal, a detector that distinguishes fully AI-generated peer reviews from human reviews merely rewritten with AI, tested on a new 5,430-review set.
sbdb12eac8f.why: Reliable detection of AI-written reviews matters to conference organizers and research teams building trust and integrity checks into review workflows.

sd132989012.title: FIG-MAC: A Fine-grained Inspiration Graph Empowered Multi-Agent Collaboration for Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation
sd132989012.description: arXiv:2611.33563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated Scientific Hypothesis Generation (ASHG) leveraging large language models (LLMs) aims to harness their strengths in knowledge integration, logical reasoning, and text generation for efficiently producing innovative, verifiable scientific hypotheses. However, existing approaches face three critical limitations: (i) insufficient fine-grained knowledge representation, as unstructured context impairs LLM comprehension and reasoning; (ii) lack of knowledge evolution traceability, constraining the generation of innovative cross-domain conjectures; (iii) absence of human-inspired and role-specialized multi-agent collaboration, failing to leverage the efficient innovation mechanisms arising from cognitive diversity and division of labor amon
sd132989012.summary: FIG-MAC proposes a multi-agent framework using fine-grained inspiration graphs to improve LLM-based automated generation of scientific hypotheses.

s758ccd72bc.title: Aligned Machine: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Embedding Similarity via Human Comparative Judgements
s758ccd72bc.description: arXiv:2611.33594v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Embedding models increasingly inform how people search, recommend, and retrieve information, yet we lack credible ways to test whether these similarity judgments reflect how humans understand meaning. Existing benchmarks typically rely on static, expert-labeled pairs with coarse Likert-style annotations, limiting scalability and making it difficult to obtain consistent, high-confidence annotations. We introduce Aligned Machine, an interactive, public-facing platform that transforms broad participation into a continuously growing Human-Aligned Similarity Benchmark (HASB) for evaluating semantic alignment in embedding-based systems. Participants complete a cognitively-natural, forced-choice task, comparing two pairs of items (text or images) an
s758ccd72bc.summary: Aligned Machine is an interactive public platform that collects human comparative judgments to build a growing benchmark for multimodal embedding similarity.
s758ccd72bc.why: Teams relying on embedding models for search and retrieval get a continuously updated check on whether similarity scores match human meaning.

s8c28a80eb4.title: Learning from Natural Images Untangles Number Sense
s8c28a80eb4.description: arXiv:2611.33615v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Numerical cognition is a simple yet fundamental ability that remains challenging for modern vision-language models. Meanwhile, number sense is already present in numerically na\"ive animals, suggesting that it can emerge without explicit numerical learning. Deep neural networks provide a related observation, with numerosity-selective units appearing after training on unrelated natural-image tasks and even before any training. However, these findings leave unresolved whether visual learning contributes beyond the spontaneous emergence of numerical selectivity. Human development provides a clue, as children become better at making judgments in which numerosity and proportion conflict. Here, we introduce a geometric framework to trace how repres
s8c28a80eb4.summary: A study examines whether visual learning on natural images contributes to number sense in vision-language and deep neural networks beyond spontaneous emergence.

s0ec3cbaa6a.title: Controllable CAD Generation and Interactive Editing of Fluid Rotors
s0ec3cbaa6a.description: arXiv:2611.33617v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Computer-aided design (CAD) provides the geometric foundation for rotors in fluid rotating machinery. However, creating models for different rotors requires different modeling processes, making it difficult to control geometry through design intent and reuse existing models. We introduce VaneCraft, an agent-driven framework for rotor generation, inverse recovery, and editing through a unified analytical representation. The agent interprets design requests and invokes geometric modeling operations. The representation defines geometric controls through meridional geometry and independent boundary angle laws. An anisotropic partial differential equation (PDE) maps these controls to the blade surfaces. Geometric parameter correction (GPC) uses a
s0ec3cbaa6a.summary: VaneCraft is an agent-driven CAD framework that generates, recovers, and edits fluid machinery rotors through a unified analytical geometry representation.
s0ec3cbaa6a.why: Shows how agents can translate design intent into editable CAD operations, relevant to engineering teams automating geometric modeling.

sef38228c8d.title: How Much Effort Does an AI Code Reviewer Need? Evidence from Claude 5.5 Models on Plausible-but-Wrong Patches
sef38228c8d.description: arXiv:2611.33639v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI coding agents write code faster than people can review it, so teams add AI reviewers. Reasoning models let such a reviewer trade cost for diligence through an effort setting. We asked how much effort a reviewer needs to catch plausible-but-wrong patches, which pass a benchmark's tests but fail stronger ones. Claude Opus 5.5 (preregistered), Sonnet 5.5 and Haiku 5.5 (exploratory) each reviewed the same 90 agent-written Django patches from SWE-bench Verified at low, medium and high effort. By strengthened SWE-ABS tests, 55 patches were wrong and 35 correct. In every model, high effort accepted fewer wrong patches than low (false success .45 against .67 for Opus, .49 against .65 for Sonnet, .51 against .78 for Haiku), a supported difference f
sef38228c8d.summary: Tests of Claude 5.5 models as AI code reviewers at varying effort levels on 90 agent-written Django patches measure how well they catch plausible-but-wrong fixes.
sef38228c8d.why: Engineering leaders deciding how much reviewer compute to spend on AI code review get evidence on effort settings versus catching subtly wrong patches.

sbcac498e79.title: SlicePlanner: Logic-Guided Agentic AI for Online QoS-Aware Network Slicing in Open RAN
sbcac498e79.description: arXiv:2611.33664v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Adaptive network slicing in Open Radio Access Network (O-RAN) demands reconfiguration decisions that respond to live traffic conditions while remaining safe with respect to Service Level Agreement (SLA) constraints, a combination that purely data-driven controllers cannot reliably guarantee without continuous retraining. We present SlicePlanner, a logic-guided closed-loop framework that treats each RAN reconfiguration as a controlled hypothesis: proposed from live and historical KeyPerformance Indicator (KPI) evidence, filtered through explicit SLA constraints and mined RAN control rules, and committed only when post-action measurements confirm improvement. SlicePlanner comprises two cooperating agents: SliceSense, which monitors live KPIs, r
sbcac498e79.summary: SlicePlanner is a logic-guided agentic framework that proposes and filters O-RAN network slicing reconfigurations against SLA constraints in closed loop.
sbcac498e79.why: Combining agentic proposals with explicit logical safety filters offers a pattern for deploying autonomous controllers where SLA violations are unacceptable.

saf04c85c97.title: Interactive Proofs as a Unified Framework for Evaluating and Leveraging Verifiable Proof Generation by LLM Agents
saf04c85c97.description: arXiv:2611.33676v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in LLM-assisted theorem proving and program verification have attracted widespread attention. Beyond determining whether a proposition is true, LLM agents must produce evidence that can be independently checked by humans or formal verification tools. To evaluate the underlying, protocol-agnostic ability of LLM agents to construct verifiable proofs-rather than their proficiency with any particular proof language or verification tool, we introduce Merlin-Bench. Drawing on interactive proof systems from computational complexity theory, we cast an LLM agent as the prover: under a designated protocol, the agent interacts with a formal verifier to substantiate its claimed answer to a problem instance. We develop an automated framewo
saf04c85c97.summary: Merlin-Bench is introduced to evaluate LLM agents' ability to produce verifiable proofs, drawing on interactive proof systems from complexity theory.
saf04c85c97.why: Evaluating whether agent outputs can be independently checked addresses a core reliability problem for LLMs in formal verification workflows.

s3d3bc7f2d8.title: Faster and Better Query (FBQ): Learning Future-Position Probes from the First Generated Token
s3d3bc7f2d8.description: arXiv:2611.33679v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a large language model (LLM) evicts prompt keys and values at the end of prefill, it must decide what to keep before it sees the queries from subsequent decoding steps. Generating a draft continuation can approximate those queries at the cost of extra autoregressive steps. Can we use the embedding of the first output token, already available from the final prefill logits, to construct low-cost pseudo queries that approximate future decoding queries? We start with FTQ-8, which places eight copies of the first token ID at consecutive future positions and reads their attention to the prompt in one causal forward pass. Each copy sees a different prefix, but a generic opening such as the offers a poor literal guess for seven successive tokens
s3d3bc7f2d8.summary: FBQ proposes using the first generated token's embedding to build low-cost pseudo queries for deciding which LLM prompt KV cache entries to keep during decoding.
s3d3bc7f2d8.why: Offers a way to improve KV cache eviction without extra draft decoding steps, relevant to teams optimizing LLM inference memory and latency.

s3fb02af113.title: EVA: Evidence-seeking Visual Agent for Hallucination-Resistant Multimodal Reasoning
s3fb02af113.description: arXiv:2611.33706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hallucinations in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) often arise from visual assumptions that go unchecked. Self-reflection, multi-agent debate, and counterfactual verification can reinforce erroneous conclusions when they rely on the same unverified visual assumptions. External visual tools can provide verifiable evidence, but models may select the wrong tools, supply incorrect parameters, or ignore or contradict the evidence they obtain. In this work, we propose EVA, an Evidence-seeking Visual Agent that reframes multimodal reasoning as an explicit process of evidence acquisition and verification. At the core of EVA is a unified evidence-grounded execution pipeline designed to address the above challenges through two tightly coupled m
s3fb02af113.summary: EVA is an evidence-seeking visual agent that uses external visual tools to verify assumptions and reduce hallucinations in multimodal LLM reasoning.
s3fb02af113.why: Grounding multimodal answers in verifiable tool evidence targets a practical hallucination problem for teams deploying vision-language systems.

sf0c5f52e5d.title: P-FedSkill: A Personalized Federated Skill Learning Framework under Task Heterogeneity
sf0c5f52e5d.description: arXiv:2611.33707v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Skill learning has become an important way to improve agent performance. However, agent trajectories often contain sensitive information and cannot be shared across clients, hindering collaborative skill learning. To tackle this issue, federated skill learning (FSL) has emerged as a solution by distilling trajectories into compact skill representations and uploading them to a central server for sharing. However, existing FSL methods typically share skills based on skill similarity without considering their contributions to heterogeneous tasks across clients, thereby degrading agent performance. To address this challenge, we propose P-FedSkill, a personalized FSL framework that comprises three key components: local skill extraction (LSE), pers
sf0c5f52e5d.summary: P-FedSkill proposes a personalized federated skill learning framework that shares agent skills across clients with heterogeneous tasks without exposing sensitive trajectories.
sf0c5f52e5d.why: Addresses sharing learned agent skills across organizations without leaking sensitive trajectory data, a privacy concern for enterprise agent deployments.

s10f075af16.title: PowerFix: Physics-Guided Iterative Repair for LLM-Assisted Power Converter Design
s10f075af16.description: arXiv:2611.33712v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly being explored for automated engineering design. However, repairing power-converter designs that fail engineering validation remains challenging: the system must identify physical causes, locate responsible design variables, and resolve violations without compromising other constraints. We introduce PowerFix, a physics-guided iterative repair framework that converts validation failures into structured diagnoses and executable patches while preserving topology and design requirements. PowerDiagGraph links failed checks to possible physical causes and constrains repair routes. An LLM prioritizes these routes, while a deterministic compiler translates selected repairs into authorized field-level
s10f075af16.summary: PowerFix is a physics-guided iterative repair framework that turns validation failures into structured diagnoses and patches for LLM-generated power converter designs.
s10f075af16.why: Shows a method for LLM design agents to repair failing engineering designs while preserving constraints, relevant to automated hardware design teams.

s7c12f552f9.title: KeyDeck: Multi-Paper-to-Slide Generation via Cross-Paper Synthesis and Reference-Guided Personalization
s7c12f552f9.description: arXiv:2611.33715v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-paper-to-slide generation (multi-PTSG) is the task of constructing a unified presentation from multiple research papers by selecting, organizing, and synthesizing information across sources. This task introduces two main challenges: (i) combining multiple sources into a coherent narrative requires identifying cross-paper relationships and synthesizing their content, and (ii) the desired organization and emphasis varies substantially across presenters, making personalization essential for user satisfaction. Motivated by these challenges, we propose KeyDeck, the first multi-PTSG framework that integrates per-paper and cross-paper analysis to identify relationships among sources and synthesize their contributions into a coherent narrative,
s7c12f552f9.summary: KeyDeck introduces multi-paper-to-slide generation that synthesizes cross-paper content and personalizes presentations to presenter preferences.

sd0e11bb3c2.title: Asset4D-Bench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Editable 3D and 4D Reconstruction
sd0e11bb3c2.description: arXiv:2611.33728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A cart can follow its reference trajectory while its cargo floats above the deck. Asset4D-Bench tests whether coding agents recover objects, motion and interactions from visual references as editable Blender scenes. Its 114 conditions span image editing, video reconstruction with matched full or partial starter assets, and independently selected from-scratch tasks. We independently reopen projects and measure them against native reference states. The 228 archived scores include original delivery outcomes and versioned measures of scene quality. On 24 from-scratch tasks, each model earns full dynamics credit on 14. Of these, three GPT-6.1-Sol and eight GPT-6-Astra reconstructions earn zero relation points. Under the fixed scoring weights, rela
sd0e11bb3c2.summary: Asset4D-Bench benchmarks coding agents on recovering editable 3D and 4D Blender scenes from visual references across 114 conditions.
sd0e11bb3c2.why: Provides a benchmark for evaluating coding agents on 3D content creation tasks, useful for teams building agentic creative or simulation tooling.

sbd0e3791a2.title: JOVE ICE: Intent Guided Cloud Edge Device Collaboration for AI Glasses
sbd0e3791a2.description: arXiv:2611.33735v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) and LLM based agents have expanded the capabilities of AI glasses, enabling egocentric visual question answering, memory retrieval, and proactive assistance. These applications involve diverse inputs, including speech, images, and video, and range from simple device control to complex visual reasoning, posing challenges for efficient computation and communication. While video centric capabilities have received considerable attention, simple text based and device executable tasks remain underexplored despite their prevalence in daily interactions. Efficiently supporting diverse workloads within a unified assistant remains an open challenge. We propose JOVE ICE, an intent guided cloud, edge, and d
sbd0e3791a2.summary: JOVE ICE proposes intent-guided collaboration between cloud and device for AI glasses, routing simple text and device-executable tasks differently from video workloads.
sbd0e3791a2.why: Intent-based splitting of work between edge and cloud is a useful pattern for latency and cost tradeoffs in on-device AI products.

s035874d82c.title: WhatIf: Counterfactual World Models over Action-Grounded Causal Graphs for Robotic Manipulation
s035874d82c.description: arXiv:2611.33745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: World models predict what happens under an action, but choosing between actions requires comparing their outcomes in the same physical situation. Factual transitions alone determine action-wise marginal futures and average effects, but not individual effects or the probability that switching actions causes harm. We introduce WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for manipulation that couples candidate futures through shared latent physics and transition noise inferred from factual history. Each candidate action induces a sparse object-factor causal graph describing the physical pathways it activates. Rolling out these graphs under the shared situation anchors predictions to observed outcomes and confines action contrasts to the objects each ac
s035874d82c.summary: Researchers propose WhatIf, a counterfactual world model for robotic manipulation that compares candidate action outcomes under shared latent physics inferred from factual history.
s035874d82c.why: It addresses comparing actions in the same physical situation, which matters for robot planning and evaluating harm from switching actions.

sf3bdc8f3bc.title: REFORGE: LLM-Assisted RTL Bug Repair with Structured Context and Verification Feedback
sf3bdc8f3bc.description: arXiv:2611.33748v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can write and repair RTL, but successful compilation or testbench execution does not establish defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, or implementation feasibility. Existing LLM-based RTL repair methods often report a single repair rate without retaining separate evidence for these properties, limiting reproducible comparison and integration into hardware design flows. We present REFORGE, which, to our knowledge, is the first LLM-assisted RTL repair framework that maintains and accumulates structured repair evidence across iterations, allowing it to generate fixes that satisfy multiple objectives simultaneously, including functionality, behavioral equivalence, security, and cost efficiency. REFORGE pro
sf3bdc8f3bc.summary: Researchers present REFORGE, an LLM-assisted RTL bug repair framework that keeps separate evidence for defect removal, behavioral preservation, security, and feasibility.
sf3bdc8f3bc.why: Compilation or passing testbenches alone do not prove a hardware repair is correct, so separated evidence aids reproducible comparison and integration into design flows.

s5f6caed495.title: TransHarness: From Benchmark Overfitting to Transferable Harness Evolution
s5f6caed495.description: arXiv:2611.33757v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Harness evolution offers a path to improving coding agents without updating model weights. However, existing methods can overfit their evolution benchmarks, producing gains that fail to carry over to new tasks. To address this challenge, we introduce Transferable Harness Evolution (TransHarness), which evolves harness intervention policies from same-task success-failure contrasts. These policies couple execution-context triggers with diagnostic guidance, enabling task-dependent checks and corrections beyond the source executions. Cross-task replay and independent semantic selection retain policies that intervene selectively and ground corrections in current-task evidence rather than source-specific solutions. We further curate an independent
s5f6caed495.summary: Researchers introduce TransHarness, a method that evolves coding-agent harness intervention policies from success-failure contrasts so gains transfer to new tasks instead of overfitting benchmarks.
s5f6caed495.why: It offers a way to improve coding agents without updating model weights, with gains that generalize beyond the evolution benchmark.

s313b762197.title: Improving Building Energy Efficiency with an Indoor Environmental World Model and Counterfactual Adaptive Learning
