s313b762197.description: arXiv:2611.33764v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimizing indoor climate systems plays a critical role in achieving the United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals 11 and 13. However, indoor delayed thermodynamic responses and partial observability severely hinder existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods, which are primarily limited by implicit thermal inertia, occupancy dynamic prediction, and cumulative prediction errors during long-horizon rollouts. Thus, we propose a novel occupant-centric indoor climate control framework. It develops indoor environmental world models to predict future physical thermal baselines and dynamic occupancy, explicitly capturing latent thermal inertia. By formulating adaptive regulation as counterfactual advantage learning against future environments v
s313b762197.summary: Researchers propose an occupant-centric indoor climate control framework that uses indoor environmental world models and counterfactual adaptive learning to improve building energy efficiency.
s313b762197.why: It applies world-model-based reinforcement learning to building control, where thermal inertia and partial observability hinder existing methods.

s0a7b71b792.title: CHD-Bench: Diagnosing Congenital Heart Disease through Interactive Examination
s0a7b71b792.description: arXiv:2611.33775v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Diagnosis of congenital heart disease (CHD) requires understanding the spatial relationships between cardiac structures, which clinicians assess by scrolling through CT or cardiac magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) slices and rotating 3D reconstructions. Although automated methods have advanced cardiac segmentation, identifying congenital heart defects from volumetric scans remains an open challenge. The two existing approaches rely on handcrafted diagnostic rules limited to static anatomical abnormalities. We introduce CHD-Bench, the first benchmark for interactive CHD diagnosis, defining a multi-label task and evaluation protocol over 247 CT and MRI scans from three cohorts covering 38 CHD types. We also present CHD-Harness, open-source softw
s0a7b71b792.summary: Researchers introduce CHD-Bench, a benchmark for diagnosing congenital heart disease through interactive examination of CT and MRI volumes rather than static anatomical rules.

sf15ab42622.title: InterGenEHR$^+$: An Interactive Framework for Natural Language-Conditioned Generation of Longitudinal Patient Trajectories
sf15ab42622.description: arXiv:2611.33788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Objective: To develop and validate InterGenEHR$^+$, an interactive framework for natural language-conditioned generation of synthetic tabular electronic health records (EHRs) and longitudinal trajectories for scenario-based evaluation of machine learning models. Methods: An optional large language model (LLM) parser converts clinical requests into structured constraints. Conditional variational autoencoders and diffusion models generate single-time-point records, while diffusion models generate longitudinal trajectories. We evaluate parsing, distributional fidelity, imputation, clinical-constraint adherence, mortality prediction, and clinical plausibility using a multi-institutional cohort of 874 patients receiving venovenous extracorporeal m
sf15ab42622.summary: Researchers present InterGenEHR+, an interactive framework that generates synthetic tabular and longitudinal EHR data from natural language requests using an optional LLM parser and diffusion models.
sf15ab42622.why: Synthetic patient data generated from natural language scenarios could support scenario-based testing of clinical machine learning models.

s1fe898ecb2.title: ExtractBench Pro: The Long Tail of Document Extraction
s1fe898ecb2.description: arXiv:2611.33791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided document extraction benchmark that tests six challenging modes of extraction underrepresented in existing datasets. It is created following a framework for synthetic document generation, in which deterministic document generators assemble challenging components into documents that are designed to be difficult at a level calibrated for frontier systems. We synthesize 100 realistic documents spanning a diverse range of styles. On this data, we evaluate ten coding agents and eight extraction API configurations for accuracy, grounding, and their ability to perfectly extract documents. No extraction system extracts more than 61% of documents error-free. The strongest general-purpose coding agents, Claud
s1fe898ecb2.summary: Researchers released ExtractBench Pro, a schema-guided document extraction benchmark of 100 synthetic documents, and evaluated ten coding agents and eight extraction API configurations on it.
s1fe898ecb2.why: It offers a harder test of extraction tools on long-tail document cases, helping teams compare coding agents and extraction APIs.

s06d40dbaf8.title: Keep or Roll Back? Out-of-Loop Judges for Self-Improving VLA and End-to-End Embodied Policies
s06d40dbaf8.description: arXiv:2611.33794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Self-improvement is now a practical recipe for embodied policies: a policy collects experience, is retrained, and is kept when a judge rates it higher. However, the judge is usually trained or chosen inside the same loop, so its evidence is not independent of the policy. We introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that adds a sealed judge: an evaluator outside the loop that the improver cannot see or optimize against. A new policy is kept only when a sequential test on the sealed judge confirms the gain, with a bounded probability of keeping a worse one. Running the same loop under each judge, we separate two sources of a false gain, which we call judge error (the loop's judge is wrong on its own data) and transfer gap (a real gain there
s06d40dbaf8.summary: Researchers introduce SealedLoop, an evaluation framework that uses a judge outside the training loop to decide whether self-improved embodied policies should be kept.
s06d40dbaf8.why: Self-improvement loops often judge with evidence not independent of the policy; a sealed evaluator can guard against false gains before deployment.

sac3e37b3c3.title: Ensuring Deployment-Time Safety of Neural Network Controlled Systems via Localized Certificate Repair
sac3e37b3c3.description: arXiv:2611.33813v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Barrier certificates provide formal safety guarantees for neural network controlled systems by ensuring that system trajectories avoid unsafe regions over time. However, after deployment, previously unseen obstacles or constraint changes may introduce new unsafe regions, invalidating the original certificate and potentially leading to unsafe behavior. We address this setting with adaptive piecewise barrier certificates, which preserve the original certificate and policy in unchanged regions while introducing localized updates around newly emerged unsafe regions. The central question is how to perform such updates efficiently during system execution without retraining from scratch. Our key idea is to cast deployment-time adaptation as a locali
sac3e37b3c3.summary: Researchers propose adaptive piecewise barrier certificates that locally repair safety certificates for neural network controlled systems when new unsafe regions appear after deployment.
sac3e37b3c3.why: Deployed controllers facing new obstacles or constraint changes can be updated locally while preserving the original certificate in unchanged regions.

s33738813d8.title: Spectral Optimal Transport for Dynamics-Aware Sign Language Generation
s33738813d8.description: arXiv:2611.33818v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Sign language generation (SLG) translates spoken-language text into pose sequences that convey its meaning. Recently, flow-based models with optimal transport (OT) have become a strong SLG baseline by handling the one-to-many nature of text-to-sign. While classifier-free guidance (CFG) could be applied to further strengthen the semantic alignment theoretically, its training involves conditional and unconditional training, which may contradict the pose-space OT, thus reducing the generation quality. Under the condition dropout, one noise sample can be paired with target motions exhibiting incompatible motion dynamics, interfering with the semantic guidance when the text condition is present. To address this issue, we propose Spectral Optimal T
s33738813d8.summary: Researchers propose a spectral optimal transport approach for dynamics-aware sign language generation that aims to improve classifier-free guidance in flow-based pose generation.

s271dd9ffff.title: RadOncGym: An Agent-Based Framework for Radiotherapy Dose-Mimicking Optimization
s271dd9ffff.description: arXiv:2611.33821v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI dose-prediction models generate patient-specific 3D dose distributions from patient anatomy, providing an important intermediate representation for automated radiotherapy planning. However, an AI-predicted dose must undergo downstream optimization to produce a physically constrained treatment plan, a process that requires balancing competing planning objectives. We present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework that enables an LLM agent to iteratively tune 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking optimization. To reduce iterative evaluation cost, RadOncGym incorporates a surrogate verifier that provides rapid feedback while allowing the agent to decide when to request a full planning solve within a fixed solve budget. We evaluate RadO
s271dd9ffff.summary: Researchers present RadOncGym, an agent-based framework where an LLM iteratively tunes 12 planning-objective weights for dose-mimicking radiotherapy plan optimization.
s271dd9ffff.why: It shows an LLM agent tuning optimization parameters in a regulated medical planning loop, though the text gives limited detail on outcomes.

s551923581e.title: MetaDecomp: Adaptive Task Decomposition via Meta-Learned Procedural Memory
s551923581e.description: arXiv:2611.33822v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Reusing past experience in long-horizon tasks requires more than storing successful procedures: Language agents must distinguish which procedures apply and what work remains as execution progresses. We introduce MetaDecomp, an in-context meta-learning framework for adaptive task decomposition that jointly learns a task-relative state space and reusable procedures. Its outer loop builds procedural memory from successful training executions, representing task progress as abstract states and procedures between states as directed acyclic graphs of operations and dependencies. As new progress distinctions are learned, MetaDecomp revisits historical execution evidence to reassess state assignments and reorganize the procedures they support. With me
s551923581e.summary: Researchers introduce MetaDecomp, an in-context meta-learning framework that builds procedural memory from successful executions to adaptively decompose long-horizon tasks for language agents.
s551923581e.why: Reusable procedures stored as state graphs could help agents pick applicable strategies and track remaining work on long tasks.

s6629749d0b.title: Can Its Own Misses Teach an MLLM to Find Small Brain Metastases?
s6629749d0b.description: arXiv:2611.33836v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) are becoming general readers of medical images, yet they remain weak at locating small abnormalities. Brain metastases expose this gap: at 384 px a 0.1 mL lesion covers less than a quarter of one visual token, and at one false positive per scan frontier MLLMs find fewer than 30% of lesions of 0.1-1 mL. Fine-tuning on one dataset helps but transfers poorly, and improving it further is slow trial and error steered by a single score. We introduce LANTERN (Lesion-finding AgeNt Through Error-driven Recursive learNing), a framework in which an MLLM improves recursively from its own misses. LANTERN recasts model development as an error-driven loop: a failure census attributes every missed lesion to one of fou
s6629749d0b.summary: Researchers introduce LANTERN, an error-driven recursive method that helps multimodal LLMs find small brain metastases, which frontier models currently miss often on 0.1-1 mL lesions.
s6629749d0b.why: It targets a clear weakness of MLLMs in medical imaging, where small lesions are hard to locate and fine-tuning transfers poorly.

s65d99987a2.title: FORK: Co-Evolving Safe Disclosure and Decision Skills Against Attackers Who Read Every Refusal
s65d99987a2.description: arXiv:2611.33879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When a guardrail rejects an LLM agent's action, its message reaches any attacker observing the trajectory: a fixed refusal leaves benign users unable to recover, whereas an explanation can tell the attacker what to try next. We study this as safe disclosure: explaining rejections so that authorized tasks recover without increasing adaptive attack success. Safe disclosure depends on both the decision and the message: what the guardrail blocks and what it reveals to the agent and the attacker. Because hand-written rules alone cannot anticipate how adaptive attackers probe decisions or use messages, we introduce FORK, which co-evolves a guardrail's natural-language decision and disclosure skills with an attacker that reads every public message.
s65d99987a2.summary: Researchers study safe disclosure, explaining LLM agent guardrail refusals so benign users recover without helping attackers, and co-evolve disclosure and decision skills.
s65d99987a2.why: Refusal messages can leak information to attackers, so guardrail designers must balance explanation quality against adaptive attack success.

s30c37cc37f.title: EATS: Scaling Tool-Use Experience for Medical Reasoning Agents
s30c37cc37f.description: arXiv:2611.33897v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine large language model (LLM) reasoning with clinical workflows and specialized neural tools. However, general-purpose LLMs receive limited training exposure to domain-specific medical tools, and the uncertainty and distributional shifts of neural tool outputs make selecting tools from simple descriptions significantly more challenging than in deterministic settings such as calculators or dictionary lookups. In this paper, we propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that leverages accumulated tool-use trajectories to improve tool selection in medical reasoning agents. EATS constructs a memory of past interactions, including queries, tool choices, arguments, and self-evaluated feedback, and re
s30c37cc37f.summary: Researchers propose EATS, an experience-augmented tool selection strategy that uses accumulated tool-use experience to help medical reasoning agents choose neural clinical tools.
s30c37cc37f.why: Selecting among uncertain neural tool outputs is harder than with deterministic tools, and experience-based selection targets that gap for agent builders.

s3e0aa1bb01.title: EGSE: Evidence-Grounded Skill Evolution for Medical Reasoning Agents
s3e0aa1bb01.description: arXiv:2611.33909v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Medical reasoning agents combine foundation models with specialized tools to interpret medical images, yet reusing their historical experience remains challenging. A correct final answer can conceal flawed reasoning or tool use, synthesized advice may lack source support, and superficially similar cases may require different diagnostic procedures. In this paper, we propose EGSE, an evidence-grounded skill evolution framework that distills historical dialogues from similar cases into reusable conditional workflows and progressively refines a multi-faceted skill library through supported and validated updates to improve medical agents. EGSE evaluates intermediate reasoning and tool use and contrasts repeated successful and failed rollouts to ex
s3e0aa1bb01.summary: EGSE is a framework that distills historical dialogues from similar medical cases into reusable conditional workflows for medical reasoning agents that interpret images.
s3e0aa1bb01.why: Shows a way to reuse agent experience while checking that correct answers reflect sound reasoning and tool use, not luck.

sf6df3ac7e3.title: What Does Skill Lift Actually Measure? A Source-Code-Level Audit and Noise-Aware Reanalysis of SkillsBench
sf6df3ac7e3.description: arXiv:2611.33943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent skills are directories of instructions, reference materials, and scripts loaded on demand by coding agents. According to SkillsBench, although human-curated skills can raise the passing rate by about 16.6 percentage points (pp) on average, they have actually reduced the results for some tasks. Later research has started to gate or eliminate skills according to the above per-task gains. We have audited the above benchmark at the source-code level and analysed 7,554 public trials to form 1,421 paired "(configuration, task) cells". Source-code audit identified two controlled-verified cases of grader dependence and one operational definition gap; the average lift on these three tasks was 74.6 pp, and the overall average lift for the full se
sf6df3ac7e3.summary: An audit of the SkillsBench benchmark at source-code level and reanalysis of 7,554 trials question whether reported agent skill gains are reliable.
sf6df3ac7e3.why: Challenges benchmark-based claims that agent skills improve pass rates, so teams should check evaluation methods before relying on skill gains.

s8ff3be331d.title: Should Service Requirements Be Scalarized or Constrained When Minimizing Costs? A Case Study on HVAC Control
s8ff3be331d.description: arXiv:2611.33946v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated decision systems, from learned policies to model-based optimizers, often minimize costs such as energy or resource use while meeting a service requirement, for example the quality of service (QoS) specified in a service level agreement (SLA), a comfort band, or a safety margin. The requirement can be scalarized with the costs into a single objective, with a fixed or an adaptively tuned (Lagrangian) weight, or it can be imposed as a constraint. We study this choice in the Smart Buildings Challenge, in which a single policy controls the heating, ventilation and air conditioning (HVAC) of previously unseen buildings and is evaluated by a weighted sum of comfort, energy cost and carbon emissions. With all other components fixed, we comp
s8ff3be331d.summary: A case study on HVAC control in the Smart Buildings Challenge compares scalarizing service requirements into the cost objective versus imposing them as constraints.
s8ff3be331d.why: Helps engineers choose how to encode SLA or comfort requirements in cost-minimizing automated control systems.

s1c2746193c.title: PatternMiner: Automated Mathematical Discovery Through LLM-Guided Training and Interpretation of Small Models
s1c2746193c.description: arXiv:2611.33966v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: There are several approaches to AI-driven mathematical discovery. One of these involves the use of large language models (LLMs) to resolve well-specified conjectures via text-based reasoning, while another uses narrow models and interpretability for more open-ended, human-in-the-loop exploration using object-based mathematical data. The latter is limited in its ability to move beyond simple empirical pattern detection while the former is not well-designed for direct, open-ended exploration of large mathematical datasets. In this paper we introduce PatternMiner, a system that combines these two paradigms. In PatternMiner, an LLM agent generates mathematical datasets based on an initial broad question, trains narrow machine learning models on t
s1c2746193c.summary: PatternMiner is a framework that uses LLM guidance to train and interpret small models for open-ended mathematical discovery on large datasets.

sa236997ea8.title: Honest but Wrong: Formalizing Retraction in the Ethics of Speech Acts
sa236997ea8.description: arXiv:2611.34011v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A speaker who asserts honestly may later discover that its assertion was false. Such erroneous truths are not lies, yet they raise the question of whether, and on which moral grounds, the speaker must retract them. Using the FIPA-ACL performative disconfirm, we extend a belief-based framework that evaluates speech acts under deontologism and consequentialism to the case of retraction. We prove that the honesty duty of deontologism, which bears on utterances when they are made, never requires retracting an erroneous truth, and add a persistent one, which forbids letting the addressee believe what the speaker no longer believes. On a legal-advice case implemented in Answer Set Programming, we show that deontologism and consequentialism both req
sa236997ea8.summary: A paper formalizes retraction of honestly made but false assertions within a belief-based speech-act framework, proving deontologism's honesty duty never requires retracting them.

sed7660ba87.title: Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models via Agentic Model Editing
sed7660ba87.description: arXiv:2611.34036v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Few-shot adaptation transfers pretrained Vision-Language Models (VLMs) to new domains using a small set of labeled images. Most methods fit prompts, representations, or classifiers within an adaptation procedure specified in advance. Yet the visual distinctions needed for recognition can differ substantially across domains, motivating the question: Can an LLM agent use few-shot examples and model observations to design the adaptation procedure itself? We propose Agentic Model Editing (AME), an agentic framework that jointly designs input transformations, encoder edits, feature computation, and classifier fitting as an executable, domain-customized adaptation program. The agent inspects images, class semantics, model parameters, intermediate r
sed7660ba87.summary: Agentic Model Editing (AME) proposes an LLM agent that designs the few-shot adaptation procedure for vision-language models, including input transforms, from few labeled images.
sed7660ba87.why: Suggests agents could automate adaptation design for VLMs rather than relying on fixed prompt or classifier pipelines.

s9d9674ee2d.title: Budget, Readout or Reasoning? Where Small Reasoning Models Lose Value in Auction Bidding
s9d9674ee2d.description: arXiv:2611.34068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ad platforms and marketplaces show bidders a bid landscape, the estimated chance of winning at each candidate bid, and increasingly let agents built on reasoning language models choose the bid. We give six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters such landscapes, with win curves from eBay closing prices and from a simulated advertising market (AuctionNet), and score their bids on held-out auctions against an exact calculator. Because the agent is handed the estimates, the lost value can be split by cause. Two failures belong to the models. They pass over the best option even when the values written in their own trace already rank it first, and their wrong answers lean toward the highest bid on the menu. The lean is about the bid's size,
s9d9674ee2d.summary: Researchers evaluated six open reasoning models of 4B to 14B parameters on auction bidding, splitting lost value into causes such as budget, readout, and reasoning failures.
s9d9674ee2d.why: Indicates where small reasoning models fail in bidding agents, informing whether to fix estimates, decision logic, or model capacity.

sda43a02054.title: Not Every Input Needs Everything: Unifying Expert Gating, Model Cascades, and Agent Orchestration
sda43a02054.description: arXiv:2611.34112v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Executing monolithic neural weights, frontier foundation models, or entire multi-agent workflows uniformly on every input incurs substantial computational, latency, and monetary overhead. Conditional computation mitigates this cost by deciding dynamically which internal experts, model endpoints, or specialized agents to invoke per request. Yet token-level gating in sparse neural architectures, query-level model cascades, and task-level multi-agent coordination have largely progressed in disconnected research silos, obscuring recurring system failures and transferable fixes. In this systematic review, we synthesize 2,289 studies published between 2017 and September 2026 (selected from 13,884 unique records) across 20 methodological families un
sda43a02054.summary: A paper unifies expert gating, model cascades, and multi-agent orchestration as conditional computation approaches that decide which experts, models, or agents to invoke per request.
sda43a02054.why: Offers a common framing for cutting compute, latency, and cost by routing requests to only the components each input needs.

s5ddc80c89f.title: Letting Models Manage Their Own Context: Where We Stand
s5ddc80c89f.description: arXiv:2611.34147v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent harnesses today manage context on the model's behalf: when the window fills, the harness triggers a compaction that summarizes the history. We study the alternative, \emph{model-driven} context management, in which the model itself decides when and what to compact through a context API. We gave models control over their own context in \nooa, NVIDIA's open source agent harness, and compared the two strategies on document research and machine learning engineering across context budgets from 8K to 512K tokens. Models that use the context API effectively reach higher accuracy, often with fewer input tokens, especially at tight budgets: \textbf{GPT 6.1 nearly triples its score at a 32K budget} on OfficeQA Pro v2 (21\%~$\rightarrow$~56\%), an
s5ddc80c89f.summary: NVIDIA researchers compared model-driven context management, where models decide when and what to compact via a context API, against harness-triggered compaction in its open source agent harness.
s5ddc80c89f.why: Gives engineers evidence on whether letting models manage their own context beats automatic summarization across budgets from 8K to 512K tokens.

s37d15bd370.title: SOLO: Towards Sample-Faithful and Detectable LLM Watermarking under Repeated Sampling via Content-Anchored Single-Owner Contexts
s37d15bd370.description: arXiv:2611.34190v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Providers watermark the outputs of large language models, while applications sample many responses per prompt for self-consistency, best-of-n selection, and uncertainty estimation. We show that deployed configurations of distortion-free watermarks, which deduplicate keyed contexts only within a response, couple the responses of a request: answer templates make all responses query the watermark with the same context before the answer, so collisions across responses, usually assumed rare, become the norm. Key pools reduce or avoid the coupling at the cost of multiple testing, and the exact remedy of a context history shared across the request leaves many positions unwatermarked. We propose SOLO, which keeps a request-scoped context history but
s37d15bd370.summary: SOLO proposes content-anchored single-owner contexts to make LLM watermarking sample-faithful and detectable when applications draw repeated samples per prompt.
s37d15bd370.why: Shows deployed distortion-free watermarks can collide across repeated samples, affecting detection for apps using self-consistency or best-of-n.

s2b73c37364.title: PROVE: Mitigating Long-Horizon LLM Collusion with Reinforcement Learning from Verified Evidence
s2b73c37364.description: arXiv:2611.34215v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: When LLM agents verify each other's work over a long interaction, they drift into collusion: they come to accept work without the evidence that the verification protocol requires. Collusion is absent at the start and builds up episode by episode, which we trace to accurate feedback accumulating in memory. An agent that follows the rule is told that its verdict was wrong whenever its peer was right, so breaking the rule is the reward-maximizing choice, and agents talk themselves into it in their private reflections. Existing mitigations leave the agents unchanged; we train the behavior out. PROVE (Protocol Reinforcement from Verified Evidence) is a multi-agent reinforcement learning method that rewards verdicts by the evidence behind them rath
s2b73c37364.summary: PROVE uses reinforcement learning from verified evidence to reduce long-horizon collusion among LLM agents that verify each other's work without required evidence.
s2b73c37364.why: Highlights that multi-agent verification pipelines can drift into accepting unsupported work, a reliability risk for agent systems.

s3dc5666ad1.title: Did the Model Forecast It, or Already Know It? Evaluating Large Language Models for Novel Drug-Target Prioritisation with a Temporal Knowledge-Graph Oracle
s3dc5666ad1.description: arXiv:2611.34247v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI systems increasingly help decide which drug targets enter costly clinical trials. We recast each target-disease hypothesis as a dated event, the pair's first clinical trial. This lets us test whether a language model can forecast such events after its training cutoff, rather than recall events before it. We rebuild a dated biomedical knowledge graph as it stood at the end of each year from 2020 up to its newest version. We then ask six open language models, with and without this graph, which targets will enter a first trial for a disease the next year. Without retrieval, the models rank about as well as trial history, a count of each target's past trials in the same therapeutic area, also after their training cutoffs. Evidence dated before
s3dc5666ad1.summary: Researchers rebuilt a dated biomedical knowledge graph and tested six open language models on forecasting which drug targets will enter a first clinical trial after training cutoffs.
s3dc5666ad1.why: Separates genuine forecasting from recall of past events, relevant to teams evaluating AI for drug-target prioritisation.

s4dae22ce7d.title: EXPOSURE: Explaining Sources of Uncertainty in Reinforcement Learning
s4dae22ce7d.description: arXiv:2611.34248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Shapley values in reinforcement learning are used to explain which observation features drive an agent's behavior and expected return, but not its certainty. Explaining certainty requires understanding how observation features influence different sources of return uncertainty, and Shapley values need the agent's prediction for every subset of visible features. We propose EXPOSURE, which uses one mask-aware belief network for both action selection and Shapley explanations. It explains the variance of the return, split into an observational part due to missing features and an inherent part due to the environment's own randomness, and the entropy of its belief over the masked features. In tic-tac-toe and Minesweeper, where exact Shapley values a
s4dae22ce7d.summary: EXPOSURE uses a mask-aware belief network to explain sources of return variance in reinforcement learning agents, splitting uncertainty into observational and other parts.

s2806cd06eb.title: Navigent: A Geometry-Grounded Agentic Framework for Vision Language Navigation
s2806cd06eb.description: arXiv:2611.34249v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Vision-and-Language Navigation (VLN) with general-purpose multimodal large language models (MLLMs) offers a flexible alternative to task-specific navigation policies, while reliable long-horizon execution remains challenging. Agents must track navigation progress, detect discrepancies between commanded and actual motion, and recognize when movement has passed relevant landmarks or entrances. We present Navigent, an agentic VLN framework built around a frozen MLLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic (GEC). GEC performs two complementary checks: action-to-motion consistency, which evaluates measured displacement against commanded movement, and motion-to-landmark consistency, which tracks agent-selected visual anchors and entrance candidate
s2806cd06eb.summary: Navigent is an agentic vision-language navigation framework built on a frozen multimodal LLM and a Geometry-Grounded Execution Critic that checks progress and motion discrepancies.
s2806cd06eb.why: Shows how adding a geometric execution critic can improve reliability of long-horizon MLLM-driven agents without retraining the base model.

sd60456d644.title: MedSkill-E$^{2}$: Evaluating and Evolving Skills for Medical Agents
sd60456d644.description: arXiv:2611.34250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly use skills to access domain knowledge and complete real-world tasks. We observe that even when a skill specifies the rules and procedures needed for a task, agents may fail to apply them effectively during autonomous execution, a phenomenon we call skill Enable But Underuse (EBU). This issue is particularly consequential in medical tasks, where overlooking a single critical constraint can yield a plausible but incorrect result. To evaluate and address EBU, we introduce MedSkill-E$^{2}$, a framework for evaluating and evolving skills for medical agents. We construct EBU-Bench, a challenging benchmark covering 12 medically relevant task groups and associated skills, to evaluate agents' ability to u
sd60456d644.summary: MedSkill-E2 is a framework to evaluate and evolve skills for medical LLM agents, targeting cases where agents fail to apply skill rules they were given, called Enable But Underuse.
sd60456d644.why: Points to a failure mode where agents ignore provided constraints, which matters for any agent relying on skills in high-stakes domains.

sf4359170ef.title: Crucible: Evaluating LLM Agents in Executable Chemistry Research Environments
sf4359170ef.description: arXiv:2611.34254v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) perform well on chemistry knowledge benchmarks, which mainly assess question answering and isolated tasks. Chemical research, however, requires using specialized tools and interpreting their outputs to obtain chemically valid results. To address this gap, we introduce Crucible Bench to evaluate this ability across all four stages of the design-make-test-analyze (DMTA) cycle. The benchmark contains 1,078 tasks in 12 task families curated from 18 published datasets, covering molecular design, synthesis planning, experimental execution, closed-loop optimization, simulation, and analytical characterization. Agents access 75 domain-specific tools through the Model Context Protocol in seven isolated environments. Sandbo
sf4359170ef.summary: Researchers introduced Crucible Bench, a 1,078-task benchmark testing LLM agents on specialized chemistry tools across the design-make-test-analyze cycle.
sf4359170ef.why: It shows where LLM agents fall short on executable, tool-driven scientific workflows beyond chemistry Q&A, useful for evaluating domain agents.

s0904d61097.title: MeterRouter: Budget-Aware Dynamic Routing for Multi-Agent Systems
s0904d61097.description: arXiv:2611.34327v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) outperform single-agent systems, but inter-agent communication incurs substantial token overhead. While assigning a large LLM to every agent is common, it results in inefficient resource utilization, leaving the system far from the Pareto frontier. The cost of answering a query is set jointly by how many agents are recruited, the role and LLM assigned to each, and communication topology among them. Most existing routers treat cost only implicitly rather than as an explicit optimization constraint. A fixed accuracy-cost preference also cannot express how much a caller is willing to pay for a particular query. We introduce MeterRouter, a budget-aware dynamic router that incremental
s0904d61097.summary: MeterRouter proposes a budget-aware router that explicitly optimizes cost when choosing how many agents, which LLMs, and which communication topology to use in multi-agent systems.
s0904d61097.why: Multi-agent systems incur heavy token overhead, so explicit cost-aware routing could cut inference spend without sacrificing quality.

s7e489d2c94.title: EvoLink-Bench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Self-Evolving Agents in Long-Horizon Interdependent Task Streams
s7e489d2c94.description: arXiv:2611.34400v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents are evolving from passive chatbots into autonomous systems that operate continuously in dynamic environments. Such agents need not only solve current tasks but also learn from past interactions to improve future performance. However, existing streaming benchmarks often rely on short task sequences or largely independent tasks, providing limited evidence of whether agents can effectively reuse experience when later tasks depend on earlier outcomes. To address this gap, we introduce \textbf{EvoLink-Bench}, a benchmark for evaluating self-evolving agents in long-horizon, interdependent task streams. It covers daily office work, multi-turn dialogue, and AutoResearch-style workflows, with persistent workspaces and
s7e489d2c94.summary: EvoLink-Bench is a benchmark testing self-evolving LLM agents on long task streams where later tasks depend on earlier outcomes, measuring experience reuse.
s7e489d2c94.why: It targets whether agents truly learn from past interactions in dependent workflows, a gap that short or independent-task benchmarks miss.

sf64f41971a.title: Agentic Waterfall: An Intent-Driven Information Discovery Framework for Reclaiming User Control in the Attention Economy
sf64f41971a.description: arXiv:2611.34407v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formalize Agentic Waterfall Feed, a new problem of personalized information discovery in which users actively direct recommendations and the system adapts to evolving needs inferred from both explicit requests and browsing behavior. We address this problem with the Agentic Waterfall framework, whose language-model controller maintains persistent user state and coordinates content retrieval, ranking, and state updates. To evaluate systems on this task, we contribute the Agentic Waterfall Dataset and a replay-based evaluation protocol. The dataset combines real content metadata with simulated interaction histories. The protocol compares systems under shared histories using relevance scores and blind judgments of how well recommendations sati
sf64f41971a.summary: The Agentic Waterfall framework uses a language-model controller with persistent user state to let users direct personalized information discovery, along with a new dataset and replay-based evaluation.

s7d8787110a.title: Evaluating Aviation Safety Knowledge Extraction with SmolLM2: From Zero-Shot to Retrieval-Grounded Prompting
s7d8787110a.description: arXiv:2611.34432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Aviation accident narratives contain safety knowledge that is difficult to capture using structured occurrence fields alone. This study evaluates prompting-based knowledge extraction across four dimensions: concept accuracy, verbatim evidence grounding, structural compliance, and directed relation extraction. SmolLM2-1.7B-Instruct was evaluated under zero-shot, one-shot, fixed few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting using 300 National Transportation Safety Board narratives from 2000-2020, containing 3,763 reference concepts and 467 directed relations. Evaluation combined structural checks, verbatim evidence matching, expert-reviewed semantic matching, and paired bootstrap confidence intervals. No prompting strategy performed best across al
s7d8787110a.summary: A study evaluates the small SmolLM2-1.7B model on extracting safety knowledge from 300 aviation accident narratives under zero-shot, few-shot, and retrieval-grounded prompting.
s7d8787110a.why: It offers evidence on how small open models perform on domain knowledge extraction under different prompting strategies, relevant to cost-constrained deployments.

sf712b8344c.title: vSFT: Learning to Verbally Tune Agents at Test Time
sf712b8344c.description: arXiv:2611.34440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model agents are increasingly improved via agentic reinforcement learning, which can be on-policy but suffers from expensive rollouts and sparse rewards, limiting its application at test time. In this paper, we present a verbally Supervised Fine-Tuning (vSFT) framework that enables the conjunction of dense feedback in natural language and weight updates at test time. Specifically, our vSFT forms a closed loop between an agent and a supervisor via a hypernetwork, in which the supervisor generates verbal supervision from the agent's failed trajectories, and the hypernetwork converts that supervision into low-rank weight updates to tune the agent. We validate that this test-time in-parameter evolving process outperforms both its i
sf712b8344c.summary: vSFT proposes a verbally supervised fine-tuning framework where a supervisor generates natural-language feedback and a hypernetwork updates agent weights at test time.
sf712b8344c.why: Combining dense natural-language feedback with test-time weight updates could reduce reliance on expensive on-policy rollouts and sparse rewards.

s653fb27d2e.title: EgoUseBench: Benchmarking Computer-Use Agents under Evolving First-Person Contexts
s653fb27d2e.description: arXiv:2611.34466v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI wearables, such as smart glasses, extend the context available to agents beyond digital environments to users' physical surroundings. With these devices, computer tasks can originate from users' ongoing activities rather than solely from explicit instructions. Through first-person observations, agents can identify objects and activities relevant to user requests and ground digital tasks in the surrounding context. We call this interaction paradigm Ego Use. However, first-person observations are limited by the wearer's viewpoint and may provide incomplete or ambiguous evidence of ongoing activities. As new observations arrive, agents may need to revise their understanding of the physical context and user intent, and reassess whether prior d
s653fb27d2e.summary: EgoUseBench benchmarks computer-use agents that draw on first-person observations from AI wearables like smart glasses to ground digital tasks in users' surroundings.
s653fb27d2e.why: It highlights a new input modality for agents, where physical context from wearables drives computer tasks, which affects future agent design.

s42a679e9ef.title: On Utilization of Edge-AI for condition monitoring towards predictive maintenance: A use case in dairy processing using explainable AI
s42a679e9ef.description: arXiv:2611.34563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are driving Industry 4.0, enhancing productivity, automation, and efficiency in manufacturing systems. This study develops an Edge-AI-based condition monitoring framework, as a step towards predictive maintenance, for a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant, using vibration data collected via a low-power IIoT sensor node and processed on an edge device.
s42a679e9ef.summary: Researchers developed an Edge-AI condition monitoring framework using vibration data and explainable AI to monitor a rotary valve in a dairy processing pilot plant.

s4e46bce9e7.title: Procedure Inference as Memory: Learning Recruiter Decision Procedures from OKF-Structured Episodes in Multi-Session Hiring Assistants
s4e46bce9e7.description: arXiv:2611.34576v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multi-session hiring assistants must infer evolving recruiter preferences and decision patterns across projects and time. We introduce Open Knowledge Format (OKF)-indexed episodic memory to organize interactions and retrieve related events through their lineage. We also introduce Procedure Memory, which learns reusable decision procedures from these episodes through prompted reflection or reinforcement learning. We compare these approaches with no memory, full-history context, and conversation search, and evaluate Jev-class models for index navigation and GPT-5.6 Luna as a lower-cost alternative to GPT-5.4. In our evaluation, OKF-indexed retrieval achieves low-priority preference F1 scores of 0.93-0.95 at medium and high preference overlap be
s4e46bce9e7.summary: The paper introduces OKF-indexed episodic memory and Procedure Memory, which learns recruiter decision procedures from past hiring episodes for multi-session hiring assistants.
s4e46bce9e7.why: Procedure memory that learns reusable decision patterns from interaction history offers a design pattern for long-running enterprise assistants.

s1128633fb0.title: Do We Really Need an LLM for Weight-Space Programming? A Deterministic Forward-Only Paradigm and Its Capability Boundaries
s1128633fb0.description: arXiv:2611.34612v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent work on Weight-Space Programming uses LLMs to edit neural weights with forward passes only, conflating LLM scripting with the underlying algebra of forward-only editing. We show that for core structured editing regimes, an LLM optimizer is unnecessary, and introduce Forward Weight-Space Programming (FWSP): a deterministic pipeline combining probing, localization, stratified operators (O1-O4), automatic blind routing (83.3% vs. 33.3% for a 27B LLM with the same tool library), and paired verification with zero additional per-token computation. For reasoning LLMs, we propose Protected FisherGate, a closed-form covariance-whitened readout edit orthogonal to normal-reasoning states: on DeepSeek-R1-0528-8B, a single frozen math-calibrated pa
s1128633fb0.summary: Forward Weight-Space Programming (FWSP) is proposed as a deterministic, forward-only pipeline for editing neural weights without an LLM optimizer, reporting 83.3% blind routing versus 33.3% for a 27B LLM.
s1128633fb0.why: If a deterministic pipeline matches LLM-driven weight editing in structured cases, it could lower cost and complexity for model editing workflows.

s2f31d0647a.title: HoMe: Toward Practical Harness Optimization of Memory Systems for AI Assistants
s2f31d0647a.description: arXiv:2611.34624v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The behavior of memory systems for long-running AI assistants is governed by a harness, which consists of the code, prompts, and configurations for memory construction, maintenance, retrieval, and answer generation. However, optimizing the harness of a memory system remains largely manual, and unrestricted editing alone does not ensure structural improvements. In this paper, we introduce HoMe, an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively evaluates candidate harnesses and derives each new candidate from any previously evaluated harness by editing any part of it. HoMe combines session-level memory versioning with execution traces to identify shared failure mechanisms across cases and localize them to the responsible sessions and harness comp
s2f31d0647a.summary: HoMe is an evaluation-driven framework that iteratively optimizes the harness, including code, prompts, and configurations, of memory systems for long-running AI assistants.
s2f31d0647a.why: Automating harness optimization for memory systems could reduce manual tuning effort for assistants that need persistent context.

s8b1416f29c.title: ZeroHero: Training Small Language Agents from Scratch
s8b1416f29c.description: arXiv:2611.34635v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large pretrained language models provide capable policies for interactive tasks, but how much model capacity is necessary for a specialized language agent? We introduce ZeroHero, a framework for training small language agents (SLAs) from scratch. In each environment, a large language model acts as the expert, and we collect its successful trajectories. We pretrain each SLA, which has fewer than 50 million parameters, to predict the expert's responses given the interaction history. We then post-train the agent on its own interactions using proximal policy optimization (PPO). During post-training, reasoning alignment supplements environment rewards with expert supervision on the language the agent generates alongside its actions. We evaluate th
s8b1416f29c.summary: ZeroHero trains small language agents with fewer than 50 million parameters from scratch, using expert LLM trajectories for pretraining and then self-interaction post-training.
s8b1416f29c.why: It suggests task-specific agents may not need large pretrained models, which could reduce serving costs for narrow environments.

sfa1af3715a.title: REE: A Scientific Research Entrance Exam for AI Agents
sfa1af3715a.description: arXiv:2611.34646v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Autonomous research agents are emerging as a promising approach to scientific problem-solving across disciplines, owing to their growing ability to improve a solution through repeated experiments. Evaluating this ability requires benchmarks that pose open-ended research problems and measure improvements over established scientific methods. We introduce REE (Research Entrance Exam), a benchmark that tests AI agents on scientific research. It consists of 100 open-ended research problems spanning five broad scientific areas and 23 domains. To ensure high quality, every problem is drawn from active research in its field and individually reviewed by domain experts. Each problem is posed as a task of iterative improvement: an agent has up to 12 hou
sfa1af3715a.summary: REE is a benchmark of 100 open-ended research problems across five scientific areas and 23 domains, testing whether AI research agents improve solutions over established methods.
sfa1af3715a.why: It provides a harder, open-ended evaluation for research agents than fixed-answer benchmarks, useful for judging scientific automation claims.

sfcf1acf95d.title: A Failure-Driven Data Flywheel for Post-Training Vision-Language-Action Models
sfcf1acf95d.description: arXiv:2611.34698v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pretrained vision-language-action (VLA) models rarely satisfy all behavioral requirements of a new platform, and teams without a large deployed fleet lack the data to address the resulting failures. We propose a failure-driven data flywheel for post-training such models. It constructs target scenarios absent from the available data by inserting task-relevant entities into reconstructed real-world scenes, and evaluates the model against each behavioral requirement of the target task. Failure rates form a failure map across task conditions and difficulty levels, which is re-evaluated after each round and assigns larger data generation quotas to conditions where the model still fails. We instantiate the framework in autonomous driving for occlud
sfcf1acf95d.summary: A failure-driven data flywheel constructs missing target scenarios by inserting entities into reconstructed scenes to post-train vision-language-action robot models without a large fleet.
sfcf1acf95d.why: Teams without large deployed fleets can use synthetic failure-targeted data to improve robot policies, lowering the data barrier for VLA models.

s81a46184d9.title: From Shared Patterns to Individual Evidence: Two-Stage Reasoning for Emerging Entities in Temporal Knowledge Graphs
s81a46184d9.description: arXiv:2611.34708v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Temporal knowledge graphs (TKGs) continually introduce emerging entities whose interaction histories evolve from zero-shot debuts into sparse, bursty few-shot trajectories. However, current paradigms are fragmented: pattern-transfer methods lack catalog-wide event memory, whereas online memory models suffer from endpoint-role asymmetry that degrades unseen-answer ranking. Furthermore, sparse early interactions exhibit both long-range dispersion and local redundancy under skewed distribution. To address these challenges, we propose INSPIRE (Integrating Shared Patterns and Individual Evidence for Reasoning), a two-stage forecasting framework over a known catalog. In Stage I, INSPIRE learns an availability-aware shared-pattern predictor that fus
s81a46184d9.summary: INSPIRE is a two-stage reasoning method for predicting interactions of emerging entities in temporal knowledge graphs, addressing sparse, bursty few-shot histories.

s29107442cb.title: What Is a Theory Worth to an LLM Solver? Measuring, Inducing, and Merging Theories in Context
s29107442cb.description: arXiv:2611.34751v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mathematicians solve problems faster when they know the right theory. We ask how much a stated theory is worth to a large language model (LLM) solver, and whether a model can write that theory itself. In a length-matched protocol, adding the right theory to the context of Qwen3-14B raises pass@1 on pattern waiting-time problems from 0.37 to 0.83 and cuts the median tokens of correct solutions from 10.2k to 6.3k, while worked examples of the same length do not help. The gain shrinks as the solver and its token budget grow (+0.46, +0.26, +0.07), and at a long budget it comes almost entirely from finishing within budget: solutions that finish are correct 98--100\% of the time in every condition. To separate induction from recall, we plant unpubl
s29107442cb.summary: Researchers show that adding the right stated theory to an LLM's context raises pass@1 on waiting-time problems from 0.37 to 0.83, while equal-length worked examples do not help.
s29107442cb.why: Suggests structured domain theory in prompts can outperform extra examples for solver accuracy and token efficiency, though the gain shrinks as models and budgets grow.

seee7245816.title: TASK Memory: Beyond Text-Only Memory with Activation Steering and Knowledge Editing against Memory Hallucination
seee7245816.description: arXiv:2611.34762v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external memory, yet they still hallucinate about what they remember. Often the correct memory is retrieved and placed in the prompt, but the answer contradicts it or the memory is applied to the wrong question. We call these use-time memory hallucinations. Across five open models, we find that they arise from the conflict between parametric knowledge and external memory and take three forms: memory-ignoring, where the model returns to a stale fact in its weights (up to 46% of queries); memory-misapplying, where it attributes the memory to unrelated entities (up to 24%, and 49% when retrieval is combined with weight editing); and version confusion, where 53% of answers about revised facts assert the superseded
seee7245816.summary: The TASK Memory paper studies use-time memory hallucinations in LLM agents across five open models, where models ignore, misapply, or otherwise mishandle correctly retrieved external memory.
seee7245816.why: Agent builders relying on retrieval memory need to know that correct retrieved facts can still be ignored or misapplied due to conflicts with parametric knowledge.

s5b8ba2ac82.title: Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent: Self-Structuring Learning through Question Answering
s5b8ba2ac82.description: arXiv:2611.34841v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the problem of constructing knowledge bases for applications based on large language models, in which the structure of a knowledge base determines how an application can retrieve and connect the information needed to answer a question. We study Self-Structuring Learning, a setting in which questions and expected answers guide the construction of a persistent knowledge base whose editable structure can be a graph schema or the organization of linked knowledge documents. We propose Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, which diagnoses discrepancies between expected answers and responses obtained through the current knowledge base. At each round, the method proposes a structural edit, rebuilds the knowledge base, and adopts the edit when
s5b8ba2ac82.summary: The paper proposes Knowledge-Base Gradient Descent, a method that uses questions and expected answers to diagnose and edit the structure of a persistent LLM knowledge base.
s5b8ba2ac82.why: Offers a possible approach for building retrieval-backed LLM applications where the knowledge base structure is learned from question-answer feedback.

s3c89154072.title: Show Your Work: Can Small Open Models Read SEC Filings with Evidence a Machine Can Check?
s3c89154072.description: arXiv:2611.24990v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A fluent answer from a language model is not a verified one. We ask whether small open models that run on a single consumer GPU can extract numbers from SEC filings with evidence a machine can check: the page and a verbatim quote containing the number. We introduce Filing-Evidence, a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 recent 10-K and 10-Q filings of 45 US companies, with answer keys taken from the filers' inline XBRL tags. We evaluate ten instruct models from ten developers (7-21B parameters) on one RTX 4090 in three setups: plain, check-and-retry, and the model's own reasoning mode. Accuracy with checkable evidence ranges from 17.1% to 82.7% in the plain setup, and the best result is 84.5% (Qwen3.5-9B). An automatic checker rejects many
s3c89154072.summary: Filing-Evidence is a benchmark of 1,000 questions over 90 SEC filings testing whether small open models on one consumer GPU can extract numbers with checkable page and verbatim-quote evidence.
s3c89154072.why: Gives teams a way to assess whether small local models can produce verifiable, auditable extractions from financial documents.

s4ab332767a.title: Attributing Agentic Failure in Reasoning Vision-Language Models with Interactive 2D Environments
s4ab332767a.description: arXiv:2611.33162v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic benchmarks report a success rate that confounds distinct causes of failure: misreading the environment, never working out how components of the environment operates, operating the components in the wrong order, and failing to recover from a mistake, each of which calls for a different fix. We present an early preview of MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld - an interactive maze environment built for attribution rather than ranking. Four different types of mechanisms, namely key-door pairs, switch-gate pairs, distractors and decoys, and ordered combinations of these mechanisms, can be added, modified, or removed independently while the renderer, the action space, and the scoring function stay fixed. A breadth-first search over the joint state of
s4ab332767a.summary: MultiNet v2.0-Gridworld is an interactive maze benchmark designed to attribute agentic failures in reasoning vision-language models to specific causes rather than just ranking success rates.
s4ab332767a.why: Separating perception, mechanism understanding, ordering, and recovery failures helps engineers target the right fix for agent failures.

s820a650720.title: Quantum Machine Learning for Signature Forgery Detection
s820a650720.description: arXiv:2611.33163v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Offline handwritten signatures remain a primary behavioural biometric in legal and financial documents. Detecting skilled forgeries from a static raster image is hard because pen pressure, timing and stroke order are missing. This work studies a family of quantum machine learning pipelines for offline signature forgery detection on a public Kaggle corpus of images split into two classes. We pair a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with three classical learners: K-Nearest Neighbours, Support Vector Machine and Random Forest. We then propose a deeper hybrid that uses EfficientNetB0 as a frozen feature extractor, reduces the resulting 1280 dimensional representation to a qubit register sized subspace through a quantum compatible principal componen
s820a650720.summary: The paper studies quantum machine learning pipelines pairing a ZZ feature map quantum kernel with classical learners for offline signature forgery detection on a Kaggle image dataset.

s766b6b8128.title: Psychophysics of Duration Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models
s766b6b8128.description: arXiv:2611.33176v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Studies of time perception in language models focus mainly on text-based settings. Yet multimodal models are increasingly used for tasks that require perceiving the passage of time, making the limits of their temporal perception important to understand. We measure the limits of duration perception from audio against a human baseline to address this gap. Drawing from psychophysics, we operationalise duration perception as a melody recognition task, testing when a melody becomes unrecognisable as it is slowed down. Of 21 tested models, most cannot recognise well-known melodies without labelled in-context examples. With in-context examples, seven recognise melodies reliably, most peaking within the median human recognition band. Generalisation
s766b6b8128.summary: A study tests duration perception in 21 multimodal models by asking when slowed-down melodies become unrecognisable, comparing results against a human baseline.
s766b6b8128.why: Shows that most tested audio-capable models struggle with temporal perception, a limit relevant to applications requiring timing judgments from audio.

se2e004cb80.title: Neighbor Crowding Predicts Feature Stability in Sparse Autoencoders
se2e004cb80.description: arXiv:2611.33182v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Sparse Autoencoders (SAEs) offer an approach to identify language model representations by breaking apart polysemantic features into more sparse, interpretable ones. Yet, it is challenging to identify which of the learned features are actually stable, rather than artifacts of initialization. One approach is to train multiple SAE seeds, and compare the learned features across seeds by cosine similarity, but this is notably costly. This raises the question of whether stable features can be identified without the computational expense of training multiple seeds. In this work, we examine cross-seed feature stability across differing levels of training tokens, and demonstrate that in TopK SAEs, it is highly predictable using six computationally
se2e004cb80.summary: The paper examines whether neighbor crowding statistics can identify stable sparse autoencoder features without training multiple costly SAE seeds.
se2e004cb80.why: A cheaper stability check for SAE features could reduce the compute needed for interpretability work on language models.

s8beb4eff22.title: REI: Learning Ideation from Repository Evolution
s8beb4eff22.description: arXiv:2611.33183v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As AI systems become increasingly capable of executing and evaluating experiments, ideation is emerging as a bottleneck in automated scientific and engineering iteration. In many real-world domains, useful ideas are sparse and their validation is costly, making direct online exploration inefficient. We observe that repository evolution provides a scalable source of reusable technical experience: code changes record concrete technical hypotheses, while subsequent revisions, adoption, and reuse provide signals about their utility. Based on this observation, we propose REI, a Repository Evolution-driven Ideation framework that learns reusable ideation policies from repository evolution, injecting domain-specific technical experience into model
s8beb4eff22.summary: REI proposes learning ideation for automated research by using repository evolution, where code changes and later revisions signal the utility of technical hypotheses.
s8beb4eff22.why: Suggests a scalable way to train idea generators for automated engineering iteration without costly online experimentation.

s1027e0aa17.title: Semantic Density Does Not Predict Agent-Memory Collapse
s1027e0aa17.description: arXiv:2611.33184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Persistent textual memory can improve LLM agents, but repeated updates can erode task performance. We ask whether memory-store statistics warn before held-out accuracy declines. We registered mean pairwise cosine similarity ($\rho$) and 13 additional geometry, retrieval, and graph statistics on 805 snapshots from 13 memory methods across ALFWorld, AppWorld, ScienceWorld, WebShop, and two ARC-AGI settings. These methods store trajectories, rules, workflows, strategies, or linked records, using selective retrieval or whole-store prompting. No such statistic reliably predicted early signs of task accuracy decline, and $\rho$ had zero median lead. With the checkpoint after peak accuracy as a secondary decline point, measures of highly similar p
s1027e0aa17.summary: The paper reports that mean pairwise cosine similarity and 13 other memory-store statistics do not predict held-out accuracy collapse in LLM agent memory across 805 snapshots.
s1027e0aa17.why: Engineers cannot rely on these simple store statistics as early warnings for agent memory degradation, so other monitoring is needed.

s8903612d16.title: Dynamics of Collective Diversity in Human-AI Co-Creation for Creative Tasks
s8903612d16.description: arXiv:2611.33192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI systems are increasingly deployed at scale to support human users in creative tasks across a variety of domains. However, as more users adopt the same AI agent, the resulting artifacts may become increasingly homogeneous, leading to a collapse in collective diversity. Prior work has documented this risk, but lacks a systematic framework for understanding how collective diversity changes as AI adoption scales across co-creation settings. In this work, we conduct a large-scale crowdsourcing study to understand and model the dynamics of collective diversity, quality, and effort in human-AI co-creation across two creative domains: Creative Hypothesis Generation and Creative Story Writing. We find that current AI agents used in co-
s8903612d16.summary: A large crowdsourcing study models how collective diversity in human-AI co-creation changes as more users adopt the same generative AI agent.
s8903612d16.why: Shows that widespread AI tool adoption may homogenize creative outputs, a risk for product designers of creative tools.

sb1d624b2fe.title: Formalization, Transparency, and Collusion in Open-Source Game Theory
sb1d624b2fe.description: arXiv:2611.33193v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cooperation among AI agents will undermine alignment protocols when it takes the form of collusion. Under these protocols, agents often have some information about one another, and how much they have may determine whether they collude. Open-source game theory studies the extreme case, in which each program reads its opponent's source code and acts based on what it can prove about it. We develop formal foundations for this theory: we specify a concrete proof system, resolve an open problem concerning DupocBot and CupodBot through a transposition argument, and mechanize the framework in Lean 4; to our knowledge, this is the first mechanization of resource-bounded open-source game theory. We then extend the framework to the more realistic sett
sb1d624b2fe.summary: The paper formalizes open-source game theory, specifying a proof system and resolving an open problem about DupocBot and CupodBot, with implications for AI agent collusion.
sb1d624b2fe.why: Clarifies when agents that read each other's source code can prove cooperative behavior, relevant to alignment protocols against collusion.

s4a06690698.title: Verified experience improves materials prediction with large language models
s4a06690698.description: arXiv:2611.33195v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Materials discovery is an iterative loop: experiments and calculations verify predictions, and each outcome can inform the next. Yet most predictors are specialized single-task models fixed after training. Large language models have recently emerged as predictors across heterogeneous tasks but generally underperform specialized models, and retrieval-augmented variants discard their own outcomes. Benchmarks also score queries in isolation, leaving improvement from outcomes untested. Here we construct MatMemBench, a sequential benchmark of 22 materials tasks that reveals outcomes only after prediction and tests online adaptation, memory retention and cross-task transfer. We present MatRecall, a framework that lets large language models store
s4a06690698.summary: MatMemBench is a sequential benchmark of 22 materials prediction tasks testing whether LLM predictors improve when they can use verified outcomes from earlier queries.
s4a06690698.why: Introduces a way to measure whether LLMs learn from verified feedback over time, rather than scoring each query in isolation.

sa1266fb70a.title: Extraneous Cognitive Load in Large Language Models
sa1266fb70a.description: arXiv:2611.33197v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cognitive Load Theory (CLT) shows that human problem-solving is affected by both intrinsic load, arising from task difficulty, and extraneous load, arising from how task information is presented. Large language models (LLMs) show analogous effects: presentation alone can affect model performance, but these effects have not yet been systematically isolated from task difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce CogLoadBench, a controlled benchmark that varies five CLT-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families. Across models, we find that higher extraneous load conditions often reduce accuracy by either adding competition or complicating the reasoning path. To support diagnosis and mitigation of load-related effects,
sa1266fb70a.summary: CogLoadBench is a benchmark that varies five cognitive-load-inspired presentation factors across three reasoning task families to isolate extraneous load effects in LLMs.
sa1266fb70a.why: Shows that how a task is presented can affect model performance independently of difficulty, which matters for prompt design.

s5c10d3ec27.title: UniMoE-CP: Unified Conditional Waveform Prediction Across Measured Optical Wireless Links
s5c10d3ec27.description: arXiv:2611.33198v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Shared prediction across measured optical wireless links requires a common model to accommodate link-dependent waveform dynamics. This paper studies unified learning for underwater optical, 100-m visible-light communication and 4.3-km free-space optical links. We formulate received-waveform forecasting from historical observations and known future transmitted excitation using one shared parameter set. UniMoE-CP combines a shared pool of temporal experts, window-dependent routing and spectral covariate fusion with an autoregressive decoder. The design permits conditional specialization while reusing expert parameters across the measured links. Pooled-training benchmarks evaluate each link separately and report an aggregated result using norm
s5c10d3ec27.summary: UniMoE-CP is a unified mixture-of-experts model that forecasts received waveforms across underwater optical, 100-m visible-light, and 4.3-km free-space optical links using one parameter set.

saae252d93f.title: The AI Disclosure Paradox: Operational Disclosure and the Rise of Corporate AI Narratives
saae252d93f.description: arXiv:2611.33201v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI-related corporate disclosure can expand while becoming less concentrated on current use. Across U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025, AI-related passage intensity increased 6.3-fold between 2017-2022 and 2023-2025, whereas corrected operational-disclosure intensity increased 3.3-fold. The operational share fell from 25.76% to 13.45%; approximately 89% of the net increase in passage intensity fell outside the operational category. The decline persists within sectors and filing types and in 10-K-only analysis. These estimates combine frozen language-model predictions for 26,279 AI-related passages with an audit of 1,000 annotated passages. The findings distinguish growth in organizational attention from growth in implementation-specific clai
saae252d93f.summary: An arXiv paper analyzing U.S. SEC filings from 2017 to 2025 finds AI-related disclosure grew sharply but became less focused on operational use.
saae252d93f.why: Suggests corporate AI claims in filings increasingly describe narratives rather than deployed operations, which matters for due diligence on AI capability claims.

sa59264ab22.title: How Many Samples Is RL Worth? Best-of-N versus RL Post-Training for Text-to-Image Models
sa59264ab22.description: arXiv:2611.33232v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) on a reward that can be checked automatically has become a common last step in the training of text-to-image models. A simpler way to get more correct images is best-of-N: draw N images from the base model and keep the one that a picker prefers. We ask how many base model samples one RL sample is worth, and call this number the exchange rate. We measure it for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its public Flow-GRPO checkpoint on 398 new prompts in the style of GenEval, the benchmark behind the RL reward, with human labels on every prompt and two automatic judges other than the reward. The answer depends on the prompt. Four fifths of the prompts do not ask for a position (for example, one object left of another). On
sa59264ab22.summary: A paper measures how many best-of-N base-model samples equal one RL post-training sample for Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium and its Flow-GRPO checkpoint.
sa59264ab22.why: Gives teams a concrete way to compare the cost of best-of-N sampling against RL post-training for text-to-image models.

s6497a83f2d.title: Diagnostically Meaningful, Privacy-aware Synthetic Chest CT via Class-Conditional Latent Sampling in Diffusion Autoencoders
s6497a83f2d.description: arXiv:2611.33234v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large, well-annotated datasets are essential for developing medical artificial intelligence models, yet data sharing is often restricted by privacy regulations. Synthetic images may help address this limitation if they preserve diagnostic information while reducing the risk of reproducing patient data. We developed a diffusion autoencoder-based framework for class-conditional synthetic chest CT generation that incorporates latent-space distance filtering to reduce the likelihood of regenerating training samples. A diffusion autoencoder was trained on the public RSNA 2020 Pulmonary Embolism (PE) dataset. PE-positive and PE-negative images were synthesized by sampling latent representations from class-specific kernel density estimates. Sample
s6497a83f2d.summary: Researchers present a diffusion autoencoder framework that generates class-conditional synthetic chest CT images, filtering out samples close to training data to reduce privacy risk.
s6497a83f2d.why: Offers a possible route to sharing medical imaging training data under privacy constraints, though the text gives limited detail on results.

s12158cf89a.title: KiRA: Kronecker Input-Gated Rank Adaptation for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models
s12158cf89a.description: arXiv:2611.33236v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Full fine-tuning of large pretrained models is expensive, and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) is the standard alternative. Most PEFT methods use low-rank updates, whose rank lies far below that of full fine-tuning and is the same for every input. Input-adaptive variants vary the capacity per input but remain within the low-rank bottleneck, and whether a task benefits from input conditioning is not known before training. This paper introduces Kronecker input-gated rank adaptation (KiRA). Instead of the conventional low-rank product, the update $\Delta W$ is the Kronecker product of a frozen random $p\times p$ matrix $A$ and a trainable factor $M(x)$, which overcomes the rank ceiling: because rank is multiplicative under this product,
s12158cf89a.summary: The paper introduces KiRA, a parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that replaces the low-rank product with an input-gated Kronecker structure.
s12158cf89a.why: Proposes a fine-tuning alternative that may achieve input-adaptive capacity beyond standard low-rank methods, though the text gives no benchmark results.

sb6042980c6.title: Sequential Testing on Complex and High Dimensional Data Streams Leveraging Unsupervised Model Errors
sb6042980c6.description: arXiv:2611.33238v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose two general, distribution-free test statistics for binary Sequential Hypothesis Testing (SHT) and Sequential Change Point Detection (SCPD) respectively, in streaming environments where the data (e.g., network traffic metadata) are too complicated for the exact probabilistic modeling required by conventional likelihood ratio-driven tests. Our framework also addresses the challenge of information asymmetry, where data is available only from the null/pre-change regime and not from the alternative/post-change one such as zero-day attacks or emerging disease related regimes. The proposed statistics monitor the errors of a predictive or reconstructive machine learning model trained solely on null/pre-change data, relying on imperfect g
sb6042980c6.summary: Researchers propose distribution-free test statistics for sequential hypothesis testing and change point detection on streaming data using unsupervised model errors.
sb6042980c6.why: Could help detect anomalies such as zero-day attacks in network streams when only normal-regime data is available.

s70764e24a9.title: CypherMAS: Benchmarking Routing Reliability in LLM-Based Multi-Agent Systems
s70764e24a9.description: arXiv:2611.33242v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-agent systems (MAS) built on large language models (LLMs) distribute reasoning across specialized agents that must exchange messages and invoke tools reliably. Existing evaluations typically couple communication with open domain tasks, making it difficult to determine whether a failure arises from reasoning, malformed tool use, lost messages, or forgotten requests. Prior benchmarks do not isolate communication execution or measure routing redundancy against a known optimal path. We introduce CypherMAS, a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing in fixed multi-agent graphs. Agents in chain, star, bipartite, or ring graphs route cyphered messages to remote peers holding the matching decoders; since the optimal route i
s70764e24a9.summary: CypherMAS is a synthetic benchmark that isolates communication and routing reliability in LLM-based multi-agent systems, separate from open-domain reasoning tasks.
s70764e24a9.why: Helps engineers diagnose whether multi-agent failures come from messaging or tool routing rather than reasoning.

sba37651d6e.title: Beyond the Efficiency-Efficacy Dilemma: A Critical Analysis of Transferability in Adversarial Malware Detection
sba37651d6e.description: arXiv:2611.33243v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Machine Learning (ML) models are already being deployed at scale for malware detection. Therefore there is a pressing need to rigorously study adversarial robustness. To that end, we introduce the Adversarial AI Engine (AAIE): a platform for automated security stress-testing. We performed transfer attacks, via EMBER2018, against a Random Forest target. Counterintuitively, we found single-step FGSM to have the highest attack success rate (ASR) of 52.9% compared to iterative PGD with 45.2% (p < 0.002). Compared to iterative attacks which tend to overfit surrogate networks creating brittle perturbations, FGSM created more transferable examples. We benchmarked our attacks using ASR, transferability score, evasion rate, and resilience index. Thr
sba37651d6e.summary: Researchers introduce the Adversarial AI Engine for stress-testing malware detectors and report transfer attacks against a Random Forest model using EMBER2018.
