sba37651d6e.why: Shows that simpler single-step attacks can outperform iterative ones against deployed ML malware detectors, relevant to security evaluation practices.

s15d8153013.title: Anti-AI in the Wild: From Toxic Discourse to Action
s15d8153013.description: arXiv:2611.33254v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online discussion of generative AI has become increasingly contentious, and communities devoted to supporting, opposing, or debating AI have emerged on social media. Some of these communities take anti-AI actions, such as deploying crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services to interfere with data collection and model training. Yet, the scope of these actions and their relationship to online discourse remain poorly understood. In this paper, we present the first measurement study of online conflict over generative AI, from toxic discourse to anti-AI actions. We collect 931,640 posts from 25 Reddit communities, label them with a large language model detector validated against human labels, identify 3,312 anti-AI actions, and trace the output
s15d8153013.summary: A measurement study examines online conflict over generative AI, tracing toxic discourse to anti-AI actions such as crawler tarpits and data-poisoning services.
s15d8153013.why: Highlights organized resistance tactics like data poisoning that could affect data collection and training pipelines.

s49088bcf7e.title: One Token, Many Lessons: Sliding-Window Attention within Gated Delta Networks
s49088bcf7e.description: arXiv:2611.33257v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Linear attention compresses historical context into a fixed-size recurrent state, reducing the computational and memory costs of long-sequence modeling. From the perspective of test-time regression (TTR), the state matrix can be viewed as an online-learned regression model, where keys and values serve as inputs and targets respectively, and queries are used to read from the model. From this perspective, the effectiveness of state learning depends not only on the update rule but also on how the key-value learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. While existing work has largely focused on how the state is updated and organized, we investigate how the learning pairs used for state updates are constructed. To this end, we propose S
s49088bcf7e.summary: A paper proposes sliding-window attention within gated delta networks to improve linear attention's state learning for long-sequence modeling.
s49088bcf7e.why: Offers an architectural variant for efficient long-context models, though the text provides no performance figures.

sba5c870601.title: Onnx2TEE: Automated Graph-Aware Model Partitioning for TEE-based Edge AI Protection
sba5c870601.description: arXiv:2611.33262v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI models are increasingly being deployed at the edge. Since these models often require significant research and development to produce, are often deployed in potentially hostile environments, and downstream systems often rely on accurate data; protecting them from theft or manipulation is worthy of serious consideration. Trusted Execution Environments (TEEs), which provide hardware-enforced separation of software execution, can protect model weights but impose strict resource constraints, making full-model execution impractical for large neural networks. We present Onnx2TEE, an automated, model-independent pipeline that partitions ONNX models across rich, trusted execution environments for non-sequential feed-forward networks using graph-a
sba5c870601.summary: Onnx2TEE is a graph-aware model partitioning approach that splits edge AI models to run within trusted execution environments under memory constraints.
sba5c870601.why: Addresses protecting proprietary edge model weights from theft or tampering while working within TEE resource limits.

s285745fc49.title: A Hierarchy of Risk Certificates for Representation-Based Prediction
s285745fc49.description: arXiv:2611.33333v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Representation-based prediction underlies many machine-learning systems. Yet a fitted predictor's failure to meet an accuracy requirement does not establish that its representation-decoder class cannot meet it. We study optimal population mean squared error (MSE) over Lipschitz decoders acting on a fixed representation. For blocks of $b\geq2$ independent and identically distributed (iid) observations, we minimize total squared error (normalized by $b-1$) under pairwise Lipschitz constraints. We prove that expected block scores form nondecreasing lower bounds on optimal class risk and converge to that risk on compact metric feature spaces, although no fixed block size provides a uniform relative guarantee. Verified dual lower bounds and iid
s285745fc49.summary: The paper studies optimal population mean squared error over Lipschitz decoders on fixed representations and derives a hierarchy of risk certificates.

s6bcbd37e56.title: Benchmarking Segmentation Models for Scalable Mangrove Mapping with Sentinel-1/2 Imagery
s6bcbd37e56.description: arXiv:2611.33369v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mangroves are dynamic coastal ecosystems that contribute to carbon storage, coastal protection and biodiversity conservation, but are vulnerable to climate change. Very-high-resolution imagery such as Pl\'eiades enables detailed mangrove mapping but it is costly and have a low revisit rate. Large-scale monitoring requires free and regularly available data such as Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 but their spatial resolution poses challenges for detailed mangrove mapping. In this work, we benchmark deep learning approaches for mangrove mapping from Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery using reference maps derived from very-high-resolution Pl\'eiades imagery. We compare four segmentation configurations based on CROMA and BigEarthNet-pretr
s6bcbd37e56.summary: Researchers benchmark deep learning segmentation models for mangrove mapping using free Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 satellite imagery.
s6bcbd37e56.why: Shows how freely available satellite data can support scalable ecological monitoring compared with costly high-resolution imagery.

sed35a45a71.title: Poisoning Self-Evolving Security Policies in LLM Agents
sed35a45a71.description: arXiv:2611.33385v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Self-evolving defenses improve LLM-agent security by learning reusable policies from observed attacks. However, we demonstrate that this learning process itself can become an attack surface. Using SED (Self-Evolving Defense) in the AgentDojo benchmark, we construct a single prompt-injection episode that causes the defense to learn an over-broad policy and subsequently refuse legitimate requests. Across 10 Nemotron runs, every poisoned run over-refuses at least one legitimate task, while unrelated-task performance remains unchanged and the original prompt-injection defense remains effective. The attack also transfers to gpt-oss-120b; however, its poisoning mechanism depends on a successful initial prompt injection and therefore fails to acti
sed35a45a71.summary: Researchers show that the learning process of a self-evolving defense in LLM agents can be poisoned via a single prompt-injection episode, causing over-refusal of legitimate tasks.
sed35a45a71.why: Shows that adaptive security policies learned from attacks can themselves become an attack surface, which matters for agent deployments.

sf354f7554c.title: RoboARC: Physical Puzzles for Robotic Manipulation under Spatial Constraints
sf354f7554c.description: arXiv:2611.33390v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many hard manipulation tasks come down to a spatial constraint that only a few motions satisfy, such as passing a part through a gap barely wider than itself or separating two interlocked parts. These motions depend on the exact geometry of each scene, so demonstrations and skills recorded elsewhere rarely transfer. We therefore ask: when manipulation hinges on spatial constraints, can robots reason out the right motions? We introduce RoboARC, a benchmark of 90 tasks in six constraint types over rigid and soft materials, on three robots in MuJoCo. Every task is a frozen scene with a physics-based grader and a verified reference solution that replays bit-identically. Each task comes in a Privileged regime, with the full simulator state and r
sf354f7554c.summary: RoboARC is a benchmark of 90 robotic manipulation tasks requiring spatial-constraint reasoning across rigid and soft materials, tested on three robots in simulation.
sf354f7554c.why: Provides a testbed for whether robots can reason about geometry-specific motions instead of relying on transferred demonstrations.

s8593cef743.title: Best-of-$N$ Test-Time Steering Can Lead to Reward Hacking in Vision-Language-Action Models
s8593cef743.description: arXiv:2611.33398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language-action (VLA) models have shown promise for general-purpose robotic manipulation, but adapting to changing environmental conditions still remains challenging. Recent test-time steering methods have shown promise in enabling adaptive VLA policies by utilizing additional computation during deployment. In this paper, we consider best-of-$N$ test-time steering for VLA models, where multiple action candidates are sampled from a fixed policy and a verifier is used to select the best one during deployment. We show that increasing $N$ does not always improve performance when the verifier is inaccurate, and can favor candidates whose scores exploit prediction errors, a form of reward hacking. We study this effect on 60 LIBERO-Safety t
s8593cef743.summary: The paper shows that best-of-N test-time steering for vision-language-action robot models can lead to reward hacking as N increases.
s8593cef743.why: Warns that scaling verifier-based action selection at deployment can degrade behavior by exploiting the verifier, a risk for robot policy engineers.

s5e908676b6.title: Sequentially Acquiring Concept Knowledge to Guide Continual Learning
s5e908676b6.description: arXiv:2611.33399v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The goal of continual learning (CL) is to adapt to new data (plasticity) while retaining the knowledge acquired from old data (stability). Existing methods are explicitly designed to focus on balancing stability and plasticity to mitigate the challenge of catastrophic forgetting while promoting learning. However, the impact of order and nature of samples from the new data that the network is trained on remains an under explored factor. We argue that a CL algorithm should have the ability to rank incoming samples in terms of their relationship with prior data and their effect on the learning process. In this work, we investigate if scoring and prioritizing incoming data based on their semantic relationships with the model's current knowledge
s5e908676b6.summary: Researchers propose a continual learning approach that ranks incoming samples by their relationship to existing knowledge, studying how sample order and nature affect stability and plasticity.
s5e908676b6.why: Sample ordering in continual training is an under-explored factor that could affect how models retain old knowledge while learning new data.

s61dd4058af.title: Temporal Selective Exploration for Reinforcement Learning-Guided Continuous-Discrete Flow Matching in 3D Molecular Design
s61dd4058af.description: arXiv:2611.33417v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Flow matching has shown strong potential in generative tasks, while its optimization via Reinforcement Learning (RL) remains underexplored, especially in continuous-discrete mixed settings. Moreover, flow matching is formulated as an Ordinary Differential Equation (ODE), whose deterministic trajectories do not naturally support RL optimization. Introducing stochasticity by converting the entire trajectory into a Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) is a common practice. Nevertheless, not all timesteps contribute to the final outcomes, and redundant exploration introduces additional noise. Furthermore, in multi-objective settings, some objectives may dominate the optimization while others receive insufficient updates. In this study, we pro
s61dd4058af.summary: Researchers apply reinforcement learning to continuous-discrete flow matching for 3D molecular design, selectively exploring timesteps when converting ODE trajectories to SDEs.

se452d5cd8e.title: When the Knowledge Runs Out: A Part-Level Pilot Evaluation of How Language Models Handle Partially Covered Questions
se452d5cd8e.description: arXiv:2611.33428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Assistants that answer from supplied reference material often receive material that covers some parts of a user's question and not others. Existing evaluations of insufficient context mostly score one answer per question, and often treat partially sufficient context as simply insufficient. We describe a small, open evaluation that scores each part of a three-part question separately, with a verdict for parts that are answered correctly from the material but carry an added unsupported claim. On 30 cases (five scenarios, six coverage patterns, five samples each) we test claude-haiku-4-5 and llama3.1:8b. Without an explicit instruction to stay within the material, both models fill most gaps from their own knowledge (unsupported-claim rates of
se452d5cd8e.summary: Researchers release a small open evaluation scoring each part of three-part questions separately when reference material only partially covers them.
se452d5cd8e.why: Per-part scoring exposes failures that single-answer evaluations miss when supplied context is only partially sufficient.

sbc50749613.title: HumblePRM: Improving VLM Abstention in Ambiguous Situations through Process Reward Modeling
sbc50749613.description: arXiv:2611.33452v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reliable deployment of Vision Language Models (VLMs) requires that a model's expressed confidence remain grounded in what it can actually see, and that it recognize when the visual evidence is too ambiguous to commit to a confident response. Standard post-training uses outcome reward models (ORMs) that supervise only the final decision, rewarding a confident answer regardless of whether the image supports one, while existing methods either tend to detect uncertainty post-hoc or assume an objective verdict always exists. We instead split multimodal reasoning into two stages: perception, where the model must factually describe the scene, and calibration, where it must judge whether that evidence is sufficient to commit to a conclusion. We int
sbc50749613.summary: HumblePRM uses process reward modeling to teach vision language models to abstain when visual evidence is too ambiguous, instead of rewarding confident answers regardless of image support.
sbc50749613.why: Reliable VLM deployment needs confidence grounded in visual evidence, and outcome-only reward models can reward overconfident answers.

s427d8bb5d0.title: SecID: An LLM-Guided Framework for Threat-Aware Secondary Asset Identification with Quantitative RTL Analysis
s427d8bb5d0.description: arXiv:2611.33453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The growing complexity of modern hardware designs is making security assurance increasingly difficult. One of the foundational steps in pre-silicon security verification is identifying security assets. While primary assets are often evident from design functionality, the internal signals that can facilitate their compromise are much less apparent. Complex data- and control-flow dependencies create many such internal security-critical locations, whose exploitation depends on the threat-specific attack mechanism---these are the secondary assets. To precisely identify these, we propose SecID, a multi-agent framework that combines deterministic RTL analysis with bounded dynamic evaluation and LLM reasoning to identify threat-specific secondary
s427d8bb5d0.summary: SecID is an LLM-guided framework for identifying secondary security assets in RTL hardware designs, combined with quantitative RTL analysis.
s427d8bb5d0.why: Pre-silicon security verification teams could use automated secondary asset identification to find internal signals that enable compromise.

sbf40509517.title: Benchmarking Open-Ended Vulnerability Discovery in Windows Kernel Binaries
sbf40509517.description: arXiv:2611.33486v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Frontier models are increasingly used to discover real-world security vulnerabilities, making it critical to systematically evaluate their cybersecurity capabilities. However, existing security benchmarks primarily focus on known vulnerabilities in open-source projects, largely overlooking closed-source binaries, which underpin much of the software industry. In this paper, we ask: how effective are frontier models at uncovering deep vulnerabilities in production binaries? To answer this question, we present DeepBinary, the first comprehensive benchmark for open-ended vulnerability discovery in Windows kernel binaries. Given a target binary, an agent analyzes it using a disassembler and kernel debugger in network-isolated VMs and reports eac
sbf40509517.summary: DeepBinary is a benchmark testing how well frontier models find deep, unknown vulnerabilities in closed-source Windows kernel binaries rather than known open-source flaws.
sbf40509517.why: Closed-source binaries underpin much of the industry, and this benchmark targets vulnerability discovery where existing security benchmarks have little coverage.

s750faf8dff.title: The Geometry Is the Memory: Task-Density Routing for Continual LoRA
s750faf8dff.description: arXiv:2611.33487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Freezing older adapters does not ensure that a continual learner will select and use them properly at inference time. When multiple adapters exist, routing among them and identifying the adapter whose representation space matches the query's answer can be difficult. We propose CONTLORA, which replaces stored examples with compact class statistics for adapter selection and classification. Gaussian class models in a frozen representation select LoRA adapters, while accumulated feature moments exactly recover a class-balanced ridge classifier for fixed training features. Trained without retaining images or feature vectors, CONTLORA reaches 88.55% accuracy on 20-task CIFAR-100 and 86.99% on CUB-200. Across three benchmarks in the matched compon
s750faf8dff.summary: CONTLORA proposes routing among frozen LoRA adapters using compact class statistics instead of stored examples, selecting adapters via Gaussian class models in a frozen representation.
s750faf8dff.why: Replacing stored examples with compact statistics could simplify continual fine-tuning systems that manage multiple adapters.

sdbd29855dd.title: Joint Estimation of Abilities and Item Parameters for Large Language Models Using Probability and Binary Responses: A Fractional-Response IRT Framework
sdbd29855dd.description: arXiv:2611.33493v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language model (LLM) evaluations provide two response types: probabilities assigned to correct answers and binary indicators of correctness. Restricting evaluation to one type narrows the range of available models or discards probability information. We propose a method to integrate both types through a common two-parameter logistic item response model and fractional-response quasi-maximum likelihood estimation. The framework includes binary-only models in common-scale evaluation without discarding available probabilityinformation; broader measurement coverage does not by itself ensure greater precision or measurement equivalence. Simulations evaluate statistical efficiency when both response types have the same expected value. Moreov
sdbd29855dd.summary: Researchers propose a fractional-response IRT framework that jointly uses probability and binary correctness responses to estimate LLM abilities and item parameters.
sdbd29855dd.why: Combining probability and binary signals could make LLM benchmark comparisons more informative without discarding data.

s1ef4fc7c2f.title: PRECEPT: Security Self-Improvement of Coding Agents via Evolving Principles
s1ef4fc7c2f.description: arXiv:2611.33519v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI coding agents increasingly write and submit code with limited human review, and much of it passes functional tests while remaining insecure. We show that these failures persist. Across 14 task sequences, Codex, Claude Code, and Qwen Code fixed a vulnerability 85.7% of the time when shown the failing security test, then reintroduced the same vulnerability class in a new session 26.7% of the time, about as often as agents that had never seen it (27.5%). The capability is present; the retention is not. Neither recording the repair in the agent's persistent context nor supplying published secure coding principles closed the gap: the recorded fix stayed tied to the family of the task it came from, and the principles, written for human develop
s1ef4fc7c2f.summary: PRECEPT proposes evolving security principles for coding agents, after finding agents reintroduced fixed vulnerability classes in new sessions 26.7% of the time.
s1ef4fc7c2f.why: Coding agents that reintroduce fixed vulnerabilities across sessions show that recorded repairs alone do not preserve security retention.

sca7c4ef13e.title: RankCast: Phase-Aware Rank Balancing in MoE Serving
sca7c4ef13e.description: arXiv:2611.33542v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern large language model (LLM) inference increasingly adopts disaggregated architectures that separate Prefill (P) and Decode (D) phases. Meanwhile, Expert Parallelism (EP) has been widely adopted in large Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model serving. However, load imbalance still slows down MoE inference because each layer must wait for the busiest EP rank. The main source of latency differs between prefill and decode. Prefill is compute-bound, and its MoE layers' latency is determined by the maximum token count of the busiest rank. At the same time, under moderate batch sizes, Decode is memory-bound, so the latency is dominated by the maximum active-expert count across ranks. To solve both problems under a unified framework, we present RankC
sca7c4ef13e.summary: RankCast proposes phase-aware rank balancing for serving Mixture-of-Experts models, addressing load imbalance across expert parallelism ranks in prefill and decode phases.
sca7c4ef13e.why: Expert load imbalance slows MoE inference, and phase-specific balancing targets different latency sources in prefill and decode.

s0d16ad717e.title: DexEngine: Scaling Human Demonstrations into Physically Executable Whole-Robot Data
s0d16ad717e.description: arXiv:2611.33579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A growing body of recent work addresses the retargeting of human hand-object demonstrations to robotic hands. To train whole-robot policies, however, the retargeted motions must be kinematically feasible and physically executable, and be produced efficiently at scale. We present DexEngine, a simulation pipeline that turns human manipulation data into train-ready, physically executable arm-hand trajectories. DexEngine first places each clip's hand-object motion where the arms can reach it, finds an arm motion that follows the human hands, and then corrects the motion in physics simulation with residual reinforcement learning. From nine human hand-object datasets, we generate about 5,200 clips for each of four dexterous hands, augmented into
s0d16ad717e.summary: DexEngine is a simulation pipeline that converts human hand-object demonstrations into physically executable arm-hand trajectories for training whole-robot policies at scale.

sc0e894dfe2.title: The Detour Is the Danger: Preserving Security During LLM Agent Recovery
sc0e894dfe2.description: arXiv:2611.33605v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM agents increasingly rely on external tools and reusable Skills to execute complex workflows, autonomously replanning when operations fail. However, such recovery may preserve task functionality while silently discarding the security protections required by the original workflow. In this paper, we investigate workflow security downgrade, a failure-induced security threat in which agents execute sensitive operations without satisfying their original protection requirements. Unlike prompt injection, this threat exploits autonomous recovery decisions triggered by execution failures, without modifying instructions or tool definitions. We systematically evaluate this behavior through fault injection in an executable MCP/Skill environment span
sc0e894dfe2.summary: Researchers identify workflow security downgrade, where LLM agents replanning after failures drop security protections of the original workflow while still completing tasks.
sc0e894dfe2.why: Autonomous recovery in agents can silently discard security requirements, a risk distinct from prompt injection that engineers building agent workflows must address.

s53b75ed3cc.title: What Is Redundant at High Resolution? Efficient Attention and Feed-Forward Design for All-in-One Image Restoration
s53b75ed3cc.description: arXiv:2611.33636v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-scale architectures are widely adopted in all-in-one image restoration (AIO-IR) to capture larger-scale context at low-resolution stages and refine details at high-resolution (HR) stages. However, processing spatially large feature maps at HR stages incurs substantial computational costs and memory traffic, making efficient HR processing challenging. To address this challenge, we propose High-resolution Global-Local Restoration (HiGLR), an efficient multi-scale AIO-IR network grounded in an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention and convolutional feed-forward networks (ConvFFNs). Specifically, this analysis identifies three key redundancies: per-query readout at the finest-scale stage, key routing across neighboring queries
s53b75ed3cc.summary: HiGLR is an efficient multi-scale all-in-one image restoration network that reduces high-resolution processing costs based on an analysis of spatial redundancy in self-attention.

se56b221d5f.title: Read Before You Use: Improving Visual Memory Utilization in Vision-Language Models
se56b221d5f.description: arXiv:2611.33687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal memory enables long-horizon vision-language agents to preserve and retrieve past experiences. While prior research has focused on memory construction and retrieval, effectively using the provided memory remains a challenge for vision-language models (VLMs). We find that VLMs often fail to answer downstream questions even when sufficient multimodal evidence is provided. To investigate why VLMs struggle, we replace memory images with reference captions and observe substantial performance gains, suggesting difficulties in reading visual evidence directly. However, model-generated captions may omit critical information, limiting this approach in practice. These limitations motivate a closer examination of memory utilization, revealin
se56b221d5f.summary: Researchers find vision-language models often fail to use provided visual memory, and replacing memory images with reference captions substantially improves performance.
se56b221d5f.why: Agents relying on multimodal memory may underperform even when correct evidence is supplied, pointing to a gap in how VLMs read visual memory.

sb90afa7ec3.title: Rethinking Sequential Locate-Then-Edit: Optimality and Stability
sb90afa7ec3.description: arXiv:2611.33692v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Locate-Then-Edit framework enables efficient knowledge updates in large language models without requiring full retraining. Recent research has increasingly focused on sequential editing, where knowledge arrives continuously and the model is updated incrementally. However, existing sequential methods commonly suffer from catastrophic forgetting and model collapse after only a few hundred edits. In contrast, batch editing - which jointly optimizes all edits and yields the optimal solution under a specified editing objective - can support tens of thousands of edits with high edit efficacy while preserving the model's general capabilities, resulting in a substantial performance gap between the two editing paradigms. In this paper, we demons
sb90afa7ec3.summary: Researchers revisit sequential Locate-Then-Edit knowledge editing for LLMs, analyzing why sequential methods collapse after a few hundred edits while batch editing scales further.
sb90afa7ec3.why: Sequential knowledge edits that collapse after a few hundred updates limit maintaining LLMs without retraining, so stability findings matter for update pipelines.

s8c845277bd.title: Sports Agent: A Self-Evolving System for Conversational Data Analytics
s8c845277bd.description: arXiv:2611.33700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conversational sports analytics requires accurate, evidence-based responses with low latency. Changes in query distributions, data resources, and model behavior can degrade static agent configurations, motivating controlled evolution guided by runtime evidence. We present Sports Agent, a self-evolving framework integrating an Agentic SQL Model for structured-data reasoning, a harness for planning and tool orchestration, and a unified Feedback Engine connecting online execution with offline evolution. The engine assesses responses and execution trajectories, verifies factual claims, diagnoses failures, and generates evolution signals. Model evolution combines SQL-to-Question Scaling for coverage expansion with Graph-Guided Scaling for error-
s8c845277bd.summary: Researchers present Sports Agent, a self-evolving framework for conversational sports analytics combining an Agentic SQL Model, a planning harness, and a Feedback Engine.
s8c845277bd.why: Shows a pattern for keeping data agents accurate over time by using runtime execution feedback to guide controlled offline evolution.

s065fab91ee.title: Practice Makes Fluent: Learning to Use Earlier Predictions in Looped Models
s065fab91ee.description: arXiv:2611.33722v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: People become faster at a task through practice, but models that improve with experience do not necessarily learn to use less computation. We train looped models, whose intermediate predictions allow earlier exits, to perform tasks with fewer iterations through practice. This is difficult because shared-weight updates can degrade the final-loop prediction while improving early ones, and the exit gate must track early predictions as their quality changes. We propose FLUENT, which requires no additional task labels or rewards: it distills the initial model's final-loop prediction into early predictions, anchors the current final-loop prediction to the same frozen teacher, and trains the exit gate to balance disagreement with the current final
s065fab91ee.summary: Researchers propose FLUENT, a method that trains looped models to use earlier intermediate predictions so they exit early and use less computation on tasks.
s065fab91ee.why: Could help teams cut inference compute by letting models learn to stop iterating once early predictions are good enough.

sf4b893f6ba.title: FlashProve-Next: Verifiable Inference for Production LLM APIs
sf4b893f6ba.description: arXiv:2611.33741v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Clients of closed-weight LLM APIs cannot verify whether a provider ran the advertised model, precision, hidden prompt, and reasoning budget. Existing approaches either trust hardware or third parties, or re-prove every layer of an integer surrogate at high cost while diverging from native floating-point serving. FlashProve-Next produces verifiable, zero-knowledge-masked proofs for individual LLM API responses without modifying native serving (bf16/fp8/mxfp4, random sampling, FlashAttention, CUDA graphs, batching, prefix caching) and without disclosing weights, hidden prompts, hidden reasoning, or activations (dense profiles fix coarse geometry; cross-architecture hiding is deferred). A non-depleting Reed-Solomon weight commitment model_id o
sf4b893f6ba.summary: FlashProve-Next proposes zero-knowledge-masked proofs that let clients verify individual responses from closed-weight LLM APIs ran the advertised model and settings.
sf4b893f6ba.why: Addresses trust in third-party LLM APIs by offering verification of model, precision, and reasoning budget without changing native serving.

s3c638ee3c3.title: Teaching Students to Stand on Their Own: Distilling Vision Foundation Models for Fine-Grained Few-Shot Class-Incremental Learning
s3c638ee3c3.description: arXiv:2611.33749v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fine-grained few-shot class-incremental learning (FG-FSCIL) aims to incrementally learn visually similar new classes from limited images without catastrophic forgetting. Prior work typically learns strong representations on base classes or leverages vision foundation models (VFMs) directly as backbones or via knowledge distillation. However, VFM backbones incur high computational costs and do not guarantee fine-grained recognition. Although knowledge distillation reduces inference cost, our preliminary experiments reveal that distilled students still lag substantially behind their VFM teachers, particularly on new classes. To address this limitation, we propose STAND, a systematic VFM-to-student distillation design tailored for FG-FSCIL. Sp
s3c638ee3c3.summary: Researchers study distilling vision foundation models into smaller students for fine-grained few-shot class-incremental learning, noting distilled students struggle with fine-grained recognition.
s3c638ee3c3.why: Relevant to teams deploying compact vision models that must learn new fine-grained classes from few images.

sb1b37bf34d.title: ScanAR: Parallel Row-Scan Decoding for Efficient Image Generation in Unified Autoregressive Models
sb1b37bf34d.description: arXiv:2611.33761v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Unified multimodal autoregressive (AR) models represent text and images in one token sequence and generate all modalities with a shared next-token prediction head. Their image generation, however, decodes an $H\times W$ visual grid token by token in raster order, which takes $HW$ sequential steps and dominates inference time. Existing acceleration methods for visual AR generation either change the tokenizer, the prediction head, or the model interface, or keep the model but cannot reach high parallelism without losing quality, so they do not carry over to unified AR models. We propose ScanAR, a row-scan parallel decoding method that only redefines the predecessors of visual tokens. The first visual row is generated from left to right as usu
sb1b37bf34d.summary: ScanAR proposes parallel row-scan decoding to speed up image generation in unified autoregressive multimodal models without changing the tokenizer or prediction head.
sb1b37bf34d.why: Targets the dominant inference bottleneck of sequential raster-order image token decoding in unified multimodal models.

s93a086adfc.title: Triage Before Fine-Tuning: Feasibility-Gated Selection and Monitored Adaptation of Embodied Foundation Models for a Fixed Physical Platform
s93a086adfc.description: arXiv:2611.33772v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied foundation models are increasingly deployed by selection: a practitioner picks a public checkpoint by benchmark rank and fine-tunes it on local data. The platform is fixed before the model is chosen, with little or no local data. We ask what such a checkpoint loses on a fixed platform and which part of the loss local data can buy back. We split the gap by what can repair it. A sensing gap, information the sensors do not capture, cannot be closed with their data; a latency gap, output arriving after the control loop needs it, belongs to the loop, not the weights; only a distribution gap is fine-tuning's to repair. TRIAGE turns this into feasibility-gated selection and monitored adaptation in five stages: gates on the sensor contract
s93a086adfc.summary: Researchers examine how to choose and fine-tune embodied foundation models for a fixed physical platform, splitting performance gaps into sensing and latency gaps.
s93a086adfc.why: Gives practitioners a framework for deciding whether benchmark-ranked robot checkpoints will work on their hardware before fine-tuning.

s0bfc5565bd.title: LSRP*-LA: Scalable and Anytime Multi-Agent Path Finding for Large Agents with Asynchronous Actions
s0bfc5565bd.description: arXiv:2611.33793v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multi-Agent Path Finding (MAPF) seeks collision-free paths for multiple agents from their start locations to their goal locations while minimizing path costs. Most MAPF algorithms assume that each agent occupies a single vertex and that the actions of all agents are synchronized. These assumptions may limit the use of MAPF planners in practice. Existing planners that get rid of both assumptions either handle only a few agents or cannot improve their solutions. Recently, a planner called LSRP* was proposed, which is scalable and anytime with asynchronous actions, but still limited by that each agent occupies a single vertex. This paper develops a new planner called LSRP*-LA for MAPF for large agents with asynchronous actions (LA-MAPF-AA), wh
s0bfc5565bd.summary: Researchers introduce LSRP*-LA, an anytime multi-agent path finding planner that handles large agents with asynchronous actions and scales to many agents.
s0bfc5565bd.why: Extends practical multi-robot path planning to larger agents and unsynchronized actions common in real warehouse or fleet settings.

sc05ac52cb0.title: QPAT: A Universal Quantum Machine Learning Framework for Quantum-Assisted Training and Classical Inference
sc05ac52cb0.description: arXiv:2611.33806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning models often struggle with sharp local optima and overfitting in limited-data regimes, and exhibit limited capacity for capturing high-order, complex probability distributions. Quantum Machine Learning (QML) models, by operating in exponentially large Hilbert spaces, can efficiently represent such distributions and provide favorable inductive biases for learning, offering a promising pathway to overcome these limitations. However, their practical deployment in the Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum (NISQ) era is severely hindered by gradient coupling, barren plateaus, data-loading bottlenecks, and high inference latency. To bridge classical AI and QML, we propose QPAT (QCBM-Prior-Assisted Training), a universal framework that em
sc05ac52cb0.summary: Researchers propose QPAT, a quantum machine learning framework that uses quantum-assisted training while keeping classical inference.
sc05ac52cb0.why: Explores a hybrid path for NISQ hardware, though the text gives limited detail on practical gains.

sff19a7f47b.title: KnitNet: Learning to Search at Inference Time for Exact RNA Inverse Design
sff19a7f47b.description: arXiv:2611.33812v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: RNA inverse design seeks nucleotide sequences that fold into specified target structures. Existing methods rely on learned generators that can miss exact structural matches, especially beyond their training distributions, or on costly search over a vast, multimodal sequence space. Search is further complicated by globally coupled nucleotide interactions, as correcting one pairing error can create new errors beyond a fixed repair scope. To address this, we introduce KnitNet, an inference-time scaling framework that learns from verifier feedback to refine sequences for exact fold-back matching. Starting from candidates generated for a target secondary structure, KnitNet uses mismatched folds to infer nucleotide dependencies and adapt its join
sff19a7f47b.summary: Researchers introduce KnitNet, an inference-time search framework that uses verifier feedback to design RNA sequences that exactly fold into target structures.

s08075d3f42.title: FEAST: Fair and Efficient Adaptive Sampling for Task-Free On-Policy Learning
s08075d3f42.description: arXiv:2611.33827v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Language agents trained from self-generated experience must allocate a limited rollout budget across heterogeneous capabilities. A common strategy is to prioritize capabilities with strong current learning signals, but in on-policy learning these signals are endogenous: past allocation changes the policy and therefore the evidence available for future allocation. This can create a feedback loop in which under-trained capabilities receive increasingly fewer opportunities to improve. We formalize this effect through the Quota-Efficiency Law (QEL), which shows that allocation history can change learning efficiency even under matched capability-specific exposure. Motivated by this, we introduce FEAST, a task-free adaptive sampling framework tha
s08075d3f42.summary: Researchers introduce FEAST, an adaptive sampling method for allocating limited rollout budgets across capabilities in task-free on-policy training of language agents.
s08075d3f42.why: Highlights a feedback loop where under-trained capabilities get fewer rollouts, relevant to teams training self-improving agents.

s6f7a1c27e0.title: When Rerankers Work Together: Better and Faster Reranking without Joint Training
s6f7a1c27e0.description: arXiv:2611.33844v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Standalone reranker quality does not determine its value in a multistage RAG pipeline. We systematically study heterogeneous rerankers composed without joint training, spanning lexical, single-vector, late-interaction, and joint query-context scoring. Two lightweight semantic coarse scorers, Cache-Pointwise and Cache-Shapley, learn from passage relevance labels and share cacheable representations and linear-time singleton inference. Under matched candidates and budgets, we compare cascades with stage-removal references to measure evidence retention, repair and breakage, reader accuracy, and online pruning cost. On NoLiMa 32K with Gemma, inserting these scorers before CrossEncoder or Provence improves answer accuracy by 4.02-9.43 percentage
s6f7a1c27e0.summary: Researchers study composing heterogeneous rerankers without joint training and propose lightweight coarse scorers that are both better and faster in multistage RAG pipelines.
s6f7a1c27e0.why: Offers practical guidance for improving retrieval quality and latency in RAG systems without costly retraining.

s89179b1d7f.title: Mitigating Overgeneralization in RND via Spectral Target Design
s89179b1d7f.description: arXiv:2611.33850v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random Network Distillation (RND) is a scalable novelty signal for RL based on a fixed random target network and a trained predictor. However, it can overgeneralize: the predictor extrapolates the random target off the data manifold, causing novelty scores to collapse on unfamiliar inputs. This paper analyzes this failure through a kernel-theoretic lens. Under a GP target model and an NTK-regime predictor, we show that the RND novelty score is a cross-kernel residual variance: it is governed jointly by the target covariance kernel and the predictor NTK, rather than by either one alone. This identifies overgeneralization as spectral under-excitation. Motivated by this view, we formulate spectral target design as a principle for shaping RND n
s89179b1d7f.summary: Researchers analyze overgeneralization in Random Network Distillation for RL novelty detection and propose a spectral target design to mitigate it.
s89179b1d7f.why: Provides a kernel-based explanation and fix for novelty signals collapsing on unfamiliar inputs in RL exploration.

sfabd3a0e05.title: Random Voronoi Networks
sfabd3a0e05.description: arXiv:2611.33875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Nearest-neighbor methods are local, simple, and interpretable, but their non-parametric form makes them memory-intensive, expensive at inference, and difficult to integrate into differentiable neural architectures. We introduce Random Voronoi Networks (RVNs), a family of structured three-layer MLPs that express nearest-neighbor geometry through sampled Voronoi comparisons. The first layer computes Random Voronoi Features (RVF) from affine pairwise separators between selected training samples, the second layer aggregates these comparisons into Voronoi cells or top-k neighborhood scores, and the readout layer produces classification or regression predictions. We show that, when all samples and pairwise comparisons are included, step RVNs reco
sfabd3a0e05.summary: Researchers introduce Random Voronoi Networks, structured three-layer MLPs that encode nearest-neighbor geometry via sampled Voronoi comparisons.
sfabd3a0e05.why: Offers a differentiable alternative to memory-heavy nearest-neighbor methods, though the text gives limited evaluation detail.

s659bc4ae46.title: When Are Parallel Subagents Effective for Coding? An Empirical Study on Repository Construction
s659bc4ae46.description: arXiv:2611.33893v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: LLM-based coding agents are increasingly used for long-horizon tasks such as building an entire program from a specification. Products like Codex and Claude Code let an agent delegate work to parallel subagents, multiplying run cost, yet it remains unclear whether and when delegation produces a better program. We compare a single agent with a main agent delegating to subagents on repository-construction tasks from NL2Repo and ProgramBench (which also provides an executable reference program). We compare scores at equal time and equal cost, run intervention experiments, and analyze fine-grained behavior. On randomly drawn tasks, parallel subagents raise hidden-test pass rates by only about 1 to 5 percentage points at up to 3.8x the cost of a
s659bc4ae46.summary: An empirical study compares single coding agents with main agents delegating to parallel subagents on repository-construction tasks, at equal time and equal cost.
s659bc4ae46.why: Helps teams decide whether parallel subagent delegation justifies its multiplied run cost for long-horizon coding tasks.

s1381b50847.title: Correlation-Aware Evidential Fusion for Trusted Multi-View Classification
s1381b50847.description: arXiv:2611.33900v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Trusted multi-view classification aims to make accurate and reliable predictions by integrating information from multiple views. Existing methods typically estimate class evidence and uncertainty for each view and combine the resulting opinions through aggregation rules. However, they generally treat different views as independent information sources, overlooking the correlations among them. Highly correlated views tend to produce similar evidence, and treating them as independent sources may repeatedly count consistent information and give it disproportionate influence, while weakening complementary evidence that provides additional information. Consequently, such correlation-unaware fusion may not only limit classification performance but
s1381b50847.summary: Researchers propose correlation-aware evidential fusion for trusted multi-view classification, accounting for correlated views that repeatedly count the same evidence.

s2f8de18b2d.title: DiCALM: Converting Autoregressive Convolution-Attention Language Models into Discrete Diffusion Language Models
s2f8de18b2d.description: arXiv:2611.33919v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing methods for adapting autoregressive (AR) language models to diffusion generation focus mainly on full-attention architectures. More efficient hybrid architectures remain underexplored. We introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting the hybrid convolution-attention models of the LFM2 family (LFM2 and LFM2.5) from AR to masked-diffusion generation. DiCALM progressively extends LFM2's causal gated convolution so that it captures local context in both directions. It combines this extension with a masking warm-up and joint AR--diffusion training. In controlled experiments, DiCALM performs comparably to the corresponding fine-tuned LFM2.5-based AR models and delivers consistent speedups over them at both the 350M and 1.2B scales: over 1.4x
s2f8de18b2d.summary: Researchers introduce DiCALM, a recipe for converting hybrid convolution-attention LFM2 language models from autoregressive to masked-diffusion text generation.
s2f8de18b2d.why: It shows a path to reuse existing hybrid AR models for diffusion generation rather than training diffusion models from scratch.

sf320574d45.title: Beyond the Happy Path: Generalizing Robot World Models from Simulated Failures
sf320574d45.description: arXiv:2611.33925v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robot world models are increasingly used to evaluate and plan policies, yet robot training data are dominated by successful demonstrations. Off the happy path, when a grasp is misaligned or mistimed and the object is pushed, tilted, or slips, their predictions break down. Across five pretrained action-conditioned models, object-motion error is at most 10.4% lower than that of a static baseline that copies the first frame, and two models are worse than this baseline. We present WorldReforge, which teaches world models what happens when manipulation goes wrong. We construct the Reforge dataset of 62k simulated trajectories by perturbing reference grasps in position, orientation, and closure timing, recording each resulting push, slip, or fail
sf320574d45.summary: WorldReforge is presented to teach robot world models how manipulation failures like misaligned grasps and slips unfold, after tested models underperformed a static baseline on failure cases.
sf320574d45.why: Robot world models used for policy evaluation and planning may be unreliable off the success path, which matters for deployment testing.

s4ac06d5874.title: Connecting AI Agents to Live Discrete Element Simulations via the Model Context Protocol
s4ac06d5874.description: arXiv:2611.33926v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper describes a Model Context Protocol (MCP) server through which a general-purpose AI agent operates a discrete element engine, commercial or open-source, while the simulation runs. The agent submits a long simulation to the engine and, while it computes, reads the running model, changes it, or stops it. The human modeler stays at the engine's console and graphical interface throughout, and the agent sees what the modeler does there. The tools are derived from what the agent needs to do at the engine and are held to four principles: correctness, coverage, orthogonality and simplicity. Two documentation tools let the agent search the engine's manual and browse it level by level. Five execution tools let the agent run code in the engi
s4ac06d5874.summary: A Model Context Protocol server lets a general-purpose AI agent operate a discrete element simulation engine while it runs, reading, changing, or stopping the model alongside a human modeler.
s4ac06d5874.why: It demonstrates a concrete pattern for connecting agents to live engineering simulation tools through MCP.

s8a9cb79c80.title: Towards 360$^\circ$ Embodied UAV Tracking Without Turning
s8a9cb79c80.description: arXiv:2611.33934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Conventional embodied UAV tracking couples target observability with heading control because targets may leave the field of view of forward-facing cameras. We investigate a complementary paradigm that uses full-spherical perception to follow designated targets without active heading adjustment. To support this setting, we introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark comprising 2,652 sequences, over 1.73 million synchronized observations, eight tracking tasks, and 150 held-out closed-loop scenarios. We propose 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision--language--action (VLA) framework integrating persistent visual referring (PVR), compressed temporal memory (CTM), and geometry-aligned trajectory supervision (GTS) for instance identification, motion
s8a9cb79c80.summary: Researchers introduce 360UAV-ETrack, a simulation benchmark of 2,652 sequences, and 360UAV-TVLA, a panoramic vision-based method for UAV tracking without turning to change heading.
s8a9cb79c80.why: Full-spherical perception could decouple target tracking from heading control for drones, a benchmark-level result rather than a deployed system.

sa0d2456a0b.title: InstructTTS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Objective Instruction-Following TTS
sa0d2456a0b.description: arXiv:2611.33937v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Instruction-following text-to-speech (Instruct-TTS) renders a target transcript in the manner described by a free-form natural-language instruction, and a good rendition must succeed on three fronts at once: following the instruction, pronouncing the transcript correctly, and sounding natural. Reinforcement learning has become the standard way to post-train such generative models toward human preferences, and TTS systems increasingly adopt it. When the three objectives are optimized together under a single scalar reward, typically with group relative policy optimization (GRPO), training tends to be unstable: the objectives compete, and the shared update drifts toward whichever one is easiest to improve, producing a seesaw among them. We ins
sa0d2456a0b.summary: InstructTTS-OPD proposes on-policy distillation to jointly optimize instruction following, pronunciation, and naturalness in instruction-following text-to-speech models.
sa0d2456a0b.why: It addresses the difficulty of balancing multiple objectives under a single scalar reward when post-training TTS models.

sc2117471d3.title: DuoMI: Dual Mutual Information Regularization for Expert Reuse in Looped Transformers
sc2117471d3.description: arXiv:2611.33952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Dual Mutual Information Regularization (DuoMI), a method for regulating expert routing across rounds in looped mixture-of-experts (MoE) Transformers. When two rounds of computation share an expert pool, their routers may favor different expert subsets, limiting the reuse of individual expert parameters across rounds. Even when aggregate expert usage is identical across rounds, we would still prefer each token to retain some experts while switching to others. DuoMI addresses both aspects of routing: it uses round-level marginal mutual information to limit the dependence of aggregate expert usage on the round, and token-level conditional mutual information to penalize average cross-round routing changes that fall outside a target
sc2117471d3.summary: DuoMI introduces dual mutual information regularization to encourage expert reuse across rounds in looped mixture-of-experts Transformers.
sc2117471d3.why: Better expert routing across loop iterations could improve parameter efficiency in looped MoE architectures.

s93a0ea757b.title: RefMix: Expanding Endpoint Proposals for Diversity-Preserving Reward Fine-Tuning
s93a0ea757b.description: arXiv:2611.33957v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online forward matching aligns flow-based generative models by repeatedly generating, rewarding, and fitting model-produced endpoints. However, this behavior creates an on-policy feedback loop: as high-reward modes become increasingly favored, alternative modes become less likely to appear in subsequent training pools, progressively reducing visual diversity. We introduce RefMix, a reference-assisted endpoint proposal strategy that addresses this limitation by injecting alternative candidates into the training pool while retaining the original task reward and forward matching objective. In particular, RefMix uses a reference model during early high-noise steps to expose alternative visual modes, followed by the current reward-tuned model fo
s93a0ea757b.summary: RefMix proposes injecting reference-assisted alternative endpoint candidates into training pools to counter diversity loss in reward fine-tuning of flow-based generative models.
s93a0ea757b.why: It targets a feedback loop where reward fine-tuning progressively reduces visual diversity, relevant to training image generators.

s83407a526d.title: AI Buckingham: Agentic Discovery of Dimensionless Scaling Laws Across Physical Regimes
s83407a526d.description: arXiv:2611.33961v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Classical dimensional analysis defines admissible dimensionless representations but does not determine which combinations capture the dominant physical dependence, whether it changes across physical regimes, or when dependent-variable rescaling is required. We present AI Buckingham, an agentic framework for autonomous dimensionless discovery from natural-language descriptions of physical problems and observational data. It couples reasoning and planning by a large language model (LLM) with predefined symbolic and numerical tools. Literature-based knowledge retrieval supports dimensional checking, gradient-based clustering identifies physical regimes, and mutual information provides an objective, reparameterization-invariant criterion for id
s83407a526d.summary: AI Buckingham is an agentic framework pairing an LLM with symbolic and numerical tools to autonomously discover dimensionless scaling laws from problem descriptions and data.

s5fd96e20be.title: Embodied-VGGT: Preserving Reliable Local Geometry for Long-Sequence Reconstruction
s5fd96e20be.description: arXiv:2611.33964v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Long sequence reconstruction must correct accumulated drift while preserving locally consistent geometry. In robotics and autonomous driving, embodied acquisition provides recurring platform- environment geometry and repeated observations of scene structure and platform motion. We present Embodied-VGGT, which exploits these cues to establish reliable local relationships and selectively preserve them during global refinement. Memory-Augmented Grounded Chunks (MAGC) builds on Scal3R's global context memory and uses relative scale references derived from predicted ground geometry to regularize test-time memory updates, encouraging cross-chunk consistency while limiting changes to reliable local geometry. Superpoint Alignment (SA) and Cross-Loo
s5fd96e20be.summary: Embodied-VGGT is presented as a method for long-sequence 3D reconstruction that preserves reliable local geometry while correcting accumulated drift during global refinement.
s5fd96e20be.why: Drift correction in long-sequence reconstruction matters for robotics and autonomous driving mapping pipelines.

s7d741a4468.title: Fine-Tuning Without Gradients? Closed-Form, LLM-Written Classifiers on a Frozen Encoder
s7d741a4468.description: arXiv:2611.33972v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Can a classifier computed in closed form on a frozen encoder match gradient fine-tuning? We present closed-form weight-space programming (WSP): a large language model (LLM), used as a design assistant, writes programs that read a frozen masked language model through cloze-style prompt templates at several layers, fit closed-form heads (shrinkage discriminant analysis, kernel ridge regression and the encoder's label-word prior) on labelled data, and select among a pool of candidate heads by cross-fitting. No gradient is computed and no encoder weight changes. We instantiate the framework on RoBERTa-large. On 11 development datasets with 512 to 8,192 training labels, WSP is ahead of full fine-tuning (FT) and LoRA at every label budget (by 0.3
s7d741a4468.summary: Closed-form weight-space programming uses an LLM to write programs that fit closed-form classifier heads on a frozen masked language model, without gradient fine-tuning.
s7d741a4468.why: It suggests a gradient-free alternative to fine-tuning for classification, though the paper's results versus fine-tuning are not stated here.

sc8f1cffabc.title: Kolpona: An Agentic Framework with Gradient-Free Neuron Programming for RTL Generation
sc8f1cffabc.description: arXiv:2611.33973v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-weight large language models (LLMs) for register-transfer level (RTL) design are usually improved by fine-tuning on curated Verilog corpora, which needs large sets of verified designs and GPU training. We present Kolpona, an agentic framework that improves such models without gradient training. Its first component is neuron programming, a new form of weight-space programming (WSP) that writes single neurons in closed form into the weights to remove failure habits found on practice tasks, and keeps each edit only when testbench results on fresh tasks favour it. At inference time, tool-using agents propose designs, and a label-free selection stage delivers one design per task from the specification, the candidates and their simulations a
sc8f1cffabc.summary: Kolpona is an agentic framework that improves open-weight LLMs for RTL Verilog generation via gradient-free neuron programming, keeping edits only when testbench results improve.
sc8f1cffabc.why: It offers a way to improve hardware-design LLMs without GPU fine-tuning or large verified Verilog corpora.

s7a5f963952.title: MolGPAO: Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree with Speculative Decoding and Sub-Millisecond Seam Healing for 3D Molecules
s7a5f963952.description: arXiv:2611.33985v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive generation over adaptive 3D octrees (Uni-3DAR) offers an intrinsic $O(N \log N)$ sparsity advantage over dense $O(N^2)$ equivariant diffusion and flow models on large drug-like molecules, yet lags in geometric equilibrium, closed-shell valence stability, and property fidelity due to Morton-seam coordinate jumps, leaf-heavy compute with root-count trapping, and target-shortcut collapse in internal critics. We introduce MolGPAO (Molecular Generative Pre-trained Autoregressive Octree), a standalone 3D octree architecture and single-output speculative tree-decoding engine using zero external surrogates, zero reinforcement learning, and zero inference-time MLIP relaxation. MolGPAO unifies: (1) non-trapping 6-D ScaleFreeBudgetEmbed
s7a5f963952.summary: MolGPAO is a standalone 3D octree autoregressive architecture for molecule generation, adding speculative decoding and seam healing to address geometric and valence issues in prior methods.

sf6f11cf908.title: Aegis-VLA: Reliability-Gated Action Refinement via a Trajectory World Model for Dynamic Object Manipulation
sf6f11cf908.description: arXiv:2611.33993v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dynamic object manipulation requires maintaining spatial and temporal alignment with targets that continue to move during inference and execution. Although future prediction can inform action correction, an accurate forecast does not establish whether modifying an existing action would be beneficial. We present Aegis-VLA, a world-model-guided vision-language-action (VLA) framework that generates predictive action corrections and separately determines whether and how strongly to apply them. A Trajectory World Model combines kinematic extrapolation with learned residual dynamics to predict object motion and estimate positional uncertainty. Discrepancy-Guided Action Refinement uses differences between history-only and base-action-conditioned e
sf6f11cf908.summary: Aegis-VLA is a world-model-guided vision-language-action framework that generates predictive action corrections for dynamic object manipulation and decides whether to apply them.
sf6f11cf908.why: Gating corrections by reliability addresses a practical failure mode for robots manipulating moving objects.

sf8e9b4a90b.title: DosePET: An Open-Source Dataset with 2100 Radiation Dose Maps for PET/CT
sf8e9b4a90b.description: arXiv:2611.34008v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large collections of three-dimensional radiation dose maps linked to patient anatomy are needed to develop artificial intelligence (AI) models for personalized internal dosimetry in nuclear medicine, but access to such data remains limited. Here we present DosePET, an open-source dataset of 2,100 patient-specific absorbed-dose maps generated by Monte Carlo simulation of publicly available PET/CT examinations: 1,503 [18F]FDG examinations from ENHANCE.PET and 369 [18F]PSMA-1007 and 228 [68Ga]Ga-PSMA-11 examinations from PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions, acquired at five institutions with seven scanner models. For each examination, the CT was resampled to the native PET grid to build a voxelized patient phantom, the quantitative PET image defined the radio
sf8e9b4a90b.summary: DosePET is an open-source dataset of 2,100 Monte Carlo-simulated patient-specific absorbed-dose maps from publicly available PET/CT examinations.
sf8e9b4a90b.why: Public dose-map data could enable training AI models for personalized internal dosimetry in nuclear medicine.

s72f6324e3e.title: CARROT: Competitive Adaptive Graph Clustering via Semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport
s72f6324e3e.description: arXiv:2611.34012v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep graph clustering (DGC) has emerged as a prominent paradigm for unsupervised attributed graph clustering. However, existing methods often struggle with two practical challenges encountered in real-world applications: the number of clusters $K$ is unknown a priori, and cluster sizes are frequently highly imbalanced. Methods relying on a pre-specified $K$ may fail to recover the underlying clustering structure when $K$ is misspecified, while many approaches implicitly favor balanced partitions, hindering the discovery of minority clusters. We propose CARROT, a Competitive Adaptive gRaph clustering framework via semi-Relaxed Optimal Transport, which introduces semi-relaxed optimal transport into deep graph clustering to jointly address bot
s72f6324e3e.summary: CARROT is a deep graph clustering method using semi-relaxed optimal transport to handle unknown cluster counts and highly imbalanced cluster sizes.

s70c6cf8fda.title: Residual Cross-Model Narrative Convergence under Shared Prompts: Auditing Prompt Controls and Narrative Measurement
s70c6cf8fda.description: arXiv:2611.34015v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Stories created by LLMs based on the same prompts can be narratively similar to one another. This similarity may reflect constraints imposed by the prompts as well as the models' writing tendencies. The current research analyzes 51,240 stories created by five models in the StoryScope corpus based on 10,248 common prompts. It uses 213 narrative features in seven dimensions to compare cross-model distances between stories generated from the same prompts with distances between stories generated from different but semantically matched prompts. To assess the relationship between narrative features and prompt content, a semantic relevance mask was evaluated against 420 author-annotated prompt-feature judgments (F1 = .813; near-threshold accuracy
s70c6cf8fda.summary: Researchers analyze 51,240 LLM-generated stories from 10,248 shared prompts, comparing narrative similarity across five models using 213 features.
s70c6cf8fda.why: It helps teams separate prompt-driven narrative similarity from model-specific writing tendencies when evaluating or auditing generated content.

s2ec896930c.title: Evaluating Ukrainian Grammatical Competence in Language Models: Probability Versus Prompting
s2ec896930c.description: arXiv:2611.34016v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Organisations deploying large language models in Ukrainian-language information systems need to know whether a model produces normative Ukrainian. This paper establishes a protocol for measuring that reliably and applies it to 19 models. The instrument is a released set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs covering the vocative case, numeral-noun and adjective agreement, verb government and calques from russian, with subject-verb agreement as a control; a quarter of the set was checked against the answer key in two independent native-speaker ratings, which agreed at Cohen's $\kappa$ = 0.963. Every pair is scored twice: by comparing the probabilities a model assigns to the two sentences, and by asking the model directly, with the sentences prese
s2ec896930c.summary: Researchers released a set of 1,444 Ukrainian minimal pairs and used them to measure grammatical competence across 19 language models.
s2ec896930c.why: Organisations deploying LLMs in Ukrainian-language systems get a released benchmark and protocol for checking whether models produce normative Ukrainian.

s4b1b63c8be.title: Assessing the Physical Interpretability of AlphaEarth Foundation Embeddings Through Multi-Sensor Satellite Time-Series Benchmarking for Agricultural Mapping
s4b1b63c8be.description: arXiv:2611.34019v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate and dynamic maps of agricultural LULC are important for agricultural water resource management, particularly in areas where water scarcity is prevalent, such as Morocco. Here, we evaluate the utility of AlphaEarth Foundation Model (AEF) embeddings for agricultural LULC and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco. AEF embeddings were compared to single-date and time-series remote-sensing features using three machine-learning classifiers: XGBoost, CatBoost, and TabPFN. We also evaluated whether AEF embeddings can: (a) provide an efficient and transferable alternative to conventional direct use of Earth observation products and (b) reconstruct biophysical information. Results showed that multi-temporal feature time series achieved the high
s4b1b63c8be.summary: Researchers evaluated AlphaEarth Foundation embeddings for agricultural land-use and irrigation-type mapping in Morocco against multi-sensor satellite time-series features.
s4b1b63c8be.why: It offers evidence on whether pretrained geospatial embeddings can replace costlier time-series feature pipelines for agricultural mapping.

s0b92564eed.title: Incorporating the Knowledge Distillation to Improve the EfficientNet Transfer Learning Capability
s0b92564eed.description: arXiv:2611.34025v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Due to the Deep Learning requirement for a large training dataset, Transfer Learning has become a central method in the field of Computer Vision, which heavily used Deep Learning. Since the adoption of transfer learning in the field, the performance of the models in computer vision is significantly upgraded. The common transfer learning practice in computer vision research is to use state-of-the-art architectures in the ImageNet dataset as the backbone network. The best performing architecture in ImageNet is currently held by EfficientNet, which is a set of architectures that were progressively grown from a baseline architecture. By observing the EfficientNet development approach, it is natural to hypothesize that the smaller EfficientNet a
s0b92564eed.summary: The paper proposes incorporating knowledge distillation to improve transfer learning capability of EfficientNet models in computer vision.

s160e5aa878.title: Counter-DECEIVR: Counterfactual Explanations for Deepfake Detectors using Detector-Guided Rectified Flow Inversion
s160e5aa878.description: arXiv:2611.34032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep-learning-generated media are increasingly passed off as real, driving an arms race between image generators and deepfake detectors. Trust in the latter is limited by their often black-box nature; and, while region-based explanations can sometimes be extracted, these become less useful as generation quality improves. Counterfactual examples, which show the minimal change that flips a detector's decision, reveal what evidence drives a verdict, helping analysts decide whether to trust it. This work introduces Counter-DECEIVR (DEtector-guided reCtifiEd flow InVeRsion for counterfactuals), a novel training-free framework that generates counterfactual examples. Counter-DECEIVR steers latents in the velocity field of a rectified flow model us
s160e5aa878.summary: Researchers introduce Counter-DECEIVR, a method that generates counterfactual explanations for deepfake detectors using detector-guided rectified flow inversion.
s160e5aa878.why: Counterfactual explanations can show analysts which evidence drives a deepfake detector's verdict, helping them decide whether to trust it.

sdce7aa564f.title: Post-Training Policy Replication for Strategy-Following Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning across Team Sizes
sdce7aa564f.description: arXiv:2611.34035v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although multi-agent deep reinforcement learning enables coordinated behavior, aligning it with managerial intent remains difficult due to complex agent interactions. Although the strategy-following distributed attentional actor architecture (sfDA7-X) improves controllability via regional instructions, instruction combinations scale exponentially with team and instruction sizes, leading to prohibitive training costs and poor transferability. To reduce this computational cost, we introduce a team-size-independent observation architecture and reconstruct collective behavior by replicating a single trained policy across agents in teams of different sizes, thereby eliminating the need to train from scratch. Additionally, we evaluate warm-start
sdce7aa564f.summary: Researchers propose a team-size-independent observation architecture and post-training policy replication for strategy-following multi-agent deep reinforcement learning.
sdce7aa564f.why: Reducing retraining costs when team sizes change could make managerially controlled multi-agent RL systems cheaper to scale and transfer.

s5b682dd5a1.title: Hijacking 3D Generation: Targeted Adversarial Attacks against Image-to-3D Models via Prefix Trajectory Alignment
s5b682dd5a1.description: arXiv:2611.34075v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Online services that deploy Image-to-3D models enable users to generate high-quality 3D assets from a single image. However, the generated 3D geometry can violate content policies and cause broader security risks. To prevent such content, these services typically use policy-restricted inspectors to examine uploaded images before generation. Since the inspector examines only the visible content of the input, a visually benign image can still induce the generation of policy-restricted 3D geometry. However, turning this vulnerability into an effective attack is non-trivial in the black-box setting: global backpropagation through the long DiT generation trajectory is difficult to fit, while different image preprocessing pipelines across service
s5b682dd5a1.summary: Researchers present a targeted adversarial attack that makes image-to-3D models generate policy-restricted 3D geometry from visually benign inputs, bypassing input inspectors.
s5b682dd5a1.why: Services relying on input-image inspectors for content policy may be bypassed, exposing generation pipelines to misuse and security risks.

safdc3f17fa.title: WorldBridge: Bridging Scattered Views for Coherent 3D World Generation
safdc3f17fa.description: arXiv:2611.34079v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generating coherent and explorable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap is a fundamental and long-standing challenge in computer vision, which existing geometry-aware methods fail to address. Meanwhile, existing image- and video-based methods may generate unseen regions but produce inconsistent geometry across views. To bridge this gap, we present WorldBridge, a framework for coherent and controllable 3D world generation under scattered images with little or no visual overlap. WorldBridge encodes scattered references into a global scene context to guide geometry and appearance generation across views. Our temporal and spatial reference attention mechanism further enhances the fidelity of temporal references along
safdc3f17fa.summary: WorldBridge is a framework for generating coherent, controllable 3D worlds from scattered images with little or no visual overlap.

s2e976358e4.title: Whose Side Are You On? A Framework and Benchmark for Assessing LLM Political Stances through Politicians Social Media Posts
s2e976358e4.description: arXiv:2611.34098v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly participate in political discussions, making it important to understand which positions they support or oppose. We propose a framework for assessing LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions. The framework uses politicians' posts and multiple prompting methods to identify consistently expressed stances. Using this framework, we construct WorldPOLL, comprising 4,600 political posts from X/Twitter collected from approximately 200 politicians representing ruling and opposition blocs across 23 countries. Our quantitative analysis shows how support and opposition vary across models, countries, and political directions, while our qualitative analysis identifies the political view
s2e976358e4.summary: Researchers propose a framework and WorldPOLL benchmark of 4,600 politicians' X/Twitter posts to assess LLMs' political stances through simulated social media interactions.
s2e976358e4.why: Teams deploying LLMs in political or public-facing contexts can use this framework to measure which stances models consistently express.

s4cc6b1e1c3.title: Will AI Replace Juniors? How Task Complexity Reduces Automation Risk
s4cc6b1e1c3.description: arXiv:2611.34099v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: How does task complexity shape firms' willingness to substitute entry-level labour with artificial intelligence (AI) tools? We study this question using a pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms in the information economy and manufacturing industry. Managers are randomly assigned to consider a long lasting need for additional capacity involving either well-structured and standardised tasks, or more complex tasks that require professional judgement, contextual knowledge and independent problem-solving. Relative to standardised tasks, complex tasks reduce willingness to use AI rather than hire an entry-level employee by 0.54 points on a five-point scale and increase the importance attached to human oversight by
s4cc6b1e1c3.summary: A pre-registered survey experiment with managers from 1,435 German firms examines how task complexity affects willingness to replace entry-level labour with AI.
s4cc6b1e1c3.why: Leaders planning junior hiring may find that managers view complex, judgement-heavy tasks as less exposed to AI substitution than standardised ones.

s966c69652e.title: AlignPre: Skill-Aligned Post-Training for Latent-Free Generative Precipitation Nowcasting
s966c69652e.description: arXiv:2611.34101v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Precipitation nowcasting requires accurate short-term predictions under rapidly evolving spatiotemporal dynamics. Generative diffusion models can produce detailed and competitive radar forecasts by modeling conditional distributions. However, most existing approaches rely on separately trained components, such as deterministic branches or latent compression modules. More fundamentally, distribution matching alone fails to explicitly optimize operational forecast skill. We propose AlignPre, a streamlined pixel-space nowcasting framework that bridges this gap via skill-aligned post-training (SAPT). AlignPre employs an end-to-end flow-matching forecaster with a hierarchical spatiotemporal architecture for distribution matching and direct radar
s966c69652e.summary: AlignPre is a pixel-space generative diffusion framework for precipitation nowcasting that aligns post-training with operational forecast skill, without latent compression modules.

s212095d9ab.title: Do Machine Learning Ensembles Beat Published Quotas? Target Parameterization, Censored Baselines, and Conformal Intervals Under Admissions Reform
