s212095d9ab.description: arXiv:2611.34104v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Public admission capacity caps published prior to matriculation are widely used by ministries and institutional analysts as default intake projections in centralized postsecondary clearinghouses. Using an audited 2022 to 2026 Vietnamese undergraduate panel (26,895 program-year records across 309 universities) linked to strictly lagged t-1 occupational vacancy signals, this paper evaluates machine learning, multilevel, and censored econometric estimators against published quotas across 5,385 continuing 2024 programs (five-fold university-grouped cross-validation) and 3,348 matched (2,179 grain-consistent) 2025 programs strictly out of time. Because 62.8% of 2024 programs enroll their exact published quota, unanchored log-growth ensembles deg
s212095d9ab.summary: The paper evaluates machine learning and econometric estimators against published Vietnamese university admission quotas using a 2022 to 2026 undergraduate panel.

sdb71e8a03f.title: SysBio-SR: Benchmarking Symbolic Regression for Trajectory Fidelity and Mechanism Recovery in Systems Biology
sdb71e8a03f.description: arXiv:2611.34106v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Symbolic regression seeks to discover interpretable governing equations for dynamical systems from data. In systems biology, however, accurately reproducing system trajectories does not necessarily imply recovery of the underlying reaction mechanisms. Existing benchmarks evaluate numerical accuracy, expression complexity, or equation-level similarity, but not agreement between recovered reactions and reference mechanisms in biological systems. We introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems with reaction annotations spanning mass action, Michaelis--Menten, Hill, and complex kinetics. Trajectory fidelity is evaluated across all systems under in-distribution reconstruction and out-of-distribution (OOD) extra
sdb71e8a03f.summary: Researchers introduce SysBio-SR, a benchmark of 198 literature-based biological ODE systems to test whether symbolic regression recovers true reaction mechanisms.
sdb71e8a03f.why: Shows that accurate trajectory fitting does not guarantee recovery of underlying mechanisms, so evaluation of scientific model-discovery tools needs mechanism-level checks.

s8fdf8b417c.title: Unstable Action Boundaries in Lethal Drone Agents
s8fdf8b417c.description: arXiv:2611.34121v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Tool-using large language model (LLM) agents raise safety risks that are not captured by text-only refusal behavior, especially when tools can trigger high-impact actions. This concern is salient in military settings, where autonomous weapons raise the possibility of delegating force decisions to software agents. In this work, we study whether a drone agent's action boundary is stable under changes to the target descriptor. We evaluate recent and popular LLMs in a simulated perception-action pipeline over real-world drone imagery, where models can localize requested targets and invoke a simulated lethal tool. We find two concerning failure modes. First, some LLM agents invoke the lethal tool for ordinary generic descriptors such as \emph{pe
s8fdf8b417c.summary: A study tests whether tool-using LLM drone agents keep stable action boundaries when target descriptors change in a simulated perception-action pipeline over drone imagery.
s8fdf8b417c.why: Tool-using agents that can trigger high-impact actions may behave unpredictably under small input changes, a safety concern beyond text-only refusal behavior.

sd2a395e74c.title: MUSE: Multi-Task Uncertainty-Aware Self-Supervised Encoder for mmWave ISAC
sd2a395e74c.description: arXiv:2611.34122v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) allows a wireless system to use the same waveform for communication and environment sensing. At mmWave frequency bands, ISAC enables diverse human sensing tasks, such as localization, gesture recognition, and pose estimation, with high precision. However, each task requires training a dedicated model, typically from scratch on a task-specific dataset, with no mechanism to flag unreliable predictions. This hurts the scalability, transferability, and reliability of mmWave ISAC models. In this work, we propose MUSE (Multi-task Uncertainty-aware Self-supervised Encoder), a unified framework for mmWave human sensing. MUSE leverages a self-supervised transformer model with per-dataset tokenization and i
sd2a395e74c.summary: MUSE is a multi-task, uncertainty-aware self-supervised encoder for mmWave integrated sensing and communication that aims to support multiple sensing tasks from one model.
sd2a395e74c.why: A shared encoder with uncertainty estimates could reduce per-task training and flag unreliable predictions in mmWave sensing systems.

s842738ac4a.title: Out of Sight, Not Out of Clues: Can Video LLMs Guess from Partial Evidence?
s842738ac4a.description: arXiv:2611.34126v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In real-world applications like egocentric recording, visual accessibility, and surveillance review, visual evidence for Video Large Language Models (Video LLMs) is often only partially captured. A reliable model should match its response to the evidence: answering when sufficient, guessing from visible clues when partial, and abstaining when absent. Yet existing benchmarks enforce a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial evidence unmeasured and obscuring whether failures arise from missing evidence or misjudging sufficiency. We introduce ClueProbe, a diagnostic benchmark to (1) separate perceiving evidence from judging sufficiency, and (2) validate our diagnosis via targeted fine-tuning. ClueProbe comprises 1,721 human-an
s842738ac4a.summary: Researchers argue existing Video LLM benchmarks use a binary answerable-or-unanswerable split, leaving partial visual evidence unmeasured, and propose evaluating responses to partial evidence.
s842738ac4a.why: Engineers deploying video models in surveillance or accessibility need to know whether models answer, guess, or abstain appropriately when evidence is incomplete.

s6f950bb8f5.title: FoundSurface: Feedforward Ray-Based 3D Scene Surface Reconstruction from Unposed Images
s6f950bb8f5.description: arXiv:2611.34128v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate 3D surface reconstruction from unposed images remains a fundamental challenge in computer vision. Recent feed-forward pointmap methods eliminate the need for camera poses but inherently produce discrete, sparse representations. In this paper, we present a generalizable pipeline that directly recovers continuous, high-fidelity 3D surfaces from unposed images by seamlessly integrating pointmap- and ray-based representations. Our approach first extracts explicit geometric priors using a pre-trained pointmap model. A query-view-centric selection module then identifies geometrically relevant reference views via a robust surfel voting mechanism. Next, a cross-attention regressor bridges target query rays with reference features to estima
s6f950bb8f5.summary: FoundSurface is a feedforward pipeline that reconstructs continuous 3D surfaces from unposed images by combining pointmap and ray-based representations.
s6f950bb8f5.why: It offers a camera-pose-free route to dense 3D surfaces, which could simplify reconstruction pipelines for vision and robotics teams.

s7e523f9148.title: WorldPhy: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Physical Plausibility of World Models in Robotics
s7e523f9148.description: arXiv:2611.34130v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models are increasingly used in robotics to improve the performance of embodied models. Compared with general-purpose video generation, robotics places more stringent requirements on world models. Generated videos must satisfy fine-grained physical constraints on robot motion and object interactions. However, existing world model benchmarks can overlook robotics specific physical details and struggle to assess them accurately. To address this problem, we introduce WorldPhy, a world model benchmark for accurate, fine-grained evaluation of physical plausibility in robotics. Our benchmark contains 300 tasks, each consisting of an initial-frame image and a task instruction, covering diverse robotics scenes, task categories, viewpoints, an
s7e523f9148.summary: WorldPhy is a new benchmark for evaluating fine-grained physical plausibility of robotics world models, covering robot motion and object interactions.
s7e523f9148.why: Teams using generated video as world models for robots need finer physics checks than general video-generation benchmarks provide.

s3ce0178dc0.title: Reproducer Synthesis for AI-Reported Bugs in the Linux Kernel
s3ce0178dc0.description: arXiv:2611.34142v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agentic review systems are increasingly flagging suspected bugs in Linux kernel patches as textual reports. A maintainer who receives such reports needs further inspection to determine whether the report is true. The inspection requires understanding whether the bug can be triggered and, if necessary, manually constructing one. As a consequence, despite the excessive textual explanation, many reports go unanswered. In this paper, we argue that a runnable proof-of-concept (PoC) is the key information in such AI-generated kernel review reports. It is, however, challenging to automatically synthesize a valid and runnable PoC. We present ReproCue, a framework that generates PoCs for AI-generated Linux kernel reviews. ReproCue replays the histor
s3ce0178dc0.summary: The paper argues that runnable proof-of-concept reproducers should accompany AI-generated bug reports for Linux kernel patches, to help maintainers verify them.
s3ce0178dc0.why: Maintainers and kernel teams receiving AI review reports could triage faster if each report included a runnable reproducer.

s2715a7dd12.title: Lost in the Grid: Where Multimodal LLMs Fail Between Seeing and Planning
s2715a7dd12.description: arXiv:2611.34152v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) excel at static visual understanding and are increasingly applied to spatial planning, where a model interprets a visual layout and outputs an action sequence to reach a goal. Grid games are a common testbed for this ability because their rules are explicit and a solver can verify every move. Yet existing benchmarks mostly report end-to-end success rates, which hide whether a failure stems from visual perception, rule application, or multi-step planning. We introduce GridProbe, a diagnostic benchmark that 1) locates the failing stage between visual perception and planning and 2) verifies the diagnosis by targeted fine-tuning. On Sokoban, GridProbe pairs end-to-end solving with four probes (recognitio
s2715a7dd12.summary: GridProbe is a diagnostic benchmark that separates visual perception, rule application, and multi-step planning failures in multimodal LLMs on grid games.
s2715a7dd12.why: End-to-end success rates hide where spatial planning fails, so this benchmark helps engineers locate the actual weakness in MLLM agents.

s769b512614.title: Strategic and Robust Task Allocation for Combat Objectives in Adversarial Multi-Agent Environments
s769b512614.description: arXiv:2611.34158v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Task allocation in contested-objective team games requires coordinated decisions under uncertainty, spatial constraints, and changing tactical conditions. In such settings, multiple agents must anticipate both teammate behavior and opponent actions. We study a hybrid predict-then-optimize approach for assigning controllable agents to objectives in real time. A masked multi-head model predicts tactical signals for each agent, including survival chance, local superiority, combat interaction, travel time, and objective contribution. These signals are combined with rule-based terms in a score matrix, and a minimum-cost flow solver computes coordinated global assignments constrained by capacity, occupancy, stability, and defensive strategies. Le
s769b512614.summary: Researchers propose a hybrid predict-then-optimize method that uses a masked multi-head model to assign agents to objectives in adversarial team games in real time.
s769b512614.why: The approach combines tactical prediction with optimization for multi-agent allocation under uncertainty, relevant to teams building coordinated agent systems.

sdc5dcf42f1.title: Multi-view fnirs identifies neurophysiological subtypes in post-stroke aphasia
sdc5dcf42f1.description: arXiv:2611.34169v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-stroke aphasia is clinically heterogeneous, and conventional classifications may not capture differences in brain functional organisation. We tested whether resting-state and task-based functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) could identify neurophysiological subgroups alongside clinical assessment.Seventy-nine patients underwent unsupervised clustering using three fNIRS feature views: resting-state activity and connectivity, language-task activation, and rest-to-task connectivity reconfiguration. Similarity network fusion and spectral clustering integrated the views. Clinical and behavioural measures were excluded from clustering.Three clusters (n = 32, 17 and 30) were identified. This solution had the largest eigengap and was t
sdc5dcf42f1.summary: A study of 79 post-stroke aphasia patients used multi-view fNIRS and unsupervised clustering to identify neurophysiological subtypes.

s36be01f6b8.title: Agentic-Level Adversarial Purification: Revisiting Diffusion Purifiers on Native-Resolution Agentic Inputs
s36be01f6b8.description: arXiv:2611.34181v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language agents act on native-resolution renders of multi-element pages, where one perturbed photo or a few altered text strokes can redirect the decision. Any content provider can craft such a perturbation on the open model behind the agent, so a plug-in purifier is the natural first line of defense. Yet diffusion purifiers were designed and evaluated at the fixed resolution of the diffusion model on classifier or natural-image benchmarks, and defense evaluations for agents test JPEG, blur and noise but no diffusion purifier. We present the first study of adversarial purification at the agentic level, for an agent built on Qwen3-VL-8B: purifiers run at native resolution on multi-element inputs, face grey-box attackers who know the a
s36be01f6b8.summary: The paper revisits diffusion purifiers as defenses for vision-language agents on native-resolution inputs, which prior agent defense evaluations did not test.
s36be01f6b8.why: Engineers securing vision-language agents against adversarial page perturbations get an evaluation of a plug-in purifier defense they may adopt.

s3fafb53ab9.title: Hierarchical Semantic Learning for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis with Missing Modalities
s3fafb53ab9.description: arXiv:2611.34184v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) in real-world systems must handle unpredictable modality missingness caused by sensor failures, privacy masking, and unstable transmission. Existing methods either learn reliability-aware representations or reconstruct missing inputs, often using a single flattened encoder output. This overlooks deep encoders' semantic hierarchy and intra- and inter-modal interactions, causing semantic averaging and ill-posed mappings. We propose Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL), a framework that exploits semantic hierarchy for robust MSA with missing modalities. Hierarchical Semantic Decoupling exposes low-, mid-, and high-level feature streams from each modality encoder. Cross-Modal Cross-Level Semantic Reconstructi
s3fafb53ab9.summary: Hierarchical Semantic Learning (HSL) is proposed for multimodal sentiment analysis, handling missing modalities by exploiting semantic hierarchy in deep encoders.
s3fafb53ab9.why: Robust handling of missing sensor or input modalities matters for real-world multimodal systems with unreliable transmission.

se302a6283f.title: MINE: A Training-Free Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection via Mutual Information and Embedding Variance
se302a6283f.description: arXiv:2611.34188v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Existing defenses against indirect prompt injection in retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) are inherently reactive: prompt-engineering methods are often overridden by the injected instructions, while supervised detectors must be retrained for each new attack style. We propose a different paradigm: defend by maximizing relevance, not by detecting attacks. Our method, MINE, is training-free and attack-agnostic, and it also serves as a query-conditioned reranker. To evaluate defenses under realistic conditions, we introduce LC-Inj-SQuAD, a long-context benchmark with an average of 4,032 words per context. We evaluate on four datasets spanning short-context QA (Inj-SQuAD, Inj-TriviaQA), long-context QA (LC-Inj-SQuAD), and agent tool-call injec
se302a6283f.summary: MINE is a training-free defense against indirect prompt injection in RAG that maximizes relevance via mutual information and embedding variance, and also works as a reranker.
se302a6283f.why: It offers an attack-agnostic defense that needs no retraining, which is useful for teams running retrieval-augmented systems exposed to injected content.

s0d5f752ef4.title: Beyond Logits: Coherent Hallucination Mitigation via Attention Contrastive Decoding
s0d5f752ef4.description: arXiv:2611.34207v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) demonstrate impressive multimodal capabilities, yet suffer from hallucination - generating factually inaccurate content. Contrastive Decoding (CD) mitigates this by contrasting amateur and expert branches at the logit level. However, our investigation reveals that such logit-level interventions fundamentally compromise generation coherence, necessitating restrictive penalty constraints unrelated to hallucination suppression. We introduce Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD), a training-free plug-in that complements logit-level CD by relocating part of the contrastive operations to the attention mechanism. Operating at an earlier stage of the forward pass, ACD performs smooth semantic-preserving intervent
s0d5f752ef4.summary: Attention Contrastive Decoding (ACD) is a training-free plug-in that reduces hallucination in vision-language models by contrasting attention rather than logits.
s0d5f752ef4.why: It targets hallucination mitigation without degrading generation coherence, a tradeoff that affects deployed LVLM output quality.

s646d942d9e.title: GeoCAM: Self-Supervised Sonar-Optical Representation Learning via Geographic Overlap Supervision
s646d942d9e.description: arXiv:2611.34218v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Cross-modal self-supervised learning for paired side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery is a promising direction for benthic habitat understanding, but it remains underexplored because existing methods do not fully exploit the one-to-many correspondences and geographic metadata available in real opti-acoustic surveys. This limits the ability to learn representations that are both semantically meaningful and geometrically consistent from abundant unlabeled marine data. To address this problem, we present GeoCAM, a geography-guided framework that learns a shared embedding space for sonar tiles and their associated optical views without semantic annotations. GeoCAM achieves its goal by combining three components: (i) a Set Attention Agg
s646d942d9e.summary: GeoCAM is a geography-guided self-supervised framework that learns representations linking side-scan sonar and underwater optical imagery for benthic habitat understanding.

s66c1d99a84.title: The Socratic PAUSE: safeguarding scientific judgement at AI speed
s66c1d99a84.description: arXiv:2611.34222v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Generative AI can turn a tentative scientific question into hypotheses, methods, code and interpretations within minutes. Yet generating a contribution does not establish that it deserves scientific reliance: researchers must still examine its evidence, assumptions and implications, and remain accountable for the decision to rely on it. Using Einstein's sketch of scientific discovery as a lens, we argue that AI has accelerated discovery far more than justification. In human-AI research partnerships, confidence can therefore outgrow evidence through three mechanisms: recursive reinforcement, loss of provenance and miscalibrated reliance on AI-generated contributions. Verification debt accumulates when such contributions are carried into late
s66c1d99a84.summary: The paper argues AI has accelerated scientific discovery far more than justification, and proposes safeguards so researchers evaluate AI-generated evidence before relying on it.
s66c1d99a84.why: Research teams adopting generative AI for hypotheses and code need checks that keep confidence tied to evidence.

saf4a833523.title: Weakly Conditioned Diffusion Model Augmentation for Prostate Segmentation
saf4a833523.description: arXiv:2611.34230v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep learning models for prostate MRI segmentation often struggle to generalize when trained on limited heterogeneous data, leading to boundary errors and over-segmentation. We present an augmentation framework using mask-conditioned synthetic and diverse T2-weighted MRI volumes to improve boundary precision and reduce over-segmentation. We employ a 2.5D weakly mask-conditioned denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) via channel concatenation. The diffusion model conditions on stacks of adjacent binary masks from training folds. The model generates T2 volumes consistent with the conditioning anatomy while diversifying tissue appearance. We evaluate the proposed approach on two cohorts of data: (i) the LUND probe cohort (n=432) for st
saf4a833523.summary: A 2.5D mask-conditioned diffusion model generates synthetic T2-weighted prostate MRI volumes to augment training data for segmentation.
saf4a833523.why: Synthetic conditioned augmentation can reduce boundary errors and over-segmentation when medical training data is limited and heterogeneous.

sc995508d63.title: LLM-coupled interpretable tool wear monitoring with multi-evidence reasoning in CNC machining
sc995508d63.description: arXiv:2611.34270v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Interpretable tool wear assessment in CNC machining is challenging. Existing diagnostic models have high accuracy but provide limited guidance for tool replacement. This study proposes a two layer framework combining deep learning wear classification and LLM assisted reasoning. The first layer uses PCA Loading feature selection and optimized GRU to recognize three wear states, achieving 98.38 percent macro F1 score on the PHM2010 dataset. The second layer uses LLMs to generate natural language reports and replacement suggestions from classification results and feature trends. Engineer evaluation shows the reports outperform rule templates. Cross dataset tests on NASA milling data support the generalizability of this framework.
sc995508d63.summary: A two-layer framework combines a GRU wear classifier, reporting 98.38% macro F1 on PHM2010, with LLM-generated reports and replacement suggestions for CNC tool wear.
sc995508d63.why: It shows pairing a classifier with LLM reasoning to produce interpretable maintenance guidance for industrial monitoring systems.

s5fbd1e925c.title: LatentCP-DPO: Conformal Pessimism for DPO with Finite-Sample Guarantees
s5fbd1e925c.description: arXiv:2611.34275v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) learns a response policy from human preference data, but with a limited dataset it can overfit to noisy or weakly informative preference labels. We introduce LatentCP-DPO, a framework that combines conformal prediction with pessimistic preference optimization for Bradley-Terry (BT) pairwise feedback and Plackett-Luce (PL) ranking feedback. Building on LatentCP's construction of uncertainty sets for unobserved model parameters, we address how to incorporate this uncertainty into preference optimization and characterize its effect on policy performance. Under exchangeability and a correctly specified preference model, we construct uncertainty sets for latent relative rewards with finite-sample marginal cov
s5fbd1e925c.summary: Researchers introduce LatentCP-DPO, combining conformal prediction with pessimistic preference optimization to reduce DPO overfitting on limited, noisy preference data.
s5fbd1e925c.why: Offers a finite-sample-guaranteed way to make preference tuning more robust when labeled preference data is scarce or noisy.

sb0c8f3c93e.title: Latent-in-the-Middle: On the Security of Cross-Model Latent Communication in Multi-Agent Systems
sb0c8f3c93e.description: arXiv:2611.34278v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As large language models increasingly collaborate in heterogeneous multi-agent systems, latent communication has emerged as an efficient alternative to exchanging natural-language messages. By sharing internal representations, agents can avoid repeatedly processing the same context, reducing communication overhead and prefill computation. One such mechanism is cross-model Key-Value (KV) cache transfer, which uses a learned mapper to translate a source model's KV cache into one a target model can use. However, this handoff means the target model consumes context it did not encode itself, thus calling into question whether its safety alignment still holds. In this work, we investigate the security implications of latent handoffs by introducin
sb0c8f3c93e.summary: A paper examines the security of cross-model latent communication, where a learned mapper translates one LLM's KV cache for use by another in multi-agent systems.
sb0c8f3c93e.why: Shared internal representations between agents may open security risks that natural-language messaging does not, which matters for multi-agent system design.

sb9a6b5b383.title: StateWeaver: Multi-Agent Coordination of Story-State Transitions for Long-Horizon Video Generation
sb9a6b5b383.description: arXiv:2611.34290v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern video foundation models generate high-quality short clips, but preserving long-video consistency and correctly depicting event-driven state changes remain challenging. Existing agentic workflows face these challenges because continual planning and repair accumulate context, while reference updates remain limited. We introduce StateWeaver, which combines Active States and Hierarchical Collaboration to connect review-driven visual reference updates with cross-shot state inheritance. Active States translate state discrepancies identified during review into concrete visual asset requirements that guide reference construction, validation, and regeneration, preserving identity and already-correct content while repairing target attributes.
sb9a6b5b383.summary: StateWeaver proposes a multi-agent framework to improve long-video consistency and event-driven state changes in video generation.
sb9a6b5b383.why: Shows how agentic planning and review loops can address long-horizon consistency limits of current video foundation models.

sa64f26372e.title: WebVibe: Multimodal Interactive Website Generation via Reverse Synthesis and Visual Self-Distillation
sa64f26372e.description: arXiv:2611.34292v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Although multimodal large language models translate single screenshots into static HTML, generating interactive functional websites from design specifications still struggles with multi-page routing and stateful widget transitions. Examining existing training pipelines reveals two bottlenecks: (1) in forward data synthesis (X -> Y), writing the specification X before code execution leaves unimplemented or altered requirements in X as supervision noise; and (2) in reinforcement learning, scalar rewards discard the rich state transitions observed during replay. Based on these findings, we introduce WebVibe and Interactive-SDPO to train InteractiveCoder. WebVibe reverses synthesis into Y -> X by verifying cross-page and in-page interactions in
sa64f26372e.summary: WebVibe introduces a method for generating interactive multi-page websites from design specs, using reverse synthesis and visual self-distillation.
sa64f26372e.why: Targets known weaknesses in generating stateful, multi-page web apps from multimodal models, relevant to automated front-end tooling.

s3bc058e630.title: RAP: Radial-Angular Random Projection for Hyperbolic Representations
s3bc058e630.description: arXiv:2611.34298v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Random projection is a basic compression primitive for Euclidean representation learning, with the Johnson--Lindenstrauss lemma giving a target dimension $k=O(\varepsilon^{-2}\log n)$ independent of the ambient dimension. As hyperbolic representations gain increasing attention in modern Transformers, vision-language models, and large language models, the same need for oblivious dimensionality reduction arises, but no analogous primitive yet exists for hyperbolic representations. We study this gap. Two natural attempts fail in dual ways: a tangent-space scheme gives a clean local guarantee but is chart-bound and pays a curvature penalty, while a fully hyperbolic projection in the hyperboloid model is geometrically native but mixes radial and
s3bc058e630.summary: RAP proposes a radial-angular random projection method for compressing hyperbolic representations, filling a gap where no analogous primitive to Euclidean random projection existed.
s3bc058e630.why: Provides a dimensionality reduction tool for hyperbolic embeddings used in some Transformers and vision-language models.

s935bc19f42.title: The cost of being seen as AI in group bargaining
s935bc19f42.description: arXiv:2611.34322v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes embedded in collective decision-making, people's perceptions of AI may shape who reaches agreement and what they receive. We studied this in a repeated three-player majoritarian bargaining game with 2,234 participants. Players saw each opponent identified as Human or AI. The instructions described AI as acting either independently or on behalf of a human. Human participants made every decision. In mixed groups, players presented as AI received fewer points in opening offers, were included in fewer final agreements and earned about 18% less per round than those presented as Human. Smaller payoffs in agreements that included them accounted for most of the observed gap. Further analysis found a payoff ga
s935bc19f42.summary: A study of 2,234 participants in a repeated three-player bargaining game finds players presented as AI received fewer points and were included in fewer final agreements.
s935bc19f42.why: Suggests labeling systems as AI may carry social costs in group decisions, relevant to deploying AI agents in negotiation settings.

sccadd24df6.title: LUDIUS: A Benchmark for Embodied Social Intelligence in Everyday Human-Robot Interactions
sccadd24df6.description: arXiv:2611.34328v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Social intelligence in a robot requires interpreting a situation from the perspectives of the people involved and using that understanding to decide when and how to act. We introduce LUDIUS, a benchmark for evaluating how vision-language models exercise this judgment through a robot's verbal responses and actions, organized around 15 social intelligence skills drawn from social psychology, sociology, and cognitive science. LUDIUS comprises six editions, each a collection of episodes spanning one simulated week. Three editions each cover all 15 skills in a different household. The other three focus on interactions involving multiple people, safety, and context-specific norms, respectively. We evaluate frontier models and a smaller model fine
sccadd24df6.summary: LUDIUS is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on embodied social intelligence across 15 skills in everyday human-robot interactions.
sccadd24df6.why: Gives teams a structured way to assess social judgment of VLM-driven robots beyond task success.

s2d0482c46c.title: Puzzling-Bench: Evaluating Language Models on 23,777 Human-Written Puzzles with Community-Verified Answers
s2d0482c46c.description: arXiv:2611.34331v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce Puzzling-Bench, a benchmark of 23,777 puzzles with community-verified answers drawn from the Puzzling Stack Exchange archive (2014-2026): riddles, ciphers, logic grids, lateral-thinking problems, wordplay and recreational mathematics, a third of them with images. Every puzzle carries the answer accepted by its author, a short reference answer taken from it (LLM-extracted for the evaluation sets and checked on a 50-puzzle human review), the author's own hints, community tags and a creation date, so that the benchmark supports hint ablations, category analysis and a rolling post-cutoff slice (254 puzzles posted after the training cutoff of six of the nine models we evaluate, including the best one) as a contamination check. We ev
s2d0482c46c.summary: Puzzling-Bench introduces a benchmark of 23,777 community-verified puzzles from Puzzling Stack Exchange, including riddles, ciphers, logic grids, and images.
s2d0482c46c.why: Provides a large, human-written reasoning benchmark with verified answers and hints for evaluating language models.

se864fbff8b.title: Inverse Reinforcement Learning with State-Dependent Foresight for Human Decision-Making
se864fbff8b.description: arXiv:2611.34351v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Computational modeling of behavior represents individuals with a model fitted to their observed behavior and characterizes them through its parameters. Naturalistic tasks incorporate the complexity of real environments and yield high-dimensional behavioral trajectories. Inverse reinforcement learning (IRL) infers the latent reward function underlying these trajectories. Standard IRL, however, assumes effectively infinite-horizon planning, whereas human foresight is both bounded and state-dependent. Here we introduce SC-AIRL (State-Conditional Adversarial IRL), which builds these two cognitive properties into the planner. Per-depth policies share one reward but differ in how far ahead they sum it explicitly. A state-conditional router mixes
se864fbff8b.summary: SC-AIRL is an inverse reinforcement learning method that models bounded, state-dependent human foresight when inferring reward functions from behavior.
se864fbff8b.why: Offers a modeling approach that better fits real human planning horizons, though the text gives little on practical applications.

s1a8125be1e.title: ConTra: A Training Framework for Effective Contextual Retrieval via Prefix Generation
s1a8125be1e.description: arXiv:2611.34366v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data management systems organize large text collections for tasks such as finding relevant studies and extracting contract clauses. Systems make long documents searchable by splitting them into independently indexed chunks. Chunking can separate text from its identifying details. The indexing challenge is to keep each chunk independently searchable while preserving the context needed to find and rank it. Existing methods either encode that context in chunk vectors or attach it as a text prefix. Context encoded only in vectors is unavailable to text rerankers. Prompted prefixes serve both vector search and reranking, but are costly to generate at indexing time and can underperform contextual encoders. We propose ConTra (Context That Travels)
s1a8125be1e.summary: ConTra is a training framework that improves contextual retrieval by generating text prefixes that keep chunks searchable while preserving document context.
s1a8125be1e.why: Addresses a common RAG problem where chunking strips identifying context, relevant to retrieval pipeline design.

sd1b25a9b29.title: When Skills Fail to Compose: Compatibility and Retention in Language Models
sd1b25a9b29.description: arXiv:2611.34398v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Skill acquisition alone does not establish a reusable skill library: task proficiency does not specify a compositional interface. Motivated by agents that acquire and refine skills, we study independently learned soft-prompt skills on frozen language models, with skill identities and execution order supplied. Across four digit-task bases and three record-editing models, mean composition accuracy in one call is at most 7.6%, compared with 88.2% to 100% over two calls that add computation and an explicit intermediate output. Neutral-insertion training improves robustness but leaves substantial interference, which block length and per-token norm alone cannot explain on two of four digit bases. Blocks of the same operation need not be interchan
sd1b25a9b29.summary: A study finds independently learned soft-prompt skills compose poorly in frozen language models, with one-call composition accuracy at most 7.6%.
sd1b25a9b29.why: Warns that reusable skill libraries built from independently trained soft prompts may not compose reliably without explicit intermediate outputs.

sb27a123d8b.title: SemProxy: Semantic 3D Proxies for Controllable Agentic 3D Modeling
sb27a123d8b.description: arXiv:2611.34414v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Coding agents are increasingly capable of generating 3D models, yet enabling users to effectively control the modeling process remains challenging. Existing workflows rely primarily on text prompts and reference images, which often struggle to convey precise spatial intentions and require iterative corrections. We introduce SemProxy, a lightweight intermediate representation that bridges intuitive human interaction and agentic 3D modeling. Instantiated as labeled 3D bounding boxes, semantic 3D proxies allow users to directly specify object parts and spatial arrangements while leaving geometric details to coding agents. These proxies can be serialized into structured text and rendered as images, making them directly accessible to existing co
sb27a123d8b.summary: SemProxy proposes labeled 3D bounding boxes as an intermediate representation letting users specify object parts and spatial intent for coding agents generating 3D models.
sb27a123d8b.why: Offers a more precise control interface for agentic 3D modeling than text prompts and reference images alone.

s608733b47e.title: CHASE: Curiosity-Guided Skill Acquisition for Embodied Task Execution
s608733b47e.description: arXiv:2611.34416v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots executing tasks in partially observed environments must resolve uncertainty while operating with incomplete skills. Inspired by human curiosity, we investigate how robots can formulate task-relevant hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution. We propose CHASE, a Curiosity-guided Harness for Acquiring Skills from Evidence, which operationalizes curiosity as selecting investigations that resolve task uncertainty and expand executable capabilities. Four modules connect dynamic scene understanding, hypothesis-driven planning, on-demand skill acquisition, and verified execution. The planner balances information value, skill reuse, and acquisition/execution cost. Missing skills trigger bounded exploration,
s608733b47e.summary: CHASE is a curiosity-guided framework that lets robots formulate hypotheses, seek evidence, and acquire missing skills during task execution.
s608733b47e.why: Describes an approach for robots to handle incomplete skills in partially observed environments, though practical details are limited in the text.

se00ebe4c27.title: Calibration of Neuromusculoskeletal Models Using Differentiable Physics: Recommendations for Improving Model Accuracy
se00ebe4c27.description: arXiv:2611.34428v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Differentiable physics has shown potential to usher in a new paradigm in human neuromusculoskeletal (NMS) model calibration. Early results from pioneering works have demonstrated that auto-differentiable NMS models can greatly reduce NMS model calibration time while achieving comparable accuracy compared to traditional calibration methods. The efficient gradient-based optimizers have enabled calibration of increasingly sophisticated human models with a large number of parameters, which seek to narrow the gap between simulation and reality. Several modules have been evaluated separately in different studies, but have never been directly compared within the same study. In this work, these modules are compared on the same differentiable upper
se00ebe4c27.summary: A paper offers recommendations for improving the accuracy of neuromusculoskeletal model calibration using differentiable physics.

s186414e1fe.title: One Representation to Rule Them All -- Open-Vocabulary Change Detection from Text or Visual Examples
s186414e1fe.description: arXiv:2611.34430v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Open-vocabulary change detection (OVCD) aims to localise user-specified changes without retraining for predefined categories. Existing approaches typically rely on textual descriptions and combine separate models for region proposal, semantic recognition, and temporal comparison. This limits how target concepts can be expressed and makes detection dependent on several intermediate predictions. We introduce OVTSID3, a training-free framework that unifies region grouping, concept identification, and temporal comparison in the representation space of DINOv3. OVTSID3 supports two complementary modes of concept specification: zero-shot textual queries or one-shot visual prompting through a masked reference pair. OVTSID3 outperforms all prior tra
s186414e1fe.summary: OVTSID3 is a training-free framework that unifies region grouping, concept identification, and temporal comparison for open-vocabulary change detection from text or visual examples.
s186414e1fe.why: Removes the need for several separate intermediate models in change detection, simplifying detection pipelines.

s741fe5fe41.title: Most of the Way There: Turning a Strong Video Prior into an Action-Conditioned World Model
s741fe5fe41.description: arXiv:2611.34435v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Modern video generators excel at producing visually plausible futures guided by text and image prompts. Yet their emphasis on semantic plausibility does not guarantee fidelity to the physical consequences of specific actions. Action-conditioned world models (ACWMs), in contrast, aim to simulate how the world responds to robot actions, enabling scalable policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts. The challenge is not merely to generate a plausible future, but to predict what follows from a specific physical action. As video priors grow stronger, we ask how little adaptation is truly needed to bridge this gap. We introduce Dianjing, a minimal recipe that preserves and unlocks the capabilities of strong video priors t
s741fe5fe41.summary: Researchers describe turning a strong video generation prior into an action-conditioned world model that simulates how the world responds to specific robot actions.
s741fe5fe41.why: It offers a path to scalable robot policy evaluation and improvement without costly real-world rollouts, though the excerpt gives limited detail on results.

s335348c4a4.title: ProxyGenBench: Benchmarking Proxy-Guided Video Generation
s335348c4a4.description: arXiv:2611.34457v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent video generators produce realistic videos, yet controlling how scenes unfold remains challenging. Structural proxies, such as animated 3D blockouts, guide generation by specifying scene layout, motion, camera behavior, and event order. However, these coarse inputs leave details unspecified and may contain artifacts that should not be reproduced. Successful proxy-guided generation must therefore Preserve intended structure, Complete missing content and correct proxy artifacts, and Bind text, image, and audio conditions to the right entities and events. We introduce ProxyGenBench to study these interacting requirements, with 312 evaluation cases from 60 scenes across three scene tasks and controlled variations in proxy fidelity, text d
s335348c4a4.summary: Researchers introduce ProxyGenBench, a benchmark for video generation guided by structural proxies such as animated 3D blockouts.
s335348c4a4.why: It gives teams a standard way to test whether generators preserve layout and motion intent while fixing proxy artifacts and binding text, image, and audio conditions.

sfdb0942993.title: Noise threshold for learning with quantum memory
sfdb0942993.description: arXiv:2611.34474v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A quantum memory can reduce exponentially the number of experiments needed to learn a physical process, but real memories are noisy. Here we show that, for Pauli memory noise with eigenvalues $\lambda_X,\lambda_Y,\lambda_Z$, the advantage is governed by $\lambda_X^2+\lambda_Y^2+\lambda_Z^2$. We prove that no protocol with an entangled probe gains an exponential advantage when this sum is at most one, reduce the general case to the additivity of a R\'enyi-2 coherent information, and find coded memories that retain a growing advantage within 1% of this threshold. On a superconducting processor, nine simultaneously operated Bell pairs show an advantage that grows or shrinks exponentially with system size, reversing where a parameter-free model
sfdb0942993.summary: A paper shows that for Pauli memory noise, quantum memory's learning advantage depends on a sum of squared eigenvalues, with a noise threshold for exponential gains.
sfdb0942993.why: It clarifies noise limits for quantum learning hardware, though its direct relevance to most engineering teams is limited.

sb4c7e9e8c5.title: Angular Interpolation in Sparse-View Low-Dose CT Reconstruction: Placement Effects and Data-Consistency Step-Size Scaling
sb4c7e9e8c5.description: arXiv:2611.34508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Dual-domain networks combine projection and image processing for sparse-view low-dose computed tomography (CT). We quantify the contribution of angular interpolation before learning and distinguish its roles in sinogram initialisation and the image residual base. On synthetic parallel-beam data, parameter-free interpolation reduces noise-free missing-view mean absolute error by 99.7% relative to zero filling at 60 views. Full-view filtered back-projection (FBP) of the jointly learned completed sinogram adds 1.27 dB of peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) over interpolated FBP. In a data-consistency dual-domain network (DC-DuNet), a 2x2 configuration ablation controls branch width, depth and training schedule while varying these placements and
sb4c7e9e8c5.summary: A study on sparse-view low-dose CT reconstruction examines how angular interpolation placement and data-consistency step sizes affect dual-domain network performance.
sb4c7e9e8c5.why: It offers practical guidance for preprocessing choices in medical imaging reconstruction pipelines, based on synthetic parallel-beam data.

s3dcc35405b.title: Long-Horizon Planning with Latent World Models via Graph Anchors
s3dcc35405b.description: arXiv:2611.34509v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Latent world models plan in a compact latent space by predicting the outcomes of actions. Their planners judge a plan by the latent distance between its predicted end state and the goal image. We show that this distance fails in two distinct ways. First, it loses directional signal a few steps from the goal, causing distant goals to fail. Second, it weighs the robot arm over the manipulated object, causing manipulation to fail at contact. We measure both failures directly on recorded data by asking whether a lower latent distance corresponds to true progress toward the goal. Across five environments, six visual representations (including raw pixels and V-JEPA 2), and nine Meta-World tasks, this ranking test cleanly separates the two failure
s3dcc35405b.summary: Researchers propose graph anchors to improve long-horizon planning with latent world models, addressing failures of latent distance as a planning metric.
s3dcc35405b.why: It identifies specific failure modes of latent-distance planners in robotics, which matter for teams building model-based manipulation systems.

s5b000b15ae.title: PURA: Video Token Pruning via Unified Spatiotemporal Redundancy Assessment
s5b000b15ae.description: arXiv:2611.34521v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video large language models incur substantial inference costs from long visual token sequences. Existing video token compression methods mitigate these costs by exploiting spatial redundancy within frames and temporal redundancy across frames. However, many approaches impose predefined processing orders or fixed allocation ratios for spatial and temporal compression, limiting their ability to adapt to the varying balance of spatiotemporal redundancy across videos. To address this limitation, we propose PURA, a training-free method that prunes visual tokens through unified spatiotemporal redundancy assessment. For each token, PURA constructs spatial and temporal reference candidates and selects the reference with the lowest representation er
s5b000b15ae.summary: PURA is a training-free method that prunes video tokens by jointly assessing spatial and temporal redundancy in video large language models.
s5b000b15ae.why: Reducing long visual token sequences without retraining can lower inference costs for video LLM deployments.

sb84b98fb6f.title: EPPC-CARE: Staged Hierarchical Annotation of Communication Behaviors in Secure Patient-Provider Messages
sb84b98fb6f.description: arXiv:2611.34539v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Objectives: Patient portal messages provide invaluable information about communication dynamics between patients and healthcare providers, but extracting it manually is labor-intensive. We developed and evaluated EPPC-CARE, an automated framework for identifying communication behaviors together with the supporting text for each classification. Materials and Methods: From 867 messages, we obtained 5,516 reference standard annotations. Each annotation is a triplet of communication-related text (span), a broader communication category (Code), and a specific subcategory (Sub-code). We evaluated EPPC-CARE's identified triplets across six open-weight large language models (LLMs) against supervised fine-tuning and communication-based models such a
sb84b98fb6f.summary: EPPC-CARE is an automated framework for annotating communication behaviors in secure patient-provider portal messages, evaluated on 867 messages.
sb84b98fb6f.why: It shows how automated annotation can reduce manual labor in analyzing clinical messaging, relevant to health-tech builders.

s4425bb71eb.title: HAS: Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling for Video Understanding
s4425bb71eb.description: arXiv:2611.34544v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Due to context-length constraints, most MLLMs cannot process full-length videos and therefore rely on sampling a subset of frames as input. However, existing sampling methods, ranging from uniform sampling to relevance-based selection, are often driven by a single sampling principle and thus struggle to accommodate the heterogeneous evidential requirements of different queries: some demand a holistic understanding of how the video unfolds over time, while others hinge on fine-grained events within a short temporal window. To address this limitation, we propose \textbf{Hierarchical Adaptive Frame Sampling (HAS)}, a two-stage frame sampling framework. In the first stage, \emph{Backbone Frame Construction}, we apply a Determinantal Point Proce
s4425bb71eb.summary: HAS is a hierarchical adaptive frame sampling method that helps multimodal LLMs choose video frames for queries needing either holistic or fine-grained understanding.
s4425bb71eb.why: Better frame selection can improve video understanding accuracy within fixed context-length limits.

se09b8ca673.title: Recalling the Past to Answer the Present: Context-Aware Multi-Evidence Reasoning for Streaming Video Question Answering
se09b8ca673.description: arXiv:2611.34545v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved remarkable progress in video understanding, yet existing video question answering (VQA) benchmarks mainly evaluate models in offline settings. Real-world streaming scenarios instead require models to answer context-dependent queries by retrieving and reasoning over evidence distributed across the video history. We introduce StreamRecall, a benchmark for context-aware Multi evidence reasoning in streaming video QA. StreamRecall requires models to retrieve, associate, and reason over temporally scattered evidence to answer queries at the appropriate moment. It contains 4,983 questions over 462 videos, with context-aligned query times and fine-grained temporal evidence annotations. We further propose
se09b8ca673.summary: StreamRecall is a benchmark testing vision-language models on answering context-dependent questions over temporally scattered evidence in streaming video.
se09b8ca673.why: It exposes limits of current offline-evaluated video QA models in real-time streaming scenarios that product teams may target.

se07a38b9a6.title: An Information-Theoretic Analysis of Information Hiding in Semantic Communication
se07a38b9a6.description: arXiv:2611.34550v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Semantic communication shifts the transmission goal from the accurate recovery of syntactic symbols to the reliable conveyance of semantic content, yet a systematic information-theoretic characterization of information hiding at the semantic layer is still missing. Building on the semantic information theory of Niu-Zhang and the classical information hiding theory of Moulin-O'Sullivan, this paper establishes an information-theoretic framework for information hiding under semantic communication. The classical hiding model is extended to a two-layer structure (semantic host, syntactic host, syntactic composite signal, syntactic received, semantic received) bridged by synonymous mappings f_s, f_x and the inverse mapping f_y^{-1}, subject to fo
se07a38b9a6.summary: The paper develops an information-theoretic framework for information hiding within semantic communication, extending classical hiding models to a semantic layer.
se07a38b9a6.why: The text gives little on practical implications; it is primarily theoretical work on semantic communication security.

s09d9e4445e.title: Sage-Med: Scaling Medical Multimodal Intelligence
s09d9e4445e.description: arXiv:2611.34575v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Establishing effective scaling laws for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) remains a persistent and fundamental challenge. Our systematic evaluation shows that existing medical MLLMs tend to underperform frontier general-purpose MLLMs across a range of medical tasks, while scaling model size primarily improves text capabilities rather than multimodal perception, and enabling reasoning modes fails to close this visual gap. To investigate how medical multimodal intelligence scales in practice, we introduce Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model with 3B activated parameters, built by combining stage-specific curation over 322.7 million candidate records with a progressive training curriculum spanning medical p
s09d9e4445e.summary: Sage-Med-Preview, a 35B-parameter medical multimodal model, is introduced alongside findings that scaling mainly improves text rather than visual capabilities.
s09d9e4445e.why: The finding that medical MLLMs trail general models on visual tasks and scaling doesn't fix this is useful for healthcare AI planning.

s53d046c3df.title: Tune for Retention, Not Just Gain: SFT Forgets Far Less than You Think
s53d046c3df.description: arXiv:2611.34579v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Catastrophic forgetting, the drastic loss of previously acquired capabilities when learning new ones, is a central challenge in language model fine-tuning. Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely believed to be prone to such forgetting. Recent works have attributed this to the off-policy nature of SFT, arguing that on-policy learning is key to continual learning. In this paper, we challenge this premise. We show that while maximizing new-task performance can induce catastrophic forgetting, alternative hyperparameter choices (lower learning rate and batch size) can yield similar gains with little to no forgetting. With hyperparameters selected jointly for gain and retention, vanilla SFT retains prior capabilities far better than previously su
s53d046c3df.summary: The paper argues that supervised fine-tuning forgets far less than assumed when hyperparameters such as lower learning rates are chosen for retention.
s53d046c3df.why: Teams fine-tuning LLMs can reduce catastrophic forgetting through hyperparameter choices rather than switching to on-policy methods.

s3f48f913d3.title: VisualMontage: Manipulating the Beliefs of Vision-Language Agents with Authentic Image Sequences
s3f48f913d3.description: arXiv:2611.34603v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: As agents based on vision-language models (VLMs) increasingly interpret social-media content, errors in their analysis may lend credibility to rumors and amplify their spread. In this paper, we study the problem of visual cognitive collusion, in which coordinated posts combine authentic images and locally faithful captions to induce VLM agents to infer and accept attacker-chosen target claims through their own reasoning. To enable systematic evaluation of this cognitive threat, we introduce a new benchmark comprising 544 target cases and 33.2K candidate images across eight application domains. We further propose VisualMontage, a multi-agent framework for simulating such attacks through narrative planning, image selection and ordering, and c
s3f48f913d3.summary: VisualMontage introduces a benchmark of 544 target cases showing how coordinated posts with authentic images and faithful captions can steer vision-language agents toward attacker-chosen claims.
s3f48f913d3.why: It highlights a manipulation risk for VLM agents that interpret social media, relevant to anyone deploying agents on untrusted content.

sdedee37d8b.title: From Models to Services: Systematizing Security Assurance for Model-as-a-Service
sdedee37d8b.description: arXiv:2611.34623v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models are mainly delivered as cloud services, in which the assets of different principals are coupled within a single service pipeline, while the related security research is scattered across several fields with differing threat models. This paper systematizes this research from a service perspective. We decompose Model-as-a-Service (MaaS) into a five-layer stack and five trust boundaries, define six adversary classes and six security goals, use them to code 120 studies, and evaluate 50 defenses under a unified set of criteria. The results show that 44.2% of the studies concentrate on behavioral integrity, while service integrity, availability and cost, and accountability together account for only 13.3%. Defenses are evaluat
sdedee37d8b.summary: A paper systematizes security research for Model-as-a-Service, decomposing it into five layers and trust boundaries and evaluating 50 defenses across 120 studies.
sdedee37d8b.why: It offers a structured threat model for teams securing cloud-hosted LLM services and choosing defenses.

sebbeb8961e.title: DecisionReplay: A Corpus and Offline Simulator for Ensembling Decision Models
sebbeb8961e.description: arXiv:2611.34627v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Comparing ensembles, routers and cascades requires the output of every model on every item, and its cost. Stored collections built for routing keep no per-option probabilities. We provide a dataset on which ensemble methods, routers and cascades are simulated quickly, without new model calls. DecisionReplay holds the probability vectors of 17 commercial decision models, endpoints that return a probability for every answer option, on 35 benchmarks, with the token counts, billed cost and measured latency of every call, all released. A deterministic simulator replays any policy that selects, combines or cascades them. One well-chosen model per benchmark is hard to beat: pooling all models loses 2.7 accuracy points to it, and stacking gains 1.0
sebbeb8961e.summary: DecisionReplay releases a corpus of probability vectors from 17 commercial decision models across 35 benchmarks, with cost and latency data, for offline simulation.
sebbeb8961e.why: Engineers can simulate ensembles, routers, and cascades offline without new model calls, cutting evaluation cost.

sf85e4c385f.title: LatentRL-QAS: Transfer via Latent Reinforcement Learning for Quantum Architecture Search
sf85e4c385f.description: arXiv:2611.34634v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) emerges as a prominent approach to quantum architecture search (QAS), the automated design of quantum circuits. However, transferring what an agent has learned from one number of qubits to another is still weakly explored: the state, the action space and the neural network of a state-of-the-art RL-QAS agent all grow with the number of qubits, which makes transfer learning across qubit counts prohibitive. We make this transfer possible by introducing LatentRL-QAS, a latent space transfer and refresh framework for RL-based QAS. At its core, a circuit variational autoencoder encodes a circuit as one token per gate and maps circuits on any number of qubits into the same latent space. An RL agent navigates this space
sf85e4c385f.summary: Researchers introduced LatentRL-QAS, a latent-space framework that lets reinforcement learning agents for quantum architecture search transfer learning across different qubit counts.
sf85e4c385f.why: Transfer across qubit counts could cut the cost of automated quantum circuit design, though the impact is limited to quantum computing research.

s5a23c7b4b6.title: Carrying Feature Ablations Across Sparse Autoencoder Seeds
s5a23c7b4b6.description: arXiv:2611.34637v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A vision encoder turns an image into one vector per patch, refined layer by layer. A sparse autoencoder (SAE) writes each vector of one layer as a sum of learned directions, most with a coefficient of zero. Researchers call each direction a feature and edit the encoder by removing one feature. An SAE trained from another random seed learns different features. Earlier work matches the two SAEs' features one to one by how closely their directions agree. Matched features can point alike yet respond to different image parts, so removing them may change the encoder differently. We remove a feature and, separately, its match, then compare the changes in the encoder's output on the same held out images. When the second change nearly reproduces the
s5a23c7b4b6.summary: Researchers study how to carry feature ablations from one sparse autoencoder trained with a given random seed to another, since SAEs with different seeds learn different features.
s5a23c7b4b6.why: Feature matching across SAE seeds affects whether interpretability edits to vision encoders transfer reliably, which matters for model editing workflows.

sdfbbf95c62.title: Motion Beyond Pixels: Learning Future Visual Representations for Object-Centric Dynamics
sdfbbf95c62.description: arXiv:2611.34644v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Many embodied world models predict future states in latent spaces optimized for RGB reconstruction, which do not explicitly prioritize object-level semantics and geometry relevant to motion generation. We present MotionRep, a visual representation world model that jointly generates future DINO representations and 3D object flow, coupling semantic and geometric information with object-centric dynamics. To make high-dimensional DINO features amenable to generative modeling, we introduce DINO-VAE, which combines temporal and channel compression with latent regularization to produce compact latents while preserving semantic and geometric information. Conditioned on an initial observation, object query points, and a language instruction, a unifi
sdfbbf95c62.summary: Researchers present MotionRep, a world model that jointly predicts future DINO visual representations and 3D object flow for object-centric dynamics in embodied settings.
sdfbbf95c62.why: Predicting semantic and geometric features rather than raw RGB may help robots plan motion, though the text gives little on practical deployment.

sb9fae07814.title: Do We Still Need Reinforcement Learning When We Can Read the World Model?
sb9fae07814.description: arXiv:2611.34656v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Reinforcement learning has achieved remarkable success in sequential decision-making, but learning effective policies often requires substantial interaction experience. Model-based reinforcement learning alleviates this dependence by leveraging world models, which are typically used to support planning or policy optimization. In this paper, we investigate an alternative paradigm in which autonomous LLM-based coding agents directly synthesize control policies by reasoning over readable world models. By examining environment source code, these agents translate environmental knowledge into executable decision rules and iteratively refine their policies using online feedback or offline data, without task-specific RL training. Experiments across
sb9fae07814.summary: The paper explores having LLM-based coding agents write control policies directly by reasoning over readable world models and environment source code, bypassing conventional reinforcement learning.
sb9fae07814.why: If coding agents can derive policies from readable world models, teams could reduce interaction data needs, but the text gives limited evidence of performance.

s4f25bdf364.title: Multi-Party Authorization of Maintenance Prescriptions on a Permissioned Blockchain
s4f25bdf364.description: arXiv:2611.34662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In industrial prescriptive maintenance, an equipment supplier's model may recommend an intervention that a plant schedules, a contractor executes, and a quality or safety function approves. A shared ledger records who submitted the prescription, yet cannot check whether the agreed model and decision rule produced it. We require permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify a succinct proof of that calculation before releasing a work order. On a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric testbed using a public engine benchmark, this stopped all nine contested or mis-operated prescriptions, whereas hash checks accepted four that either raised simulated maintenance cost or reintroduced late failures.
s4f25bdf364.summary: Researchers propose requiring permissioned-blockchain endorsers to verify succinct proofs of model calculations before approving maintenance prescriptions, tested on a four-organization Hyperledger Fabric setup.
s4f25bdf364.why: Verifiable proofs could let multi-party industrial workflows confirm that recommendations actually came from the agreed model and decision rule.

saa05e66da8.title: DemoFoundry: Toward Scalable Photorealistic Robot Data with Coding Agents and Generative Rendering
saa05e66da8.description: arXiv:2611.34671v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Scaling robot learning requires demonstrations that combine realistic visual observations with reliable action supervision. Simulation-based synthesis faces a substantial visual gap relative to real environments, while video-only generation struggles to maintain physically consistent interactions and provide aligned action labels. We present DemoFoundry, an automated framework that couples coding agents with generative rendering to synthesize photorealistic and physically grounded robot demonstrations. Coding agents both construct aligned real--proxy video pairs from existing robot episodes to train a video renderer and write executable interaction programs to generate new demonstrations. Given a scene reference and task instruction, an age
saa05e66da8.summary: DemoFoundry couples coding agents with generative rendering to automatically synthesize photorealistic, physically grounded robot demonstrations with aligned action labels.
saa05e66da8.why: Automated generation of realistic robot training data could reduce the cost of scaling robot learning beyond human demonstrations.

s397e5bf7d9.title: RoboEvo$^2$: Recursive Robot Self-Improvement via Harness-Policy Co-Evolution
s397e5bf7d9.description: arXiv:2611.34675v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Robots should adapt to unfamiliar environments and acquire new skills through interaction, then execute those skills efficiently with practice. Vision-language-action policies provide efficient control, but often need additional human demonstrations to handle unfamiliar settings; reasoning agents can discover solutions using broad prior knowledge and robot-control APIs, but repeated deliberation and repair are costly. Inspired by human learning through reasoning and practice, we propose RoboEvo$^2$, a framework for recursive harness-policy co-evolution. In Policy-to-Harness (P2H) evolution, policy failures guide a coding agent to search complementary Code, Code+ICL, and Code+Policy routes, consolidating verified solutions into reusable skil
s397e5bf7d9.summary: RoboEvo² proposes a framework where robot reasoning agents and vision-language-action policies co-evolve recursively, so robots improve skills through interaction and practice.
s397e5bf7d9.why: Co-evolving reasoning agents and control policies could reduce reliance on human demonstrations for robots in unfamiliar settings.

s2f3fc3de1f.title: Find the Clue, Not the Scene: Rethinking Reasoning for Entity Recognition in Vision-Language Models
s2f3fc3de1f.description: arXiv:2611.34681v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Answering a knowledge-based visual question requires first recognizing the entity in the image and then recalling knowledge about it. Thinking vision-language models (VLMs) reason for thousands of tokens before answering, yet it remains underexplored how well such thinking VLMs perform each of these two steps. We therefore analyze thinking VLMs on this task and make two key observations. (1) Recognition is the bottleneck, since 76.3% of errors across four models on ViQuAE stem from misrecognizing the entity, and 84.9% of these failures are resolved once the entity name is provided in the question. (2) Recognition is driven by entity-recall clues rather than by general descriptions of the image. An entity-recall clue is a distinctive visual
s2f3fc3de1f.summary: Analysis of thinking vision-language models finds that entity recognition is the main bottleneck in knowledge-based visual question answering, accounting for 76.3% of errors.
s2f3fc3de1f.why: Recognition, not reasoning, drives most errors, suggesting teams should focus on visual grounding when building VLM-based QA systems.

s7bb39f3924.title: Evacuation Traffic Prediction for Dynamic Transportation Networks over Multiple Hurricanes: A Generalized Graph Learning Approach
s7bb39f3924.description: arXiv:2611.34687v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High traffic demand during hurricane evacuations causes severe congestion on major highways, leading to delays and safety risks for evacuees. Predicting evacuation traffic in real-time can significantly enhance evacuation management efforts. However, evacuation traffic is highly dynamic and uncertain due to evolving hurricane characteristics and diverse population response. Each hurricane has unique characteristics and evacuation contexts, resulting in different spatial-temporal traffic patterns. Moreover, the structure of detector-based transportation networks varies across multiple hurricanes. Hence, a model trained on the data from one hurricane may not generalize well for others. This study proposes a generalized dynamic graph learning
s7bb39f3924.summary: Researchers propose a generalized graph learning approach to predict evacuation traffic on highways across multiple hurricanes using detector-based transportation network data.
s7bb39f3924.why: The text gives limited detail on results, so its relevance for engineers is unclear beyond transportation forecasting use cases.

sd8155ccb00.title: Maco-RL: Scaling Agent Capabilities with Mixed-Task Reinforcement Learning
sd8155ccb00.description: arXiv:2611.34703v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Mixed-task reinforcement learning (MixRL) directly trains a unified policy across domains to continually expand agent capabilities without training separate specialists or requiring an extra distillation stage. Despite its appeal, scaling MixRL poses significant challenges in achieving stable and efficient mixed-task learning, effectively allocating rollout compute, and supporting continual domain expansion. To address these challenges, we propose Maco-RL, an approach that effectively scales MixRL. Specifically, Maco-RL employs a quota-based scheduler for asynchronous rollouts across multiple task domains, thereby stabilizing training by balancing gradient contributions and mitigating off-policy effects. Along an orthogonal axis, Maco-RL fu
sd8155ccb00.summary: Maco-RL proposes a method to scale mixed-task reinforcement learning, training a unified agent policy across domains with quota-based scheduling and continual domain expansion.
sd8155ccb00.why: Training one policy across multiple task domains without separate specialists or distillation could simplify agent training pipelines.

sd53ed3dac4.title: When the Proxy Is Wrong: Mismatch-Corrected Bandits for Adaptive Data Sampling
sd53ed3dac4.description: arXiv:2611.34707v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Data allocation methods often use a small proxy model to select training data for a larger target model. However, this proxy can rank data differently from the target, leading to suboptimal training performance. To address this problem, we model the mismatch between the proxy and target models and incorporate it into the allocation decision. To do so, the problem is cast as a multi-fidelity bandit, where each arm is a data intervention. The proxy reward is observed every round, whereas the target reward is revealed only on rare audits of the same update. These paired observations identify arm-wise mismatches without assuming a shared offset or preservation of rankings. Mismatch-corrected bandits correct the proxy with paired residuals, audi
sd53ed3dac4.summary: Researchers model the mismatch between small proxy models and larger target models as a multi-fidelity bandit for adaptive training data selection.
sd53ed3dac4.why: Correcting for proxy-target ranking mismatch could improve data selection efficiency when small models guide training of larger ones.

s259547581b.title: How Well Do Vision-Language Scene Graphs Serve as Memory for Embodied Question Answering?
s259547581b.description: arXiv:2611.34745v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Embodied QA needs memory, but answer accuracy mixes retained evidence, reading errors and question priors. For a simulated multi-room scene-graph pipeline we define answerability: the fraction of questions a fixed rule-based reader answers correctly from the graph alone. The baseline recovers 24.1% of visible object types and its room labels flicker. Four targeted repairs double recall, raise answerability from 27.2% to 37.4%, and improve retrained QA from 71.4% to 75.9%, yet better object F1 can lower answerability. A question-type prior beats this reader on every predicted graph. In one real-video test, graph memory lowers accuracy. These exploratory findings favour scoring retained evidence alongside accuracy.
s259547581b.summary: A study defines answerability for vision-language scene graphs used as memory in embodied question answering, showing targeted repairs raise answerability from 27.2% to 37.4%.
s259547581b.why: Better object recall does not always improve answerability, so teams building graph-based memory should measure answer utility directly.

s77ac846f97.title: Collect for Coverage, Replay with Evidence: Adaptive and Efficient On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents
s77ac846f97.description: arXiv:2611.34756v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Fully online on-policy distillation (OPD) is costly for long-horizon agents because each update depends on fresh environment rollouts. Prefix replay offers an efficient alternative by sampling current-student responses from stored histories, reducing idle time for long-tail rollouts and allowing each collected trajectory to support multiple updates. However, our analysis of the complete prefix replay pipeline identifies two limitations in long-horizon settings. In trajectory collection, teacher-only trajectories miss student-induced histories, while broader history coverage can reduce teacher reliability. In trajectory reuse, fixed position-based schedules cannot identify critical decisions that may occur at any trajectory depth. We introdu
s77ac846f97.summary: Researchers propose an adaptive method for on-policy distillation in long-horizon agents that reuses stored prefix histories to reduce costly fresh environment rollouts.
s77ac846f97.why: Reducing rollout costs for long-horizon agent training could make distillation practical for teams with limited environment compute.

sc90513705f.title: Reading Fine-Tuning Diffs Through Lenses: Model Diffing for Backdoor Detection
sc90513705f.description: arXiv:2611.34758v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a common scoring system based on token readouts to evaluate weight, activation and output-based model diffing methods for backdoor detection in fine-tuning processes. We also improve existing weight and activation based methods by incorporating the $J$-lens and its refinement, the $J{+}{+}$-lens. We test our setup in experiments where we compare a backdoored model with the base model from which it was fine-tuned. Our results show that incorporating the $J{+}{+}$-lens improves the weight-based method in all our settings, while the $J$-lens improves its ranks within single layers. The strongest single method is $\Delta W J{+}{+}$, the weight difference decoded through the $J{+}{+}$-lens of the base model, which ranks a token nami
sc90513705f.summary: Researchers introduce a scoring system based on token readouts to compare weight, activation, and output-based model diffing methods for detecting backdoors in fine-tuned models.
sc90513705f.why: Standardized comparison of diffing methods gives security teams a clearer basis for checking whether fine-tuning introduced a backdoor.

s2afc837aa8.title: One Model, Many Modes: Evolving System Prompt Ensembles for Creative Generation
s2afc837aa8.description: arXiv:2611.34760v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Preference-aligned LLMs can exhibit mode collapse, concentrating their output distributions around a narrow set of high-reward responses. This limits creative generation, which requires quality, novelty, and diversity. Existing test-time methods often emphasize diversity, giving less attention to whether individual responses are both high-quality and novel. This distinction matters in practical use, where users may seek a single compelling, original response. We formalize creative generation as a multi-objective distributional optimization problem and introduce SEPO, a training-free framework for System Prompt Ensemble Optimization. The framework combines prompt evolution with greedy max-min selection to identify behaviorally distinct syste
