s2afc837aa8.summary: Researchers formalize creative generation as a multi-objective optimization and propose evolving system prompt ensembles to produce responses that are both high-quality and novel.
s2afc837aa8.why: Ensembles of system prompts could help teams counter mode collapse in aligned LLMs when they need diverse, original outputs.

s73fa4f721e.title: InterConRank: Joint Node Centrality in Interconnected Heterogeneous Networks
s73fa4f721e.description: arXiv:2611.34763v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Two nodes with identical connections within their own layer can differ in importance if their neighbors in another layer occupy different positions in the network. We introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that computes a separate node ranking for each layer of an interconnected network. Directed dependencies specify which layers supply scores to each receiving layer. InterConRank normalizes each type of link separately and updates all layers together, so a score can cross into a layer in one iteration and propagate along its internal links in the next. We prove convergence of this joint update and evaluate the resulting rankings on four scholarly networks. On all four networks, InterConRank gives the highest rank correlations with
s73fa4f721e.summary: Researchers introduce InterConRank, a centrality algorithm that ranks nodes separately in each layer of interconnected heterogeneous networks, letting cross-layer neighbors shift scores.
s73fa4f721e.why: Offers a way to rank node importance in multi-layer graphs where same-layer connections alone miss cross-layer influence.

sedfbdcb3eb.title: Make the Adversary Spend More: Stateful Deception as a Cost-Exchange Primitive for AI-Era Cyber Defense
sedfbdcb3eb.description: arXiv:2611.34770v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are transforming the economics of intrusion by reducing the attacker's cost to scan and adapt, while tempting defenders into unbounded compute. We argue that cyber deception should be judged by the cost exchange it imposes, not by realism or detection, and that the primitive making that exchange favorable is adversary-specific persistent state. Rather than a honeypot that resets or merges sessions, each recognized adversary re-enters the world it believes it has compromised, kept coherent with its own past actions and isolated from every other adversary, while the language model acts only as a constrained renderer of explicit state, never as its store. We formalize the trade-off as a Deception Exchange Rate (DER
sedfbdcb3eb.summary: Researchers propose stateful cyber deception that keeps each recognized adversary in a persistent, coherent fake environment to raise attackers' costs.
sedfbdcb3eb.why: Suggests defenders can judge deception by cost imposed on LLM-enabled attackers rather than realism or detection rates.

s73a6964aff.title: When Every Rollout Fails: Splicing Learner-Conditioned Options into Long-Horizon Agent RL
s73a6964aff.description: arXiv:2611.34777v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Group-based reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards often yields all-fail groups on long-horizon agent tasks: every sampled trajectory receives zero reward, leaving group-relative methods without a reward-based policy gradient. A common remedy supplies complete solutions from a stronger model, but full trajectories are expensive and expose the learner to long off-policy histories. We introduce SPLICE, which constructs local training targets from failed current-policy trajectories online. For each all-fail group, a proposal model selects a splice point in a current-policy trajectory and generates several bounded options from that point. We estimate each option's value using repeated current-policy continuations, convert positive estim
s73a6964aff.summary: SPLICE constructs local training targets from failed policy trajectories online, helping group-based RL on long-horizon agent tasks where every rollout fails.
s73a6964aff.why: Addresses zero-gradient failure in RL for long-horizon agents without relying on expensive full expert trajectories.

s489801fe9a.title: PersonaFactory: Stylistic User Prompt Augmentation with Synthetic Persona Bank
s489801fe9a.description: arXiv:2611.34785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large language models increasingly replace real people in the AI development pipeline, as they are used to generate training dialogues at scale and to drive alignment and evaluation. However, out-of-the-box models produce monolingual and stylistically flat texts as synthetic user prompts, failing to replicate the real user-AI communication mechanics. We present PersonaFactory, an end-to-end pipeline that generates detailed user personas and uses them to augment existing user prompts from their point of view, producing a bank of over 740000 structured synthetic personas detailing their background and communication behaviors, and a corpus of roughly 1.24 million persona-styled synthetic conversations spanning 85 languages. We evaluate the eff
s489801fe9a.summary: PersonaFactory is a pipeline that generates synthetic user personas to augment prompts, producing a bank of over 740,000 stylistically varied user prompts.
s489801fe9a.why: Could improve synthetic training and evaluation data that currently sounds monolingual and stylistically flat.

s1e213fee8e.title: HOG-WAM: Improving Visual Robustness through Future Gradient Prediction
s1e213fee8e.description: arXiv:2611.34811v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World-action models jointly predict future observations and actions, yet visual corruption can disrupt the resulting policies. We introduce HOG-WAM, which adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients (HOG) as structural supervision derived directly from demonstration images. An auxiliary HOG diffusion transformer (DiT) module reads RGB features through asymmetric attention, allowing its objective to shape the visual representation used for control. The module is used only during training and removed at inference, preserving FastWAM's RGB-to-action architecture. We evaluate four controlled observation corruptions through a visual-corruption extension of RoboTwin, termed RoboTwin-Plus; HOG-WAM achieves the highest success among the compared p
s1e213fee8e.summary: HOG-WAM adds future Histograms of Oriented Gradients as training-only supervision to world-action models to improve policy robustness against visual corruption.
s1e213fee8e.why: Offers a training-time fix for robot policies failing under visual corruption, with no added inference cost.

s86b16d1b32.title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
s86b16d1b32.description: arXiv:2611.34813v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video generation models are increasingly evaluated as visual reasoners: given a first frame and a natural-language prompt, can the model produce the video in which the specified task is carried out? The paradigm is considered advantageous because the reasoning is native to the visual medium, unfolding directly in the frames rather than through language or code. Whether this native route is in fact the more reliable path to visual reasoning has not been tested against a symbolic alternative under the same conditions. We therefore pose the same tasks, with identical inputs, output specification and evaluator, to both media: rather than denoising pixels, a coding agent writes a program that renders the answer video, which an unmodified rule-ba
s86b16d1b32.summary: A study compares coding agents against video generation models on visual reasoning tasks under matched conditions, finding code-based solving stronger.
s86b16d1b32.why: Suggests symbolic code execution may be more reliable than video generation for visual reasoning tasks.

s647e74c303.title: Transferring Architecture as an Optimization Prior
s647e74c303.description: arXiv:2611.34816v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Initialization determines the optimization "fate" of a model, going far beyond just setting the scale of its weights. It establishes a fundamental initial geometry over the input data, dictating certain aspects such as which examples are considered close and which representations gradient descent will naturally refine first. In this paper, we view the initial geometry of a network as an optimization prior and ask whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a completely different architecture. To investigate this question, we use an initialization procedure where a target network is aligned to the representational geometry of a randomly initialized guide network before any downstream training occurs. Crucially, alignme
s647e74c303.summary: The paper investigates whether a network can change its optimization prior by referencing a different architecture during initialization.
s647e74c303.why: Explores how initialization geometry shapes training, a question relevant to model design and training efficiency.

sb9c51e53f2.title: Not all world models can doubt: how training objective and architecture shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models
sb9c51e53f2.description: arXiv:2611.34830v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: World models predict how an environment responds to actions, so that candidate actions can be evaluated before execution. Executed actions, or decisions, taken in this manner are only as reliable as the model's predictive capabilities, and predictions in turn are only reliable within the model's experience. Epistemic uncertainty (EU) is the signal that marks where that experience ends. In this work we offer an extensive empirical study on how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty of world models. More precisely, we present a controlled comparison of post-hoc EU (last-layer Laplace and ensembles) between two dominant models of different paradigms: 1) LeWorldModel (LeWM): A joint-embedding predictive architecture (
sb9c51e53f2.summary: An empirical study examines how training objectives and architectures shape epistemic uncertainty in JEPA and RSSM world models.
sb9c51e53f2.why: Helps teams choose world model architectures and objectives based on how reliably they signal unfamiliar situations.

sb9ca720819.title: Probing Visual Idiosyncrasies in Text-to-Image Models
sb9ca720819.description: arXiv:2611.34843v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Text-to-Image (T2I) models turn short text descriptions into images, and the leading models now produce images of comparable visual quality. Whether their outputs still carry model-specific characteristics matters for attribution, for model comparison beyond aggregate quality, and for evaluations that assume anonymity. We ask whether images from frontier T2I models can still be classified by source, and which visual properties make this possible. Here we show that a standard ResNet-50 identifies the source of an image among HiDream-O1-Dev, FLUX.2-dev, HunyuanImage-3.0, and Qwen-Image-2512, the four highest-ranked open-source models on the Text-to-Image Arena, with 100.00% accuracy on held-out prompts. Human participants reach only 62.61% on
sb9ca720819.summary: Researchers show a standard ResNet-50 can identify which frontier text-to-image model produced an image, indicating models retain distinct visual signatures.
sb9ca720819.why: Relevant to attribution and to evaluations that assume anonymity of model outputs.

s38d96de02c.title: DRBench Pro: A Knowledge-Centric Benchmark for Professional Deep Research Agents
s38d96de02c.description: arXiv:2611.34852v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Deep research agents gather information from multiple sources and synthesize it into reports on complex, open-ended questions. Existing benchmarks assess report quality along several dimensions, but lack a dedicated knowledge-centric evaluation of which research directions a report covers and how deeply it explores them. We introduce DRBench Pro, a benchmark that makes structured knowledge coverage the primary evaluation target. Our automated pipeline builds local knowledge trees from Wikipedia and uses sampled subgraphs to generate research queries and evidence-grounded rubrics. Each rubric corresponds to a relation in the tree, preserving the structure of the knowledge being evaluated. Agents receive only the research query. This structur
s38d96de02c.summary: DRBench Pro is a benchmark that evaluates deep research agents primarily on structured knowledge coverage, built from Wikipedia-derived knowledge trees.
s38d96de02c.why: Gives teams a knowledge-coverage metric for evaluating research agents beyond overall report quality.

sdf932a8f5b.title: From Prediction to Decision: Decision-Focused Fine-Tuning of Autoregressive Tabular Transformers for Cost-Sensitive Financial Events
sdf932a8f5b.description: arXiv:2611.34858v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Autoregressive transformers trained on tokenized tabular event streams are a simple and strong baseline for predicting financial events such as fraud. Yet institutions do not act on probabilities; they act on decisions whose consequences are asymmetric and heteroscedastic: the cost of a missed high-value fraud and that of a wrongly declined small purchase are not the same. The standard bridge is post-hoc Bayes-optimal thresholding of calibrated probabilities under a cost matrix. We ask whether fine-tuning the model to the decision objective can do better. We fine-tune the same pretrained model so that its restricted softmax over label tokens (already a distribution over business actions) maximizes expected utility under an institution-speci
sdf932a8f5b.summary: The paper fine-tunes autoregressive tabular transformers on the decision objective with asymmetric costs for financial event prediction such as fraud.
sdf932a8f5b.why: Suggests fine-tuning for cost-sensitive decisions may beat post-hoc thresholding of calibrated probabilities in fraud systems.

se5938d5e16.title: BOP-Refer: Benchmark for Monocular 3D and 2D Object Grounding
se5938d5e16.description: arXiv:2611.34862v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce BOP-Refer, the first benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of everyday and industrial objects sourced from 9 diverse BOP datasets. We pair images from these datasets with VLM-generated and human-verified referring expressions, and derive accurate ground-truth 3D and 2D bounding boxes of the referred objects from their 3D models and 6DoF pose annotations. Our systematic evaluation of 17 frontier VLMs across the major proprietary and open-weight families (Gemini, GPT, Claude, Qwen, Gemma) shows that the best model, Gemini 4 Carbon, reaches 72.6% AP_IoU2D in 2D but only 12.4% AP_IoU3D in 3D, despite the more lenient IoU thresholds in 3D. The predicted 3D boxes are usually centered on the target objects in the image but often
se5938d5e16.summary: BOP-Refer introduces a benchmark for monocular 3D and 2D grounding of objects, evaluating 17 frontier VLMs with the best model named Gemini 4 Car...
se5938d5e16.why: Shows current VLMs' limits on 3D object grounding from single images, relevant to robotics and industrial vision.

sa81a318c23.title: RePace: Reasoning about Demonstration Speedup for Faster Vision-Language-Action Policies
sa81a318c23.description: arXiv:2611.34864v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Since vision-language-action (VLA) policies can inherit the slow pace of human demonstrations, accelerating these demonstrations before fine-tuning can lead to faster VLA policies without an additional speed-selection module at deployment. Several offline speedup methods have focused on identifying segments that require less precision and assigning predefined speedup factors to the segments. However, even within a single segment, a speedup factor suitable for steady motion may be too high when precise alignment is required. To this end, this paper presents RePace, an offline reasoning framework that determines how much to accelerate each part of a demonstration. For the same recorded movement, RePace measures how much each candidate speedup
sa81a318c23.summary: RePace reasons about demonstration speedup, assigning varying speed factors within segments to accelerate vision-language-action policy training data.
sa81a318c23.why: Offers a way to speed up VLA policies without adding a speed-selection module at deployment.

sa8c2e4dbb0.title: A Survey of Security, Privacy, and Ethics of Large Language Models in Telecom
sa8c2e4dbb0.description: arXiv:2611.34868v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly integrated into telecommunications for customer service, network analytics, and operational support. While offering efficiency and innovation, their deployment raises critical privacy, security, and ethical challenges due to the uniquely sensitive and longitudinal nature of telecom data. This paper presents a survey of LLM risks and safeguards in telecom context. Our survey introduces a telecom-specific taxonomy linking privacy, security, and ethics with use cases and outlines open research challenges such as longitudinal data privacy, cross-border compliance, and scalable guardrails.
sa8c2e4dbb0.summary: A survey reviews security, privacy, and ethical risks of LLMs in telecom, introducing a telecom-specific taxonomy linking risks to use cases.
sa8c2e4dbb0.why: Useful checklist for telecom teams deploying LLMs on sensitive longitudinal customer and network data.

s308e8397fe.title: Shape-Aware Three-Way Merge for RDF Knowledge Graphs: The schema defines the conflict: an implementation and evaluation
s308e8397fe.description: arXiv:2611.34870v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Merging RDF serializations creates ordering conflicts and misses semantic ones. We describe and evaluate a three-way merge in which the schema defines a conflict: set algebra combines canonical triples, and a slot is contended only where a SHACL shape bounds its cardinality and both sides' changes cannot stand within that bound. Unbounded predicates union; contended slots go to a person. The same shapes graph validates the result. We do not claim the first three-way merge for RDF. Our contribution is an implementation in a production multi-agent store and an evaluation against a reimplementation of Quit Store's Context Merge overlap rule, which it extends rather than replaces, and six other strategies. Across five synthetic seeds, the shape
s308e8397fe.summary: The paper presents a shape-aware three-way merge for RDF knowledge graphs that uses SHACL shapes to define conflicts, implemented in a production multi-agent system.
s308e8397fe.why: Provides a schema-driven approach to resolving merge conflicts in knowledge graphs maintained by multiple agents or editors.

s1edb70c330.title: How Much Do Coding Agents Over-Edit, and Why? An Empirical Study of Unneeded Edits in Repository-Level Agent Patches
s1edb70c330.description: arXiv:2611.34875v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Agent patches are larger than developers', which is widely read as over-editing. But patch size does not say whether the extra edits are needed, what they are, or where they come from. We introduce Delta Residue Attribution (DRA), which replays agent trajectories, traces every block (unit) of the final patch to the step that wrote it, reverts each unit, and reruns the task tests to decide whether the unit is needed. We apply DRA to 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories from 18 frontier models on SWE-bench Verified (6,728) and DeepSWE (932), and grade developer patches using the same method. Agent patches do change more lines than developers'; on SWE-bench Verified the majority of extra edits add tests (61%) and documentation (13%)
s1edb70c330.summary: Researchers introduce Delta Residue Attribution to test whether extra edits in agent patches are needed, applying it to 7,660 resolved GitHub Copilot CLI trajectories across 18 models.
s1edb70c330.why: It separates necessary from unneeded agent edits, offering a way to judge whether coding agents' larger patches are actually wasteful.

sc7f5832645.title: Interpretable and Accurate Hybrid Decision Trees with Selective Case-Based Splits
sc7f5832645.description: arXiv:2611.34887v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Decision trees are among the most well-known interpretable models in Machine Learning. Over the years, a wide variety of strategies have been proposed to define split conditions within the greedy learning framework, aiming to guide instance routing and enhance predictive performance. These strategies range from axis-parallel and oblique splits based on feature values to proximity-based splits using exemplar instances and more complex hybrid approaches. However, no single method has emerged as universally superior. In this work, we present two key contributions to the construction of greedy decision trees. First, we propose a hybrid tree architecture that integrates both feature-based and case-based splits, allowing for heterogeneous splits
sc7f5832645.summary: Researchers present two hybrid decision tree methods that selectively combine different split strategies, including case-based splits, to improve interpretability and accuracy.

s6f1345c358.title: Enhancing Maritime Domain Awareness using Latent Space Representations
s6f1345c358.description: arXiv:2611.34899v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This work presents a novel application of Earth Observation (EO) embeddings for Maritime Domain Awareness (MDA) from the perspective of the geospatial foundation model TerraMind. By operating directly on compressed latent-space representations rather than on the original Sentinel-1 imagery, this approach directly addresses the data gravity bottleneck that increasingly constrains operational EO processing, in line with the objectives of the Embed2Scale project. In particular, linear and non-linear probing of compressed embeddings, latent space representations of synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery, is used to detect, localise, and characterise vessels from Sentinel-1 GRD images. Vessel detection achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.95, while vessel lo
s6f1345c358.summary: Researchers apply compressed Earth Observation embeddings from the TerraMind geospatial model to Maritime Domain Awareness, probing latent representations instead of raw Sentinel-1 imagery.
s6f1345c358.why: Working on compressed latent embeddings rather than raw imagery addresses data volume bottlenecks in operational Earth observation pipelines.

s967b83bfb4.title: $\mu$-Bench: Benchmarking Multi-User Task Completion in Shared Interaction Voice Agents
s967b83bfb4.description: arXiv:2611.34920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Voice agents in shared spaces must satisfy interdependent multi-user requests while upholding per-user authority, privacy, and task constraints. Existing evaluations offer limited coverage when participants react throughout a session. We introduce $\mu$-Bench, a benchmark for joint task completion in closed-loop, full-duplex multi-user voice interaction. Simulated participants act from isolated profiles of goals, knowledge, and permissions, adapting to the agent's speech and tool outcomes. Across 20 domains, 100 scenarios vary group size, acoustics, and follow-up demands to form 800 cases (408 tool-augmented, 392 tool-free). Joint Task Success (JTS) requires all user goals, privacy boundaries, and terminal states to hold jointly, while Pure
s967b83bfb4.summary: Researchers introduce μ-Bench, a benchmark for voice agents completing joint tasks with multiple users in full-duplex, closed-loop interaction across 20 domains and 100 scenarios.
s967b83bfb4.why: It targets multi-user voice agent evaluation, where per-user permissions and privacy constraints make single-user benchmarks insufficient.

sfb43eb5392.title: Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces for Hard Math Problems
sfb43eb5392.description: arXiv:2611.34928v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Post-training large language models (LLMs) for mathematical reasoning often relies on accepted traces whose final answers pass a verifier. For hard math problems, however, such traces can be rare under independent Monte Carlo (MC) sampling. To address this, we propose Diverse Alternative Reasoning Traces (DART), a trace-mining method that starts from a rejected trace, decomposes it into reasoning steps, and ranks them by position-weighted uncertainty. It then generates deliberately distinct alternative candidates for highly ranked steps using reference-answer guidance and a meta-thought before completing the resulting traces. On greedy-unsolved DeepMath-103K problems, DART recovers 37% more problems than MC sampling at a matched number of g
sfb43eb5392.summary: Researchers propose DART, a method that mines diverse alternative reasoning traces from rejected solutions to build training data for hard math problems.
sfb43eb5392.why: It offers a way to generate more training signal for math reasoning when verified correct traces are rare.

s59d18ef749.title: Attack Policy Selection can Mislead Monitor Evaluators
s59d18ef749.description: arXiv:2611.34934v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: AI monitors, classifiers that flag dangerous behaviour by AI agents, are often evaluated against transcripts generated by attack policies acting as proxies for dangerous behaviour in deployment. We evaluate an ex-production OpenAI monitor as a case study and find that measured false negative rate is highly sensitive to both the method used to generate attack policies and the level of optimisation applied within that method. This rate ranged from 0.5\% to 20.8\% across optimisation levels of a single method (reinforcement learning), and from 6.4\% to 23.0\% across methods at their best observed optimisation level (optimised prompting vs.\ transcript editing). Every attack policy was developed against proxy monitors only: all reported results
s59d18ef749.summary: A study finds that the choice of attack policy strongly affects measured false negative rates when evaluating an ex-production OpenAI AI monitor, ranging from 0.5% to 20.8%.
s59d18ef749.why: Monitor evaluation results depend heavily on how attack transcripts are generated, so safety metrics may be misleading.

s5a2e3bf2cc.title: Spectrum Adaptation of AI-Native Autoencoder Communications with Transfer Learning
s5a2e3bf2cc.description: arXiv:2611.34942v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: End-to-end physical-layer learning replaces separate modulation, coding, and detection operations with an autoencoder (AE) that consists of a jointly trained encoder-decoder pair at the transmitter and the receiver. This paper studies AI-native communications with AEs and quantifies the sensitivity to training-test mismatch in channel models. Models trained only on an AWGN channel achieve low bit error rates (BERs) under matched conditions but degrade severely on Rayleigh fading with practical front-end impairments. To reduce the time and energy required to adapt to new channel conditions, we propose a low-latency transfer-learning procedure that starts from an AWGN-pretrained system and fine-tunes only a small subset of transmitter and rec
s5a2e3bf2cc.summary: Researchers study autoencoder-based physical-layer communications, showing models trained on AWGN degrade on Rayleigh fading and proposing transfer learning to adapt spectrum conditions.

s9919d86395.title: MathConstruct: Challenging LLM Reasoning with Constructive Proofs
s9919d86395.description: arXiv:2502.10197v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: While Large Language Models (LLMs) demonstrate impressive performance in mathematics, existing math benchmarks come with significant limitations. Many focus on problems with fixed ground-truth answers, and are often saturated due to problem simplicity or the viability of guessing or memorization. Crucially, they capture only a narrow subset of relevant math problems. To address this research gap, we introduce MathConstruct, a new benchmark of 121 challenging problems sourced from various math competitions, which targets constructive proofs, a widely encountered problem type requiring the construction of mathematical objects with specific properties. These proofs are particularly suitable for LLM evaluation, as solution correctness can be
s9919d86395.summary: MathConstruct is a benchmark of 121 competition math problems targeting constructive proofs, aimed at reducing saturation and guessing in existing LLM math evaluations.
s9919d86395.why: Existing math benchmarks are saturated, so constructive-proof benchmarks give teams a harder test of model reasoning.

se9387cb2a7.title: MathArena: Evaluating LLMs on Uncontaminated Math Competitions
se9387cb2a7.description: arXiv:2505.23281v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The rapid advancement of reasoning capabilities in large language models (LLMs) has led to notable improvements on mathematical benchmarks. However, many of the most commonly used evaluation datasets (e.g., AIME 2024) are widely available online, making it difficult to disentangle genuine reasoning from potential memorization. Furthermore, these benchmarks do not evaluate proof-writing capabilities, which are crucial for many mathematical tasks. To address this, we introduce MathArena, a new benchmark based on the following key insight: recurring math competitions provide a stream of high-quality, challenging problems that can be used for real-time evaluation of LLMs. By evaluating models as soon as new problems are released, we effective
se9387cb2a7.summary: MathArena is a benchmark that evaluates LLMs on recent, uncontaminated math competitions and includes proof-writing tasks.
se9387cb2a7.why: Freshly sourced competition problems reduce memorization concerns when comparing models' mathematical reasoning.

s38a68eacce.title: K12Vista: Exploring the Boundaries of MLLMs in K-12 Education
s38a68eacce.description: arXiv:2506.01676v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal large language models have demonstrated remarkable reasoning capabilities in various visual tasks. However, their abilities in K12 scenarios are still systematically underexplored. Previous studies suffer from various limitations including narrow subject coverage, insufficient data scale, lack of diversity in question types, and naive answer-centric evaluation method, resulting in insufficient exploration of model capabilities. To address these gaps, we propose K12Vista, the most comprehensive multimodal benchmark for Chinese K12 subject knowledge understanding and reasoning to date, featuring 33,000 questions across five core subjects from primary to high school and three question types. Moreover, beyond the final outcome, we
s38a68eacce.summary: K12Vista is a multimodal benchmark for evaluating MLLMs on Chinese K-12 educational content, covering more subjects and question types than prior work.

s402c7a7280.title: Beyond Moral Performance: Empirical Assessment of LLMs' Moral Competence Through Judgment Stability
s402c7a7280.description: arXiv:2509.10297v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Evaluations of large language models (LLMs) have largely measured moral performance, whether their outputs are morally appropriate, rather than moral competence, the capacity to judge on the basis of morally relevant considerations. We test for competence by varying morally irrelevant features of moral dilemmas. Because moral dilemmas rarely admit a single correct answer, we assess the stability of framework preferences, a model's relative ordering of five normative ethical frameworks, rather than of verdicts. We test 16 LLM configurations, reasoning and non-reasoning, on 18 dilemmas in six thematic domains for reliability across repeated runs and stability across prompt length, thematic domain, and reporting format. The configurations sh
s402c7a7280.summary: Researchers test 16 LLM configurations for moral competence by measuring stability of framework preferences when morally irrelevant features of dilemmas are varied.

s0c4b6201c5.title: ReviewSense: Cluster-Guided Evidence Selection for Actionable Review-to-Advice Generation
s0c4b6201c5.description: arXiv:2510.16466v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Customer reviews are a rich but weakly structured source of operational feedback. We study ReviewSense, a cluster-guided evidence-selection workflow that converts review corpora into action-oriented advice for human decision support. Reviews are embedded with a sentence transformer, grouped by iterative cosine-similarity clustering with threshold decay, and reduced to compact evidence before Large Language Model (LLM) generation. Evaluating on dental and healthcare service reviews with expert judgment of actionability and annotator-based theme alignment, we find that a single central representative preserves the dominant cluster theme in 77.3% of cases but only 60.6% of secondary themes: central evidence captures main issues more reliably
s0c4b6201c5.summary: ReviewSense is a workflow that clusters customer reviews with embeddings and LLMs to generate actionable advice, evaluated on dental and healthcare service reviews.

s96daf9fdc5.title: Semantic Gravity Wells: Why Negative Constraints Backfire
s96daf9fdc5.description: arXiv:2601.08070v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Negative constraints (instructions of the form "do not use word X") represent a fundamental test of instruction-following capability in large language models. Despite their apparent simplicity, these constraints fail with striking regularity, and the conditions governing failure have remained poorly understood. This paper presents a mechanistic investigation of negative instruction failure in Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. We introduce semantic pressure, a quantitative measure of the model's intrinsic probability of generating the forbidden word, and show that violation probability rises with pressure ($p = \sigma(-2.95 + 2.76 P_0)$; $n=40{,}000$ samples from 2,500 prompts; prompt-bootstrap 95% CI for slope: [2.53, 3.01]), from 5% of samples at low
s96daf9fdc5.summary: A mechanistic study of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct examines why negative constraints such as 'do not use word X' fail, introducing a measure called semantic pressure.
s96daf9fdc5.why: Explains a common instruction-following failure mode, useful for teams relying on negative prompt constraints.

s589d447f42.title: HLA: Hadamard Linear Attention
s589d447f42.description: arXiv:2602.12128v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The attention mechanism is an important reason for the success of transformers. It relies on computing pairwise relations between tokens. To reduce the high computational cost of standard quadratic attention, linear attention has been proposed as an efficient approximation. It employs kernel functions that are applied independently to the inputs before the pairwise similarities are calculated. That allows for an efficient computational procedure which, however, amounts to a low-degree rational function approximating softmax. We propose Hadamard Linear Attention (HLA). Unlike previous works on linear attention, the nonlinearity in HLA is not applied separately to queries and keys, but, analogously to standard softmax attention, after the p
s589d447f42.summary: Researchers propose Hadamard Linear Attention, a linear attention variant that aims to approximate softmax attention more closely than standard low-degree kernel methods.

s6608d48080.title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Cognitive Complexity in LLMs via Linear Probing using Bloom's Taxonomy
s6608d48080.description: arXiv:2602.17229v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The black-box nature of Large Language Models necessitates novel evaluation frameworks that transcend surface-level performance metrics. This study investigates the internal neural representations of the levels of complexity using Bloom's Taxonomy as a hierarchical lens. By analyzing high-dimensional activation vectors from different LLMs, we probe whether different Bloom levels, ranging from basic recall (Remember) to abstract synthesis (Create), are linearly separable within the model's residual streams. Our results demonstrate that linear classifiers achieve high accuracy across all Bloom levels, providing evidence that level information is encoded in a linearly accessible subspace of the model's representations. These findings provide
s6608d48080.summary: A study probes LLM residual streams with linear classifiers to test whether Bloom's Taxonomy cognitive levels, from recall to synthesis, are linearly separable.

s90d6d48da3.title: VibeServe: Can AI Agents Build Bespoke LLM Serving Systems?
s90d6d48da3.description: arXiv:2605.06068v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For years, we have built LLM serving systems like any other critical infrastructure, with a single general-purpose stack hand-tuned over many engineer-years to support every model and workload. In this paper, we instead let coding agents build bespoke serving systems for different usage scenarios. We propose VibeServe, the first agentic loop that generates entire LLM serving stacks end-to-end. VibeServe uses an outer loop to plan and track the search over system designs, and an inner loop to implement candidates, check correctness, and measure performance on the target benchmark. In standard serving settings, VibeServe matches vLLM and SGLang on Llama-3.1-8B, and delivers 2.3x the goodput of a tuned SGLang for a 397B MoE model on four AMD
s90d6d48da3.summary: VibeServe, an agentic loop, lets coding agents generate complete bespoke LLM serving stacks end-to-end, planning design search and checking correctness and performance.
s90d6d48da3.why: Suggests agents may automate building workload-specific inference infrastructure that today relies on hand-tuned general-purpose serving stacks.

s97968efdb1.title: Search-E1: Self-Distillation Drives Self-Evolution in Search-Augmented Reasoning
s97968efdb1.description: arXiv:2605.22511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Outcome based reinforcement learning provides a simple and effective recipe for training search augmented reasoning agents. Recent work seeks further improvements through stronger external teachers, auxiliary process supervision, specialized reward shaping, and increasingly elaborate training pipelines. This raises a natural question: can agents continue improving by learning from their own successful experience? We present Search-E1, a simple self evolution framework that alternates vanilla GRPO with on policy self distillation (OPSD). After each GRPO round, Search-E1 mines sibling trajectories generated by the policy itself and exposes the search skeleton of an efficient successful trajectory, that is, the sequence of queries it issued,
s97968efdb1.summary: Search-E1 is a self-evolution framework that alternates GRPO reinforcement learning with on-policy self-distillation to train search-augmented reasoning agents.
s97968efdb1.why: Offers a training recipe for search agents that learns from their own successful trajectories rather than relying on stronger external teachers.

s95e0e0eabd.title: Personalize-then-Store: Benchmarking and Learning Personalized Memory for Long-horizon Agents
s95e0e0eabd.description: arXiv:2605.25535v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing large language model (LLM) based memory systems apply universal, static policies that overlook a fundamental reality: the contexts that are worth storing in memory are different across users. This misalignment wastes limited memory budget on transient interactions while failing to preserve critical context for longhorizon tasks. To address this gap, we investigate an underexplored question: can LLM based memory systems learn personalized memory policies? We introduce PerMemBench, the first benchmark that jointly models multi domain interaction histories and cross user heterogeneity in agent use patterns to evaluate personalized memory systems. We further present the first empirical study of memory personalization, proposing sessi
s95e0e0eabd.summary: Researchers introduce PerMemBench, a benchmark for learning personalized memory policies so LLM agents store user-specific context instead of applying universal static rules.
s95e0e0eabd.why: Highlights that static memory policies waste budget on transient interactions, a design concern for long-running agent memory.

s52dd7e0c8b.title: Towards Faithful Agentic XAI: A Verification Method and an Open-World Benchmark for Better Model Faithfulness
s52dd7e0c8b.description: arXiv:2605.27879v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) helps users interpret model behavior and identify potential faults. Agentic XAI systems use Large Language Models (LLMs) to make explanations more accessible through natural-language interaction, but they can also produce plausible yet unfaithful explanations. This risk arises because unreliable XAI outputs for complex models can be amplified by LLMs and mislead users. We propose Faithful Agentic XAI (FAX), a verification method that improves the faithfulness of Agentic XAI explanations. FAX decomposes draft explanations into claims and tests them with inherently faithful tools that query the target model directly, filtering unsupported or contradicted claims before final generation. We also introduce CRAFTER-XAI-Benc
s52dd7e0c8b.summary: The paper proposes FAX, a verification method that decomposes draft explanations to improve faithfulness of agentic explainable AI, plus an open-world benchmark.
s52dd7e0c8b.why: Shows LLM-based explanation layers can amplify unfaithful outputs, so teams need verification before trusting agent-generated model explanations.

s40e737f99f.title: Benchmark Everything Everywhere All at Once
s40e737f99f.description: arXiv:2606.06462v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Benchmarks provide standardized measures for evaluating and advancing large language models (LLMs) and multimodal LLMs (MLLMs). As models improve, existing benchmarks can approach saturation, making it harder to challenge models and distinguish among them. While reusing annotated datasets can reduce data collection and labeling effort, constructing new benchmarks remains labor-intensive, and existing agent-based approaches often target specific tasks or automate only parts of the process. To address these challenges, we introduce BenchHarness, an autonomous harness for end-to-end benchmark customization. It coordinates multiple agents and tools to analyze user requirements, search for suitable datasets, and construct validated benchmarks,
s40e737f99f.summary: BenchHarness is introduced to automate benchmark construction for LLMs and multimodal LLMs by reusing annotated datasets with agent-based tooling.
s40e737f99f.why: Could reduce the cost of building fresh evaluations as existing benchmarks approach saturation.

s638600bb93.title: A History-Aware Visually Grounded Critic for Computer Use Agents
s638600bb93.description: arXiv:2606.11078v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Various test-time interventions for Computer Use Agents (CUAs), including critic models, have been developed to improve performance through pre-execution action evaluation in complex Graphical User Interface (GUI) environments. However, existing critics suffer from two key limitations: they (1) focus primarily on short-sighted decision loops (e.g., forgetting earlier actions) and (2) lack the visual grounding needed to detect flawed actions (e.g., clicking wrong UI elements). To address these, we introduce HiViG, a History-aware Visually Grounded test-time framework, built around a multimodal critic trained on real GUI trajectories to abstract past interactions into a compact record and to evaluate actions with visual grounding. At test t
s638600bb93.summary: HiViG is a history-aware, visually grounded critic that evaluates actions before execution for Computer Use Agents, aiming to catch wrong clicks and forgotten earlier steps.
s638600bb93.why: Pre-execution critics may reduce costly mistakes for GUI agents, though the abstract gives no quantitative results here.

s78a9d7231a.title: Are You Still the Agent I Authorized? Earned Authority under a Fixed Ceiling for Evolving Agents
s78a9d7231a.description: arXiv:2607.23586v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Long-lived AI agents increasingly evolve after deployment by retaining experience, acquiring skills and tools, revising workflows, delegating work, and moving across task phases. This improves adaptation but creates a distinct authorization problem. Tool-enabled agents can turn model errors and prompt injections into consequential external actions; when evolution occurs under a live grant, the subject exercising that authority or the context in which it acts may no longer match what the user evaluated. Evolution can change both the effects reachable under an old grant and the authority required by the task, which may rise, fall, or become incomparable. Existing tool policies constrain actions but do not determine when a grant survives thi
s78a9d7231a.summary: The paper examines authorization for long-lived agents that evolve after deployment, arguing that changes can make a previously approved grant no longer match the agent acting under it.
s78a9d7231a.why: Raises a concrete governance problem for enterprises granting tool-using agents ongoing authority as they change.

sc3dfba8772.title: Fisher-R1: Training LLM Agents for Reliable Hypothesis Testing
sc3dfba8772.description: arXiv:2608.07437v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Reliable hypothesis testing is the foundation of many empirical scientific claims. Large language model (LLM) agents are increasingly used to automate this process, as they can inspect datasets, generate code, and produce analyses end-to-end. However, we show that they frequently make subtle inferential errors that lead to incorrect conclusions despite correctly executed analyses. Existing benchmarks fail to capture this failure mode, as they rarely assess whether a reported p-value is statistically valid given the assumptions underlying the data. We address this gap by building P-Bench, a benchmark comprising 425 open-ended, realistic hypothesis-testing tasks spanning economics, biology, and medicine. Each task requires an agent to selec
sc3dfba8772.summary: Fisher-R1 trains LLM agents for statistically valid hypothesis testing, after showing agents often make subtle inferential errors despite correctly executed analyses.
sc3dfba8772.why: Shows agents can produce wrong conclusions even with correct code, so p-value validity needs checking beyond execution success.

scabbcd3886.title: iBrain: A Unified Foundation Model Reading the Brain from Surface to Spikes
scabbcd3886.description: arXiv:2609.06960v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Invasive neural recordings provide high-fidelity measurements of brain activity, with signals such as intracranial EEG (iEEG) and intracortical spiking activity capturing neural dynamics at different spatial and temporal scales. Yet existing neural foundation models have largely been developed independently for different invasive recording paradigms, leaving joint pretraining across heterogeneous invasive signals underexplored. In this work, we introduce iBrain, a unified foundation model that jointly learns from iEEG and spiking activity. iBrain employs signal-specific encoders to accommodate their distinct signal characteristics and a shared spatiotemporal Transformer backbone to model dependencies across recording channels and time. We
scabbcd3886.summary: iBrain is a unified foundation model that jointly pretrains on intracranial EEG and intracortical spiking activity from heterogeneous invasive neural recordings.
scabbcd3886.why: Limited relevance to typical engineering work; mainly of interest to neurotech and biomedical ML teams.

scd28a5be71.title: SpecRead: A Benchmark for Measuring Whether Language Models Understand Hardware Specifications
scd28a5be71.description: arXiv:2609.33699v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing benchmarks for large language models (LLMs) in hardware design evaluate downstream artifacts such as generated RTL, assertions, or testbenches. When a model fails, it may have misread the specification or understood it and failed to write the code. We present SpecRead, a benchmark that isolates specification comprehension from generation ability. SpecRead v2.2 contains 383 questions over 10 open-source OpenTitan IP blocks in four types: exact retrieval, cross-section reasoning, contradiction detection in mutated specifications, and spec-RTL consistency checking, plus 41 distractor controls and 41 consistent-RTL controls. Type-4 items use real RTL mutations retained only when Icarus Verilog simulation shows a behavioral change. A
scd28a5be71.summary: SpecRead is a 383-question benchmark testing whether LLMs understand hardware specifications, separately from their ability to generate RTL code.
scd28a5be71.why: Isolates spec comprehension from code generation, helping teams diagnose whether hardware design failures stem from misreading specs.

s8200ce4d55.title: Agent Calibration under Deployment Change: Acceptance Contracts, Trajectory Repair, and Adaptation Costs
s8200ce4d55.description: arXiv:2609.35149v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An agent can remain operational after a model, tool, or user-context change while losing capabilities required at its destination. We define agent calibration as qualification against a versioned deployment contract. The contract specifies basic capabilities and end-to-end reachability, technical and professional precision, and acceptance by intended users. For each requirement, a source-to-destination map records what must be preserved, transformed, added, or retired. Experts supply benchmarks, positive and negative examples, annotated trajectories, and cost limits. These instruments guide changes to prompts and context, tool calls and other harness settings, or an external compact policy while the foundation model remains frozen. Candid
s8200ce4d55.summary: The paper defines agent calibration as qualifying an agent against a versioned deployment contract after a model, tool, or user-context change.
s8200ce4d55.why: Gives teams a framework for checking whether agents keep required capabilities when models or tools are swapped.

sadbcb2db2f.title: FinAutoRubric: Expert-Guided Automatic Rubric Generation for Evaluating Financial Research Agents
sadbcb2db2f.description: arXiv:2609.35744v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Evaluating finance research agents requires rubrics that reflect expert standards and fix the values correct as of an information cutoff. Expert-reviewed finance benchmarks rely on fixed, per-item rubrics, which are costly to extend and cannot encode each institution's own standard. In FinAutoRubric, experts specify reusable evaluation guidance, while agents and code carry out query-specific rubric generation, review, and validation. This expert guidance governs every agent, as prompts and as rules that code enforces, and a Task Bank of reusable criteria carries it across tasks. In long-horizon loops that follow the expert guidance, a writer agent researches every expected value and a reviewer agent verifies it, and failures escalate to a
sadbcb2db2f.summary: FinAutoRubric generates evaluation rubrics for financial research agents, with experts specifying reusable guidance that agents and code apply per query.
sadbcb2db2f.why: Offers a way to evaluate domain agents against institution-specific standards without costly fixed per-item rubrics.

s6f893bcbb1.title: ACTR: Aligning Thoughts and Responses for Multilingual Safety in Reasoning LLMs
s6f893bcbb1.description: arXiv:2609.37054v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Ensuring the safety of reasoning large language models (LLMs) across languages is essential for their reliable deployment. However, when exposed to jailbreak attacks in non-high-resource languages, these models may generate unsafe responses even when their reasoning traces identify safety risks. To address this issue, we propose aligning cross-lingual thoughts and responses (ACTR), a framework that improves multilingual safety alignment by strengthening the use of existing safety reasoning. Specifically, we first present the think gap score (TGS) to compare the normalized contributions of reasoning traces to attention outputs during response generation across languages, and use reasoning- trace substitution to measure the cross-lingual sa
s6f893bcbb1.summary: ACTR proposes aligning reasoning traces and final responses to improve multilingual safety in reasoning LLMs facing jailbreaks in non-high-resource languages.
s6f893bcbb1.why: Shows safety of reasoning models can differ across languages even when traces identify risks, relevant for global deployments.

sfd8a046567.title: CompMat-Bench: Benchmarking AI Agents for Computational Materials Science
sfd8a046567.description: arXiv:2610.00636v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Evaluating AI agents on scientific research tasks is constrained by the time and resources required for the underlying experiments or calculations. In computational materials research, repeating the same expensive simulations across agents and trials can make evaluation impractical. We introduce CompMat-Bench, a benchmark of 94 tasks derived from recently published computational materials studies, each asking agents to complete a step toward achieving the study's scientific goal. We reproduce the research steps in advance and assess agents on preparing inputs and analyzing outputs for expensive simulations, so expensive simulations can be avoided during evaluation. The reproduced inputs and results serve as ground truth for grading agents
sfd8a046567.summary: CompMat-Bench is a 94-task benchmark for AI agents in computational materials science, derived from published studies with pre-reproduced research steps.
sfd8a046567.why: Provides a reusable, cheaper way to evaluate scientific agents without rerunning expensive simulations each trial.

sbdc134cd22.title: FluidPD: In-Place Elasticity for SLO-Aware Prefill-Decode Disaggregated LLM Serving
sbdc134cd22.description: arXiv:2610.06917v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Prefill-decode (P/D) disaggregation serves the two phases of LLM inference on separate workers, typically with a fixed prefill/decode worker ratio. Real workloads exhibit both short bursts and sustained shifts in the prefill-to-decode demand ratio, so a fixed split can violate latency SLOs while capacity sits idle in the other pool. Autoscaling adds capacity, but it reacts slowly, requires spare GPUs, and does not address short-timescale phase imbalance. We present FluidPD, a P/D-disaggregated serving system with SLO-aware in-place elasticity. FluidToken absorbs transient imbalance by offloading a bounded portion of prefill computation to decode workers that have slack. FluidRole absorbs sustained imbalance by switching running workers be
sbdc134cd22.summary: FluidPD is a prefill-decode disaggregated LLM serving system that adds SLO-aware in-place elasticity to shift capacity between prefill and decode workers during workload shifts.
sbdc134cd22.why: Addresses latency SLO violations from fixed prefill/decode ratios without waiting for slow autoscaling or spare GPUs.

sb2f9ba3495.title: SearchWorld: Spatial Value-Grounded Imagination for UAV Object Search via World Models
sb2f9ba3495.description: arXiv:2610.09335v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Autonomous unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) object search involves a closed loop of perception, decision-making, and action under partial observability. Urban environments pose several challenges: large search areas and narrow egocentric views limit coverage, dense 3D geometry constrains safe motion, and open-world instructions require identifying a specific target among distractors. Many existing methods mitigate partial observability through explicit maps or memory representations, yet remain largely reactive, reasoning over past observations without explicitly predicting future states. World models enable prospective reasoning through imagined rollouts. However, image-generating world models can incur high inference latency, while spatial
sb2f9ba3495.summary: Researchers propose SearchWorld, a world-model approach for UAV object search in urban areas under partial observability, using spatial value-grounded imagination.
sb2f9ba3495.why: Offers a planning approach for embodied drone search in cluttered 3D environments, relevant to teams building autonomous aerial systems.

sf791514422.title: Where Can a Decision Model Diagnose HVAC Faults? Reasoning Demand, Physical Representation, and Robustness Under Shift
sf791514422.description: arXiv:2610.09937v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Artificial intelligence supports building operations in several forms, each with its own barrier. Expert rules must be tuned for every system, supervised models need labeled data that buildings rarely record, and language models return free text that requires human-in-the-loop checking, since their stated confidence is unreliable. A newer kind of pretrained model, here called a decision model, returns a probability for every allowed answer, so one model could serve many decisions without training. This study answers three open questions for fault diagnosis in heating, ventilation, and air-conditioning systems: which decisions such a model can make, what input it needs, and whether its probabilities hold when conditions change. On 128 faul
sf791514422.summary: A study evaluates whether pretrained decision models, which output probabilities over allowed answers, can diagnose HVAC faults without task-specific training.
sf791514422.why: Suggests one pretrained model might serve multiple building-operations decisions without labeled data, though the abstract's findings are cut off.

s85cfae30e1.title: RAN-JEPA: An Action-Conditioned World Model for Energy-efficient Mobile Network Control
s85cfae30e1.description: arXiv:2610.17584v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Operational mobile networks are rich in observations but poor in interventions: they continuously generate large volumes of passive telemetry, while controlled action--response trajectories remain comparatively scarce and costly to collect. This observation--intervention asymmetry is a central obstacle to building practical world models for RAN control. We address this problem with RAN-JEPA, an action-conditioned world model that separates representation learning from intervention learning. The model first learns a predictive latent representation from observation-only network data, adapts that representation to the target deployment domain, and then learns action-conditioned latent dynamics from controlled sleep/wake trajectories while k
s85cfae30e1.summary: RAN-JEPA is an action-conditioned world model for mobile network control that learns representations from passive telemetry before learning interventions.
s85cfae30e1.why: Addresses scarce controlled action data in telecom networks by pretraining on abundant passive telemetry, a useful pattern for energy-efficient network control.

sc50e63ab99.title: OwlSight: A Panoramic Monitor for Chain-of-Thought Reasoning
sc50e63ab99.description: arXiv:2610.23670v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) monitoring offers actionable evidence for oversight AI systems, with the potential to enable early detection and intervention. However, existing approaches are focused on specific tasks, whereas the regulation of AI, particularly reasoning models, requires monitoring a broader range of tasks. We introduce Factor for CoT monitoring, a strategy that supports customizing monitoring requirements in the prompt, which enables a single monitor to cover different tasks by relying on different factors. Furthermore, we introduce two types of factors, fine-grained and coarse-grained (e.g., monitoring whether a specific email address has been leaked versus monitoring privacy leakage), to accommodate diverse user monitoring need
sc50e63ab99.summary: OwlSight introduces Factor, a Chain-of-Thought monitoring strategy that lets a single monitor cover multiple tasks by customizing monitoring factors in the prompt.
sc50e63ab99.why: Offers a way for teams to oversee reasoning models across varied tasks with one monitor rather than task-specific tooling.

s11ef88e9fe.title: Kairos: Fast and Reliable Symbolic Task Planning for Autonomous Robots
s11ef88e9fe.description: arXiv:2610.39454v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Robots that plan while they act need a task planner that reads the models their designers write, answers within milliseconds, and says what each answer means. Models are written in the Planning Domain Definition Language (PDDL), which has grown from classical planning to durative actions, numeric resources, time windows and continuous change, while planners cover one fragment each and differ in what their failures mean. The contribution in artificial intelligence is Kairos, a single planner, not a portfolio of existing planners, that covers the whole language and derives what each answer guarantees from the search that produced it. We prove when the exhaustion of a search shows that no plan exists, and give a relaxation of temporal tasks
s11ef88e9fe.summary: Kairos is a single symbolic task planner for robots that handles PDDL features including durative actions, numeric resources, time windows, and continuous change.
s11ef88e9fe.why: A unified planner for expressive PDDL fragments could simplify robotics stacks that currently need multiple planners with differing failure semantics.

sfb210c28b8.title: Researcher-in-the-Loop Evolutionary Discovery of Entanglement-Assisted Quantum Code Families
sfb210c28b8.description: arXiv:2610.41183v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLM-guided program evolution can produce mathematical constructions, but validity, generality, and reproducibility require distinct evidence. In this paper, we develop a researcher-in-the-loop discovery pipeline combining program evolution, exact evaluation, mathematical generalization, and independent verification. We apply it to entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting codes (EAQECCs). Evolved programs produced finite qubit constructions from specifications that supplied no family formula. Researcher-directed analysis with a language model led to a general construction and proof drafts, which the researchers revised and checked. The resulting family $[[n,1,n-1;n-q-1]]_q$ exists for prime powers $q\ge3$ at $n\ge2q+1$ and for $q=2$
sfb210c28b8.summary: Researchers present a researcher-in-the-loop pipeline combining LLM-guided program evolution with exact evaluation and verification to discover entanglement-assisted quantum error-correcting code families.
sfb210c28b8.why: Shows a pattern for pairing LLM-driven program search with rigorous verification, though the item is mainly of interest to quantum coding researchers.

s7c6fef01cd.title: AceAction-5M: Hierarchical Goals for Generalist Action Learning Across 3D Game Worlds
s7c6fef01cd.description: arXiv:2611.04241v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Video games provide a practical setting for collecting vision-language-action (VLA) data, whose acquisition in physical environments is costly. Existing datasets, however, remain limited by restricted game coverage, sparse language supervision, or temporal hierarchies that do not necessarily reflect changes in task objectives. We introduce AceAction, a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games for learning skill composition and subgoal transitions. AceAction organizes demonstrations around complete tasks, linking overall instructions, ordered subgoals, and local skill instructions to temporally aligned visual observations and keyboard-and-mouse actions. To construct these annotations, we develop a vision-language model pipeline t
s7c6fef01cd.summary: AceAction-5M is a dataset of human gameplay across multiple 3D games, organized around hierarchical goals for vision-language-action learning.
s7c6fef01cd.why: Provides a game-derived VLA dataset with subgoal structure, a lower-cost data source for training generalist action models.

s946c6ee042.title: ConceptARC at Scale: Studying Conceptual Understanding in Reasoning Models
s946c6ee042.description: arXiv:2611.06732v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large reasoning models (LRMs) perform well on challenging benchmarks, yet it remains unclear whether they form generalizable abstractions across conceptually related reasoning tasks. The Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus (ARC) provides a controlled testbed for studying abstraction, requiring solvers to infer transformation rules over two-dimensional grids from a small set of examples. While ARC evaluates rule abstraction within individual tasks, different tasks may share higher-level structure despite requiring different transformations$\unicode{x2014}$for example, several tasks may involve reasoning about objects contained within other objects. Benchmarks such as ConceptARC capture this structure by grouping ARC-style tasks into recurring
s946c6ee042.summary: A study examines whether large reasoning models form generalizable abstractions across conceptually related ARC tasks, scaling up the ConceptARC benchmark.
s946c6ee042.why: Clarifies how far reasoning models generalize abstract concepts beyond individual tasks, informing expectations for model reasoning reliability.

s7f59416e57.title: Measuring Generative AI Content in Political Campaigns: Evidence of Rising Adoption and Non-Disclosure
s7f59416e57.description: arXiv:2611.11658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The use of generative AI in political campaigns has drawn public concern and policy attention. Public concerns range from distrust of candidates to skepticism about the authenticity and accuracy of political advertising, including AI-generated images and video. Nearly half of U.S. states have enacted laws that prohibit, or require disclosure of, "materially deceptive" AI-generated content (AIGC) in elections to guard against these concerns. This study measures how candidates and their campaigns produce and circulate AIGC during an election cycle. We develop two measures that estimate not only wether campaigns use AIGC, but how much they produce (magnitude) and in what forms (modality). We apply these measures to a novel dataset of text an
s7f59416e57.summary: A study measures how political campaigns produce and circulate AI-generated content during an election cycle, finding rising adoption and non-disclosure.
s7f59416e57.why: Highlights gaps between AI content use and disclosure rules, relevant to teams building provenance or disclosure compliance tooling.

s332ba74db4.title: The WoW: A Large-Scale World Knowledge Corpus for Full-Lifecycle LLM Training
s332ba74db4.description: arXiv:2611.13487v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Existing Chinese educational corpora often suffer from fragmented coverage and a lack of systematic organization. In this paper, we propose WoW (\textbf{Wo}rld Kno\textbf{w}ledge), a large-scale dataset designed for the full-cycle training of foundation models. The construction of this dataset is driven by an Educational Knowledge Graph, which serves as a taxonomic backbone for the systematic collection and completion of missing educational modules across all levels. Compared to previous versions, this iteration provides enhanced systematicity, superior quality, and a larger scale, while incorporating multimodal signals and supporting every stage of model development. Experiments demonstrate that WoW significantly improves model performan
s332ba74db4.summary: WoW is a large-scale Chinese educational world-knowledge corpus built on an Educational Knowledge Graph for full-lifecycle foundation model training.
s332ba74db4.why: A structured, curated Chinese education dataset could be useful for training or evaluating domain-specific models, though the abstract gives limited detail.

sbfec2ce0ac.title: RSI-PDEbench: A Benchmark for Self-Improving Agents in PDE Solving
sbfec2ce0ac.description: arXiv:2611.14949v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Identifying and solving partial differential equations (PDEs) from sampled solution data often requires substantial expert effort in equation discovery, coefficient estimation, and numerical solver configuration, especially under noise and distribution shifts. Can large language model (LLM) agents automate this workflow accurately and efficiently? To investigate this question, we introduce RSI-PDEbench, a benchmark of 1,001 cases spanning 42 equation templates, including both classical and fractional PDEs. It provides three evaluation settings: Full evaluates performance on noise-free solution data; Noisy tests robustness to Gaussian noise with an RMS equal to 50\% of the clean-signal RMS; and Hard-OOD tests challenging out-of-distributio
sbfec2ce0ac.summary: RSI-PDEbench is a benchmark of 1,001 cases across 42 PDE templates for testing whether LLM agents can automate PDE identification and solving.
sbfec2ce0ac.why: Provides a concrete benchmark for evaluating agent automation of scientific computing workflows under noise and distribution shift.

s5f213382ce.title: $\varepsilon$-WM: Error-Driven Dynamics Adaptation across Fast--Slow Timescales for World Modeling
s5f213382ce.description: arXiv:2611.15215v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A core challenge for world models is adapting to sudden, persistent, yet initially unknown changes in robot dynamics. If the world model fails to adapt, its prediction errors accumulate over the open-loop rollout and ultimately mislead the robot's actions. Existing world models, however, struggle to balance three key requirements for dynamics adaptation: responsiveness, rapidly correcting sudden changes; stability, avoiding lasting model updates from transient disturbances; and persistence, retaining adapted dynamics during the observation-free open-loop rollout. Inspired by multi-timescale predictive coding in the human brain, we propose $\varepsilon$-WM, a world model that adapts to unknown dynamics through error-driven corrections acro
s5f213382ce.summary: ε-WM is a world model that adapts to sudden, persistent robot dynamics changes across fast and slow timescales using error-driven updates.
s5f213382ce.why: Targets a practical failure mode where world-model prediction errors accumulate in rollouts and degrade robot control.

s7540914d78.title: AutoE2E: Don't speak - Language free end-to-end autonomy for L2++ ADAS and L4 Robotaxis
s7540914d78.description: arXiv:2611.22374v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model developed by the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group. It introduces a temporal bird's-eye-view (BEV) architecture that combines multi-camera perception, HD-map information and route conditioning to predict future vehicle motion. The evaluated model uses a pretrained camera-BEV backbone, temporal feature fusion and a lightweight recurrent trajectory planner. It contains approximately 79.9 million parameters, of which approximately 1.45 million are trainable in the evaluated configuration. The v1.0 release provides model checkpoints, training and evaluation code, and DataModelConsole, a dashboard for visualizing and inspecting model experiments. On the KITScenes validation benchmark,
s7540914d78.summary: AutoE2E is an open-source end-to-end driving model from the Autoware Foundation Robotaxi Working Group using temporal BEV architecture with about 79.9M parameters.
s7540914d78.why: An open-source end-to-end autonomy reference for ADAS and robotaxi work gives engineers a concrete architecture to study and build on.

s81f7397512.title: Auditable Clinical Support with Decision Agents
s81f7397512.description: arXiv:2611.23700v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Emergency care requires auditable decisions, but a language-model agent just outputs text. We introduce Decision2Care, a decision agent that generates a probability for every option at each step. It diagnosed 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases with 86.5% accuracy in a median of 2.2 s; language-model agents reached 86.1 to 91.7% but took more than 90 s. Its drug orders were judged guideline-adherent more often than documented first-day care and with about half as many records, it predicted death as well as three ICU clinicians. In the four cases where it was confident but wrong, we traced each decision to one imaging report. Our study suggests that an agent's work-up can be reviewed like a clinician's, motivating prospective trial
s81f7397512.summary: Decision2Care is a decision agent that outputs probabilities for each option and diagnosed 546 emergency admissions across 12 diseases with 86.5% accuracy.
s81f7397512.why: Shows probability-outputting agents can be faster and more auditable than language-model agents in a high-stakes clinical setting, though it remains a research result.

s64c2a355e9.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
s64c2a355e9.description: arXiv:2611.23702v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are pushing research toward semi-automation: ideas turn into preprints ever faster, and autoresearch pipelines add papers of uneven rigor. When a technique can be overtaken within months, citations arrive too late to tell which new papers deserve reading, so strong work goes unnoticed and newcomers lose their bearings. Yet from the day it appears, a preprint carries the track records of the people and institutions behind it. Established researchers guard their reputations and choose problems and collaborators with research taste, so their involvement tends to raise a paper's quality floor. Building on this signal, we present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight arXiv discovery tool that weights each paper's topic
s64c2a355e9.summary: KnowMe Paper Radar proposes a lightweight method for discovering promising preprints by using author and institution track records amid rising autoresearch output.
s64c2a355e9.why: Addresses discovery problems as LLM-assisted papers multiply, though the abstract provides little on results or tools.

s1b99b0ff5e.title: Can Vision-Language Models Synthesize Executable Game-Playing Programs?
s1b99b0ff5e.description: arXiv:2611.27741v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have endowed multimodal agents with increasingly strong visual perception and long-horizon reasoning capabilities, making VLM-based autonomous game playing feasible. Existing game benchmarks primarily evaluate whether an agent can select appropriate actions from the current visual state across different scenarios and games. However, most of them adopt a step-by-step interaction paradigm where the current visual observation is sent to the agent before each action. In practical deployment, this paradigm introduces two fundamental limitations: the game loop must wait for model inference, making real-time interaction impractical, and repeated VLM calls incur substantial cost. Therefore, we prop
s1b99b0ff5e.summary: A revised arXiv paper asks whether vision-language models can synthesize executable programs that play games, rather than choosing actions step by step.
s1b99b0ff5e.why: It suggests agents might write game-playing code from visual input instead of querying the model before every action, which could cut inference costs in deployment.

sd948e33594.title: Neur2BiLO: Neural Bilevel Optimization
sd948e33594.description: arXiv:2402.02552v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Bilevel optimization deals with nested problems in which a leader takes the first decision to minimize their objective function while accounting for a follower's best-response reaction. Constrained bilevel problems with integer variables are particularly notorious for their hardness. While exact solvers have been proposed for mixed-integer linear bilevel optimization, they tend to scale poorly with problem size and are hard to generalize to the non-linear case. On the other hand, problem-specific algorithms (exact and heuristic) are limited in scope. Under a data-driven setting in which similar instances of a bilevel problem are solved routinely, our proposed framework, Neur2BiLO, embeds a neural network approximation of the leader'
sd948e33594.summary: A revised arXiv paper introduces Neur2BiLO, a neural approach to constrained bilevel optimization with integer variables, which is hard for existing exact solvers.
sd948e33594.why: Exact solvers scale poorly and generalize badly to nonlinear cases, so a learned method could help teams solve hard leader-follower decision problems.

s4bf33bb5a8.title: Polyrating: A Cost-Effective and Bias-Aware Rating System for LLM Evaluation
s4bf33bb5a8.description: arXiv:2409.00696v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Rating-based human evaluation has become an essential tool to accurately evaluate the impressive performance of large language models (LLMs). However, current rating systems suffer from several important limitations: first, they fail to account for biases that significantly influence evaluation results, second, they require large and expensive preference datasets to obtain accurate ratings, and third, they do not facilitate meaningful comparisons of model ratings across different tasks. To address these issues, we introduce Polyrating, an expressive and flexible rating system based on maximum a posteriori estimation that enables a more nuanced and thorough analysis of model performance at lower costs. Polyrating can detect and quant
s4bf33bb5a8.summary: A revised arXiv paper proposes Polyrating, a rating system for LLM human evaluation that accounts for bias, needs less preference data, and compares ratings across tasks.
s4bf33bb5a8.why: Teams running LLM evaluations could get more reliable model rankings from fewer expensive human judgments while controlling for evaluator bias.
