s5f295f7079.title: Pitfalls of Dependency-Ready Decoding for Masked Diffusion Language Models
s5f295f7079.description: arXiv:2611.33823v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Masked diffusion models (MDMs) have shown strong performance on structured reasoning tasks such as Sudoku, Trip Planning, and Countdown. MDMs introduce a freedom in the order in which tokens may be unmasked, and to exercise this freedom for good accuracy, early decoding strategies relied on signals of confidence or the downstream impact of decoding a token. However, simple examples seem to illustrate that resolving a token's dependencies before unmasking it should be important. Therefore, we examine whether this principle, which we call dependency-ready decoding, would contribute to better accuracy, from a practical and a theoretical perspective. We examine a recent decoder that implements dependency-readiness through attention, and general
s5f295f7079.summary: Researchers examine whether resolving token dependencies before unmasking, called dependency-ready decoding, improves accuracy in masked diffusion language models on structured reasoning tasks.
s5f295f7079.why: It tests a decoding-order assumption that could affect how engineers schedule generation in masked diffusion models for reasoning tasks.

sb476751966.title: Information Discernment in Large Language Models
sb476751966.description: arXiv:2607.19355v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: LLMs are increasingly used with external knowledge sources like the internet. Do they weigh information appropriately -- updating more for reliable sources (source discernment) and more when claims bring priors closer to the truth (truth discernment)? We formalize this as information discernment and introduce Learn2Discern (L2D), an experimental framework and benchmark grounded in three normative axioms with interpretable metrics. To establish external validity, a pre-registered, quota-matched user study (n=299) confirms that real LLM users endorse all three axioms and report that violations reduce their trust and usage intent. Across 13 models and nearly 670K trials, we find consistent failures across both dimensions: models perform near
sb476751966.summary: Researchers introduce Learn2Discern, a framework and benchmark measuring how LLMs weigh information by source reliability and by truth relative to their priors, backed by a 299-person user study.
sb476751966.why: Shows whether LLMs update appropriately on external sources, which matters for any product that feeds web or retrieved content into models.

s50bbe0428a.title: AutoPILOT: A Visual Agent Harness for Real-Time Gameplay
s50bbe0428a.description: arXiv:2611.28202v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Multimodal foundation models can play video games well when the game waits for them, but often fail when it keeps running. We find that much of this gap lies in the harness, which decides what the model sees, what it remembers, and how its outputs become actions over time. Existing harnesses such as VISTA improve the first two, yet turn each model call into at most one action, so the agent acts only as often as its model thinks. We introduce AutoPILOT, which changes the third: in each model call, the model can send a primitive action, start an open-loop macro, or write a closed-loop controller that keeps playing from the screen without further model calls until it hands control back. To evaluate agents in real-time games, we build AFK-Ben
s50bbe0428a.summary: AutoPILOT is a visual agent harness that lets a multimodal model send primitive actions and keep acting during real-time games rather than one action per model call.
s50bbe0428a.why: It shows harness design, not just model choice, can close the gap for agents operating in continuously running environments.

s17e2ca2217.title: Engram: Multi-Stage Memory for Agentic Tuning of Heterogeneous Models
s17e2ca2217.description: arXiv:2611.28356v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents can now tune neural networks, yet without cross-session memory they spend costly trials rediscovering known lessons. Reuse is difficult because production models differ in architecture, training setup and inference budget. We present Engram, a memory system that links past trial outcomes with the hypotheses and rationale behind them and assesses whether this evidence applies to the current model. An online agent curates evidence at the decision points where it is needed: Initial Guidance supplies validated lessons at the start, Session Retrieval supplies related past sessions before each batch of hypotheses is generated, and Trial Candidate Review checks each trial candidate against matching past trials.
s17e2ca2217.summary: Engram is a multi-stage memory system that lets LLM agents reuse past tuning trial outcomes and rationale across sessions and heterogeneous models, checking whether evidence applies to the current model.
s17e2ca2217.why: Cross-session memory could cut costly repeated trials for agents that tune models in production settings.

s8deca33384.title: Learning Heterogeneous Reasoning in Large Language Models: From Mode Compatibility to Local Bottlenecks
s8deca33384.description: arXiv:2611.30281v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Post-training large language models routinely pools reasoning trajectories from diverse teachers or algorithms, yet it remains unclear whether standard supervised fine-tuning (SFT) can learn such heterogeneous strategies without explicit mode conditioning. We study the learnability and local bottlenecks of heterogeneous reasoning through a formal mixture formulation and controlled experiments. We first formalize the representational compatibility of the optimal autoregressive model with latent reasoning mixtures: the target next-token distribution weights modes by their prefix posteriors and concentrates on a single mode once alternative modes assign negligible likelihood to the prefix. In a verifiable symbolic graph-search environment wi
s8deca33384.summary: The paper studies whether standard supervised fine-tuning can learn heterogeneous reasoning mixtures from diverse teachers without explicit mode conditioning, and identifies local bottlenecks.
s8deca33384.why: Clarifies when pooling reasoning traces from multiple teachers into SFT works, relevant to post-training data pipelines.

s5292c9ad0d.title: Reproducible by Seed? Not on GPUs: Batch-Dependent Non-Determinism in Text-to-Image Models
s5292c9ad0d.description: arXiv:2611.30545v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In text to image AI models, fixing the prompt and the random seed is widely assumed to fix the image. We show that it does not on GPUs. We evaluate six text-to-image models (diffusion and autoregressive) under four numerical precisions and quantizations on three GPU types (RTX A6000, RTX 6000 Ada, and H100 NVL), across up to 100 prompts per set for all six models. For each configuration we compare, with the prompt and seed fixed, the image generated alone with the image generated inside a batch, and we also compare across GPUs. Every replay control reported here is bit-exact, so the variation is not random noise: the execution setting, mainly the batch composition and the GPU, decides the output. The effect is large and model dependent. S
s5292c9ad0d.summary: Researchers find that fixing prompt and seed does not reproduce text-to-image outputs on GPUs, because batch composition and GPU type change results across six models and several precisions.
s5292c9ad0d.why: Reproducibility tests and image pipelines must account for batching and hardware, or identical seeds will yield different outputs.

sb6fc1cc13f.title: United in Diversity? Contextual Biases in LLM-Based Predictions of the 2024 European Parliament Elections
sb6fc1cc13f.description: arXiv:2409.09045v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: "Silicon samples" based on large language models (LLMs) have been argued to serve as efficient alternatives to surveys of humans, assuming that their training data includes information on human attitudes and behavior. However, LLM-generated survey data might exhibit biases, for example due to a lack of diversity in training and alignment processes, which risk reinforcing existing biases in research and policymaking. In this study, we examine to what extent LLM-based predictions of individual public opinion exhibit context-dependent biases by predicting the results of the 2024 EU elections. Before the elections have taken place, we prompt three LLMs with individual-level background information of 26,000 eligible European voters to pr
sb6fc1cc13f.summary: A study finds LLM-based predictions of individual public opinion for the 2024 European Parliament elections show context-dependent biases, questioning use of silicon samples as survey substitutes.
sb6fc1cc13f.why: Teams using LLM-generated survey data for research or policy should note context-dependent bias that could skew results.
